Supplicating the majesty of God the Father and of our Lord Jesus Christ, who rules everywhere, let us humbly beseech him, making commemoration for all bishops, priests, deacons, subdeacons, and all his ministers, that he may govern them by the Holy Spirit; that he may grant to those consecrated and devoted to him the virginal purity and the resolve of continence, whole and undefiled in every respect; that in his mercy he may sustain the laborious endurance of widows; that he may bestow the help of paternal compassion upon orphans; that he may grant mercy to the merciful and healing to the sick; that he may supply the earth’s abundance and a plentiful harvest; and that he may graciously hear those afflicted by punishments and vexations and the devout prayers of all. Through the Lord.

[Note: Cf. the prayer in Mabill., p. 294.]

[Note: Mabill., p. 253, has: “that he may preserve everywhere for himself the devoted and consecrated virginal purity and the glorious and blessed resolve of continence; that in his mercy he may sustain the laborious continence of widows; that he may bestow the help of paternal compassion upon orphans.”]

### Collect

Hear us, almighty God the Father, and grant what we ask through your only-begotten and firstborn Son, Jesus Christ, our Lord and God, living and abiding with you and the Holy Spirit forever and ever. Amen.

### Before the Names

Let us pray, dearest brothers, for our brothers who offer spiritual gifts to our God, asking that he may graciously accept their offering and restore to them, for their small...

## (Mass VIII)

### Preface

O good Creator of the world, shining from your starry seat,

show yourself merciful: do not here weigh our crimes;

receive the prayers laid before you, and, in the balance of judgment,

being more merciful, do not render punishment in equal measure;

forgive the errors of the flock, and, faithful shepherd,

return the rescued sheep to the pastures of paradise. Through the Lord our God.

[Note: *pensas* (“you weigh”) is to be read.]

[Note: *ovibus*, “sheep,” is in place of *obibus*.]

### Collect

Most high, who satisfy all things, cultivator who uprooted the thorns,

you planted the faithful plantings of the catholic Church.

Bend your eyes toward the vows, merciful one; act with serene mind,

so that this vineyard, dug by the apostolic mattock,

smiling in its leaves and flourishing with living branches,

refreshed by your dewy spring and troubled by no heat,

may nourish eternal fruits with a fruitful shoot,

and may please you by the abundant birth of its harvest. Through the Lord.

[Note: *flecte*, “bend,” is printed as *plecte*.]

[Note: *aeternos*, “eternal,” is intended in place of *aeternus*, “eternity.”]

[Note: *fertilis*, “fruitful,” is intended in place of *fertiles*, “fertile.”]

[Note: *vindemia*, “harvest,” should be read in place of *vindimiae*, “vintage.”]

### Before the Names

Grant help, O ruler, and turn your favorable face toward us,

receiving what we give and yourself repaying what we ask;

and although the mind, touched by its own guilt, trembles,

or the sacred cause commends those who render sacred things,

grant this special good: that with faithful heart

we may live for the Lord and die cleansed from sin. Through the Lord.

[Note: *adnue*, “grant,” should be read in place of *adnuae*.]

[Note: *reatu*, “guilt,” should be read in place of *reatus*, “guilty.”]

[Note: Cf. Romans 6:2, 10; 8:12. Hence Mone concludes that *crimine*, “sin,” is used in the dative and that *et* has been omitted through asyndeton. It may perhaps be better to say that *crimine* is ablative, indicating that in or by sin the Christian ceases to live, while *mundo* is dative, indicating the one for whom he dies, to whom, through death, he is taken away. D.]

### After the Names

What divine honor demands, and what the funeral rites of those who love demand, rendering a solemn tribute to God by their service: for these let us humbly beseech the Lord with twin prayers [the verse is compressed and its construction uncertain],

so that those whom guilt has pressed down, merciful compassion may release,

and through the intervention of this sacred offering

life may be given to the living and forgiveness to the dead. Through the Lord.

[Note: *solemne*, “solemn,” is intended in place of *solemni*, “solemnly.”]

[Note: *precemur*, “let us pray,” should be read in place of *praecemur*, “let us beseech.”]

[Note: *libaminis*, “of the offering,” should be read in place of *libamini*. Mabill., p. 191: “that you may grant life to the living and rest to the dead.” From this prayer Mone wrongly concluded that the Mass was for the dead, rather than—as the Preface shows—in honor of the Holy Innocents, since in each Mass the prayer after the names concerns both the living and the dead.]

### At Peace

Ruler of the world, summit of things, single refuge of the accused,

slow to vengeance, swift to pardon, unmindful of anger,

you search out places where you may spare the wretched,

inviting them rather to gifts, lest you condemn their crimes.

Bind faith among the peoples; sow peace; join hearts,

so that they may hold in mind what gentle lips reveal. Through the Lord our God.

[Note: *damnes*, “you condemn,” is intended.]

[Note: *sere*, “sow,” should be read in place of *serere*, “to sow.”]

### Contestatio

It is fitting and just that we offer worthy thanks to you, supreme God, who always remain and rule everywhere,

and who, powerful over all things, animate them in their proper forms;

you make them by the craftsman’s word, and, seeing and creating what has been brought forth, you form their shapes through names.

When they were being made, the voice was the seed; nor did nature, following the command, delay their birth.

Then the spirit of the mouth bent the ether, joined the solid [elements], and poured out the accustomed seas;

the will alone supplied the material of the work,

lest a similar image bear a deformed yoke.

The ruler lay hidden beneath a servile covering,

so that the gentiles might complete the beginnings of their fury.

What deceit of Herod, when he stirred up mournful wars,

[ordering] infants to death! As they are snatched away [printed *ubire* is corrupt], wounds meet them, wandering over their little limbs and scarcely likely to find a place; and, when the savage tyrant commanded it,

to be born became a punishment, whose assault carried away their lives.

He destroyed the one whom he did not know was being attacked [the printed construction is uncertain]. O new condition of death: to undergo life alone in place of an end [printed *pro fine*; the sense remains uncertain].

And when the first day and the last day are simultaneously one,

to be able rather than to know how to die.

Who, with dry eyes or without ceasing from lamentation,

could recount, in memory of Pilate, the crime over which the elements grieved?

Under whose judgment Christ willed to subject his limbs to dangers for the world,

so that flesh might undo carnal evil and savage enemies [printed plural *feros hostis*],

from whose ingenuity the arrows of poison flowed;

so that he might destroy the tearful guilt of the ancient war,

the equal material overcoming it, and so that thereafter

the burden of sin might not proceed through offspring.

The condemnation of the Just One became freedom for the guilty.

Give the seeds of the Word through your gifts; cultivate them

and use the new signs.

May this hand gather these sheaves, with you making them fruitful,

from which you yourself may fill the granaries of heaven,

and crown faithful wheat when the darnel perishes.

Through him all things that are heavenly always [offer] you,

and your virtues, in sacred melody, sing a hymn with this song:

We ask that you now command us to hear those who sing,

and that our praises may be pleasing to you when we say them:

To whom: Holy, holy, holy.

[Note: *artefice*, “by the craftsman,” is intended, as below *servile* is used for *servili*.]

[Note: *cernens* and *creans*, “seeing” and “creating,” are participles in the text, but the sense requires the indicatives *cernis* and *creas*, “you see” and “you create.”]

[Note: Mueller correctly observed that *nexuit*, “joined,” should be read. Mone, not having noticed this, supposed an elision in *sueta aequora* and proposed changing only *sola* to *solida* or *solidata*. *Sola* is the plural neuter of the very common word *solum*.]

[Note: The printed text has *sola ++*; the critical sign is attached to *sola*, “alone,” not to the following words.]

[Note: The final two characters are missing. Perhaps *regnatur* was read here, as above *dominatur*.]

[Note: Since the gentiles also contributed to the killing of infants, the killers are called “gentiles.”]

[Note: *raptos*, “snatched-away infants,” is intended.]

[Note: *quo judice*, “under whose judgment,” is intended in place of *quod judice*.]

[Note: Read *carnale*; the text has *ferus*.]

[Note: *ingenio*, “ingenuity,” should be read in place of *injenium*.]

[Note: *proderit*, “would proceed,” is intended in place of *prodiret*, “would go forth.”]

[Note: *colis* should be joined with *per tua dona*: “cultivate through your gifts.” Perhaps *colis* is used in place of the future *coles*.]

[Note: *maniplos*, “sheaves,” is intended in place of *manipolus*, “sheaf.”]

[Note: *corones*, “crown,” is intended in place of *coronis*, “crowned.”]

## Contestatio

It is fitting, right, and just that we strike out worthy praises to you, pious one:

light, way, life, beauty, refuge, spring, sower, ruler,

grace, sweetness, wisdom, glory, kingdom,

who, without beginning, endure without end through the age.

Your triple summit established the three greatest things of creation:

the sun, moon, and stars lit the world with radiance;

springs, cattle, grass, and shrub adorned the earth with varied beauty;

fish, shellfish, stone, salt, and purple dye fill the seas.

Thus, Father, you fashioned the human being from pliable clay

and re-formed him after his sins through the cleansing spring.

Therefore, God of the universe, one Trinity,

this holy song resounds to you in angelic voices. To whom...

[Note: *perstas*, “you endure,” is intended in place of *praestas*, “you provide.”]

[Note: Here *eum* means *aevum*, “the age.” This form was still used for *aevum* by Frankish poets of the seventh century. For example: “And he will illuminate the house, never to be extinguished through the age” (Marten, *Thesaurus Anecdotorum* III, 1655).]

[Note: The “three greatest things of creation” are the three greatest divisions—heaven, earth, and sea—which correspond in the divine sphere to the Holy Trinity.]

[Note: *ductili*, “pliable,” is intended in place of *ductile*.]

[Note: *triades* means *trias*, “Trinity,” just as later hymns use *theoteta* in place of *theotes*. These forms arose from ignorance of Greek.]

### After the Sanctus

Truly fearful, holy, to be feared and loved,

creator, teacher, ruler, protector, worker,

you who, through your own only-begotten one, through whom [you manifested] paternal power, formed the beginnings of the world as they came to maturity [the syntax is corrupt], finally deigned to send him from the seat of heaven into the world.

He is present as the restorer of our souls. Through the Lord our God. Who, on the day before [his Passion]...

[Note: *reparator*, “restorer,” is intended in place of *reparatur*, “who is restored.”]

[Note: *virtute paterna*, “through paternal power,” is intended in place of *paternam*, “of the Father’s power.”]

[Note: *adolescentis*, “of the young one,” is intended in place of *adoliscentes*, “young ones.”]

### After the Secret

Have mercy, Lord, upon your suppliants, and, appeased, understand the humble petition of your people. Let the danger that presses upon us, when you have departed, move you to mercy. Look, we beg you, upon our tears. Hear, amid the abundance of our weeping, the sighs scarcely falling and the sobs that have been interrupted in prayer. Grant in judgment freedom to those whom you see pierced by confession, and whom you behold humbled by guilt, deign to reward with recompense, mitigating...

## (Mass IX)

### At Peace

...in the name of the Holy Spirit, in communion with all the saints, we shall believe in the remission of all our sins. We believe, Lord, that you will grant this to us when we ask with steadfast faith. Through the Lord.

[Note: *fixa*, “steadfast,” is intended in place of *fessa*, “wearied.”]

### Contestatio

It is fitting, just, right, and just that we always give thanks to you, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God. Among your holy patriarchs you deigned to give the most famous prophet Elijah, who moved between God and human beings as a vigorous ambassador, girded with the belt of chastity, and stood as a most faithful servant to appease the divine power.

He overflowed, desiring [something]; the printed phrase about the people (*gens cernicatam*) is corrupt. Amid lavish feasts he had neglected his homeland [the connection is uncertain]. The rights of a single shameless woman were observed; portentous images were worshiped, and the lawful commands of the sacred volumes were despised.

But Elijah burned, kindled by heavenly zeal, against the untamed people. Immediately he commanded the elements: he ordered the heavens and clouds not to give dew or rain. The earth mourned, deprived of dew; the dewy meadows were barren, and the earthly surface grew pale, fasting from sacred rites.

He again entreats the one who can be appeased, and the cataracts of rain are opened. He commands fire to descend from the heavenly region upon the sacrifice, so that the unpolluted victim may be carried from the starry [region] to *side*; the manuscript has *side*, and the editor proposes *sedes*, “seats.” The corrupt line does not securely say “to the stars.”

“What was that, I ask,” so wondrous and so great a prodigy? He restored alive to his mother her only son, now dead, who had earlier struck the infernal and death-bearing cavern [the printed syntax is corrupt, and the subject of “had struck” is uncertain].

Surrounded by these virtues, he proceeded as a servant toward the life of the angels. He is carried away in a fiery chariot, and, with horses surrounded by fire, flies through the stars. He ascends, surrounded by the ranks of angels; at whose translation one witness, Elisha, remains. He now enjoys the glorious choir and praises the King seated upon the throne. Rightly [we praise him].

[Note: The phrase concerning the people being marked out is apparently corrupt.]

[Note: These lines are scarcely not verse: “The earth mourned, deprived of dew; the dewy meadows [were barren], and the earthly surfaces grew pale, fasting from sacred rites.” Mone. Perhaps *ieiunis*, “with fasts,” should be read. D.]

[Note: *impolluta*, “unpolluted,” is intended.]

[Note: The manuscript reads *side*. It seems that *sedes*, “seat,” should be read.]

[Note: “What, I ask, was that?” is intended.]

[Note: *fruitur choro*, “he enjoys the choir,” is intended.]

### Contestatio

It is fitting and just; it is right and just that we always give thanks to you, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God.

You are glorified in holy praises; you reign in the heavens. You are the unblemished Lamb; you are the Son of the everlasting Father. You are the sacred splendour; crowned by all the martyrs; protector of souls, shepherd of orphans, governor of widows, illuminator of the blind, promiser of pardon to sinners, liberator of captives, saviour of the sick, raiser of the dead; planter of paradise, stabilizer of the sea, maker of heaven and earth, giver of understanding to the nations, summoner of catechumens to baptism, giver of priesthood to priests and apostolic authority to bishops.

You, Lord, possess heavenly things, judge earthly things, raise the things below, and govern eternal things. Rightly, Lord, all the angels [praise you]. Holy, holy, holy.

[Note: *pater*, “Father,” stands in place of the genitive.]

[Note: Mabill., p. 190, has: “Grant redemption to captives, sight to the blind, and remission to sinners.”]

## (Mass X)

### After the Prophecy

Holy God, founder of the Church, who, standing among your disciples, taught the mysteries of this veneration, grant grace from your divinity to my mouth, so that words acceptable in your praise may be found upon my lips. Let your face shine upon your servant, so that, freed from my burdens, I may also stand rightly to pray to you for your people. Through the Lord our God Jesus.

### Collect

Merciful and compassionate Lord, if you were to repay us what we deserve, you would find no one worthy of your mercies. Multiply your indulgence toward us, so that where sin abounded, the grace of forgiveness may overflow. Through the Lord.

[Note: Mabill., p. 258: “Where sin abounded, grace abounded still more.” Cf. p. 370; Romans 5:20.]

[Note: This Mass is not complete. Nothing is missing from the manuscript; the eleventh Mass follows immediately.]

[Note: “VII” is written here.]

[Note: This numeral corresponds to the numeral III at the beginning of Mass VII.]

## (Mass XI)

### On Saint Germanus, Bishop of Auxerre

[Note: The Mass of Saint Germanus in Mabill., p. 329, is much longer and therefore appears more recent.]

### Collect

Dearest brothers, let us pray together to the Lord that this solemnity of our most blessed father Germanus, bishop, begun with his merits and through his intercession, may grant peace to his people, increase faith, purify hearts, gird the loins, and open the gate of salvation. Through the Lord.

[Note: This form of the word *unianimes* is also found in Mabill., pp. 243, 244, and 246.]

### Before the Names

Hear us, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God. Through the merits or intercessions of your holy bishop and pontiff Germanus, preserve this people of yours in your mercy’s protection; preserve it through kindness and save it through compassion. Through the Lord.

### Collect after the Names

Let us pray, dearest brothers, that this offering of ours may be acceptable to the Lord, and that he may grant that those whom he sees devoted to the honor of his supreme priest, Bishop Germanus, may be pleasing to him, so that he may also grant rest and blessedness to the spirits of the dead. Through the Lord.

### At Peace

Grant, Lord, that through the intercession of your holy bishop Germanus, whose glory of blessedness we celebrate today in the sight of your majesty with worthy praises, we may lay aside hatreds and, in peace—for we are going to give ourselves to one another—open our pure and peaceful hearts to you. Through the Lord. May the peace of the Lord be [with you].

## Restored apparatus omitted from the draft

- **Mass V · Col. 0872D · after *profetarum oracula*:** Mabill., p. 190 reads *oracula vatum*, “the oracles of the seers.”
- **Mass V · Col. 0873D · after *veterisque delecti*:** read *delicti*, “offense/sin,” for *delecti*, “chosen.”
- **Mass VI · Col. 0873D · after *sanguis in uinis*:** read *venis*, “veins,” for *uinis*, “wines/vines.”
- **Mass VI · Col. 0874D · after *creatoris*:** the letters printed in italics are absent from the manuscript; Mone supplied the word in this form.
- **Mass VI · Col. 0874D · after “earth [received] soul, soul spirit, spirit reason”:** Mone compares the similar ascending sequence at Mabill., p. 298: “may you look favorably; by looking, sanctify; by sanctifying, bless.” The editor warns that the distinction of body, soul, spirit, and reason must not be referred to Platonic anthropology, which admitted three substances in a human being: soul and spirit here are only distinct faculties of the same substance.
- **Mass VI · Col. 0874D · at *distenas*:** read *destinas*, “you appoint/designate.”
- **Mass VI · Col. 0874D · at *mittendum*:** read *mittendo*, “by sending”; the clause means that God appoints the means of redemption by sending the only-begotten Son.
- **Mass VIII · Col. 0877D · at *relaxit*:** read subjunctive *relaxet*, “may release,” for indicative *relaxit*, “released.”
- **Mass VIII · Col. 0877D · at *dominatur*:** read noun *dominator*, “ruler,” for verb *dominatur*, “rules.”
- **Mass VIII · Col. 0878C · after “the voice was the seed”:** Mabill. reads *quod seminavit verbo*, “which he sowed by the Word.”
- **Mass VIII · Col. 0878D · at *uirtuisque toas*:** read *tuas, virtutes*, “your virtues,” correcting both transmitted forms.
- **Mass VIII · Col. 0878D · at *piae*:** *piae*, “pious” in an oblique form, is used in place of vocative *pie*, “O pious one.”
- **Mass VIII · Col. 0879D · at *tria maxime rerum*:** read *maxima*, “greatest,” for *maxime*, “especially,” as in the last verse of this Contestatio, *carmina*.
- **Mass IX · Col. 0880D · at *purtentuosae*:** read *portentosa*, “portentous/monstrous.”
- **Mass IX · Col. 0880D · at *indometa plebem*:** *indometa*, “untamed,” is used in place of the accusative *indometam* required with *plebem*, “people.”
- **Mass X · Col. 0881D · after the numeral VII:** this numeral corresponds specifically to the cipher III at the beginning of Mass VII.

## Contestation

It is worthy and just, O our God; truly it is worthy always to give thanks to your majesty and, with joy and exultation, to proclaim in your praises the praises of your saints; to raise up their praises and continually exult in their virtue [Note: “to exalt,” Col. 0882D]. For our most blessed father, your bishop Germanus, whose annual and principal feast of disposition [Note: “deposition,” Col. 0882D] we celebrate today, possessed such great love and affection toward you, O Lord, such that, trampling underfoot the seduction of the present age, he stretched forth by wondrous virtue toward future blessedness. He could not be bound by the cords of sins, nor touched by the swords or arrows of the ancient enemy, since your protection had made him a free and secure shepherd for his sheep through the breastplate of justice and the shield of faith.

For these sheep, to be sure, he was established at all times in almsgiving, fasting, and vigils as an outstanding shepherd; he desired rather to die than in any way to be overcome by the bites of the rapacious wolf. He was also the most just judge of the Church, first in wisdom, outstanding in spiritual instruction, great in humility, gentle in affability, strong in patience, necessary in the discernment of doctrine, a father in religion, a brother in love, a friend of faith, close to mercy. He helped his fellow bishops by prayer, supplemented them by counsel, and admonished them by authority. He loved your priests, deacons, and the entire clergy, and your whole people, O Lord, as his own members [Note: “and the whole,” Col. 0882D]; he raised up the oppressed, sustained the tireless, made the dissenting peaceful, and taught the discordant to preserve concord. He restored sight to the blind, walking to the lame, and medicine to the feverish; and he swiftly freed souls cast down by unclean spirits.

Therefore, with him interceding, we, your suppliants [Note: “suppliant,” Col. 0882D], ask for the mercy of your compassion [Note: “of your compassion,” Col. 0882D], almighty Lord: since we cannot be made equal to his merits, may we at least [Note: “at least,” Col. 0882D] deserve to obtain forgiveness for our sins, praising you with angelic exultation, for whom the angels rightly cry out, saying:

[Col. 0882C]

1. [lacuna] our sins, unequal to our [lacuna]. Unjustly we are in need; we have committed iniquity; we have lost all the inheritances of your gifts. The shame of our sinful stain: our house, an alien [Note: “alien,” Col. 0882D], has been invaded by the enemy. We have been made subject, slaves to those who rule over us, bound by the chain of offenses [Note: “delicts,” Col. 0882D]. Turn us, O Lord, to serve you; renew us by the working of your commandment [Note: “renew the working,” Col. 0882D]. Through our Lord.

2. Hear, O Lord, I beseech you, the groaning of your people. May the offense of those who sin not have more weight with you than mercy, always forgiving those who weep and entreat. Through our Lord.

# Ancient Litanies and Prayers

[Col. 0885]

# Carolingian Litanies

*(From Mabillon, Analecta, new edition, p. 170.)*

## Notice

I call these litanies Carolingian because they were written during the rule of Charlemagne, under Hadrian, the supreme pontiff, in the Parthenon—so I suppose—of blessed Mary at Soissons. My conjecture rests not only on the fact that these litanies celebrate the holy bishops of that city, Bantaridus and Drauscius, the latter the first founder of the said Parthenon, but especially because they mention the saints Vodoalus and Leodardus, one of whom was a recluse and the other a baker in the same monastery before the ninth century.

Nevertheless, the learned and religious Peter Francis Chiffletius of the Society of Jesus extracted these litanies from a manuscript codex of Besançon and transmitted them to our Achery. What is added at the end concerning Rotrude, Charlemagne’s daughter, if I am not mistaken, is an addition by her brother or sister.

In these litanies one may observe the barbarous Roman language that had been adopted for ordinary use in that age, in the expressions “Tulo juva” and “Tulos juva,” where we ordinarily say “Help him” and “Help them.”

In the list of saints I note only one matter: among the holy angels, Orie[l], Rague[l], and Tobie[l] are invoked. Pope Zacharias determined that these names belonged not to angels but to demons, at the Roman council convened against Clement and Adalbert in 745. The letter of the learned John Baptist Thiers, prefixed to his dissertation *On Retaining the Word PARACLETE*, concerns this matter.

Be merciful; spare us, Lord.

Be merciful; deliver us, Lord.

From every evil, deliver us.

From every iniquity, deliver us.

From every evil thought, deliver us.

From every uncleanness of mind and body, deliver us.

From our sins, deliver us.

From your anger, deliver us.

From the persecution of enemies, deliver us.

From anger, hatred, and every evil will, deliver us.

From the snares of the devil, deliver us.

From the snares of men, deliver us.

From future anger, deliver us.

From the evil sword, deliver us.

From pagan peoples, deliver us.

[Col. 0896B] From faithless nations, deliver us.

From plague and destruction, deliver us.

From lightning and storm, deliver us.

From sudden and eternal death, deliver us.

From blindness of heart, deliver us.

From plague, famine, and the sword, deliver us.

From carnal desires, deliver us.

From every uncleanness of mind and body (twice), deliver us.

From unclean thoughts, deliver us.

From visible and invisible enemies, deliver us.

From various illnesses, deliver us.

From the punishments of hell, deliver us.

From the power of the devil, deliver us.

From the pleasures of the flesh, deliver us.

From the spirit of lust and uncleanness, deliver us.

[Col. 0896C] From domination by every vice, deliver us.

From sudden death, deliver us.

From the punishments of hell (twice), deliver us.

From all eternal torments, deliver us.

From excessive rain, deliver us.

Through the mystery of your holy incarnation, deliver us.

Through your coming, deliver us.

Through your birth, deliver us.

Through your baptism, deliver us.

Through your holy fasting, deliver us.

Through your passion, deliver us.

Through your holy cross, deliver us.

Through your holy resurrection, deliver us.

Through your wondrous ascension, deliver us.

Through the grace of the Holy Spirit the Paraclete, deliver us.

[Col. 0896D] On the day of judgment, deliver us.

At your second coming, deliver us.

A sinner, we ask you, hear us.

That you may spare us, we ask you.

That you may grant us peace, we ask you.

That you may grant us health, we ask you.

That you may deign to rule and defend your Church, we ask you.

That you may always deign to exalt her, we ask you.

That you may deign to preserve the apostolic lord and all the ranks of the Church in holy religion, we ask you.

That you may deign to grant our kings and princes peace, [Col. 0897A] true concord, and victory, we ask you.

That you may deign to preserve our bishops and abbots, and all the communities entrusted to them, in holy religion, we ask you.

That you may deign to preserve our community in holy religion, we ask you.

That you may deign to grant the entire Christian people peace and unity, we ask you.

That you may deign to preserve the assembly of all your saints in your holy service, we ask you.

That you may grant us contrition of heart and a fountain of tears, we ask you.

That you may grant us tranquil times, we ask you.

[Col. 0897B] That you may grant us amendment, we ask you.

That you may grant us contrition of heart and body, we ask you.

That you may grant us temperate weather, we ask you.

That you may deign to give and preserve the fruit of the earth, we ask you.

That you may grant us a fountain of tears, we ask you.

That you may grant us the spirit of repentance, we ask you.

That you may deign to grant us and enable us to perform true repentance, we ask you.

That you may give us indulgence and remission of all our sins, we ask you.

That you may deign mercifully to pour the grace of the Holy Spirit into our hearts, we ask you.

That you may give us faith, hope, and charity, we ask you.

[Col. 0897C] That you may give us right faith, we ask you.

That you may give us your grace, we ask you.

That you may deign to lead us to eternal joys, we ask you.

That your mercy and compassion may guard us, we ask you.

That you may deign to guard us here and forever, we ask you.

That you may order our days and deeds in your peace, we ask you.

That you may make the service of our servitude reasonable, we ask you.

That you may give us eternal life, we ask you.

That you may rescue our souls and those of our parents from eternal damnation, we ask you.

[Col. 0897D] That you may lead those who wander back to their way, we ask you.

[Col. 0898A] That you may deign to instruct us in regular disciplines, we ask you.

That you may deign to turn the eyes of your mercy upon us, we ask you.

That you may deign to send your holy angel from your protection to us, we ask you.

That we may deserve to obtain forgiveness for our sins, we ask you.

That you may deign to humble the enemies of the holy Church of God, we ask you.

That you may deign to crush the pagan nation, we ask you.

That you may deign to guard and strengthen us, your servants, in your holy service, we ask you.

That you may deign to humble all our enemies and adversaries, we ask you.

[Col. 0898B] That you may deign to save all our faithful friends, we ask you.

That you may deign to preserve all the ranks of the ecclesiastical order in holy religion, we ask you.

That you may restore health of mind and body to our brothers and to all the faithful who are ill, we ask you.

That you may direct us into the way of peace and charity, we ask you.

That you may deign to grant eternal rest to our deceased brothers and to all the faithful, we ask you.

That the nations which trust in their savagery may be crushed by your right hand, we ask you.

That you may deign to protect and defend this city, we ask you.

[Col. 0898C] That you may deign to preserve all your faithful who dwell in it, we ask you.

That you may guard us today without sin, we ask you.

That you may deign to hear us, we ask you.

That you may deign to have mercy on us, we ask you.

Through the merits of these and all your saints, spare, forgive, and have mercy, Lord. Take away from me whatever in me displeases you. Receive the sacrifice from my hands, peacefully and kindly. Deliver me from [Col. 0901A] the hands of my enemies and from those who persecute me. Make your face shine upon your servant, and save [Col. 0902A] me in your mercy; let me not be put to shame, for I call upon you, who live and reign.

*(In Bandini, Catalogue of the Laurentian Library, p. 183.)*

8 Kalends of October. For the conception of Saint John the Baptist.

[Col. 0903A]

Prayer. Almighty and everlasting God, who fulfilled the legal institutions and the proclamations of the holy prophets in the days of the conception of blessed John the Baptist, grant, we ask, that when the figures of the signs have ceased, the truth itself may speak through its manifestation. Through, etc.

Secret. Grant, we ask, merciful God, that, instructed by the mystical beginnings of your Church and by the sacred proclamations of blessed John the Baptist, it may continually produce worthy fruits of salvation for avoiding the wrath of the coming judgment. Through, etc.

At Communion. Bless your people, Lord, and grant that those who trust in the intercessions of blessed John the Baptist may attain the help of devotion. Through, etc.

8 Ides of October. Of Saint Reparata the virgin.

Grant, we ask, Lord, that your faithful may worthily celebrate the mysteries of Saint Reparata, so that those who faithfully perform her solemn rites may experience her help here and attain the effects of eternity. Through, etc.

Secret. Look favorably, Lord, we ask, upon these gifts; and, so that we may be acceptable to you, may this offering, consecrated with a contrite heart, be made pleasing to you through the prayers of your martyr Reparata. Through, etc.

Communion. May this communion of your grace, Lord, we ask, render us acceptable to you, and may the venerable commemoration of your martyr Reparata renew our hearts through the divine mysteries. Through, etc.

8 Kalends of November. Of Saint Miniatus the martyr.

[Col. 0904A]

Prayer. Almighty and everlasting God, who raised the martyrs Miniatus and his companions to immortal triumphs through the glorious battles of their contest, grant our hearts worthy joy at their commemoration, so that we, who celebrate their bodies with devoted love, may be aided by their prayers. Through, etc.

Secret. May your people always rejoice, Lord, in the saving sacrifice by which due honor is shown to the holy martyrs and the gift of your sanctification is acquired. Through, etc.

At Communion. As we celebrate the blessed passion of your martyrs Miniatus and his companions, may these rites, we ask, become saving for us through their intercession, on whose birthdays they are joyfully performed. Through, etc.

Ides of November. Of Saint Britius the confessor.

[Col. 0904B]

Be favorable, Lord, to your people, so that those whom you grant to participate in the commemoration of your blessed priest and confessor Britius, you may always make secure through perpetual protection. Through, etc.

Secret. May the gifts we bring, Lord, we ask, in commemoration of your blessed priest and confessor Britius be pleasing to you, as we beseech you that we may attain in mind what we proclaim with our lips. Through, etc.

At Communion. Grant, we ask, Lord, that through the prayers of your blessed priest and confessor Britius, whose feast we celebrate, we may experience forgiveness. Through, etc.

[Col. 0903]

THE PENITENTIAL RITE OF GERONA

*(In Flórez, Sacred Spain, vol. XLIII.)*

The reconciliation of penitents according to the ancient custom of the Church of Gerona.

[Col. 0903C] When the ninth hour has been sung, the bishop shall be vested in an alb, stole, and cope, with two archdeacons accompanying him in white stoles without dalmatics, and one subdeacon and two acolytes likewise in white, carrying a cross and lighted candlesticks, together with blessed water. The bishop shall go with them and with the entire clergy as far as the doors of the church, saying nothing.

The penitents who are to be reconciled shall stand there outside the very doors of the church. Their priests shall be with them, and shall give the bishop a true testimony concerning the conduct and amendment of life of those penitents, whether they have worthily observed the penance imposed upon them with all their strength, [Col. 0904C] and whether the priests themselves, as required by their office, have vigilantly attended to this.

One archdeacon, standing outside the doors of the church with the penitents, shall say in a loud voice:

“Behold, venerable pontiff, the acceptable time, the day of divine propitiation and human salvation, when death received destruction and eternal life its beginning; when new planting must be made in the vineyard of the Lord of Hosts in such a way that the curse of antiquity may be cleansed.

“For although no time is lacking for the way of the goodness and compassion of God, now nevertheless the forgiveness of all sins is more abundant through indulgence, and the reception of those reborn is richer through grace. We are increased by those being regenerated; we grow by those returning. The waters wash; the tears wash. From that comes the joy of those who are called; from this, the gladness arising from the absolution of penitents.

“Thus it is that your suppliants, after falling into various forms of crime through neglect of the heavenly commandments and transgression of commendable conduct, humbled and prostrate, cry out in the prophetic voice, saying: ‘We have sinned with our fathers; we have acted unjustly; we have committed iniquity. Have mercy on us, Lord; have mercy on us.’ And, not in vain receiving the evangelical saying, ‘Blessed are those who mourn, for they shall be comforted,’ they have eaten, as it is written, the bread of sorrow; [Col. 0905B] they have watered their bed with tears; they have afflicted their heart with grief and their body with fasts, so that they might recover the health of their souls which they had lost.

“There is therefore one aid of repentance, which benefits each person individually and comes to the assistance of all in common.”

When this has been completed, the bishop shall stand in the doorway of the church and give an exhortation to the penitents. But because this day, through the very works of healing of our Redeemer that today’s Gospel reading sets before us, is a day of forgiveness and grace, he shall mercifully relax the burden of penance for those who groan, promise amendment of life with great tears and deep sighs, until the octave of Pentecost; and he shall sing this antiphon:

“Come, come, come, children.”

And the choir shall respond:

“Come, listen to me; I will teach you the fear of the Lord.”

The deacon, on behalf of the penitents, shall say:

“Let us bend the knees.”

Then another deacon shall say:

“Rise.”

The bishop shall repeat a second time:

“Come, come, come, children.”

And the choir:

“Come, listen to me; I will teach you the fear of the Lord.”

And the archdeacon:

“Let us bend the knees.”

And the other:

“Rise.”

And the bishop:

“Come, come, come, children.”

And the choir:

“Come, listen to me; I will teach you the fear of the Lord.”

And the archdeacon:

“Draw near to him and be enlightened, and your faces shall not be put to shame.”

When this is finished, the clergy, divided into choirs beside the bishop, shall sing the entire psalm:

“I will bless the Lord at all times.”

Meanwhile, while this psalm is being sung, the penitents shall fall at the bishop’s feet and lie prostrate until the psalm is finished.

*(In the margin: Here let him sprinkle blessed water.)*

When this has been said, the bishop shall signal to the other deacon, who says:

“Rise.”

The penitents shall immediately rise. While they are presented to the bishop by their priests so that he may reconcile them to Mother Church, he shall take one of the penitents and ask his priest, saying:

“Is he worthy to be reconciled?” *(with chant)*

The priest:

“He is worthy.”

And the bishop shall say:

“Let him remain with you.”

And he shall give peace to the penitent, saying:

“Peace be with you.”

Afterward, all the other penitents shall likewise receive the kiss of peace from that penitent.

Then the bishop shall again ask all the remaining priests collectively about each of their own penitents, saying:

“Are they worthy to be reconciled?”

Response of the priests:

“They are worthy.”

And the bishop shall say to them:

“Let them remain with you.”

Thus all shall enter the church, the cantor beginning this antiphon:

“A clean heart.”

With the psalm:

“Have mercy on me, O God.”

Another psalm:

“Have mercy on me, O God, for he has trampled me down.”

Another psalm:

“Have mercy on me, O God; have mercy on me.”

After all those who are to be reconciled have been brought into the church, the bishop shall prostrate himself before the altar with his ministers and the penitents. When the psalms mentioned above, with the antiphon, have been completed, let the following be said:

“Lord, have mercy,” and “Our Father.”

And the bishop:

“O Lord, not according to our sins,” etc.

Response:

“Nor according to,” etc.

“O Lord, do not remember our iniquities,” etc.

Response:

“May they quickly go before us,” etc.

Let us pray.

Be present, Lord, to our supplications, and mercifully hear me, who also first need your healing; and since you have appointed me as minister of this work, not by a choice based on merit but by the gift of your grace, grant me confidence to carry out your charge, and work yourself through our ministry what belongs to your mercy. Through, etc.

Prayer for reconciliation. Grant, we ask, Lord, to your servants the fruit of repentance, so that those who, by sinning, had departed from the integrity of your Church may be restored harmless through obtaining forgiveness for their offenses. Through, etc.

Another. Most kind creator and most merciful restorer of the human race, who redeemed the human being cast down from eternity by the envy of the devil through the blood of your only Son, revive these servants of yours, whom you do not at all desire to perish for you; and, since you do not abandon those who have strayed, receive them when corrected. [Col. 0906C] Let the tearful sighs of these servants of yours move your mercy, Lord, we ask. Heal their wounds yourself. Stretch out your saving hand to those who lie fallen, lest your Church be ravaged in any part of its body, lest your flock suffer loss, lest the enemy rejoice at the ruin of your household, lest a second death possess those reborn through the saving washing.

To you, therefore, Lord, we pour out suppliant prayers; to you, the sorrow of our hearts. Spare those who confess, so that, with your help, they may mourn their sins in this mortal life in such a way that on the day of the dreadful judgment they may escape the sentence of eternal damnation and may not know what terrifies in darkness and what crackles in the flames. Having returned from the path of error to the way of righteousness, may they no longer be wounded by injuries, but may there remain whole and perpetual for them both what your grace has bestowed and what your mercy has restored. Through the same, etc.

Another prayer. We humbly beseech your Majesty, almighty God, that you may deign to grant the forgiveness of your compassion to these male and female servants of yours, long afflicted by the squalor of penance, so that, having received the wedding garment, they may be worthy to enter the royal banquet from which they had been cast out. Through, etc.

The final one: as in the order for commendation or in extreme unction.

[Col. 0907]

THE NECROLOGY OF GERONA

Taken from the Martyrology of Ado, written in the eleventh century and preserved in the church of Gerona.

*(In Flórez, at the place cited above.)*

[Col. 0907A] 3 Ides of January. On this day Berengarius, archbishop of Tarragona, died in the year 1099.

4 Kalends of March. On this day Count Raymond died in the sixteenth year after 1000 of the Lord’s *trabeatio* (wearing of the trabea).

2 Kalends of March. On this day Senderedus, archpriest, died in the year 966.

15 Kalends of May. On this day Arnulf, most illustrious bishop of Gerona, died in the year of the Lord 970. He ruled the Church for 15 years, 7 months, and 7 days, in the fifteenth year counted from the beginning of the reign of Lothair, king of the Franks.

9 Kalends of May. On this day, in the year 111 after 1000, Ermengaudus, bishop of Elne, died.

8 Kalends of June. In the year 1076 of the Lord’s incarnation, in the era 1114, indiction 13, Lord Raymond Berengar, count of Barcelona and marquis, died. [Col. 0907B]

4 Ides of July. On this day Peter, son of Pontius, archlevite of this see, died. He died on the expedition to Jerusalem in the year 1098 from the incarnation of the Lord. [Col. 0908A]

Kalends of August. On this day Bishop P. G. (Peter of Gerona) died. While diligently exercising the see of Gerona, in which he had held various ranks of honor, through divine calling he deserved a celibate life for love of the Mother of God.

12 Kalends of September. On this day Bishop Ato and Count Ermengaudus died. On this day Guillelmus Guifredi died, in the year 1067 of the Lord’s incarnation.

3 Nones of September. On this day Bernardus Umberti, bishop of this see, died in the year 111 after 1000 of the Lord’s incarnation.

5 Ides of October. On this day Sicardis, mother of Bishop Bernard, died.

15 Kalends of December. On this day Berengarius, bishop of Gerona, died in the year 93 after 1000 from the Lord’s incarnation. [Col. 0908B]

Nones of December. Raymond Berengar, count of Barcelona, died.

[Col. 0907]

THE MASS OF THE ETHIOPIANS, ALSO CALLED THE UNIVERSAL CANON

*(Maxima Bibliotheca Patrum, Supplement, vol. XXVII.)*

IN THE NAME OF THE FATHER, AND OF THE SON, AND OF THE HOLY SPIRIT. AMEN.

[Col. 0907C]

The choir begins: Alleluia.

But I, in the abundance of your mercy, shall enter your house.

I shall worship toward your holy temple in fear of you.

I shall give thanks to you, Lord, with my whole heart, for you have heard the words of my mouth.

In the presence of the angels I shall sing to you; I shall worship toward your holy temple.

Let your priests be clothed with righteousness, and let your holy ones rejoice with rejoicing.

You shall sprinkle me with hyssop, Lord, and I shall be cleansed; you shall wash me, and I shall become whiter than snow.

Wash me yet more from my iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin. [Col. 0907D]

And spare your servant from strangers.

[Col. 0908C] He gave them the bread of heaven.

Man ate the bread of angels.

I shall wash my hands among the innocent, and I shall encompass your altar, Lord.

I went around and sacrificed in his tabernacle a sacrifice of shouting.

You have prepared a table before me against those who afflict me.

You have anointed my head with oil, and how splendid is my overflowing cup!

I shall receive the cup of salvation and call upon the name of the Lord.

Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord! We have blessed you from the house of the Lord.

Hail, our mother, holy Church, fortified by a wall, adorned with topaz. Our mother, the Church, hail.

[Col. 0909A] You are that vessel of pure gold in which the hidden manna was kept, and you are the tabernacle of bread descending from heaven, giving life to all for eternity.

IN THE NAME OF THE FATHER, AND OF THE SON, AND OF THE HOLY SPIRIT. AMEN.

Before everything else, the priest says the following prayers for the church, the altar, and their vestments:

Lord our God, you alone are holy, who have given sanctification to all through your hidden power. Thus we humbly beseech you, Lord, that you may deign to send the Holy Spirit upon this church, upon this altar, and upon everything prepared for the sacred mysteries. Bless again, sanctify, and cleanse them from every stain and pollution, so that nothing unbelieving or unclean may remain in them. Make the things of this church and altar clean and chosen, like silver tested by fire, proved, and purified sevenfold. Complete the mystery of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit upon them, now and always and throughout ages of ages. Amen.

When the prayer is finished, the altar is vested and everything is prepared for the sacrifice, and the following follows:

Lord, Lord God, searcher of every heart, who reveal hidden things and know everything, each thing individually: you are holy, resting upon the holy. You alone are without sin, powerful to erase sins. You know, Lord, that I am unclean for this holy mystery that proceeds from you; I am not fit to approach it, nor to open my mouth to praise your holiness and give thanks. But because of the abundance of your mercies alone, spare me, Lord, for I am a sinner. Grant and permit me, Lord—if in this hour I may find mercy—and send down from above, Lord, your strength, so that I may become worthy to complete your holy mysteries, for the sake of the desire and joy of your heart.

May this incense and offering be a good fragrance in your sight; and may you, Lord our God and our Savior Jesus Christ, be with us and bless us. You are the one who removes our sins, the illuminator of our soul, our life, our power, and our entrance. To you we give thanks before your throne, now and always and throughout ages of ages. Amen.

Prayer over the paten.

Lord our God, Jesus Christ, who stretched out your hands upon the wood of the holy cross, stretch them likewise over this paten on which your sacred body is ministered. Bless + it now, sanctify it, and cleanse it, so that your holy body may be perfected upon it in this holy and apostolic church, for to you be glory, and to your heavenly Father, with the life-giving Holy Spirit, now and always and throughout ages of ages. Amen.

Prayer over the chalice.

Lord our God Jesus Christ, truly (*ἀληθεῶς*), who truly became God and human being and were never separated from your divinity, and who willingly poured out your precious blood for the sake of your fragile creature, [Col. 0910A] now cause your hands to be over this chalice. + Bless, + sanctify, + and purify it, so that your holy blood may be consecrated in it, in this your apostolic church. To you be glory, with your most excellent Father and the Holy Spirit, now and always and throughout ages of ages. Amen.

Blessing, purity, + and sweetness to all who receive your precious blood, truly (*alitheos*). Amen.

Prayer over the spoon, by which the lance of the cross is signified.

Lord our God, who deigned to grant to Isaiah the prophet and your servant that he should see the seraph receiving with tongs a burning coal from the sacrifice and cleansing his lips, likewise, almighty Father, [Col. 0910B] our Lord and our God, who contain all things, grant that your hands may be over this lance, so that it may be able worthily to minister the precious body and blood of your only Son, our Lord, God, and Savior Jesus Christ. Bless + it now, sanctify + it, and purify + it; grant it power and glory, as you granted to that pair of tongs. To you be glory with your only Son and the Holy Spirit, now and always and throughout ages of ages. Amen.

The power, + blessing, + and sanctification of the Holy Trinity be upon this church of Saint N. of Sceva [Note: [Col. 0909] The kingdom of Sceva is that which is called Saba.]. To you be glory with your Son and the Holy Spirit, now and always and throughout ages of ages. Amen.

Prayer over the small ark in which the host for the sacrifice is placed.

[Col. 0910C] Lord our God, who on Mount Sinai commanded Moses, your servant and prophet, to gather selected things whose use was in the ministry of the altar, the ark, and the sanctuary in your tabernacle, now, Lord our almighty God, grant that your hands may be over this small ark, and fill it with the power, strength, purity, and grace of the Holy Spirit for your glory, so that in it the body of our only Lord, our God and Savior, Jesus Christ, may be perfected in this holy apostolic church. To you be glory, and to your only Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and always and throughout ages of ages. Amen.

+ May God the Father, to whom praise and honor belong, grant us acceptable sanctification and forgiveness of sins, now and always and throughout ages of ages. [Col. 0910D] Amen.

When the priest offers the host upon the altar, he says the following prayer:

Lord our God, who accepted the sacrifice of Abel in the wilderness, of Noah upon the altar, of Abraham on the mountaintop, of Elijah on Mount Carmel, of David on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite, and the offering of the poor widow in the holy temple, likewise receive my offering and that of all your male and female servants who offer in your holy name, so that it may be redemption for my sins and theirs. And just as we offer, so repay us our reward in the present age, in the future age, and throughout ages of ages. Amen.

Prayer when wine and water are put into the chalice by the deacon.

[Col. 0911A]

Truly, Christ, our God and our Lord, who were invited to the wedding at Cana of Galilee, blessed it, and made wine from water: do likewise, and + bless, + sanctify, and + purify this wine in your sight. May it become rejoicing and life for our soul and body, and may the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit remain with us at all times, because we have no other gods besides you, Lord.

Therefore fill us with the wine of rejoicing, salvation, and joy, of life, understanding, and counsel of the Holy Spirit, throughout ages of ages. Amen.

+ Blessed is the Lord God, the almighty Father.

+ Blessed is the only-begotten Son, Jesus Christ, who was born of the Virgin Mary.

+ Blessed is the Paraclete Spirit, our God, through whom there is true strength for the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit throughout ages of ages. Amen.

Afterward he repeats the prayer over the chalice:

Lord our God, who accepted, etc., as above, in the offering of the host.

The priest says while singing and extending his palms upward, but in such a way that they do not rise above his head:

“One is the holy Father, one is the holy Son, and one is the Holy Spirit.”

The people respond:

Amen.

The priest says while singing:

“Praise the Lord, all nations; praise him, all peoples, for his mercy has been confirmed over us, and the truth of the Lord remains forever. Glory to the Father,” etc.

[Col. 0911C] The deacon says:

“Rise for prayer.”

The people:

“Lord, have mercy on us.”

The priest:

“Peace be with you.”

The people:

“And with your spirit.”

The priest, in thanksgiving, says the following prayer:

Let us give thanks to our benefactor, the merciful Lord, the Father of the Lord God and of our Redeemer Jesus Christ, because he protected us, helped us, guarded us, entrusted us to himself, drew us, embraced us, strengthened us, and brought us to this hour. Let us ask him also to guard us on this holy day, throughout the whole time of our life, and in complete peace, our almighty God.

The deacon says:

“Pray.”

[Col. 0911D] The priest continues:

“O Lord, Lord, good and almighty Father, Father of the Lord God and of our Redeemer Jesus Christ, we praise you above every work, for every work, and in every work, because you protected us, helped us, guarded us, and entrusted us to yourself; you drew us and embraced us; you strengthened us and brought us to this hour. We also ask and beseech your goodness, O lover of humankind.”

The deacon says:

“Ask and pray that the Lord may spare us, have mercy on us, and receive the prayer made for us by his saints; and that he may make us worthy to receive what he grants, and to partake of and receive his blessed sacrament, so that our sins may be forgiven.”

[Col. 0912A] The priest continues:

“That we may pass this holy day throughout the whole time of our life, in complete peace, with fear of you. Remove and drive far from me and from all your people, and from this your holy place, every envy, every temptation, every work of Satan, the counsel of wicked people, and the enemy’s hidden and manifest insults. Obtain for them every good thing, whatever in every respect grants benefit and help through us, because you are the one who gave us power to tread upon the serpent and the scorpion and every force of the enemy.

“Do not lead us, Lord, into temptation, but redeem and deliver us from every evil through the grace, mercy, and love for humankind of your only Son, [Col. 0912B] our Lord, God, and Redeemer Jesus Christ, with whom, together with the Holy Spirit, you possess glory and power, now and always and throughout ages of ages. Amen.”

For those offering gifts, the priest says:

“Again let us ask almighty God, the Father of the Lord, God and Redeemer Jesus Christ, for those who have offered gifts to the holy, unique Church, which is above all: namely, a sacrifice, a sign and memorial of the first tithes of thanksgiving. Whether someone has offered much or little, secretly or openly, willingly or while lacking the means, may the Lord, who gives the heavenly Spirit and in whom is the power of every good work, embrace the will of all.”

[Col. 0912C] Read this carefully, for if the word “Spirit” is in the nominative, he will say that the Son is of the Holy Spirit—that is, of the Father—and then the word “Spirit” will be understood essentially, as it is common to the three persons, not personally. But if it is in the oblique case, it is entirely certain that Christ, according to his divinity, cannot in any way be the Son of the Holy Spirit, unless the name “Holy Spirit” is understood essentially, namely as referring to the Father—which, nevertheless, is an unusual and alien expression. Nor, according to his humanity, do theologians teach that Christ can be called the son of the Holy Spirit. See Saint Thomas, part III, question 32, article 3.

The deacon says:

“Pray for those who have offered gifts.”

The priest:

“Lord, almighty God, we ask and beseech you for those who have offered gifts to the holy, unique Church, which is above all, whether they have offered much or little, secretly or openly, whether willing or lacking the means. Accepting the will of all, grant each of them, as a reward, blessing through your only Son, with whom you possess glory and power, together with the Holy Spirit, now and always and throughout ages of ages. Amen.”

Prayer of the sacred offering:

“O our prince, Jesus Christ, whose substance was not created but is pure Word; you are the Son of the Father and of the Holy Spirit. You are the bread of life, descending from heaven, who, before you came, were present in the figure of the immaculate Lamb for the redemption of the world.

“Now show your goodness over this bread and chalice on this portable altar. [Col. 0913A] + Bless, + sanctify, + cleanse, and transform this bread into your immaculate flesh, and this wine into your precious blood. May it become a burning and acceptable sacrifice, healing and salvation for our soul and body; for you are our King and our God Christ. We give thanks to you with all praise, reverence, and glory, with your heavenly Father and the life-giving Holy Spirit, now and always and throughout ages of ages. Amen.”

The deacon:

“Bend the knees.”

The people:

“Before you, Lord, we bend our knees and praise you.”

The priest’s assistant says what follows:

Lord, Lord, only-begotten Son, Jesus Christ, Word of God the Father, who by your life-giving and saving [Col. 0913B] passion have broken all the bonds of our sins, who breathed upon the face of your holy, undefiled ministers, the disciples, saying: “Receive the Holy Spirit: whose sins you forgive are forgiven them, and whose sins you retain are retained”; grant, Lord, that just as you granted them this priestly office of your holy Church, with power at all times to bind and absolve sins and the bonds of our iniquities, so we may implore your goodness and clemency, O lover of humankind, that they may absolve us your servants, and our parents, brothers, sisters, and friends, and me, a sinner, and all who bow their heads before your presence in this your holy sacrifice. Direct us, Lord, into the way of your mercy; break and shatter [Col. 0913C] all the bonds of our sins.

O Lord, whether knowingly or unknowingly, through malice of heart, frivolity of spirit, or the inclination and stain of the flesh, in deeds, words, and circumstances, we have sinned against you: spare us, Lord, for you know our frailty. O best Lord of all, and lover of humankind, grant us forgiveness of our sins. + Bless, + sanctify, + cleanse and make fragrant, and make us free and absolved. Absolve our pontiffs, princes, and kings; our patriarchs, archbishops, bishops, priests, deacons, and ministers, and your people, our parents and brothers. Remember, Lord, the princes, pontiffs, kings, patriarchs, archbishops, bishops, priests, deacons, and ministers who have fallen asleep, [Col. 0913D] our parents, and all who rest in the true faith; fill us with fear of your name, and direct us to do your will. To you be glory and honor, because you alone are worthy of these things, forever and ever. Amen.

May your servants ministering today—the priest, the deacon, and all the ministers, the people, and I, your poor servant and sinner—be absolved through the mouth of the Trinity, the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, and of blessed Mary of the second heaven, Mother of God; through the mouth of Michael, Gabriel, and all the archangels, and of the ninety-nine orders of angels, and of the thousands upon thousands of ministers whose names we do not know how to count; and of the four living creatures, and the twenty-four elders, and the first [Col. 0914A] holy fathers; and of the fifteen prophets and their twelve sons; and through the mouth of the twelve apostles, and of Saint James, bishop of Jerusalem, and of Saints Paul, Timothy, Silas, Barnabas, Titus, Philemon, Clement, and all the seventy-two disciples and their five hundred companions; and through the mouth of Saint Mark, who proclaimed the divinity, and of the other evangelists; and through the mouth of the three hundred and eighteen bishops who assembled for the true faith at the Council of Nicaea, and of the one hundred and fifty at Constantinople, and of the two hundred at the Council of Ephesus; and through the mouth of our pontiff Saviros, John Chrysostom, “golden-mouthed,” Cyril, Basil, Theophilus, Athanasius, Gregory, and our pontiffs Matthew, Gabriel, John, Salama, [Col. 0914B] Bartholomew, Isaac, and Marcius; and through the mouth of the one Church that was gathered by the holy apostles; and through me, a sinner. May you be absolved and filled with grace, to the glory and honor of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. Amen.

Here the priest declares the epact, the golden number, the movable and immovable feasts, indulgences, and all the rites and ceremonies from beginning to end; he offers incense in memory of the living and the dead, and continues this prayer by placing incense three times in the censer, saying:

+ Blessed is the almighty Father. + Blessed is the only-begotten Son, Jesus Christ. + Blessed is the Paraclete Spirit, to whom belong honor and glory, now and always. Amen.

[Col. 0914C] Then, censing all around the altar, he says:

Alleluia to the Father, alleluia to the Son, alleluia to the Holy Spirit, now and always, and forever and ever. Amen.

+ O God, you are eternal; you are before and after, lacking beginning and end, great in providence, powerful in action, and wise in counsel; all these things are shown in all things. We pray and earnestly beseech you, Lord, that on this day you remain with us and show your face upon us; dwell with us, blot out our sins and iniquities, which we have committed willingly and unwillingly, knowingly and unknowingly; cleanse our heart and sanctify our soul. Permit us to draw near to you. May the offering, the sacrifice of thanksgiving, and the spiritual incense enter and ascend into [Col. 0914D] the presence of your holiness.

While censing the altar, he says the prayer:

Remember, Lord, your one holy apostolic Church and your congregation, which you possessed from the beginning. Remember, Lord, our prince, N., and our venerable fathers, the patriarchs, archbishops, bishops, priests, deacons, and all who profess the apostolic faith. Remember, Lord, our king, N., and all Christian kings, our parents, your male and female servants, and all the faithful brothers and sisters who have fallen asleep and rest in the sign of the true faith. Remember, Lord, our congregations, and bless them.

[Col. 0915A] The deacon says: “Rise for prayer.”

The priest: “Peace be with you.”

The people: “And with your spirit.”

The priest continues in a loud voice, three times: “We adore the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, three and one.”

The people repeat the same three times.

The priest continues: “Peace to you, holy Church, dwelling of peace. Hail, Virgin Mary, Mother of God; you are the golden censer who carried the burning coal. Blessed is he who receives it from the sanctuary, for he himself is truly the Word of God, who forgives sins and blots out guilt; he became human from you and offered himself to the Father as true incense and a precious sacrifice. We adore you, Christ, with your best and merciful Father and your life-giving Spirit, because you came and freed [Col. 0915B] us.”

The people repeat the same.

Afterward the priest’s assistant continues the prayer:

Lord of understanding, and announcer of the wisdom that had previously been hidden from us, you made it manifest. Lord, giver of the word of exultation and joy, to those proclaiming the magnificence of your power. You are the one who, through the multitude of your goodness, called Paul, who had previously been a persecutor of the Church; you appointed him a chosen Vessel of your kingdom and chose him as apostle and preacher of the Gospel, and as herald of your kingdom.

O Christ, our God, best lover of humankind, we ask you to grant us wisdom, understanding, knowledge, and discernment, which may always remain with us, so that we may be wise, understand, know, and perceive the Scripture of your holiness that is read in your presence. Just as you gave this gift to Paul and made him worthy of such grace, so, we ask, make us also worthy, O source of life, to imitate him, walk in his way, follow his footsteps, praise your holy name, and glory at all times in your cross, just as he himself always gloried. To you belong power, kingdom, triumph, magnificence, honor, and glory, forever and ever. Amen.

Before the Epistle is read, the deacon says: “Let all who do not love our Lord, and who do not in the least believe in his birth, and in holy Mary the Virgin, be anathema until his coming.”

Then the Epistle of Paul that occurs according to the day is read, and [Col. 0915D] likewise according to the day being observed. When the Epistle has been read, the deacon says:

“May the glory of the Father, the love of the Son, and the gift of the Holy Spirit, which descended upon the blessed and pure apostles in the holy place of Zion, be doubled upon us Christians, forever and ever. Amen.”

The people: “O good minister, holy Paul, healer of the sick, who received the crown, pray and intercede for us, that our soul may be freed through the multitude of the mercies of Jesus Christ and of his holy name.”

The deacon says: “Rise for prayer.”

The people: “Lord, have mercy on us.”

The priest: “Peace be with you.”

[Col. 0916A] The people: “And with your spirit.”

The priest continues the prayer marked with the sign + as above, beginning: “O God, you are eternal,” and so forth.

Before the Epistle, the minister or subdeacon says: “From the Epistle of Peter, or of another apostle: disciple and apostle of the Lord and of our Savior Jesus Christ, whose prayer and blessing may always be upon us. Amen.”

Then he reads the Epistle in a loud voice.

When the Epistle has been completed and read, the deacon continues:

“My brothers, do not love the world, nor the things that are in the world, because everything that is in the world is the desire of the flesh, the desire of the eyes, and the pride of life; which is not from the Father but from the world. And the world passes away, and its desire [Col. 0916B] as well. But whoever does his will remains forever.”

The people say: “Holy, three and one in your substance, guard our congregation for the sake of your holy elect and your disciples; console us through your mercy and for the sake of your holy name.”

The deacon says: “Rise for prayer.”

The people: “Lord, have mercy on us.”

The priest: “Peace be with you.”

The people: “And with your spirit.”

The priest: “Lord, our Lord and our God, you are the one who revealed to your holy apostles the mystery of the glory of your Christ and gave them great and innumerable gifts, the riches and hidden things of your mercy; you sent them to preach. Be gracious, Lord, and deign to grant that we may become participants and companions in their inheritance, and walk and follow in their footsteps. Grant, we ask, that we may at all times be like them, be strengthened in their love, and share in their labors. Guard, Lord, the holy Christian Church in good worship, which was built and founded through the holy apostles.”

The priest continues toward the people:

+ Bless your flock and your lambs. Increase, Lord, this vine of grapes, which you planted through your holy hands, through our Lord Jesus Christ; to him, to you, and to the Holy Spirit belong glory and power, now and always, and forever and ever. [Col. 0916D] Amen.

Here the priest places incense in the censer, saying:

Lord our God, who accepted the sacrifice of Abraham our father and caused a lamb to descend in place of, and for the salvation of, his son Isaac: so, Lord, accept the fragrance of this incense; and just as you received the sacrifice of that lamb, so, Lord, send the riches of your grace and mercy. Make us pure and clean from all evil odors of sins, and worthy of your power and majesty in praise of your purity. O lover of humankind, make us righteous and without blemish, with joy, all the days of our life.

He continues: “Remember, Lord, your one holy Church, which from end to end, throughout the whole world, [Col. 0917A] was gathered in your apostles. Rejoice, Lady, for we beseech holy salvation. O Virgin, Mother of God and of Christ, raise our prayer continually on high before the elect of your Son, that our sins may be forgiven. Rejoice, Lady, for you bore for us the true light, Jesus Christ, our Lord. Pray for us before him, that he may have mercy on our soul; pray for us in the presence of the throne of your Son, Jesus Christ. Rejoice, Immaculate One, true Queen. Rejoice, Glory of our fathers, for you bore Emmanuel for us. O true mediatrix before our Lord Jesus Christ, we earnestly beseech you to remember us. Pray for us, that our iniquities may be blotted out.”

The priest’s assistant, before the Acts of the Apostles are read, says: [Col. 0917B] “This is the work and sayings of our fathers, the holy and undefiled apostles. May the grace of the Holy Spirit and mercy be doubled upon us and upon all Christians. Amen.”

Afterward a passage from the Acts of the Apostles is read, according to the day being observed. When the reading is finished, the following is said:

“The great words of the Lord, multiplied in the holy Church, multiplied the peoples who believed in the Lord Jesus Christ, to whom be glory forever and ever.”

The people respond: “Amen.”

Then follows: “Holy, holy, holy, the Lord almighty Father. Holy, holy, holy, the only-begotten Jesus Christ, the Son, the Word of the Father. Holy, holy, holy, the Holy Spirit, who knows [Col. 0917C] all things.”

The deacon says: “Rise for prayer.”

The people: “Lord, have mercy on us.”

The priest: “Peace be with you.”

The people: “And with your spirit.”

The priest: “Lord our God, Jesus Christ, you said to your holy and elect disciples: ‘Many prophets and righteous people desired to see what you see and to hear what you hear, and they did not see or hear it; but blessed are your eyes and your ears, seeing and hearing.’ So make us worthy to hear and do the words of your holy Gospel, through the prayers and supplications of your saints.”

The deacon says: “Pray.”

The priest continues: “Remember again, Lord, [Col. 0917D] your words, for those who have commended themselves to our prayers when we pray to you. Lord our God, remember those who have fallen asleep and rest in the true faith; grant health to the sick, for you are the life, hope, deliverer, and resurrection of all. We give you thanks forever and ever. Amen.”

The deacon, taking the cross, says:

“Pray that you may be made worthy to hear the Gospel.”

Then he sings: “I will bless the Lord at all times; his praise is always in my mouth. In the Lord my soul shall be praised,” and so forth.

The priest says the same; the people say the same three times; and in the final verse “Alleluia” is always said.

[Col. 0918A] The deacon goes around the church, crying out: “Rise; hear the holy Gospel and the good announcement of our Lord and our Savior Jesus Christ.”

Afterward the assistant takes the censer and presents it to the priest, who censes three times while receiving the Gospel facing the people, and says:

“Great God, bless + us and the Christian people, and make our entrance into your holy church together with the holy angels who serve God and praise him at all times, forever and ever. Amen.”

The priest announces the Gospel, singing as follows:

“The Holy Gospel announced by Matthew,” or “by Mark,” or “by Luke,” or “by John.”

The ministers light the lamps and prepare the other necessities, [Col. 0918B] and say:

“Glory always to Christ, our Lord and our God; rejoice in the Lord, who helps us, and sing praise to the God of Jacob; take up the psalter with the lyre,” and so forth.

The priest reads the Gospel of the day in a loud voice. When the Gospel is finished, the deacon says:

“Go outside, you who do not wish to receive the sacrament, that is, the Eucharist. Depart, catechumens.”

The ministers say: “And may they, the Cherubim and Seraphim, render glory: Holy, holy, holy, and holy Omnipotent One. The heavens and the earth are full of your glory and holiness. We adore you, Christ, with your best and merciful Father and your life-giving Holy Spirit; you came and freed us.”

[Col. 0918C] The deacon says: “Rise for prayer.”

The people: “Lord, have mercy on us.”

The priest: “Peace be with you.”

The people: “And with your spirit.”

The deacon says: “Rise for prayer.”

The priest says: “Peace be with all of you. And again let us beseech almighty God, the Father of our Lord and God and Savior Jesus Christ. We ask and entreat your goodness, O lover of humankind: remember, Lord, the peace of the holy Church gathered into one through the apostles.”

The deacon says: “Pray for this holy Church, gathered into one through the apostles, upright in the Lord.”

The people say: “Lord our God, give us [Col. 0918D] peace; Lord our God, give us peace; Christ our King, have mercy on us.”

The priest says:

“Bless the Church that was from the beginning and will remain until the end of the age, all peoples and all flocks. Send peace from heaven upon all our souls; grant us the peace of our life through this Church itself. Give, Lord, peace to our king, N., and to his princes, his judges, and his subjects, and to those gathered around us, both outside and within the Church. Adorn them with every kind of peace, O King of peace; give us peace, for you have given us all things. Preserve us, Lord, for apart from you we know no one; we name and invoke your holy name, so that our soul may live in the Holy Spirit [Col. 0919A] and the death of sin may not prevail over us, your servants, and over all your people.”

For the pontiffs.

“And again let us beseech almighty God, the Father of our Lord and God and Savior Jesus Christ. We ask and entreat your goodness, O lover of humankind: remember, Lord, our revered father, the prince of our archbishops, N., and our holy and blessed hierarch, N.”

The deacon says: “Pray for our prince, the prince of our archbishops, N., and head of the bishops of the great province of Alexandria; for the head of our homeland, our revered archbishop, N., and for all bishops, priests, and deacons of the true faith.”

[Col. 0919B] The priest says: “Guard them carefully for us for many years and a long time, in justice and peace, so that they may complete the consecration which you entrusted to the priestly dignity, according to your holy and blessed will; so that they may judge in justice and righteousness and feed your peoples in equity. Guard carefully also all bishops, priests, and deacons of the true faith, and all who conform to the holy and one Church that is the apostolic congregation. Accept the prayers that they make for us and for all your peoples as a sacrifice to your most high offering, in a fragrant odor of sweetness; scatter all their enemies and adversaries and swiftly crush them beneath their feet. Guard them for us in justice and peace in your holy Church.”

For those gathered.

[Col. 0919C]

The priest says: “And again let us beseech almighty God, the Father of our Lord and God and Savior Jesus Christ. We seek and ask from your goodness, O lover of humankind: remember, Lord, our congregation, and bless it.”

The deacon says: “Pray for this holy church and for our congregation that is in it.”

The people say: “Bless our congregation and guard it in peace.”

The deacon says: “In the wisdom of the Lord, speak and sing the prayer of faith.”

The people say: “I believe in one God, the almighty Father, maker of heaven and earth, of all things visible and invisible. And in one Lord Jesus [Col. 0919D] Christ, the only-begotten Son of God, born of the Father before all ages; God from God, light from light, true God from true God; begotten, not made, consubstantial with the Father, through whom all things were made. For us human beings and for our salvation he descended from heaven. And he was incarnate from the Holy Spirit and the Virgin Mary, and became human. He was also crucified for us under Pontius Pilate; he suffered and was buried. And he rose again on the third day according to the Scriptures. And he ascended into heaven and sits at the right hand of the Father. And he will come again in glory to judge the living and the dead, and his kingdom will have no end. And in the Holy Spirit, the Lord and giver of life, who proceeds from the Father and the Son. Who together with the Father and the Son is worshiped and glorified. Who spoke through the prophets. And in one holy catholic and apostolic Church. I confess one baptism for the remission of sins; and I await the resurrection of the dead and the life of the age to come. Amen.”

The priest says: “Make them undivided for you, and make them carry out your holy and blessed will without sluggishness. Make them a house of prayer, a house of purity, a house of abundance and grace; graciously favor us, Lord, your servants, and those who will come after us forever. Arise, Lord our God, and let your enemies be scattered; let all who hate your holy and blessed name flee before your face. May your peoples be blessed a thousand times a thousand, [Col. 0920B] and again a thousand times a thousand blessings, and may they do all your will, through the grace, kindness, and love for humankind of your only-begotten Son, the Lord God and our Savior Jesus Christ; to him, to you, and to the Holy Spirit be glory and power, now and always, and forever and ever. Amen.”

Prayer for perfect peace; the priest says:

“The great and eternal Lord created the human being immaculate and incorruptible. But death entered the world from the beginning through the envy of the devil. You, Lord, deprived it of its power through the coming of your only-begotten Son, the Lord God and our Savior Jesus Christ, and filled the whole earth with your peace. Therefore the heavenly armies praise you, saying: ‘Glory to the Lord [Col. 0920C] in the heavens, and peace on earth to people of good will.’”
