The deacon says: “Pray for perfect, lovable, salutary, and apostolic peace. Greet one another. Those who do not wish to communicate, depart. But those who wish to communicate, embrace one another with a full heart. Let the communicant guard himself from evil.”

The priest says: “O Lord, by your good pleasure fill our hearts with your peace, and cleanse us from every evil thought and impurity, from every memory of injuries, from every envy, and from remembrance of evils, which bring death. O Lord, make us wholly worthy to greet one another with a holy and undefiled greeting, and to receive without judgment and [Col. 0920D] without death your heavenly gift, that is, your grace with the Holy Spirit.”

The people say: “Christ, our God, make us worthy to greet you with a heavenly greeting and to praise you together with the Cherubim and Seraphim, saying: ‘Holy, holy, holy, Omnipotent One. The heavens and the earth are full of the holiness of your glory.’”

The priest says: “The Lord be with you, holy among the holy, holy among the holy, holy among the holy. We give you thanks, Lord, through your beloved only-begotten Son, the Lord God and our Savior Jesus Christ, whom in the latter time you sent to us as your Son, Savior and Redeemer, messenger of your counsel, who is your Word [Col. 0921A] and through whom you made all things according to your will.”

The deacon says: “Through our blessed and holy patriarch, N., and through our venerable hierarch, N., who praise you with their prayers and supplications; through Stephen the protomartyr, Zechariah the priest, and John the Baptist; through all the holy martyrs who have rested in the faith of Jesus Christ; through Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John the evangelists; through Mary, Mother of God; through Simon Peter, Andrew, James, John, Philip, Bartholomew, Thomas, Matthew, Thaddeus, Nathanael, James of Alphaeus [Note: The Ethiopians believe that in this liturgy James of Alphaeus was a different apostle from James the brother of the Lord.], and Matthias the apostles; through James the apostle, brother of our Lord and bishop of holy Jerusalem; through Paul, Timothy, Silas, [Col. 0921B] Barnabas, Titus, Philemon, Clement; and through the seventy-two disciples and their five hundred companions; and through the three hundred and eighteen fathers of the true faith, visit us and make us participants in all their prayers. And above all, remember the catholic and apostolic Church, built in peace through Christ’s precious blood. Remember also all the patriarchs, archbishops, bishops, priests, and deacons who direct the way of the word that is in truth.”

The people say: “Have mercy, Lord, on the souls of your male and female servants who have eaten your flesh and drunk your blood, and have rested in your faith.”

Prayer of blessing.

[Col. 0921C] The priest says: “O holy Trinity, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, bless your chosen Christian people with a heavenly blessing, and send upon us the grace of the Holy Spirit. Open for us the doors of your holy Church, because of your mercy and our faith. Perfect in us the faith of the Trinity until our final breath, O our prince, Jesus Christ. Visit your sick people and heal them. Direct our fathers and brothers who are traveling; bring them back to their homes in health and peace. Bless the winds of heaven, the rains, and the fruits of the earth in this present year through your grace. Always grant joy and delights upon the face of the earth, and strengthen your peace upon us. Incline the hearts of good kings to do good to us; graciously grant honor to the princes of the holy Church, each of them according to his name; make them pleasing in the sight of powerful kings. O Lord, grant rest to the souls of our fathers and brothers who sleep and rest in the true faith, and bless those who labor with incense, sacrifices, wine, oil, butter, curtains, books, and seats, and with all the things of the holy Church, so that Jesus Christ our God may reward them in the heavenly Jerusalem. Have mercy on all who have gathered with us to seek the mercy of our God Jesus Christ, and be gentle and gracious at your judgment seat toward all those who have given us alms. Deliver, Lord, through the multitude of your mercy, all needy and afflicted souls, and those imprisoned, captive, exiled, driven into slavery, and detained in bitter labors. Remember, our Lord Jesus Christ, in the kingdom of heaven, all those who asked us to remember them. O Lord, deliver your people and bless your inheritance; nourish it and exalt it forever. Guard them in the true faith and in glory at all times, and make them burn with ineffable and inconceivable charity, through the prayers and intercession made for us by our Lady, the holy and immaculate Virgin Mary; and through the prayers of the radiant chief angels, Michael, [Col. 0922B] Gabriel, Raphael, and Uriel; and of the four bodiless living creatures; and of the twenty-four elders of heaven; and of our holy fathers, the patriarchs Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; and of all the righteous fathers of old; and of our fifteen prophetic fathers; and of Saint John the Baptist; and of the fourteen thousand children of Bethlehem; and of our fathers, the twelve chief apostles; and of the seventy-two disciples and their five hundred companions; and of the three children, Hananiah, Azariah, and Mishael; and of Saint Mark the evangelist and martyr; and of Saint Stephen the archdeacon and protomartyr; and of Saint George, star of honor; Theodore, Banadlius, Claudius, Minas the elect, Cosmas, and Damian; and of our fathers, the chief bishops, the three hundred [Col. 0922C] and eighteen who were at Nicaea, the one hundred and fifty who were at Constantinople, and the two hundred who were at Ephesus; and of Tecla Aimanor. May their prayers, blessings, help, and grace be with us forever and ever. Amen. Grant rest to the souls of all these and all those others, and have mercy on them, for it was for this reason that you sent your Son from heaven into the Virgin’s womb.”

The deacon says: “You who are seated, rise.”

The priest says: “In him he was carried, became flesh, and was made known through the Holy Spirit at his birth.”

The deacon says: “Look toward the east.”

The priest says: “Before you stand thousands upon thousands of holy angels and their princes.”

[Col. 0922D] The deacon says: “Let us look.”

The priest says: “The honored living creatures also, having six wings, the Seraphim and Cherubim, cover their faces with two of their wings and their feet with two; with the other two they fly from the end of the world to its end. Just as they always sanctify and praise you, so may you receive our sanctification from us, who continually say: ‘Holy.’”

The deacon says: “Say it.”

The people say: “Holy, holy, holy, Lord Sabaoth. The heavens and the earth are perfectly full of the holiness of your glory.”

[Col. 0923A] The priest says: “Truly the heavens and the earth are full of the holiness of your glory, through the Lord and our Savior Jesus Christ, with the Holy Spirit, forever and ever. Amen. Your holy Son came from the Virgin to fulfill your will and establish a holy people for you.”

The people say: “According to your mercy, Lord, and not according to our sins.”

The priest says: “He stretched out his hands toward weakness. He became weak in order to heal those who are weak and hope in him. He was also handed over by his own will to weakness, in order to destroy death, dissolve the bonds of the devil, trample hell, guide the righteous, establish order, and manifest his resurrection. On the night on which he was handed over, he took bread in his holy, blessed, and undefiled hands, looked up to heaven toward you, his Father, gave thanks, blessed and sanctified it, and gave it to his disciples, saying: ‘Take and eat from it, all of you: this is my body, which will be handed over for you for the remission of sins.’ Amen.”

The people say: “Amen, amen, amen. We believe, trust, and praise you, O Lord our God. This is truly your body.”

The priest says: “Likewise, giving thanks, he blessed and sanctified the cup and said to them: ‘Take and drink from it, all of you: this is the cup of my blood, which will be poured out for you and for the redemption of many.’ Amen.”

[Col. 0923C] The people say: “Amen, amen, amen. We believe, trust, and praise you, O Lord our God. This is truly your blood.”

The priest says: “Whenever you do this, you will do it in remembrance of me.”

The people say: “We proclaim your death, Lord, and your holy resurrection; we believe your ascension and your second coming. We beseech you, Lord our God; we believe that these things are true.”

The priest says: “Now, remembering your death and your resurrection, we offer you this bread and this cup, and we give you thanks because through this sacrifice you have made us worthy to stand in your presence and perform the priestly office before you. [Col. 0923D] We pray to you, Lord, and earnestly ask you to send the Holy Spirit upon this bread and this cup, namely, the body and blood of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, forever and ever. Amen. Grant also to all who partake of it that it may become for them sanctification and fullness of the Holy Spirit and strengthening of faith, so that they may sanctify and praise you, through our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ with the Holy Spirit, forever and ever. Amen.”

The deacon says: “We beseech you, Lord our God, with our whole heart, to give us a good union of the Holy Spirit.”

The priest continues: “Grant us that we may be united in [Col. 0924A] your Holy Spirit, and heal us through this sacrifice, so that we may be saved in you, forever and ever. Amen.”

“Blessed be the name of the Lord, and blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord, and blessed is the name of his glory. Let it be, let it be, let it be.”

The people say: “Blessed be the name of the Lord, and blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord, and blessed is the name of his glory. Let it be, let it be, let it be.”

The priest says: “Send the grace of the Holy Spirit upon us, Lord.”

The deacon says: “Rise for prayer.”

The priest says the prayer over the fragment:

“I confess to you, Lord, my almighty God, who sit upon the throne of the Cherubim and dwell on high, and are praised by the humble; while existing in splendor, you knew the world and revealed to us the hidden mystery on the cross. What merciful and holy God is like you? Your power has not been removed far from us; you gave it to your disciples, who serve you with a pure and sincere heart and offer you a sacrifice of sweet fragrance, through our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, to whom, and to you, and to the Holy Spirit be grace, honor, and glory, forever and ever.”

The deacon says: “You who are standing, bow your heads.”

The priest says: “Lord, who dwell upon the Cherubim and look upon your people and your inheritance, bless your male and female servants and [Col. 0924C] their children. Grant a portion to those who come to receive from your miraculous table, for the cleansing of their minds, the remission of sins, the union of the Holy Spirit, the salvation of soul and body, and the inheritance of the heavenly kingdom, with honor and according to your will, through your only-begotten Son, to whom, and to you with him, and to the Holy Spirit be praise and glory, now and always, and forever and ever. Amen.”

The subdeacon says with the people: “The armies of the angels of the Savior of the world stand before him and read the body and blood of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. Let us approach before his presence and revere him in faith.”

The deacon says: “Worship God with fear.”

The priest says:

“O Lord God Almighty, salvation of our soul and body, who through the mouth of your only-begotten Son, the Lord God and our Savior Jesus Christ, said to our father Peter: ‘You are Peter, and upon this rock I will build my Church, and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it or shake it; and I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven. Whatever you bind on earth shall be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven’—may your servants and handmaids be loosed by the mouth of the holy Trinity, of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, and also by my mouth, your sinful servant, full of transgressions.

“Lord our God, you take away the sins of the world: receive the repentance of your servants and handmaids. Cause the light of life to rise upon them. Remove their sins from them, for you are merciful and compassionate, O Lord our God, far removed from anger, abounding in mercy, and truly just. Whenever we sin against you, Lord, whether in thought, word, or deed, spare us, remove it, and have compassion, for you are merciful and the lover of humanity.

“Lord our God, loose us all, and all your peoples. Loose, O Lord, our supreme pontiff N., and our holy and blessed bishop N., and all the other pontiffs, bishops, priests, and deacons; keeping them according to their names, preserve them because of us for many years and long days, in righteousness and peace. Loose, O Lord, our king N., from every bond of transgression.

“Remember, O Lord, all who sleep and rest in the faith of Christ; [Col. 0925B] place their souls in the bosom of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Deliver us from all transgressions and curses, from every denial of the truth, from every perjury, and from communion with unbelievers, Gentiles, and heretics. Give us a heart and understanding to flee from all the works of the devil. Grant us to do your will at all times, and inscribe our names in the kingdoms of heaven; unite us with all the saints and martyrs, through Jesus Christ our Lord, to whom, and to you, and to the Holy Spirit, be glory and power, now and always, and for ages of ages. Amen.”

The deacon says: “Let us look.”

The priest says: “Give the holy things to the holy.”

The people say: “One is the holy Father, one is the holy Son, one is the Holy Spirit.”

The priest says: “May the Lord be with you.”

The people say: “And with your spirit.”

The priest, raising the sacrament, says in a loud voice:

“Lord Jesus Christ, have mercy on us; Lord Jesus Christ, have mercy on us; Lord Jesus Christ, have mercy on us.”

The people repeat the same words.

The priest says: “Let us pray, you who are penitent. Bow your heads. Rise to adore. Peace be with you all.”

The people say: “And with your spirit.”

The priest says:

“This is the holy, honored, and life-giving body of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, which has been given for the remission of sins and [Col. 0925D] for the attainment of eternal life by those who truly receive it. Amen.

“This is the holy, honored, and life-giving blood of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, which has been given for the remission of sins and for the attainment of eternal life by those who truly receive it. Amen.

“Truly, this is the body, and this is the blood of Emmanuel, our God. Amen.

“I believe, I believe, I believe, from this time and forever. Amen.

“This is the body, and this is the blood of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, which he assumed from our holy and immaculate Lady, the Virgin Mary, and united with his divinity without mixture or natural conjunction, without separation or alteration of the divinity—a matter which he confirmed with the strongest testimony, [Col. 0926A] in the time of Pontius Pilate, when he willingly offered himself for us upon the holy wood of the cross. Amen.

“I believe, I believe, I believe that the divinity was not separated from the humanity, not even for an hour or for the blink of an eye; rather, he gave himself for us for salvation and for the remission of sins, and for the attainment of eternal life by those who truly receive him. Amen.

“I believe, I believe, I believe, from this time and forever. Amen.

“These things belong to him who is worthy of honor, glory, and reverence.”

Here the priest receives the body and blood, and afterward communicates the ministers of the sacrifice from the same host, saying: “This is the body,” and so forth.

The deacon says:

“Pray for us and for all Christian peoples, and make remembrance of those who told us to remember them. Praise and sing psalms in the peace and love of Jesus Christ.”

At this point, while the sacrament is being administered to the people, the learned sing various hymns composed in honor of the sacrament and of the saints whose feasts are being celebrated. The people repeat them in song.

The priest says:

“Those whom you have called, O Lord, and whom you have sanctified, grant them a portion in your calling; strengthen them in your love, and preserve them in your sanctification, through Christ, your only Son, to whom, and to you with him, and to the Holy Spirit, be glory and honor, now and always, and for ages of ages. Amen.

“O Lord, who have granted your servants the eternal light of life and strength, and have preserved them through many days and nights that have passed in peace, bless them also on this day, after our Lord Jesus Christ, to whom, and to you with him, and to the Holy Spirit, be glory and honor, now and always, and for ages of ages. Amen.”

The deacon says:

“Let us give thanks to the Lord. We have received his holy offering; may what we have received be a remedy for giving life to the soul. Let us praise the Lord our God. We have received the holy body and venerable blood; this is the body of Christ. Let us also give him thanks, because we have been found worthy to share in this venerable and holy mystery.”

The priest says:

“I will exalt you, my king and my God, and I will bless your name forever and unto the age of ages.”

The people say in a loud voice:

“Our Father, who are in [Col. 0926D] heaven, do not lead us, Lord, into temptation.”

The priest says:

“Every day I will bless you, and I will praise your name forever and unto the age of ages.”

The people again say:

“Our Father, who are in heaven, do not lead us into temptation.”

The priest says:

“My mouth shall speak the praise of the Lord, and all flesh shall bless his holy name forever and unto the age of ages.”

The people again say:

“Our Father, and so forth, as above.”

The priest says:

“O Lord, guide of souls, director of the holy, and honor of the righteous, give us eyes of understanding that may always see you, and ears that may always hear you alone, after you have satisfied our soul [Col. 0927A] with your grace. Create in us a clean heart, O Lord, so that we may understand your greatness and goodness and your love toward humanity. Let your will be done upon our soul, and grant us a pure and upright mind, who have received from your body and your blood, your humble servants, for yours is the kingdom, O Lord. Glory and blessing be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and always, and for ages of ages. Amen.”

The priest says:

“O Lord our God, unquenchable light, look upon your servants and your handmaids, and sow in our hearts fear of your name. Number those to whom your body and your blood have been given, so that they may bear fruit in blessing. Cause yourself to dwell among those of your people who bow their heads before you, both men and women and children, and join us also to them. Protect, cherish, and guide us through the powers of your angelic princes. Separate us from all evil works and join us to every good work, through Christ your only Son, to whom, and to you with him and the Holy Spirit, be glory and honor, now and always, and for ages of ages. Amen.”

The whole people say while eating:

“Holy, holy, holy, thrice-holy, ineffable One, grant us to receive life through this your body, without judgment. Grant us to bear fruit according to your good pleasure, and may our fruit [Col. 0928A] be manifested in your glory. Give us life in you, so that we may do your will. With faith we call upon you, Father, and we ask for your kingdom. May your name be sanctified upon us, for you are strong, praiseworthy, and glorious. To you be glory for ages of ages.”

The deacon says:

“Bow your heads before the immortal Lord, so that he may bless you through the hand of his servant, the priest.”

The people say:

“Amen. May the Lord bless us, his servants. May forgiveness be upon us in peace, who have received the holy body and precious blood. Grant us that, in spirit, we may trample underfoot every power of the enemy. The blessing of your holy hand is full of mercy; in it we all hope. Separate us from all evil works, [Col. 0928B] and place us among all good works. Blessed is he who has given us his holy body and precious blood. We have received grace and found life through the power of the cross of Jesus Christ. We give you thanks when we have received the grace of the Holy Spirit. Glory be to the Lord, who has given us his holy body and precious blood. Glory be to the divine Mary, who is our glory and who gave birth to the sacrifice for us.”

End of the canon of our fathers, the apostles; may their prayer and blessing be with us. Amen.

[Col. 0927]

# BLESSING OF THE WOMAN AFTER CHILDBIRTH According to the Usage of the Ethiopians

[Col. 0927C] IN THE NAME OF THE FATHER, AND OF THE SON, AND OF THE HOLY SPIRIT. AMEN.

Prayers said by the priest as he lays his hands upon the mother and the infant, after they have entered the church.

First the priest exhorts the people to give thanks to God, saying:

“Let us give thanks to our benefactor, the merciful Lord, the Father of the Lord God and of our Redeemer Jesus Christ, because he has protected us, helped us, guarded us, entrusted us to himself, drawn us, embraced us, strengthened us, and brought us to this hour. Let us also ask him to guard us on this holy day and at all times of our life, in complete peace, O almighty Lord our God.”

The deacon says: “Pray.”

The priest says:

“O Lord, O Lord, good and almighty Father, Father of the Lord God and of our Redeemer Jesus Christ, we praise you above every work, for every work, and in every work, because you have protected us and helped us, guarded us, entrusted us to yourself, drawn us, and embraced [Col. 0928C] us, strengthened us, and brought us to this hour. We also ask and seek from your goodness, O lover of humanity—”

Here the deacon says:

“Ask and pray that the Lord may spare us, have mercy upon us, receive the prayer made for us by his saints, and make us worthy to receive what he grants and to partake of and receive his blessed sacrament, so that our sins may be forgiven.”

The priest continues:

“Grant us to pass this holy day and the whole time of our life in complete peace and with your fear. Remove and drive far from me, from all your people, and from this your holy place, every envy, every temptation, every work of Satan, the counsel of evil men, and the enemy’s hidden and manifest insults. Command every good thing—the whole of whatever grants and helps—through us, because you are the one who has given us power to tread upon the serpent and the scorpion and every hostile force. Do not lead us, Lord, into temptation, but redeem and deliver us from every evil, through the grace, mercy, and love for humanity of your only Son, the Lord God and our Redeemer Jesus Christ, with whom, together with the Holy Spirit, you possess glory and power, now and always, and for ages of ages. Amen.”

Afterward the priest offers incense and says this prayer:

“O Lord our God, almighty Father of the Lord God and of our Redeemer Jesus Christ, creator of the ages, who fashioned our birth; you, Lord, appointed Moses your servant in your law and taught him the pure ordinance appropriate to every woman who has given birth: namely, that she should be separated for a short time. You commanded her not to approach your holy things, but to remain apart until she was freed. Thus we also ask your goodness and beseech you on behalf of your servant N., who has observed your ordinance and desires to enter your holy tabernacle, to adore before your holy altar [Col. 0929B] and desires to receive your holy and life-giving sacrament. We ask, then, your goodness, O lover of humanity: bless your servant N. at this hour and deliver her from every malignant impurity that drives her away from your holy royal dwelling, and grant that she may receive from your holy sacrament.

“Bless, sanctify, and strengthen also this little infant, Lord, who has been born from her. Give [Col. 0930A] him strength, protect him, and bring him to the goal of his age. May he become one who fears you and grow in your holy will. Guard and strengthen him in right faith, hope, peace, and your charity, through your only Son Jesus Christ our Lord, with whom, together with the Holy Spirit, glory and thanksgiving are fitting for you, for ages of ages. Amen.”

The priest anoints the foreheads of both the woman and the infant with holy anointing, and says the following prayer of the laying on of hands:

“O Lord, O Lord, good Father, our God, we have laid our hands upon the heads of your servants as a crown of honor and glory. Amen. A crown of faith and beauty. Amen. A crown of righteousness, which the enemy cannot conquer. Amen. Make your servants full of the grace of the Holy Spirit, through the mercy and propitiation of the lover of humanity, your Son Jesus Christ; for to you, and to him, together with the Holy Spirit, belong glory and power, for ages of ages. Amen.”

Afterward the mother receives the holy sacrament of the Eucharist.

End of the blessing of the woman after childbirth.

[Col. 0929]

# ORDER OF BAPTISM ACCORDING TO THE USAGE OF THE ETHIOPIANS

[Col. 0929C] IN THE NAME OF THE FATHER, AND OF THE SON, AND OF THE HOLY SPIRIT. AMEN.

Prayers said in holy baptism.

First the priest says Psalm Fifty, namely:

“Have mercy on me, O God, according to your great mercy,” to the end.

He offers incense, asks the names of those who are to be baptized, and prays over them.

The deacon says: “Pray.”

The priest says:

“Our Lord Jesus Christ, who bowed down and descended to earth, whose word cleaves rocks and is sharper than a sword, whose presence disturbed the waters and drove them backward: heal these your servants who have entered into your teaching. Show them the way that is suitable for them, so that they may walk in it through the grace of the immaculate Holy Spirit, and grant them forgiveness of their sins. Give them grace, so that they may find healing from their sins, which defile them, and become worthy of your holy baptism, which is incorruptible regeneration. Let them find the Holy Spirit, so that they may see its greatness and splendor and the understanding of your powers, and glorify you, our Lord. For glory is fitting to you, to your good Father, and to the life-giving Holy Spirit, now and always, and for ages of ages. Amen.”

The deacon says: “Pray.”

The priest says:

“O Lord, good Father, almighty God, Father of the Lord God and of our Redeemer [Col. 0930C] Jesus Christ, we pray and beseech your goodness, O lover of humanity, for your servants who are being instructed. Teach them, and drive far away and expel from their hearts all remaining idolatry. Place your law, fear, and commandments, your righteousness and your holy ordinances, in their hearts. Make them fit to preserve the power of your word which they are being taught, so that at the appointed time they may find the washing of regeneration for the remission of their sins and become a dwelling place of the Holy Spirit, through the grace of your only Son, so that to you, to him, and to the Holy Spirit be glory and thanksgiving, for ages of ages. Amen.”

Afterward the priest takes a vessel of oil in his hands and prays over it in this manner, saying:

[Col. 0930D] “O Lord, O Lord, good Father, our almighty God, Father of the Lord God and of our Redeemer Jesus Christ, your only Son, the incarnate Word for our sake in the time of Pontius Pilate—which we truly believe—we pray and beseech your goodness, O lover of humanity. Send your holy power upon this oil, and let it become oil for cleansing and a defense against all things that oppose it. Amen.

“May every unbelief, every sorcery, every worship of idols, and every evil work be turned back through the power of your only Son, Jesus Christ our Lord and Redeemer, to whom, with you and the Holy Spirit, glory and honor are fitting for ages of ages. Amen.”

[Col. 0931A] The deacon says: “Pray.”

The priest says:

“O Lord, O Lord, good Father, our almighty God, Father of the Lord God and of our Redeemer Jesus Christ, we pray and beseech your goodness, O lover of humanity, who alone are the God of righteousness, with your only Son Jesus Christ our Lord and with the Holy Spirit: look attentively upon this oil and make it repel all demons, all sorceries and incantations, and every idolatry. Change it and make it a pure anointing, which will cause the soul to believe in Jesus Christ, to whom, with you and the Holy Spirit, belongs glory, for ages of ages. Amen.”

Afterward the priest anoints the foreheads of those who are to be baptized, their shoulders, arms, the upper part of the chest, [Col. 0931B] the inner and outer parts of their hands, and the tips of their fingers, while saying:

“I anoint you, N., in the name of the one Church, which is the council or assembly of the apostles of the Lord.”

The one being baptized says: “Amen.”

The priest says:

“May this oil wipe away every work of the enemy who opposes.”

The one being baptized says: “Amen.”

The priest then says the prayer of thanksgiving, which is as above and begins: “Let us give thanks to our benefactor,” and so forth.

Then he bends the arms of those who are to be baptized, prays over them, and says:

“Blessed is the Lord our almighty God. Amen. Blessed is the name of his glory. Amen.

“Blessed is his only Son Jesus Christ. Amen. Through him all nations have been called from darkness [Col. 0931C] to the true and wondrous light, and from the error that is idolatry to right knowledge. Amen.”

The deacon says: “Pray.”

The priest says:

“Write the names of your servants, whom you have called to your holy and blessed name, in the book of life, and count them among your flocks and among your people who fear your name, O Lord. Grant them to reach the goal of their age in faith and the remission of sins. Make them a dwelling place of the Holy Spirit, through your only Son Jesus Christ, so that to you, to him, and to the Holy Spirit be glory and honor, for ages of ages. Amen.”

## Prayer for those who have given their names for baptism

[Col. 0931D] The priest says:

“We also pray and ask, O Lord, good and almighty Father, Father of the Lord God and of our Redeemer Jesus Christ: have mercy upon your servants who have given their names and entered through your faith into your grace, so that they may be worthy to find the gift for which they have come, namely regeneration for the remission of sins. They have approached you so that they may be cleansed from sins forever and delivered from their shame, because the judgment of all is in your hand, O Lord our almighty God.”

The deacon says:

“Pray for those who have given their names, that God may make them worthy of his holy baptism and of the remission of sins.”

[Col. 0932A] Then the priest bends the knees of those who are to be baptized and says this prayer over them:

“O Lord, O Lord, good Father, our almighty God, Father of the Lord God and of our Redeemer Jesus Christ, we ask your goodness and beseech you, O lover of humanity: have mercy upon your servants who have given their names, and make them worthy of the grace to which they have approached, so that they may find the Holy Spirit, be filled with your Spirit, become like your Son Jesus Christ our Lord, and become one with him.

“Give them a clean heart and an upright mind. For this we implore and beseech you on our knees. Give your hand, Lord, and raise us from the earth; lift up our mind and understanding. Give us an understanding mind and [Col. 0932B] instruction. Make us your servants and guard us by the grace of the Holy Spirit. Direct these your servants by the hope of your eternal goodness, through your only-begotten Son Jesus Christ, with whom, and with the Holy Spirit, glory and honor are fitting for you, for ages of ages. Amen.”

Afterward the priest bends the feet of those who are to be baptized and says:

“We ask you, Lord; with many prayers and groans we beseech your goodness, almighty Lord, Father of the Lord God and of our Redeemer Jesus Christ, on behalf of your servants who have given their names. We ask you, Lord, to open the ears of their hearts, enlighten them with the light of understanding, and give them the desire to know the power of your word which they are being taught, because the power that is in you is power [Col. 0932C] for mercy, O Lord our almighty God.”

The deacon says: “Pray.”

The priest says:

“Lord Jesus Christ, our God and Redeemer, who made all things, we pray and beseech your goodness, O lover of humanity, that secretly and invisibly, through the Holy Spirit, you may abolish all evil demons who oppose us, restrain and punish them, because you yourself have called your people and these your servants, who have come from darkness to light, from death to life, and from error to understanding of righteousness.

“After the knowledge of you, O most just God, search also the inner parts of their hearts, O Lord, as you say: ‘They shall search Jerusalem with the lamp of wisdom,’ [Col. 0932D] and do not permit the evil spirit to lie hidden in them. Give them purity and salvation; give them eternal life. Generate them through the washing of regeneration for the remission of sins, and make them a dwelling place of the Holy Spirit through your only-begotten Son Jesus Christ, the Lord God and our Redeemer, because glory and power are fitting to you, with him and the Holy Spirit, for ages of ages. Amen.”

Then the priest again bends the feet of those who are to be baptized and says this prayer:

“O lover of humanity, merciful one, begetter of light and life, fountain of all purity, you made everything that was made from the beginning and gave a sign to each of your works. Since you yourself can change all things, change the souls of these people and grant them a second, heavenly generation, so that they may no longer be flesh but truly children of the Holy Spirit, through your only Son; for with him and the Holy Spirit glory and power belong to you, for ages of ages. Amen.”

Again the priest bends the feet of those who are to be baptized and says this prayer:

“O Lord, O Lord, good Father, our almighty God, Father of the Lord God and of our Redeemer Jesus Christ, who gives life to our souls, guide, we beseech you, those who seek it. O lover of humanity, look from heaven, from your sanctuary, and from the exalted seat of your kingdom upon these your servants who have given their names to your Church, so that they may venerate your holy name and serve it.

“Rule their hearts, so that they may become chosen vessels for you. Make them fit, Lord, for every good work, and ward off from them the weakening and falling away of their former faith, so that they may embrace your holy word, receive the power of your faith, and carry out your commandments. Strip them of the old state through the hope of life, which is eternal. Wipe out in them every power of the enemy.

“Search their hearts, as you say through the prophet Jeremiah: ‘They shall search Jerusalem with the lamp of wisdom.’ Do not permit the unclean and evil spirit to lie hidden in them. Let them not be members of the flesh or possess an evil mind, but grant them purity through this holy water. Give them the word of eternal life, and generate them through the washing of regeneration for the remission of sins. Make them a dwelling place of the Holy Spirit, through the grace of your only Son Jesus Christ, now and always, [Col. 0933C] and for ages of ages. Amen.”

Afterward the priest lays his hand upon the heads of those who are to be baptized and says this prayer:

“In the name of your only Son Jesus Christ, receive, cleanse, and prepare these souls, so that they may become free from all demons, from every error and fault. Let all darkness flee from them, together with everything that weakens faith and every evil thought. In the name of your only Son Jesus Christ, cleanse and free them forever from all the deceits of Satan. Amen.”

Afterward they remove the garments and all ornaments of those who are to be baptized, raise their right hands, and cause them to look toward the west.

[Note: [Col. 0933D] Since darkness arises from that direction, looking toward that place signifies in the Mystery the prince of darkness, whom they renounce.]

The person renouncing Satan does so if he is of sufficient age; but if he is an infant, those who speak on his behalf answer for him and say as follows:

“I renounce you, Satan, and all your unclean works, all your ministers, your evil incantations, and all your power; all your princes, all your deceits, and all your evil and dark flatteries and enticements; and all your authority and unbelief.”

Afterward they turn their faces toward the East.

[Note: [Col. 0934D] This is so that they may remember that they have turned toward him who testifies that he is the light.]

They raise their right hands high and say:

“I believe in you, Christ, my God. I believe in your saving law, in all your life-giving angels, [Col. 0934A] and in all your works that give life.”

Afterward the priest says the creed, and those who are to be baptized say it with him:

“We believe in one God, the Lord, the almighty Father; and in his only Son, Jesus Christ our Lord; and in the life-giving Holy Spirit; and in the resurrection of the flesh; and in the one holy apostolic Church, which is above all. And we believe in one baptism for the remission of sins, for ages of ages. Amen.”

Then the priest asks them: “Do you believe?”

They say three times: “We believe, we believe, we believe.”

Those who are of sufficient age answer for themselves; for infants who cannot speak, their sponsors answer.

Then the priest says this prayer:

[Col. 0934B] “O Lord, O Lord, good Father, our almighty God, Father of the Lord God and of our Redeemer Jesus Christ, Lord of heaven and earth, maker of all the ages, who have given understanding to those who are on earth through your only Son Jesus Christ, our Lord and Redeemer, who have prepared them for the kingdom of heaven through this calling: strengthen these same people by your power, and strengthen their mind, because they are your servants.

“May your power dwell in them, so that they do not return to their former state, which they renounced; rather, strengthen their faith, so that nothing may separate them from you. Strengthen them in the will of the faith that belongs to the apostles, the true and holy faith. Make them worthy of the greatness of your grace; drive the old state away from them, renew their life, and pour out upon them the power [Col. 0934C] of the Holy Spirit, so that they may become worthy and share with your only Son, and may be not children of the flesh but children of righteousness. May they be your wise and believing servants, through Jesus Christ, with whom, and with you and the Holy Spirit, is glory, for ages of ages. Amen.”

Afterward the deacon says: “Bow your heads.”

Then the priest bends the feet of those who are to be baptized and prays over them, saying:

“Lord our Redeemer, lover of humanity, maker of heaven and earth: since you alone perfect this mystery, since every knee in heaven and on earth adores you and every tongue praises you, according to what Paul says—our Redeemer and Lord Jesus Christ has accomplished all things for the glory of God the Father—embrace these your servants, who have hastened and come to adore you with bent knees.”

The deacon says: “Pray.”

The priest says:

“Therefore we beseech and ask you, O lover of humanity: drive every envy and every temptation far from them; remove every weakness and every affliction from them; search their inward parts and enlighten their hearts and minds with the light of understanding. Keep every work of Satan, every change and falling away from the faith, and every worship of idols away from them. Strengthen and guide their hearts through the reception of your Holy Spirit and through the will of your Son, which [Col. 0935A] is without defect, now and always, and for ages of ages. Amen.”

Afterward the priest takes oil and anoints the shoulders, the upper part of the chest—that is, the pit of the stomach—the inner and outer parts of the hands, the knees, and all the joints of their bodies, in the sign of the cross, saying:

“I anoint you, N., with the oil of gladness, which breaks through every power of the enemy, which has been planted in the midst of the wood of the sweet olive, which is the holy Church of the apostles of the Lord.”

The deacon and those who are anointed say: “Amen.”

After anointing them with oil, the priest says this prayer:

“O Lord, O Lord, good Father, our almighty God, we invoke your holy and blessed name, that you may disperse and drive away every opposing power. We ask through all your saints: search the hearts of your servants, who have come to complete and perfect your holy grace. If they possess any remaining evil of the demon that lies hidden, draw it out and destroy it from their souls and bodies, because they are your servants and believe in your holy name.

“Renew their life, and make them worthy to receive without stain and with sincerity the light and sign of your Christ and the grace of your Holy Spirit, to whom, with you, belong equal honor and light. Amen.

“Garment of salvation. Amen.

“Shield of faith that cannot be conquered by the enemy. Amen.

“May they become sheep of your flock and of the glory of your heavenly faith, and heirs [Col. 0935C] of your kingdom, which does not grow old or decay. Amen. Through Jesus Christ our Lord, with whom, and with you and the Holy Spirit, be honor and glory, for ages of ages. Amen.”

The deacon says: “Pray.”

The priest prays in this manner:

“Being Lord, good Father, our almighty God, who fashioned humanity in your image and likeness and gave it the power of life, the power that remains forever, and when it fell into sin did not abandon it but corrected it through salvation—namely, through the incarnation of your only-begotten Son Jesus Christ our Lord, who is full of salvation—free these your creatures from the works of the enemy, receive them into your kingdom, and open the eyes of their hearts. Amen.

“May they be illumined [Col. 0935D] by the light of your kingdom, and may your divinity be with them throughout the span of their life. Deliver them from every evil of the enemy and from the evil temptation of the noonday demon. Amen.

“From the arrow that flies by day. Amen.

“From the work that walks in darkness and from the vision of the night. Amen.

“Keep all unclean spirits away from them. Amen.

“And the evil spirit that disturbs the heart. Amen.

“And the spirit of error and every wickedness. Amen.

“The spirit of love of gold. Amen.

“And every servitude to idols and spirits of falsehood. Amen.

“And every shamefulness practiced according to the teaching of Satan. Amen.

“Make them sheep of your flock, O Christ. Amen.

“And chosen members of your Church, which is above all. Amen.

“Children of light and holy vessels. Amen.

“And [Col. 0936A] heirs of your kingdom. Amen.

“And may they fight to preserve the commandments of Christ and guard them with an unshakable sign. Amen.

“And an undefiled garment; and may they find the steadfastness and perseverance that belong to the elect, through Jesus Christ our Lord, to whom, with you and the Holy Spirit, glory and power are fitting for ages of ages. Amen.”

Afterward, at the baptismal font, the priest says secretly:

“Holy Lord and light, strengthen your servants and make them worthy of this great grace, namely, the Church and holy baptism. Take the old state away from them and generate them by a second generation into everlasting life. Pour out upon them the power of the Holy Spirit and the wisdom of your Christ, so that they may not be children of the flesh but children of your glory and heirs of your kingdom, which never grows old, [Col. 0936B] according to the will of the Only-Begotten, to whom, with you and the Holy Spirit, glory, divinity, and honor are fitting, for ages of ages. Amen.”

Then the priest says the prayer of thanksgiving and offers incense; the deacon reads from Paul’s Epistle to Titus, chapter eleven:

For the grace of God our Savior has appeared to all people, teaching us that, having renounced ungodliness and worldly desires, we should live soberly, justly, and devoutly in this present age, awaiting the blessed hope and the appearing of the glory of our great God and Savior Jesus Christ, who gave himself for us, that he might redeem us from all iniquity and cleanse for himself a people acceptable to him, devoted to good works. Speak these things, exhort, and rebuke with all authority; let no one despise you. Remind them to be subject to rulers and authorities, to obey commands, to be ready for every good work, to slander no one, not to be quarrelsome, but gentle, showing all meekness toward all people. For we too were once foolish, unbelieving, wandering astray, serving various desires and pleasures, living in malice and envy, hateful and hating one another. But when the kindness and humanity of God our Savior appeared, not because of works of righteousness that we had done, but according to his mercy, he saved us through the washing of regeneration and renewal by the Holy Spirit, whom he poured out upon us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Savior, so that, having been justified by his grace, we might become heirs according to the hope of eternal life. [Col. 0936C–D]

Then the subdeacon reads from the First Epistle of John, chapter 5:

Who is it that conquers the world, except the one who believes that Jesus is the Son of God? This is he who came through water and blood, Jesus Christ—not in water only, but in water and blood. And it is the Spirit who bears witness, because Christ is the truth. For there are three who bear witness in heaven: the Father, the Word, and the Holy Spirit; and these three are one. And there are three who bear witness on earth: the spirit, the water, and the blood; and these three are one. If we receive the testimony of human beings, the testimony of God is greater, because this is the testimony of God, which is greater: that he has borne witness concerning his Son. Whoever believes in the Son of God has the testimony of God within himself. Whoever does not believe the Son makes him a liar, because he does not believe the testimony that God has borne concerning his Son. And this is the testimony: God gave us eternal life, and this life is in his Son. Whoever has the Son of God has life; whoever does not have the Son of God does not have life. I write these things to you so that you may know that you have eternal life—you who believe in the name of the Son of God. [Col. 0936D–0937A]

The priest who assists the priest performing the baptism then reads from the Acts of the Apostles, chapter 8:

An angel of the Lord spoke to Philip, saying: “Rise and go toward the south, to the road that descends from Jerusalem to Gaza; this is deserted.” And he arose and went. And behold, an Ethiopian man, a eunuch, a powerful official of Candace, queen of the Ethiopians, who was over all her treasury, had come to Jerusalem to worship and was returning, seated in his chariot and reading the prophet Isaiah. The Spirit said to Philip: “Approach and join yourself to this chariot.” Philip ran up and heard him reading the prophet Isaiah, and he said: “Do you think you understand what you are reading?” He replied: “And how can I, unless someone should guide me?” And he asked Philip to come up and sit with him. The passage of Scripture that he was reading was this:

“Like a sheep he was led to slaughter, and like a lamb before its shearer is silent, so he did not open his mouth. In his humiliation judgment was taken away from him. Who will declare his generation? For his life will be taken from the earth.”

The eunuch answered Philip and said: “I beg you, concerning whom does the prophet say this—concerning himself or concerning someone else?” Then Philip opened his mouth, and beginning from this Scripture, proclaimed Jesus to him. As they traveled along the road, they came to some water, and the eunuch said: “Look, here is water. What prevents me from being baptized?” Philip said: “If you believe with all your heart, it is permitted.” He answered: “I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God.” And he ordered the chariot to stop; and both Philip and the eunuch went down into the water, and he baptized him. When they had come up from the water, the Spirit of the Lord carried Philip away, and the eunuch no longer saw him; but he went on his way rejoicing. [Col. 0937A–C]

Then the priest who performs the baptism says:

Holy, holy, holy is the Lord, the strong and immortal God; have mercy on us, O Lord. Blessed are those whose iniquities have been forgiven and whose sins have been covered. Blessed is the man to whom the Lord has not reckoned sin. Draw near to him, and he will enlighten you, and your faces will not be put to shame. This poor man cried out, and the Lord heard him. [Col. 0937D]

Then he reads from the Gospel of John, chapter 3:

Now there was a man among the Pharisees, named Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews. He came to Jesus by night and said to him: “Rabbi, we know that you have come from God as a teacher; for no one can perform these signs that you perform unless God is with him.” Jesus answered and said to him: “Amen, amen, I say to you: unless someone is born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God.” Nicodemus said to him: “How can a person be born when he is old? Can he enter a second time into his mother’s womb and be born?” Jesus answered: “Amen, amen, I say to you: unless someone is born of water and the Holy Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of God. What is born of flesh is flesh, and what is born of spirit is spirit. Do not marvel that I said to you: You must be born again. The Spirit breathes where it wills, and you hear its voice, but you do not know where it comes from or where it goes. So it is with everyone who is born of the Spirit.” Nicodemus answered and said to him: “How can these things happen?” Jesus answered and said to him: “You are a teacher in Israel, and you do not know these things? Amen, amen, I say to you: we speak what we know and testify to what we have seen, and you do not accept our testimony. If I have told you earthly things and you do not believe, how will you believe if I tell you heavenly things? And no one has ascended into heaven except the one who descended from heaven, the Son of Man who is in heaven. And just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up, so that everyone who believes in him may not perish but have eternal life. For God so loved the world that he gave his only-begotten Son, so that everyone who believes in him may not perish but have eternal life. For God did not send his Son into the world to judge the world, but so that the world might be saved through him. Whoever believes in him is not judged; but whoever does not believe has already been judged, because he has not believed in the name of the only-begotten Son of God. And this is the judgment: the light has come into the world, and people loved darkness more than the light, for their works were evil. For everyone who does evil hates the light and does not come to the light, so that his works may not be exposed. But whoever does the truth comes to the light, so that his works may be revealed, because they have been done in God.” [Col. 0937D–0938C]

Afterward he says the following prayer for the sick, first exhorting the people to pray in this manner:

Let us beseech almighty God, the Father of our Lord, God, and Savior Jesus Christ, for our sick brethren, that he may drive away from them every illness and every affliction, and, having driven away the spirit of infirmity, himself grant them health—he in whom is all power of healing, the Lord our God.

The deacon says: Pray for the sick.

The priest says:

Lord, our almighty God, we ask and beseech you: grant health to our sick brethren; destroy the spirit of infirmity; remove from them every sickness and every suffering. May your mercy quickly find us, O Lord. [Col. 0938D]

The deacon says to the people:

You are the healing of the soul, the physician of the body, the visitor of all flesh and of those tormented by unclean spirits. Free every afflicted and oppressed soul; grant it relief, grant it rest. Destroy every illness and every suffering from us and from this house, which invokes your holy and blessed name; and, once the infirmity of each of our souls has been healed, bestow perfect health through your only-begotten Son, with whom glory and power belong to you and to the Holy Spirit, now and always and forever and ever. Amen. [Col. 0938D–0939A]

Then the priest exhorts the people to pray for travelers and afterward prays:

Let us also beseech almighty God, the Father of our Lord and Redeemer Jesus Christ, for our brethren who have departed on a journey and for those who are about to travel, whether by sea, rivers, lakes, or whatever route they take, that our Lord God, who encompasses all things, may guide them all to a safe harbor.

The deacon says: Pray for those who are traveling.

The priest says:

Lord our God, who encompass all things, we ask and beseech you: guide the steps of our brethren who have departed on a journey and of those who are about to depart, and be with them so that they may attain what they desire. May your mercy quickly find us, O Lord.

The deacon says: Let us all say:

Lead them to a safe harbor; present them and restore them to their relatives with rejoicing and gladness, so that they may rejoice and cause others to rejoice, through your only Son, with whom glory and power belong to you and to the Holy Spirit, now and always and forever and ever. Amen. [Col. 0939A–B]

Afterward the priest exhorts everyone to pray for rain in this manner:

Let us also beseech almighty God, the Father of our Lord and Redeemer Jesus Christ, for rain, that he may send it where it is needed—our Lord God, who encompasses all things. [Col. 0939B–C]

The deacon says: Pray.

The priest says:

Lord, our almighty God, we ask and beseech you: send your rain to the places where it is desired; gladden the face of the earth; water its furrows; bring the seed to the harvest; and, because of your goodness, may your mercy quickly find us, O Lord.

The deacon says: Let us all say:

For your poor people, O Lord, and for all who hope in you, deal with us according to your mercy. Feed our heart with the divinity of your teaching and with the understanding that comes from you, through your only-begotten Son, with whom glory and power belong to you and to the Holy Spirit, now and always and forever and ever. Amen. [Col. 0939C–D]

For the fruits of the earth. The priest:

Let us again beseech almighty God, the Father of our Lord and Redeemer Jesus Christ, for the fruits of the earth, that he may increase them and make them abundant, and that the Lord our God may bestow the riches of grace.

The deacon says: Pray for the fruits of the earth.

The priest:

Lord, our almighty God, we ask and beseech you: increase the fruits of the earth and make them abundant; gladden the face of the earth; water its furrows; bring the seed to the harvest. May what comes from your goodness quickly find us—your mercy, O Lord.

The deacon says: Let us all say:

For your poor people, O Lord, and for all who invoke your holy name, through your only Son, with whom glory and power belong to you and to the Holy Spirit, now and always and forever and ever. Amen. [Col. 0939D–0940A]

For the flowing waters. The priest:

Let us also beseech almighty God, the Father of our Lord and Redeemer Jesus Christ, for the flowing waters, that they may rise to their proper measure and that the Lord our God may bestow the riches of grace.

The deacon says: Pray for the flowing waters.

The priest says:

Lord, our almighty God, we ask and beseech you: increase the streams of water to their proper measure; make the face of the earth glad; water its furrows; multiply the crops; and bless the cycle of the year with the kindness that comes from you. May your mercy quickly find us, O Lord.

The deacon says: Let us all say:

For your poor people, O Lord, and for all who invoke your holy name, through your only Son, with whom glory and power belong to you and to the Holy Spirit, now and always and forever and ever. Amen. [Col. 0940A–B]

For peace.

The priest:

Let us also beseech almighty God, the Father of our Lord and Redeemer Jesus Christ, for the peace of the holy and only apostolic Church, which is above all Churches.

The deacon:

Pray for this holy and only Church, which is the assembly directed by the apostles in the Lord. [Col. 0940B–C]

The priest:

We ask and entreat your goodness, O lover of humankind: remember, Lord, the peace of the holy Church, the one apostolic assembly, which existed from the beginning and will endure until the end of the age. Bless through it every people and every food. Send the peace that comes from heaven upon the soul of each one of us, and grant us the peace of our life. Grant the same peace, Lord, to our king N., to his princes, judges, and subjects, and to the assembly of our neighbors, both those who are outside the Church and those who are contained within it; adorn them with every kind of peace. King of peace, grant us peace, because you have given us all things, and make us your own, since we know no one other than you. We call upon and invoke your holy name, so that our soul may live through the Holy Spirit and the death of sin may not prevail over us, your servants, or over all your people.

For the bishops.

The priest:

And again let us beseech almighty God, the Father of the Lord, God, and our Redeemer Jesus Christ.

The deacon says:

Pray for our principal ruler, the chief of the archbishops and bishops, our lord N., and for the head of the bishops of the great province N., and for the head of our city, the venerable bishop, Father N., and for all bishops, priests, and deacons who are upright in the faith. [Col. 0940D–0941A]

The priest:

We ask and seek from your goodness, O lover of humankind: remember our venerable Father and lord, the chief of the archbishops and bishops, Father N., and our lord archbishop, Father N. Preserve them carefully for us for many years and a long time, in justice and peace, together with all bishops, priests, and deacons of the true faith, and the whole image of the holy and only Church of Christ, which is the apostolic assembly, so that they may exercise the sanctification that you entrusted to them in the dignity of the priesthood, according to your holy and blessed will, and that they may discharge [their office] in justice and equity and shepherd your people in truth. Receive the prayer that they offer for us and for all your people as a sacrifice offered to you on high, with a pleasing fragrance. Restrain and crush all their enemies and adversaries beneath their feet as soon as possible, but preserve them for us in justice and peace within your holy Church. Amen. [Col. 0941A–B]

Prayer for the king.

The priest:

Let us also beseech almighty God, the Father of our Lord and Redeemer Jesus Christ, for our God-loving king N., that he may preserve his kingdom in peace and justice, without affliction—our Lord God, who encompasses all things.

The deacon says: Pray for the king.

The priest:

Our God, who contains all things, we ask and beseech you: grant the king of this province, your beloved, our king, what is beneficial for him; restrain on every side the hostile nation against him; speak justice into his heart for your holy Church. May your mercy quickly find us, O Lord.

The deacon says: Let us all say:

Grant him, without error, to preserve the understanding of the faith, to the honor of your divinity, through your only Son, with whom glory and power belong to you and to the Holy Spirit, now and always and forever and ever. Amen. [Col. 0941B–C]

For the assembly of each place.

The priest:

Let us again beseech almighty God, the Father of the Lord, God, and our Redeemer Jesus Christ.

The deacon says: Pray for the holy Church and for our assembly that is within it.

The priest:

We ask and entreat your goodness, O lover of humankind: remember, Lord, our assembly and bless it. Make them undivided for you and free from idleness, and make them do your holy and blessed will. Make them a house of prayer, a house of sincerity, and a house of abundance and grace. Grant this favor, Lord, to us your servants and to those who will come after us, forever. Arise, Lord our God, and let your enemies be scattered; let all who hate your holy and blessed name flee from your presence. Let your people be blessed with the infinite blessing of the angels who do all your will, through the grace, kindness, and love for humankind of your only-begotten Son, the Lord, God, and our Redeemer Jesus Christ, with whom power and glory belong to you and to the Holy Spirit, now and always and forever and ever. Amen. [Col. 0941C–0942A]

For the little ones or new Christians, that is, catechumens.

The priest:

Let us also beseech almighty God, the Father of our Lord and Redeemer Jesus Christ, for the newly initiated Christian servants, that at the proper time he may grant them the washing of regeneration and the forgiveness of sins—our Lord God, who encompasses all things.

The deacon says: Pray for the new Christians.

The priest:

Lord, our almighty God, we ask and beseech you: have mercy on your servants who are not yet mature Christians; restrain from them every remnant of idolatry; place your law, commandments, justice, and ordinances in their hearts; and at the proper time grant them the washing of regeneration, namely, the forgiveness of their sins. Make them a dwelling place of the Holy Spirit, through your only Son, with whom glory and power belong to you and to the Holy Spirit, now and always and forever and ever. Amen. [Col. 0942A–B]

For those offering gifts.

The priest:

Let us again beseech almighty God, the Father of the Lord, God, and our Redeemer Jesus Christ, for those who have offered gifts to the holy and only Church, which is above all: the sacrifice of firstfruits, tithes, and the sign and memorial of thanksgiving. Whether someone has offered much or little, secretly or publicly, willingly or without possessing anything, may the Lord our God, who gives the heavenly Spirit and in whom is the power of every good work, accept the will of all. [Col. 0942B–C]

The deacon says: Pray for those who have offered gifts.

The priest:

Lord, almighty God, we ask and beseech you for those who have offered gifts to the holy and only Church, which is above all—whether they have offered much or little, secretly or publicly, willingly or without possessing anything—accepting the will of all. Grant each of them a blessing as a reward, through your only Son, with whom glory and power belong to you and to the Holy Spirit, now and always and forever and ever. Amen.

For those who have fallen asleep, that is, for the dead.

The priest:

Let us also beseech almighty God, the Father of the Lord, God, and our Redeemer Jesus Christ, for those who have fallen asleep. [Col. 0942C–D]

Lord of the living, life of the dead, hope of the hopeless, helper of the afflicted, cleanser of sinners, who rendered death powerless and, by cutting off the snares of Satan, bestowed salvation upon the human race: we ask and beseech you, O immortal one, with whom is the treasury of life, for those who have fallen asleep and rested in the faith: Fathers, first leaders of the archbishops, archbishops, bishops, priests, deacons, antagonists, virgins, monks, married teachers, those deprived of a spouse, infants, and orphans; and for the soul of your servant N.; and for the souls of all whom you yourself have justly and rightly called from the people. Grant their souls rest in a pleasant place, beside the water of rest, in the bosom of Abraham, together with Isaac and Jacob—you in whom is the power of rest, Lord our God. [Col. 0942D–0943A]

The deacon says: Pray.

The priest:

Lord, our almighty God, we ask and beseech you: receive the souls of your servants who have fallen asleep and rested in the faith, together with the soul of your servant N.; and nourish the souls of all who have died here or are dying, in a pleasant place beside the water of rest, in the bosom of Abraham, together with Isaac and Jacob. Grant them the passage of their souls without sin. Send the spirit of consolation and tranquility to their relatives. Comfort them and make them rejoice in Christ, through your only Son, with whom glory and power belong to you and to the Holy Spirit, now and always and forever and ever. Amen. [Col. 0943A–B]

Then the priest lays his hands upon those who are to be baptized and says:

Protect, O Lord, your servants who serve and cling to your holy name and bow their heads before you, and be with them. Help them in every good work. Awaken their hearts from every evil work that is done on earth. Make them alive, so that they may think upon all things that belong to life and remember all your works, O Lord, through your only Son, so that glory may belong to you and to that same Holy Spirit forever and ever. Amen.

Then he says the following prayer over the font:

God of the prophets, Lord of the apostles, who announced the coming of your Christ through the mouth of the holy prophets before you sent John the prophet, who was to go before you, we ask and beseech you, O lover of humankind, for your servants who have come to you, that your power may be present at this font. Strengthen your male and female servants. Make them worthy to receive your baptism, namely, the second birth for the forgiveness of sins, and your hope, which does not deceive, through your only Son, so that glory may belong to you, to him, and to the Holy Spirit, now and always and forever and ever. Amen. [Col. 0943B–C]

Then, before baptizing, the priest says secretly for himself:

Merciful, compassionate, and gracious one, who searches heart and inward parts and knows the hidden things of a person—for nothing is hidden from you, but everything is open before you—you know my hidden things. Do not abandon me, nor turn your face away from me, but at this hour take away all my guilt and absolve the sins of these people whom you have turned to repentance. Wash away the stains of my soul and body, and cleanse my inward parts completely by your invisible power. Strengthen me with your life-giving right hand, so that I may announce to others who seek liberation from me—that is, faith—and may hand it on to them, whom your ineffable greatness has prepared, O lover of humankind. Moreover, do not let me be like the sinful servant who is condemned. Far be that, Lord; let it not happen so. For you alone are good, and you are a lover of humankind. I will not depart in shame. Absolve me from my sin and send your help upon me from heaven. Give me power to carry out this great ministry worthily, your mystery, your heavenly ordinance. And may Christ dwell in those who are baptized, through the regeneration and baptism administered by me, because I am poor, asking you for mercy. Build them upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets; do not destroy them any further, but make them true plants in your holy Church, which is above all, the Church of the apostles, so that they may devote themselves to what is beneficial and your holy name may be glorified in them—your name which, in heaven and on earth, before every age, is full of the glory of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, now and always and forever and ever. Amen. [Col. 0943C–0944A]

Then he says the prayer for peace,

and the prayer for the bishops,

and the prayer for the assembly,

and the Apostles’ Creed. [Col. 0944A–B]

Then he takes unblessed oil and pours it three times into the baptismal water, each time making the sign of the cross and saying:

Blessed is the Lord our God, now and forever.

Blessed is the Lord the Father +. Amen.

Blessed is the only-begotten Son, Jesus Christ, our Lord +. Amen.

Blessed is the Holy Spirit, the Paraclete +. Amen.

Then he prays over the baptism in this manner:

God of heaven, God of light, God of the angels who preside over judges; God of the angels who preside over the powers of kings, peoples, and rulers; God of glory, who dwell above the Cherubim and Seraphim; Father of the Lord, God, and our Redeemer Jesus Christ, who released the souls of those bound by sin and enlightened those fastened in darkness through sin by the wounds of the passion of your only Son, Jesus Christ our Lord, who removed suffering from us and freed us from the whole burden of our sins; who drove far from us every hostile seed, whom all fear and dread—we call upon your holy power, upon your name that surpasses every name, namely, upon your only Son Jesus Christ, who was crucified for us in the time of Pontius Pilate. We ask you, Lord, for these male and female servants of yours: turn them and transform them. Amen. Bless them and strengthen them. Amen. So that through this water and this oil every power of the enemy may be destroyed. Amen. Remove, restrain, and scatter every evil spirit. Amen. Take away from them every worship of idols and every disgrace. Amen.

And he blows upon the water three times in the form of a cross, saying:

Sanctify this water and this oil. Amen. And let them be for the washing of regeneration. Amen. And for eternal life. Amen. And for an undefiled garment. Amen. And for a generation of grace. Amen. And for renewal by the Holy Spirit. Amen. In the name of your only Son Jesus Christ, whom you caused to be baptized in the Jordan, and who sanctified and cleansed it, [Col. 0944D–0945A] and bore witness, saying: “Whoever is not born of water and the Holy Spirit cannot enter the kingdom of heaven.” Then he commanded his disciples, saying: “Go therefore, teach all nations, and baptize them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit.” Receive, Lord, your male and female servants, because in you are power and liberation. O Holy One, thunder over this water, so that from it and from the Holy Spirit these your servants may be regenerated by the power of your divinity. They have come to you; make them fit for the forgiveness of their sins and for the undefiled garment, to the honor of your only Son, with whom glory belongs to you and to the Holy Spirit forever and ever. Amen. [Col. 0944D–0945A]

Then the deacon says: Pray.

The priest says the sanctification of the Jordan, that is, of the baptism:

The love of God, the grace of Jesus Christ, and the gift of the Holy Spirit be with you.

The people answer: And with your spirit.

The priest says:

Let your hearts be lifted up.

The people answer:

We have them with the Lord our God.

The priest says:

Let us give thanks to the Lord, the good Father.

The people answer:

It is right and fitting.

The priest says:

It is truly worthy and just. Blessed is the Most High God, who is strong forever over all things, in whom is the power to rule and guard the world. He gives life to all things, for in him is the Spirit of life; he nourishes every soul; he strengthens every spirit; he contains the powers of the whole world. He called all things from non-being and made all things. You, Lord, who are highest of the high, who see and know the end of the ages and awaken those sunk in sleep, who gave a voice to all moving things, stir this water and fill it with your Holy Spirit, and let it be a washing for the second birth. Amen. And for eternal life. Amen. So that these your male and female servants may be regenerated, just as you established understanding and reason in the soul, and through them made the human being rule and made him judge of all the adornments of the world. Therefore glory and greatness belong to you. [Col. 0945B–C]

Blessed are you, God, above all powers; blessed are you, God, above all rulers; blessed are you, God, above every thought and speech; blessed are you, God, above all understanding and knowledge; blessed are you, God, above all thrones and kingdoms. You sent water and fire, cold and ice, storm and whirlwinds over the earth, and caused water to gush forth from the hard rock. You are the one whom the sea saw and fled, and the Jordan turned back before you; the mountains leaped like rams and the hills like lambs of sheep. You are the one concerning whom, and concerning whose kindness, John bore witness—he who was sent before you, crying out with the herald’s voice in the wilderness and saying: “Prepare the way of the Lord; make his path straight. The voice of the Lord is over the waters; the God of glory has thundered.” [Col. 0945C–0946A]

Thunder, Lord, over this water and oil; prepare both, and give them power so that they may become your baptism, which is new birth and eternal life, and so that these your servants may be regenerated.

The deacon says: Let those who are seated rise.

The priest says:

Lord, O Lord, good Father, our almighty God, Father of the Lord, God, and our Redeemer Jesus Christ, maker of all creatures displayed by heaven, earth, and sea, and of all things hidden within them; maker of all visible and invisible creatures; you who gathered the waters into their channels, which you created, formed, and sealed, and the waters that are above the heavens; you curbed the sea and the rivers by your power and crushed the heads of the dragon in the water. You are terrible—for who can withstand you? Look, Lord, upon this water which you have made, and give it grace, salvation, and the blessing of the Jordan, so that from it may flee all things that work evil against your creatures, because I have invoked your holy and wondrous name, which is full of glory and terror against the things that oppose us. [Col. 0946A–B]

The deacon says: Face toward the east.

The priest continues in this manner:

And before the sign of the cross let all their powers who oppose us be scattered, and let all the demons who are in water and on earth, though unseen, flee from it. Let no dark pride lie hidden in this water, and let no evil spirit descend with those who are baptized, to darken their mind and trouble their heart. Rather, we all beseech you, Lord, to make this water water of rest. Amen. Pure water for cleansing. Amen. Water of salvation. Amen. Let it be a washing of the filth of soul and body. Amen. Water for the absolution and remission of sins. Amen. Light of soul and body. Amen. A washing for regeneration. Amen. An undefiled garment. Amen. Renewal by the Holy Spirit and a fountain of life. Amen.

Those present say: Amen.

The priest:

For he himself says: “Wash yourselves, cleanse yourselves, and drive evil away from your hearts.” You who gave us birth from heaven through water and the Holy Spirit, appear, Lord, over this water, [Col. 0946C–D] and make those who are baptized in it clean, so that they may cast off the old person and the disgrace of deceptive pleasure, put on the new person, and be renewed again in the likeness of their Creator. Amen. Let them become participants in the death of your Christ through the baptism of that same only Son, Jesus Christ. Amen. And let them share in his resurrection and preserve the gift of the Holy Spirit. Amen. Let the teaching of your grace abound over them. Amen. And let them find the pledge of the heavenly calling, which is yours, O Lord. Amen. Let them be numbered among the assembly of the firstborn, namely, the assembly of those whose names are written in heaven. Amen. Through Jesus Christ our Lord, with whom glory belongs to you and to the Holy Spirit, now and always and forever and ever. Amen. [Col. 0946D–0947A]

Then he says:

Holy, holy, holy are you, God of hosts. Heaven and earth are perfectly full of the holiness of your glory.

And the people say:

Holy, holy, holy are you, God of hosts. Heaven and earth are perfectly full of the holiness of your glory.

The priest says:

To you we look up, and we direct the eyes of our hearts toward heaven. We ask you, Lord our God: guard us all. Our God, God of our fathers, who created heaven and earth and all their adornments; creator of the waters above the heavens; who founded the earth upon the waters; who gathered the waters into their channels; who girded and restrained the sea and sealed its depths with the great name of the sign, which is full of glory and which all things fear and dread at the sight of your strength and power, O Lord. You founded the sea by your power; you crushed the heads of the dragon in the waters; you split open springs and fountains and gave the waters a path. The waters saw you, Lord, and the depths trembled because of the multitude of the waters. [Col. 0947A–B]

You are the one whom the Red Sea saw and before whose fear it stood still. You led Israel across and baptized it through Moses. You commanded the hard rock, and it poured forth water for your people. You changed bitter water and made it sweet. You, Lord, in the time of Jesus son of Nave, removed and caused to turn back the rivers that flowed terribly. You—for who could endure the sight of you?—also received Elijah’s sacrifice in water through flame and fire from heaven. You are the Lord who showed through Elisha the water of the generation of life, and who caused Naaman the Syrian to be cleansed through the water of the Jordan. You can do all things, and nothing is impossible for you. [Col. 0947B–C]

The deacon says: Pray.

The priest says:

Lord, O Lord, good Father, our God, king of the heavenly and earthly orders, look, you who sit above the cherubim; direct your eyes, you who dwell in heaven. Look upon and visit your creation. Give this water the great, mighty, heavenly gift of the Jordan, and let the Holy Spirit descend upon it. Amen.

Grant it the blessing of the Jordan; give it power, so that it may be water of life. Amen. Water of holiness. Amen. Water for the cleansing [Col. 0947D] of sins. Amen. Water for washing unto regeneration. Amen. Grant it that, if any evil spirit is hiding outside it, he may not return again to those who are baptized. Amen. Nor the spirit of the day. Amen. Nor the spirit of midday. Amen. Nor the spirit of evening. Amen. Nor the spirit of night. Amen. Nor the spirit of the air. Amen. Nor the spirit of pride that is beneath the earth. Amen.

But drive away all evil spirits by your power and goodness, and let them be broken before the sign of the cross of your Son. Amen. In your holy name, which we invoke, which is full of glory and terrible against those things that oppose us: may everyone who is baptized in it drive from himself the old person, who has been defiled by the pleasure of error, and may he put on the new [Col. 0948A] person, who is renewed in the likeness of his Creator. Enlighten them with the light of righteousness, which is the Holy Spirit. Amen. And may they find eternal life. Amen. Strengthen their hope. Amen. And may they stand before the throne of your Christ. Amen. May they find forgiveness of their sins. Amen. And may they receive a heavenly crown. Amen.
