Lord Jesus Christ, who spare while reproving and forgive while showing mercy, who reprove by scourging and convert by compassion, reprove your servant N. in your mercy and not in anger; may he be corrected by your correction, consoled by indulgence, instructed by discipline, cured by medicine, chastised by blows, and healed by goodness. Therefore may it please you, O Lord, to free, reprove, rescue, and not destroy him. Through him.

Another. Grant us, O Lord, that just as you were appeased by the prayers and confession of the publican, so you may be appeased by this servant of yours, and graciously attend to his prayers, so that, remaining in tearful confession and perpetual petition, he may swiftly entreat your clemency, and, restored to the holy altars and sacraments, may again be devoted to heavenly glory. Through him.

Another. Merciful God, gracious God, who according to the multitude of your mercies erase the sins of penitents and remove the guilt of past crimes by the forgiveness of remission, look upon this servant of yours and graciously hear him as he asks you for the remission of all his sins with complete confession of heart. Most loving Father, renew in him whatever has been corrupted by earthly weakness or violated by diabolical deceit, and restore him by perfect remission as a member of the body of Christ and to the unity of the members of your Church. Have mercy, O Lord, on his groans; have mercy on his tears; and admit him, we ask, to the sacrament of reconciliation, since he has confidence in nothing except your mercy. Through him.

Another. We humbly beseech your majesty, O Lord, to deign to grant the forgiveness of your mercy to this servant of yours, worn down by the long squalor of repentance, so that, having received the wedding garment, he may deserve to enter the royal table from which he had been cast out. Through him.

Another. May God the Father bless you; may God the Son heal you; may the Holy Spirit enlighten you. May he guard your body, save your soul, illumine your heart, and lead you to the things above. May Christ make you persevere in his holy service and lead you into eternal life. [Col. 0994C] May you deserve to have a share with God’s saints and elect. May God forgive you all your sins; may Christ, the Son of God, have mercy on you; may the almighty Father, who created you through his only Son, our Lord, who with that same Father and the Holy Spirit lives and reigns throughout the ages of ages, always preserve you healthy, sound, and protected from all the snares of all enemies. Amen.

Another. Attend, O Lord, to our supplications, and may your gracious mercy not be absent from this servant of yours. Heal his wounds and forgive his sins, so that, separated from you by no iniquities of his, he may always be able to cling to you, O Lord. Through him.

Another. Spare, O Lord, spare your servant whom you redeemed with your blood, O Christ; do not be angry with him forever.

Here the seven penitential psalms are to be sung, with the litany inserted below.

Lord, have mercy. Christ, have mercy. Christ, hear us. Savior of the world, help us. Holy Mary, pray for us. Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for your servant. Holy and perpetual Virgin, come to the aid of him who is placed in distress. [Col. 0995A] All holy angels, pray for this sick person. All holy archangels, pray for this sick person. All holy patriarchs, pray for this sick person. All holy prophets, pray for this sick person. Saint John the Baptist, pray for this sick person. Saint Peter, pray for this sick person. Saint Paul, pray for this sick person. Saint Andrew, pray for this sick person. Saint John and the others who follow, pray for this sick person. All holy apostles and evangelists, pray for this sick person. All holy martyrs, pray for this sick person. All holy confessors, pray for this sick person. All holy virgins, pray for this sick person. All saints from the beginning of the world until the present, [Col. 0995B] pray for this sick person.

Be favorable and free him, O Lord. Be favorable and spare him, O Lord. From every evil, free him, O Lord. From your anger, free him, O Lord. From an evil death, free him, O Lord. From every uncleanness of heart and body, free him, O Lord. From the bonds of the devil, free him, O Lord. Through your cross, free him, O Lord. Through your passion, free him, O Lord. Through your coming, free him, O Lord.

We sinners—

We ask you, hear us.

That you may grant him perpetual peace—

We ask you.

That you may grant him a fountain of tears—

We ask you.

That you may deign to pour the grace of the Holy Spirit into his heart—

We ask you.

That you may grant him a period of repentance, if it can be granted—

We ask you.

That you may grant him the intercession and consolation of the saints—

We ask you.

That you may deign to come to his aid in the present danger—

We ask you.

That you may drive away from him all the princes of darkness—

We ask you.

That you may deign to lead him to eternal joys—

We ask you.

That you may deign to exalt your Church in him—

We ask you.

That you may deign to hear us—

We ask you.

Son of God—

We ask you, hear us.

Lamb of God, who take away the sins of the world, spare this person, O Lord.

Lamb of God, who take away the sins of the world, have mercy on this person, O Lord.

Christ, hear us.

Lord, have mercy. Christ, have mercy. Lord, have mercy.

Our Father.

And lead us not—

Save your servant.

Send him, O Lord—

Rise, O Lord.

## Prayer

Most gentle almighty God, look favorably upon our prayers, and free the heart of your servant from the temptation of evil thoughts, so that he may be found worthy to become a dwelling place of the Holy Spirit. Through him.

Another. O God, who enlighten every person coming into this world, enlighten, we ask, the heart of your servant with the splendor of your grace, so that he may be able to think and love what is worthy of your majesty. Through him.

Another. Forgive, O Lord, our sins and grant us your mercy. Attend, we beseech you through the address of our mouth, to the humility and anguish of your servant; loose his bonds, erase his offenses, regard his tribulation, and, graciously granting effect to our petition, hear us. Through him.

When these things have been completed, the priest who is the sick person’s confessor should ask other priests to say over him the following prayers, which concern the reconciliation of a penitent at the point of death.

## Prayer

Merciful God, gracious God.

Another. Your majesty—

Another. We beseech your majesty, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, who always seek not the death but the life of sinners: look upon your weeping servant, attend to him who lies prostrate, and turn his lament by your mercy into joy. Tear apart the sack of sins and clothe him in saving gladness, so that, after the long hunger of his pilgrimage, he may be satisfied from your holy altars, and, having entered the king’s chamber, may always bless the name of your glory in his hall. Through him.

Then they should prepare blessed water sprinkled with salt and sprinkle it, with the antiphon and prayers, over the sick person and throughout the house in which he lies. After this the priest should say the prayer:

Lord God, who spoke through your apostle: “Is anyone among you sick? Let him summon the presbyters of the Church, and let them pray over him, anointing him with holy oil in the name of the Lord; and the prayer of faith will save the sick person, and the Lord will raise him up; and if he is in sins, they will be forgiven him”—we ask you, our Redeemer, to cure the illnesses of this sick person by the grace of the Holy Spirit, to heal his wounds, forgive his sins, drive every pain from his heart and body, and mercifully restore to him complete inward and outward health, so that, restored and healed by the help of your mercy, he may return to the former duties of your goodness. You who with the Father live and reign, God.

Then the sick person should bend his knees at the priest’s right hand, and this antiphon should be sung:

Heal, O Lord, this sick person whose bones are troubled and whose soul is greatly troubled; but turn, O Lord, and heal him, and rescue his soul from death.

Psalm: “O Lord, rebuke me not in your anger,” with the Gloria.

### Prayer

Let us pray to our Lord Jesus Christ, and with every supplication let us ask that he may deign to visit and strengthen this servant of his through his holy angel. He who lives.

The following antiphon:

The Lord spoke to his disciples: “In my name they will cast out demons; lay hands on the sick, and they will be well.”

Psalm: “God of gods,” with the Gloria.

The following prayer:

O God, who to your servant Hezekiah—

Again the antiphon:

A contrite and humbled heart, O God, you will not despise.

Psalm: “Have mercy on me, O God,” with the Gloria.

Prayer:

Look upon your servant, O Lord, in his illness.

Antiphon:

Come to the aid of this sick person, O Lord, in his present illness and by your remedy, so that, restored by you to his former health, he may, once well, render thanks to you in your Church.

Psalm: “To the Lord,” with the Gloria.

Prayer:

Attend, O Lord, to our supplications, and may there not be from this—

Another. Lord Jesus Christ, who are our salvation and redemption, who are true health and medicine, and from whom all health and healing come; who instruct us through the voice of your apostle to touch the sick with the liquid of oil and ask for your merciful goodness: look favorably upon this servant of yours from that wondrous summit of heaven, so that your remedy of grace may restore to health the one whom illness bends toward death and the contraction of his strength already drags toward its setting.

Extinguish in him the actions of lust and fevers, the goads of pains, and the torments of vices; dissolve the tortures of illnesses and desires; restrain the swelling of pride and fear; empty out the ulcers and corruptions of vices; heal the inward parts of the viscera, the disorders of hearts, marrow, and thoughts; cover the scars of consciences and wounds; be present in physical and figurative dangers; remove ancient and immeasurable afflictions; compose the material of flesh and blood; and, being reconciled, grant him the forgiveness of his offenses.

Thus may your goodness continually guard him, so that, with your aid, neither health may at any time lead to corruption nor illness now lead to destruction. May this sacred anointing with oil be for him, by your granting, the expulsion of the present disease and the desired remission of all sins, O Savior of the world, who live and reign.

Another.

May the Lord be reconciled concerning all the iniquities of this sick person, heal all his illnesses, redeem his life from the destruction of everlasting death, and strengthen and fulfill his desire in every good thing—he who alone, in the Trinity, lives and reigns as one God throughout immortal ages of ages. Amen.

When these things have been completed, for seven successive days, [Note: [Col. 0997D] Most ritual books before and after the year 1000, and even into the following twelfth century, continue this rite for seven complete days. In that period Geoffrey of Vendôme, book II, letter 19; Ivo of Chartres, in the letter following that one; Theobald of Sens, abbot of Saint-Columba; and others judged that the anointing of the sick should not be repeated, whether in the same illness or in a different one, any more than baptism, confirmation, or orders. Peter of Cluny, Lombard, and others refuted their opinion.] if necessity arises, they should give him Communion and perform the other office, and the Lord will raise him up to salvation; and if he is in sins, they will be forgiven him, as the apostle says.

The ministers of the holy Church should also, with the utmost reverence, sing for the sick person each day, at evening and at morning, praises with antiphons and responsories, or readings and prayers pertaining to this.

### Prayer

Almighty everlasting God, who come to the aid of those laboring in dangers and need, we humbly beseech your majesty to deign to send your holy angel, who may raise up your servant, laboring amid distress and necessities, with his consolations, through which he may obtain help in the present and grasp eternal remedies. Through him.

## Mass when the soul struggles in the agony of departure

Antiphon: “The groans of death surrounded me.”

Psalm: “I will love you, O Lord.”

Almighty everlasting God, preserver of souls, who chastise those whom you love and restrain those whom you receive with loving correction, we invoke you, O Lord, asking that you deign to confer your healing upon your servant, who suffers in body the weakness of his limbs, the force of distress, and the goads of illnesses. Give him, O Lord, your grace at the hour of his departure from the body, so that his soul may deserve to be presented to you, its own giver, without the stain of sin, through the hands of the holy angels. Through him.

Another.

Look favorably, we ask, O Lord, upon the affliction of your servant, so that, once the forgiveness of sins has been granted, he may always glory in your benefits. Through him.

Another. Grant, we ask, O Lord, to your servant the help of consolation, and graciously allow him, who labors under prolonged calamities, to breathe again. Through him.

### Reading from the Prophet Jeremiah

In those days Jeremiah said:

“Lord, all who forsake you will be put to shame. Those who depart from you will be written in the earth, because they have abandoned the fountain of living waters, the Lord. Heal me, O Lord, and I shall be healed; save me, and I shall be saved, for you are my praise. Behold, they themselves say to me, ‘Where is the word of the Lord? Let it come.’ [Col. 0998C] But I did not become troubled, following you as shepherd, and I did not desire the day of man. You know that what came forth from my lips was right in your sight. Do not become a terror to me; you are my hope in the day of affliction. Let those who persecute me be put to shame, but let me not be put to shame; let them be afraid, but let me not be afraid. Bring upon them the day of affliction, and crush them with a double crushing, O Lord our God.”

### Gradual

Be my helper and deliverer, O Lord; do not delay.

**Verse.** Let my enemies who seek my life be put to shame and dismayed.

### According to John

At that time Jesus said to his disciples:

“Amen, amen, I say to you: you will weep and lament, but the world will rejoice; you will be sorrowful, but your sorrow will be turned into joy. When a woman gives birth, she has sorrow because her hour has come; but when she has borne the child, she no longer remembers her distress because of the joy that a human being has been born into the world. So you too now have sorrow; but I will see you again, and your heart will rejoice, and no one will take your joy from you.”

[Col. 0999A]

### Offertory

Blessed are you, O Lord; teach me your judgments.

Blessed are you, O Lord; teach me your judgments. With my lips I have proclaimed all the judgments of your mouth.

### Secret

Attend, O Lord, in your goodness to our supplications, and receive the offering that we offer to you for your servant N., lying on a pallet and asking not for bodily health but for the salvation of his soul, granting him, O Lord Almighty, forgiveness of all his iniquities because of your immense mercy and through the intercession of all your saints, so that, through the scourging he endures, his soul, received by your holy angels, may deserve to reach the kingdom of your glory. Through him.

### Within the Canon

Therefore, O Lord, we ask that you graciously receive this offering which we offer to you for your servant N., and grant him heavenly desire at his departure from his body, and the spirit of refreshment. Through him.

### Communion

Redeem me, O God of Israel.

### Post-Communion

We give thanks to you, O Lord, for your manifold gifts, by which you have been accustomed to heal the souls of those who hope in you. Trusting in your goodness, we pray that you deign to have mercy on your servant, so that the adversary may not prevail against him at the hour of his death and departure from the body, but that he may deserve passage into life. Through him.

[Col. 0999]

# Order for Visiting the Sick

*(From the Rhenish manuscript, circa eleventh century.)*

[Col. 0999B] When a sick person is to be anointed, the priest, dressed in an alb and stole, goes before the procession with the oil of the sick, blessed water, a cross, and two candleholders; the assembly follows, with the psalm “Have mercy” begun. First the priest says this collect:

Almighty everlasting God, who through your blessed apostle said, “Is anyone among you sick? Let him summon the presbyters of the Church, and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord; and the prayer of faith will save the sick person, and the Lord will raise him up; and if he is in sins, they will be forgiven him”—we humbly beseech you that this servant of yours, through the ministry of our anointing and the gift of your holy goodness, may deserve to obtain forgiveness of his sins and reach eternal life. [Col. 0999C] Through him.

Seven psalms are appointed, with these antiphons:

**Antiphon.** Heal me, O Lord, for my bones are troubled, and my soul is greatly troubled; but you, O Lord, turn and rescue my soul.

Psalm: “O Lord, rebuke me not in your anger.”

**Antiphon.** There was a certain royal official whose son was sick at Capernaum. When he heard that Jesus had come into Galilee, he asked him to heal his son.

Psalm: “Blessed are they whose…”

**Antiphon.** Lord, my servant lies paralyzed in the house and is suffering terribly. “Amen, I say to you, I will come and cure him.”

Psalm: “O Lord, rebuke me not in your anger.”

**Antiphon.** A contrite and humbled heart, O God, do not despise; but because of your great mercy, [Col. 0999D] have mercy on me, O God.

Psalm: “Have mercy.”

**Antiphon.** Lord, come down before my son dies, so that you may heal him. Jesus says to him: “Go; your son lives.”

Psalm: “O Lord, hear.”

**Antiphon.** Lord, I am not worthy that you should enter under my roof; but only say the word, and my servant will be healed.

Psalm: “Out of the depths.”

Antiphon: “When the sun had set, all who had [Col. 1000B] persons sick with various diseases brought them to Jesus, and they were healed.” Psalm: “Lord, hear.”

Meanwhile the priest performs the anointing in this manner: he applies oil to his thumb and, with his thumb, makes the sign over each eye, saying this each time:

“Through this anointing, and through his most compassionate mercy, may the Lord Jesus Christ forgive you whatever you have sinned (or: transgressed) by sight, hearing, taste, smell, touch, walking (of the feet), and the burning of lust.”

Afterward these prayers are said, together with the following collects:

Save your servant (female: your handmaid).

Send him (her), O Lord, help from the holy place.

May the enemy have no success against him (her).

[Col. 1000C] Be for him (her), O Lord, a tower of strength.

The Lord be with you. Let us pray.

O God, who granted your servant fifteen years of life, so may your power raise your servant from the bed of sickness to salvation. Through [Christ our Lord].

Look upon your servant, O Lord, suffering from illness of the body, and refresh the soul which you created, so that, corrected by chastisements, he may immediately recognize himself as saved by your healing. Through Christ our Lord.

O God, who always rule your creation with loving devotion, incline your ear to our supplications, and, appeased, look upon your servant suffering from adverse bodily health; visit him with your salvation, and grant him the medicine of heavenly grace. Through [Col. 1000D] Christ.

O God, who have bestowed upon the human race both the remedy of salvation and the gifts of eternal life, preserve in your servant the gifts of your virtues, and grant that he may feel your healing not only in body but also in soul. Through [Christ our Lord].

O God of the heavenly powers, who by the authority of your command drive away every sickness and every infirmity [Col. 1001A] from human bodies, mercifully be present to this servant of yours, so that, his infirmities driven away and his strength restored, he may immediately bless your holy name with renewed health. Through X.

Holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, who strengthen the frailty of our condition by the infusion of your gracious power, so that our bodies and limbs may be invigorated by the saving remedies of your mercy: look favorably upon this servant of yours, so that, every bodily necessity of infirmity having been removed, the grace of his former health may be perfectly restored in him. Through the Lord.

Hear our prayers, O Lord, and pardon the sins of one who confesses to you, so that the one whom the guilt of conscience accuses may be absolved by the indulgence of your mercy. Through.

[Col. 1001B] May your mercy, we beseech you, O Lord, go before this servant (handmaid) of yours, so that his (her) iniquities may be erased by swift pardon. Through.

O Lord our God, who are not overcome by our offense but are appeased by satisfaction, look, we beseech you, upon this servant of yours, who confesses that he has grievously sinned against you. It is yours to grant the washing away of crimes and to bestow forgiveness upon sinners; for you have said that you prefer the repentance of sinners to their death. Grant, therefore, O Lord, that he may celebrate the vigils of repentance before you and, when his deeds have been corrected, rejoice that eternal joys are conferred upon him by you. Through.

Be present to our supplications, O Lord, and let the compassion of your clemency not be far from this servant of yours, N. Heal his wounds and forgive his sins, so that, separated from you by no iniquities, he may always be able to cling to you, the Lord. Through.

Be present to our supplications, O Lord, and mercifully hear me, who also am the first to need your mercy, so that, although you appointed me minister of this work not because of any merit of my own but by the gift of your grace, you may give me confidence to carry out your commission, and that you yourself may work through our ministry, which belongs to your goodness. Through.

Grant, we beseech you, O Lord, to this servant of yours, N., worthy fruits of repentance, so that, having obtained forgiveness for his offenses, he may be restored unharmed to your holy Church, from whose integrity he had strayed by sinning. Through.

Most gracious Creator and most merciful restorer of the human race, who redeemed by the blood of your only Son the human being cast down from eternity by the envy of the devil: give life to this servant of yours, whose death you in no way desire; and you who did not abandon the one who had strayed, receive him once corrected. May the tearful sighs of this servant of yours, we beseech you, O Lord, move your compassion. You heal his wounds; you extend to the one who lies fallen a saving hand. Let not your Church be ravaged in any part of her body; let not your flock suffer loss; let not the enemy exult over the loss of your household; and let not the second death possess one reborn through the saving bath. [Col. 1002A] To you, O Lord, we pour out our suppliant prayers; to you we pour out the grief of our heart. Spare the one who confesses, so that, with your help, he may lament his sins in this mortal life in such a manner that on the day of the fearsome judgment he may escape the sentence of eternal damnation and may not experience what terrifies in darkness and what crackles in flames. And when he has returned from the path of error to the way of righteousness, may he never again be wounded by wounds; rather, may what your grace has bestowed and what your mercy has restored remain whole and perpetual for him. Through the same [Christ our Lord].

O God, singular protection of human infirmity, display the power of your help over our sick person, so that, aided by the assistance of your mercy, he may deserve to be restored to your holy Church. Through.

Holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, [Col. 1002B] who, by pouring the grace of your blessing into sick bodies, preserve your creation with manifold mercy: graciously attend to the invocation of your name, and raise this servant of yours, freed from sickness and restored to health, by your right hand; strengthen him by your power, protect him by your authority, and restore him to your Church and to your holy altars with every prosperity he desires. Through.

Merciful God, gracious God, who, according to the multitude of your mercies, blot out the sins of the penitent and, by the forgiveness of remission, wipe away the guilt of past crimes: look upon this servant of yours and, graciously entreated, hear him as he asks with complete confession of heart for the remission of all his sins.

[Col. 1002C] Renew in him, most compassionate Father, whatever has been corrupted by earthly frailty or violated by diabolical deceit, and restore complete remission in the unity of the members of your Church’s body. Have mercy, O Lord, on his groans; have mercy on his tears; and admit him, who has confidence in nothing except your mercy, to the sacrament of reconciliation. Through.

We suppliantly beseech your majesty, O Lord, that you may deign to grant this servant of yours, worn down by the squalor of repentance, the forgiveness of your mercy, so that, having received the wedding garment, he may deserve to enter the royal banquet, from which he had been cast out. Through.

Absolve the soul of your servant (handmaid) through the intercession of the most blessed Mary, Mother of God, [Col. 1002D] and of blessed Peter and of all the saints, from every bond of sin before it is separated from the earthly frame of its members. Grant that, when it begins to be separated from the body, it may deserve to be received by the most blessed and gracious angels, presented before your most compassionate presence, and, by your gift, led into the bosom of blessed rest. Through.

If his departure should be delayed, the Litany is to be recited in this manner, with the lord Abbot or Prior leading it:

[Col. 1003]

## ORDER OF THE SACRED ORDERS

[Col. 1003A] The Psalmist, that is, the cantor, after he has been instructed by the archdeacon, may undertake the office by the sole command of the presbyter, without the bishop’s knowledge. See that what you sing with your mouth you believe in your heart, and that what you believe in your heart you prove by your works.

When the doorkeeper is ordained, after he has been instructed by the archdeacon how he ought to conduct himself in the house of God, the bishop, at the archdeacon’s direction, gives him the keys of the church from the altar, saying: “Act as though you were going to render an account to God for all the things that are locked up by these keys.” The deacon then hands over to him the church door.

### PREFACE OF THE DOORKEEPER

We humbly beseech God the almighty Father to deign to bless this servant of yours, named N., whom you have deigned to choose for the office of doorkeeper, so that he may faithfully care, by day and by night, at the appointed division of the hours, for invoking the name of the Lord. Through.

### BLESSING OF THE SAME

Holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, deign to bless this servant of yours, N., the doorkeeper, so that he may perform his duties among the doorkeepers of the church and may deserve to have a share of your reward with your elect. Through.

## ORDINATION OF THE LECTOR

When the lector is ordained, the bishop speaks about him to the people, judging his faith, life, and aptitude. After this, while the people wait, he hands him the book from which he is to read, saying to him: “Receive [Col. 1003C] this and be a messenger of the word of God. If you faithfully and usefully fulfill your office, you will have a share with those who have ministered the word of God. Your brothers choose you to be a lector in the house of your God. Recognize your office, so that you may fulfill it. For your God is powerful: may he increase his grace toward you. May he deign himself to grant this, he who reigns with the Father in the unity of the Holy Spirit, through all ages of ages. Amen.”

The portions missing here in the Zurich manuscript because a leaf has been cut out are supplied in full from the Einsiedeln manuscript, approximately of the tenth century.

## ORDINATION OF THE EXORCIST

Holy Lord, Father … When the exorcist is ordained, he receives from the bishop’s hand a booklet in which the exorcisms are written, while the bishop says to him: “Receive this, commend it to memory, and have authority to lay your hand upon one possessed, whether baptized or a catechumen.”

### PREFACE OF THE EXORCIST

God the almighty Father. Blessing of the exorcist. Holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God.

## ORDINATION OF THE ACOLYTE

When the acolyte is ordained, he is first instructed by the bishop [Col. 1004A] how he ought to perform his office. From the archdeacon, however, he receives a candlestick with a candle, so that he may know that he is assigned to light the lamps of the church. He also receives an empty cruet for supplying wine at the communion of the Body. Holy Lord, almighty Father.

## ALSO, THE ORDER OF HOW PRESBYTERS, DEACONS, AND SUBDEACONS ARE TO BE CHOSEN AT THE APOSTOLIC SEE OF ROME

On the Saturday of the first, fourth, seventh, and tenth months, at the twelfth lesson, at Saint Peter’s, where Mass is celebrated. After they have said the Introit and the prayer has been given, the Pontiff announces to the people, saying: “With the help of the Lord our God and Savior Jesus Christ.” Again he says: “With the help of the Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, we have chosen for the order of deacons or presbyters N., a subdeacon from that title.” If anyone has anything against these men, let him come out with confidence for the Lord and because of the Lord, and speak. Nevertheless, let him remember his own communion. After a brief interval, all immediately begin: “Kyrie eleison” (“Lord, have mercy”), together with the Litany. When this has been completed, the elect themselves ascend to the pontiff’s seat. He blesses them by whom they have been called, and they descend and stand in their order. Blessing. [The text is fragmentary here.]

## CHAPTERS OF POPE GREGORY

Just as one who, when invited, refuses, and when sought, withdraws, must be removed from the sacred altars, so without doubt one who ambitiously seeks office or intrudes himself importunately must be rejected. For one who strives to climb to higher things—what does he do except diminish as he increases? Why is it not considered [Col. 1004C] that the blessing is turned into a curse for him, because he is promoted in order to become a heretic? The Apostle Paul commanded Timothy: “Lay hands hastily on no one, nor share in the sins of others.” What does “lay hands hastily on no one” mean except before the age of maturity, before the time of examination, before the merit of labor, before experience of discipline? Just as the fruit of good work strengthens the one who examines rightly in choosing a priest, so he brings serious harm upon himself who elevates an unworthy man into the fellowship of his dignity.

## ORDINATION OF THE SUBDEACON

When the subdeacon is ordained, since he does not receive the imposition of hands, he receives from the bishop’s hand an empty paten [Col. 1004D] and an empty chalice; from the archdeacon’s hand, however, he receives a cruet with a water vessel and a towel.

### PREFACE OF THE SUBDEACON

Let us pray to God and our Lord Jesus Christ that he pour his blessing and grace upon his servant, N., whom he has deigned to call to the office of his diaconate, so that, faithfully serving in his sight, he may obtain the rewards predestined for the saints. Through.

### BLESSING OF THE SUBDEACON

Holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, deign to bless this servant of yours, N., whom you have deigned to choose for the office of subdeacon, so that you may establish him diligent and attentive in your holy sacristy and in the heavenly warfare; that he may faithfully minister at the holy altars; and that the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and fortitude, the spirit of knowledge and piety may rest upon him. Fill him with the spirit of your fear, so that you may strengthen him for divine ministry, and so that, obedient in deed and submissive in word, he may obtain your grace. Through.

## ORDINATION OF THE DEACON

[Col. 1005B] When the deacon is ordained, only the bishop who blesses him places his hand upon his head, because he is consecrated not to the priesthood but to the ministry.

### BLESSING OF THE SAME

Let us pray, most beloved, that God the almighty Father may mercifully pour out the grace of his blessing upon this servant of yours, N., whom he has deigned to assume into the sacred order, and grant him the gift of consecration, through which he may lead him to eternal rewards.

Another.

Hear our prayers, O Lord, and send upon this servant of yours, N., the spirit of your blessing, so that, enriched by a heavenly gift, he may be able to acquire the majesty of your grace and offer others an example of good living.

## CONSECRATION

Be present, we beseech you, almighty God, giver of honors, distributor of orders, and disposer of offices. Remaining in yourself, you renew all things and arrange everything. Through your Word, power, and wisdom, Jesus Christ your Son, our Lord, by eternal providence you prepare and dispense what is suited to each particular time. His body, the Church, distinguished by the variety of heavenly graces and joined together by the distinction of its members, you graciously cause to grow and expand into the increase of your temple, united by the wondrous law of its whole structure. By the power of the sacred gift you have established three grades of ministers to serve your name, choosing from the beginning the sons of Levi, who, remaining in faithful watch over the mystical works of your house, might possess by perpetual allotment the inheritance of eternal blessing.

Upon this servant of yours also, N., we beseech you, O Lord, look favorably. We humbly dedicate him to serve your sacred things in the office of the diaconate. We, indeed, as human beings ignorant of divine understanding and supreme reason, assess this man’s life as best we can. But you, O Lord, are not unaware of what is unknown to us, nor are hidden things concealed from you. You are the knower of secrets; you are the searcher of hearts. You can examine his life by heavenly judgment, by which you always have power both to cleanse what has been committed and to grant what must be done.

Send upon him, O Lord, we beseech you, the Holy Spirit, so that they may be strengthened for faithfully carrying out the work of the ministry by the gift of sevenfold grace. May the whole form of virtue abound in him: authority, modesty, constant shamefastness, purity of innocence, and spiritual observance of discipline. May your precepts shine in their (eorum), or his (ejus), conduct, so that by the example of their chastity they may gain the imitation of the holy people. May they offer a good testimony of conscience, persevere firm and steadfast, and, by your grace, deserve through worthy advancement to receive greater things from a lower rank. Through.

## ORDINATION OF THE PRESBYTER

When the presbyter is ordained, while the bishop blesses him and holds his hand upon his head, all the presbyters who are present also hold their hands upon his head beside the bishop’s hands.

### BLESSING OF THE PRESBYTERS

Let us pray, most beloved, that God the almighty Father may multiply heavenly gifts upon this servant of yours, N., whom he has chosen for the office of presbyter, and that those who undertake his dignity may carry it out with his help. Through.

The following prayer.

Hear us, O Lord our God, and pour upon this servant of yours the blessing of the Holy Spirit and the power of priestly grace, so that, having offered him for consecration to the sight of your goodness, he may obtain the perpetual abundance of the ministry. Through.

## CONSECRATION

[Col. 1006C]

Holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, author of honors and distributor of all dignities, through whom all things advance and through whom all things are strengthened, with the rational creation always increasing for the better according to an order arranged by fitting reason. Hence the priestly grades and the offices of the Levites, instituted through mystical sacraments, also grew, so that, when you had placed the highest pontiffs over the governance of peoples, you might choose men of the next order and second dignity to assist them in their fellowship and work.

Thus, in the wilderness, through the minds of seventy prudent men, you extended the spirit of Moses, by whose assistance he easily governed the countless multitudes of the people. Thus you transferred to Eleazar and Ithamar the abundance of their father’s blessedness, so that the ministry of priests would suffice for the saving sacrifices and for the more frequent sacramental offices. By this providence, O Lord, you added to the Apostles, the teachers of your Son, companions in the presbyterate, through whom they filled the whole world with secondary preachers.

Therefore, O Lord, we beseech you, grant these helps also to our weakness; for the more fragile we are, the more we need them. Grant, we beseech you, almighty Father, the dignity of the presbyterate to this servant of yours. Renew in his heart the Spirit of holiness. May he receive from you, O God, the gift corresponding to his merit, and may he commend the discipline of conduct by the example of his manner of life. May they be worthy fellow workers of our order. May the whole form of righteousness shine in him, so that, when he renders a good account of the stewardship entrusted to him, he may obtain the rewards of eternal blessedness. Through.

## CONSECRATION OF THE HANDS OF THE PRESBYTERS

Deign, O Lord, to consecrate and sanctify these hands through this anointing and our blessing, so that whatever they consecrate may be consecrated. The rest is missing; as it appears in the Einsiedeln manuscript, we add it here.

## ORDINATION OF THE BISHOP

When a bishop is ordained, two bishops hold him and place the book of the Gospels upon his neck, while one gives the blessing. All the other bishops who are present touch his head with their hands.

### BLESSING OF THE BISHOPS

[Col. 1007B] Be present, O Lord. The following. Be favorable, O Lord. Consecration. God of all good things. Prayer at Mass. God of all good things. Over the offerings. “This sacrifice.” Within the Canon. “Therefore, O Lord, we beseech you.” At Communion. “May this Communion.” The end.

(From Codex Vindobonensis theol. 149, ninth century, formerly of the monastery of Reichenau. [Note: In manuscript Codex Caesareus bibliothecae theol. 277 there is a special order describing how a bishop is ordained in the Roman Church. There, after the Introit, the Gloria in excelsis, the prayer, and the procession of the man already to be consecrated, the examination in the ordination of a bishop according to the Gauls begins, the same as is found in the Roman Pontifical: “The ancient institution of the holy Fathers teaches,” etc.])

## BLESSING OF THE BISHOPS

Be present to our supplications, almighty God, and may what must be performed through the ministry of our humility be fulfilled by the effect of your power. Through the Lord.

Another. Be favorable, O Lord, to our supplications, and, with the horn of priestly grace inclined over this servant of yours, pour into him the power of your blessing. Through the Lord.

## CONSECRATION

[Col. 1007C]

God of all honors, God of all dignities, which serve your glory in consecrated orders. God, who, through the breath of intimate revelation, instructed your servant Moses, among the other heavenly lessons of worship, also concerning the form of priestly clothing, and commanded the chosen Aaron to be clothed in a mystical garment amid sacred rites, so that posterity might derive understanding from the examples of the pious and so that no age might lack the instruction of your teaching.

For among the ancients the very appearance of the signs possessed reverence, whereas among us the experience of realities is more certain than the enigmas of figures. The clothing of that earlier priesthood is the adornment of our mind. And now priestly glory is commended to us not by the honor of garments but by the splendor of souls. For those things which then pleased carnal eyes demanded instead that what was contained within them be understood.

Therefore, we beseech you, O Lord, grant this servant of yours, whom you have chosen for the ministry of the highest priesthood, this grace: whatever those vestments signified by the gleam of gold, the brilliance of gems, and the varied forms of their many kinds of workmanship, may shine forth in his conduct and actions. Complete in your priest the fullness of your mystery, and sanctify him, equipped with the adornments of complete glorification, with the flower of heavenly ointment. May this flow abundantly upon his head; may it run down upon his mouth and what lies beneath it; may it descend to the extremities of his whole body, so that the power of your Spirit may fill his inward parts and surround his outward parts.

May steadfastness of faith, purity of love, and sincerity of peace abound in him. Grant him an episcopal chair for governing your Church and the whole people. Be his authority; be his firmness; be his power. Multiply your blessing and grace upon him, so that, always made capable by your gift of entreating your mercy, he may be devoted through your grace. Through the Lord.

## OVER THE OFFERINGS

May this sacrifice, O Lord, we beseech you, cleanse our offenses and sanctify the bodies and minds of those subject to you through the sacrifice that is to be celebrated. Through the Lord.

Therefore, O Lord, we beseech you, graciously accept this offering of our service and also of your entire household, which we offer to you for your servant, N., whom you have deigned to advance to the order of bishop. Preserve your gifts in him with favor, so that what he has obtained through divine gift he may carry out through divine effects, and so forth.

## AT COMMUNION

May this Communion, O Lord, cleanse us from guilt and [Col. 1008C] make us participants in heavenly remedies. Through the Lord. [Note: In the same manuscript, immediately before the votive Masses, the first of which is for Sunday on the Holy Trinity, there is added, concerning the ordination of a bishop, “What should be added in the consecration of the bishop to be ordained.” It begins: “God of all honors,” continuing to the passage: “And therefore, to this servant of yours, whom you have given as the bishop of the apostolic see, the primate of all priests throughout the world, and the teacher of your universal Church, and whom you have chosen for the ministry of the highest priesthood, we beseech you to grant this grace.” It continues: “Grant him a pontifical chair for governing your Church and the whole people.”]

## FOR ORDAINING A PRESBYTER

Prayer. Let us pray, most beloved, that God the almighty Father may multiply heavenly gifts upon this servant of yours, whom he has chosen for the office of presbyter. Through the Lord.

Another. Hear us, we beseech you, O Lord our God, and so forth.

## CONSECRATION

Holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, author of good things, and so forth.

## FOR ORDAINING A DEACON

Let us pray, most beloved, to God the almighty Father, [Col. 1008D] and so forth.

Another. Hear our prayers, O Lord, and send upon this servant of yours, and so forth.

## CONSECRATION

Be present, we beseech you, almighty God, giver of honors and orders.

[Col. 1009A] These prayers are to be said by the lord pope over an archbishop before the pallium.

(From manuscript Vindobonensis theol. 277, twelfth or thirteenth century.)

Almighty Lord God, Father, who commanded this servant of yours, N., to preside over your people not because of merits supporting him personally but solely through the ineffable generosity of your grace: grant him, through the grace of your Holy Spirit, to render worthily to you the ministry of priestly office, to serve ecclesiastical ministries fittingly, and to govern the people entrusted to him for the glory of your name, while you protect him in all things. Through the same [Lord].

Another. God, restorer and lover of innocence, direct this servant of yours, N., by the fervor of your Spirit, so that he may be found steadfast in faith and effective in your works. Enlighten him with the light of wisdom; cleanse and sanctify him; give him right counsel and holy teaching. Since you have wished to number him among the highest priests, grant that what you have willed him to be called by human lips he may, through the grace of your goodness, be made in your sight, so that with your elect he may deserve to receive the blessedness of eternal life. Through.

When the pallium has been given, this prayer is said:

Holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, King of kings and Lord of lords, we humbly beseech your clemency, and likewise that of your only-begotten Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, who, surpassing all in eternal pontificate, alone fulfilled the priestly ministry without stain; and that of the Holy Spirit, whose sevenfold grace sanctifies all things by heavenly power. We beseech you to graciously receive into the embrace of your heavenly goodness this servant of yours, N., who, by the grace of divine providence, has ascended by degrees from lesser things to greater.

Since he appears in the present before us unworthy men—whom you have appointed ministers of the apostolic see and of the highest service, not because of our merits but by the gift of your clemency—outwardly clothed in the saving garments for the office of the sacred altar, grant that, purified from every contagion of crimes, he may be inwardly filled perpetually with the sanctification of your Spirit. Grant that, watered by the streams of the living fountain, he may grow in the fruits of virtues and shine before all, so that his life may offer examples to others.

May the honor of the pallium be an ornament of his soul; and from the place where visible eminence has arisen, may invisible love blossom. May your divine [Col. 1009D] power strengthen him; may the power of your Son make his inward parts fruitful; may the grace of your Spirit fill his interior. Through you may he preserve the firmness of Catholic faith, not only for himself but also for the purpose of teaching others. Through you may he deserve to have the episcopal chair as a shield not only against the spiritual but also against the bodily adversities of this age. Through you may he receive, by the grace of the divine Godhead, the apostolic dignity in heaven and on earth, and the dominical power of loosing and binding not only bodies but also souls. Thus, living devoutly through worthy advancement and reaching the rewards destined for the saints, may he receive eternal blessedness. Through. [Note: Recently Benedict XIV, who in *De synodis*, book II, chapter 6, showed that the Roman pontiff had also given bishops the authority to wear the *λογίον* (*logion*), *πολυσταύριον* (*polystaurion*), or *φαινόλιον* (*phainolion*), which the Greeks call the pallium, also ordained a solemn blessing of the pallium. Although, as he says in the special bull issued for this matter, he did not doubt that a solemn blessing had always preceded the giving or transmission of the pallium, nevertheless, because the rite of this blessing is known to have undergone certain changes in the course of time, “we judged it to be our duty,” he continues, “to establish its form for observance in all future times and to confirm it by the authority of these present letters.” Joseph Catalanus gives this constitution in full, volume I of the *Caeremoniale S. R. E.*, p. 341. Also worthy of reading are the remarks in volume I, chapter 16, paragraph [blank], of the *Caeremoniale episcoporum* concerning the form of the pallium, which began to be shortened in the age of Sixtus IV. See also the same author’s notes on the Roman Pontifical, book I, title 14; Du Cange, *De inferioris aevi numismatibus*, §§ 6, 7, 9; Giovanni Maragoni, prologue to the *Chronologia of the Roman Patriarchal Basilica of Ostia*, chapter 10; Barthelius, *De Pallio*.]

## GREGORY TO VICTOR, BISHOP

(From manuscript Vindobonensis theol. 277, twelfth or thirteenth century.)

Whoever of the metropolitans—which we very much doubt—has dared to ordain someone without the pallium, both he who ordains and the one who is ordained, as well as their collaborators, are to be irrecoverably deposed from every order.

Let us pray, most beloved brothers, that God and our Lord Jesus Christ may deign to enlighten us and our elect by the grace of the Holy Spirit. Through. In the unity of the same [Spirit]. Then let this verse be said:

“And let them exalt him in the assembly of the people.”

“And in the seat of the elders let them praise him.”

Afterward he is sent to the chair, and this prayer is said:

Holy, eternal, almighty Father, you deigned to establish human beings in the heavenly seats, as the Psalmist says: “O Lord, your word remains forever in heaven.” You willed angels and archangels to be dedicated to you according to their order. In the privilege of the Old Testament, you ordained Moses, Aaron, and Samuel among your priests, who invoke his name; you ordained patriarchs and prophets to be anointed. In the New Testament, through your Son Jesus Christ, you chose the holy Apostles for the consolation of all of us, your servants. You honored the first Apostle Peter in the chair of honor and called him into the number of all the holy Apostles, so that the Holy Spirit says through the Prophet: “Let him praise him in the seat of the elders.”

In those times, by divine will, similar things happened through others like these. And now, O Lord, in your immense mercy, grant in our time a similar grace to our brother N., after the pattern of your holy Apostles seated in the chair of honor and dignity, so that he may appear worthy of honor in the sight of your majesty and, in that honor, may deserve to offer to all subject to him examples of every kind of virtue in words and deeds, with complete humility. After this life, may he be exalted among the angelic choirs to the throne of eternal seats. Through the same [Christ our Lord].

[Col. 1010D] Pontifical manuscript of the Library of San Blas, fourteenth century. For celebrating the sacred orders at the appointed times, its rite likewise begins with the Psalmist, unlike the Roman Pontifical, from which it also differs in many places. It begins as follows:

For celebrating the sacred orders, the bishop, clothed in full pontifical vestments as noted above, proceeds to the altar to say Mass in the proper order of ministers. After the first collect has been said, let those to be ordained be summoned. Sitting on his seat, let him read, or have another read, this prohibition:

“By the authority of our Lord Jesus Christ and of the Church, we firmly command and order all of you, under penalty of excommunication, that no servants of lords, unless they have been manumitted; no clerics of another diocese without the permission or letters of release of their bishop; no excommunicated persons; no illegitimately born persons, unless sufficient dispensation has been granted to them; no one who has stolen away [or: is furtive] or who is severely deformed in his limbs, unless they have been proved and admitted by the certain knowledge of the examiners; no one receive minor orders together with any sacred order, or even one sacred order together with another at the same time; no one lacking sufficient age; no one by jumping over the proper sequence; and no one who has profaned sacred things contrary to apostolic commands, unless sufficient dispensation has been granted to them, or who is otherwise prevented by a canonical impediment, whether expressed here or not expressed, presume to come forward or approach these sacred orders. If anyone attempts the contrary, we declare it invalid and void, and he shall know that he has incurred the aforementioned penalty of excommunication.”

When this prohibition has been read, the archdeacon, or another whom the bishop has appointed to perform the task, says in the manner of a reading:

“Holy Mother Church asks, reverend father, that these men, suited to the orders, be consecrated by your fatherhood.”

The bishop says:

“See to it that such men, distinguished by birth, knowledge, and conduct, are introduced by you—or rather, that such persons are ordained by us in the house of the Lord—through whom the devil may be driven far away and the clergy multiplied for God.”

The cleric likewise says:

“As far as human examination is concerned, they are considered worthy in birth, knowledge, and conduct, and, God willing, they can become worthy fellow workers in these matters.”

The bishop says:

“With the help of the Lord God and our Savior Jesus Christ, we choose these men to be consecrated. If anyone has anything against them, let him come out with confidence for God and because of God, and speak. Nevertheless, let him remember his own condition.”

After this the bishop prostrates himself before his seat with knees bent, and two clerics sing the Litany as noted above. At its proper place he rises and, turning toward those to be ordained, says:

“That you may deign to bene+dicere (‘bless’), sancti+ficare (‘sanctify’), and conse+crare (‘consecrate’) these men to be ordained: we beseech you, hear us.”

The bishop repeats this three times. [Col. 1011D] Afterward the Litany is completed by those clerics:

“That you may deign to preserve our pontiff in holy religion: we beseech you, hear us.”

The bishop then returns to his seat and remains there until the end of the Litany. When it has ended, he sits on his seat and hands an antiphonary to those being ordained, saying:

“See that what you sing with your mouth you believe in your heart, and that what you believe in your heart you prove by your works.”

Having said this, he rises and says the prayer over them, standing without the mitre.

The Lord be with you.

Let us pray, beloved brothers, to our Lord Jesus Christ for these his servants, who hasten, for love of him, to have the hair of their heads cut off, that he may give them the Holy Spirit, who will preserve the religious habit perpetually in them and defend their hearts from worldly impediment and secular desire; so that, just as their faces are changed, the right hand of God may grant them an increase of virtues, open their eyes from every spiritual or human blindness, and grant them the light of eternal grace. He who lives and reigns, God, forever and ever.

Clergy: Amen.

Bishop: Let us pray.

Deacon: Let us bend our knees.

Rise.

The bishop says the prayer:

He hands over the surplice:

Be present, O Lord, to our supplications, and graciously bless these your servants, upon whom we impose the religious habit in your name, so that, with your help, they may deserve to persevere devoutly in your Church and receive eternal life. Through the Lord.

The bishop sits and says:

You are the Lord who will restore my inheritance to me, etc. [Col. 1012B]

## Prayer for Blessing Brides

(From Codex Bibliothecae Caesareae theol. 149, ninth century, formerly of the monastery of Reichenau.)

Hear us, almighty and merciful God, so that what is administered by our office may rather be accomplished by your blessing. Through.

### Secret

Receive, we beseech you, O Lord, the offering presented for the sacred law of marriage, and, since you are the giver of the work, be its disposer. Through.

### Preface

It is truly right, just, and salutary. You have joined the covenants of marriage with the gentle yoke of concord and the unbreakable bond of peace, so that the chaste fruitfulness of holy marriages might preserve the adoption of sons. For your providence, O Lord, and your grace administer both, so that what the generation of the world produced for adornment, regeneration may bring to the increase of the Church. And therefore, with angels and archangels …

Therefore, O Lord, graciously receive this offering of your servants, which they offer to you for your servant N., whom you have deigned to bring to the state of maturity and to the day of marriage, for whom we pour forth humble prayers to your Majesty, that you may graciously deign to join her to her husband. We beseech you, O Lord, that you receive it favorably.

Before “The peace of the Lord,” he says the prayer:

Be favorable, O Lord, to our supplications, and kindly assist your institutions by which you ordained the propagation of the human race, so that what is joined with you as its author may be preserved with you as its helper. Through the Lord.

### Blessing

O God, who by the power of your strength made all things from nothing; who, after arranging the beginnings of the universe, created inseparable assistance for man made in the image of God, so that you might give the female body its beginning from male flesh, teaching that what had pleased you to establish from one should never be permitted to be divided.

O God, who consecrated the marital union through so great a mystery that you prefigured the sacrament of Christ and the Church in the marriage covenant.

O God, through whom woman is joined to man and the society principally ordained is endowed with that blessing which alone has not been taken away either by the punishment of original sin or by the sentence of the flood.

Look graciously upon this your servant, who, to be joined in marital companionship, seeks to be fortified by your protection. May the yoke of love and peace be upon her. May she marry faithfully and chastely in Christ, and, imitating holy women, remain steadfast. May she be lovable to her husband like Rachel, wise like Rebecca, long-lived and faithful like Sarah. May that author of transgression seize nothing in her on account of her deeds. Bound by the commandment of faith, may she remain joined to one marriage bed; may she avoid illicit contact; may she fortify her weakness with the strength of discipline. May she be truly modest, dignified, venerable for her chastity, and instructed in heavenly teachings. May she be fruitful in offspring, approved and innocent, and may they attain both the rest of the blessed and the heavenly kingdoms; may they see their children’s children to the third and fourth generation, and may they reach the desired old age. Through.

May the peace of the Lord be always with you.

### Communion

We beseech you, almighty God, accompany the institutions of your providence with devoted love, so that those whom you join in lawful society you may preserve in enduring peace. Through.

[Note: [Col. 1013D] The rubric still read today in the Roman Ritual, in the rite for celebrating the sacrament of marriage, looks back to a very ancient usage in which the Mass was, as it were, used in place of the nuptial blessing. We cited it in volume I, p. 258: substantially the same form is read in the Leonine, Gelasian, and Gregorian sacramentaries, both ancient and more recent—that is, in the present-day missals—with only this difference: in our sacramentary the rubric concerning the place and manner of the blessing itself is lacking: “And you say the Lord’s Prayer, and then bless her [the bride] with these words: ‘O God, who established the beginning of the growing world,’ etc.” The rubric of the Roman Ritual after the blessing of the ring reads as follows: “When these things have been completed, if the marriage is to be blessed, the parish priest shall celebrate the Mass for the bridegroom and bride as in the Roman Missal, observing everything prescribed.”]

## Prayer for Visiting the Sick

(From Codex Vindobonensis theol. 149, ninth century, the Augiensian Sacramentary.)

O God, who [—] your servant Hezekiah, etc.

Another:

Look upon your servant, O Lord, etc.

## Prayer over a Penitent

Grant us, O Lord, that, just as you were appeased by the prayers and confession of the publican, so you may be appeased by this your servant N.; and kindly incline toward his prayers, so that, persevering in tearful confession and petition, he may quickly obtain your perpetual mercy, and, restored to the holy altars and Sacraments, may again be devoted to heavenly glory. Through.

## Prayer for the Banquet of the Poor

[Col. 1013C]

Grant, O Lord, that your servant N. may obtain the assistance he hopes for, so that he who is remembered for [his care of] your poor or your churches may deserve fellowship with all the saints and with your blessed martyr Lawrence, whose example he has now followed. Through the Lord.

## Prayer for the Tonsure

Almighty and everlasting God, look graciously upon this your servant N., whom you have deigned to call to the new grace of tonsure, granting him remission of all sins and that he may receive a share in heavenly gifts. Through.

## Prayer for Making a Cleric

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that to this your servant N., who hastens to have the hair of his head cut off for love of Christ your Son, you may give the Holy Spirit, who will preserve the religious habit perpetually in him and defend his heart from worldly impediments and secular desire, so that, just as his face is changed, your right hand may grant him perfection of virtue, open his eyes from every human blindness, and grant him the light of eternal grace. Through.

## Prayer for Cutting the Beard

[Note: [Col. 1014D] In the Roman Pontifical, in a variant form, the following three prayers are also found.]

O God, by whose Spirit every creature rejoices when it grows to maturity, hear our prayers for this your servant N., rejoicing in the beauty of youthful age and at the first beginnings of tonsure. Hear, O Lord, so that, fortified in all things by the help of your protection, he may receive heavenly blessing and rejoice in the safeguards both of the present life and of the eternal one. Through.

## Prayer for Making a Deaconess

Hear, O Lord, our prayers, and send upon this your servant N. the Spirit of your blessing. Enriched by your gift, may she be able to obtain the grace of your Majesty and offer others an example of good living. Through the Lord.

## Prayer for Veiling the Handmaids of God

May your loving protection, O Lord, fortify your handmaids, so that the resolve of holy virginity which they have undertaken at your inspiration they may preserve unharmed under your protection. Through.

## Prayer for Making an Abbot or Abbess

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, and accompany with the gift of your grace your servant N., or your handmaid N., whom we have chosen for the governance of souls, so that, by your generosity, we may please you through our election of him or her. Through.

## Prayer in Time of War

Almighty and merciful God, we beseech you, make us quiet amid the storm of wars; for you will provide us with every good thing if you grant peace of mind and body. Through the Lord.

Another:

Almighty God, by the power of your Majesty, we beseech you, restrain the enemies of the Roman name, so that your people may rejoice in the integrity of faith and always exult in the tranquility of the times. Through.

## Prayer for Those Who Are Traveling

Hear us, O Lord, and may the journey of your servant N. always be protected by your help amid the dangers of this life. Through.

## Prayer for Asking for Rain

Pour heavenly waters upon your land, O Lord, which we see wasting away because of our iniquities, and water it with the benefits of eternal grace. Through.

Another:

Grant us, O Lord, we beseech you, saving rain, and graciously pour heavenly streams upon the dry face of the earth. Through our Lord.

Another:

Almighty and everlasting God, who save all and desire no one to perish, open the fountain of your kindness, and graciously pour heavenly streams upon the dry earth. Through the Lord.

## Prayer When It Rains Excessively

[Col. 1015A]

Lord God, who in the mystery of the waters of your salvation have established the Sacraments for us, hear the prayer of your people, and command the terrors of the overflowing rains to cease; turn the scourge of this element toward the fulfillment of your mystery, so that those who rejoice to have been reborn through regenerating waters may rejoice to have been corrected through these chastising waters. Through.

Another:

We beseech your mercy, almighty God, that you restrain the overflowing rains and graciously grant us the joyfulness of your countenance. Through.

## Prayer in a Threshing Floor

Multiply, O Lord, this threshing floor filled with gifts of your grain, and just as you are accustomed to grant your faithful the thirtieth, sixtieth, or hundredfold fruit, so also grant your servant N. more abundantly the gifts of the present time. Through the Lord.

## Prayer against a Plague among Animals

O God, who have supplied consolation for human labors even through diminished animals, we humbly beseech you to ensure that those without which human existence cannot be maintained may not perish from our uses. Through.

[Note: [Col. 1015D] The Roman Pontifical reads otherwise.]

## Prayer concerning Mortality

O God, who desire not the death but the repentance of sinners, we beseech you, turn your people back to yourself in mercy, so that, while they remain devoted to you, you may remove from them the scourges of your anger. Through.

[Note: [Col. 1015D] The same: “Look graciously upon those returning to you.”]

Another:

Receive your people, O almighty God, who flee from your anger to you, with paternal mercy, so that those who fear the scourges of your Majesty may deserve to rejoice in your pardon. Through the Lord.

## Prayer When Relics Are Raised

(From the same codex.)

Take away our iniquities from us, we beseech you, O Lord, so that we may deserve to enter the Holy of Holies with pure minds. Through the Lord.

## Prayer at the Dedication of a Church

[Note: [Col. 1015D] What follows is read partly in the Pontifical and partly in the Roman Missal.]

We beseech you, O Lord, graciously enter your house, and establish in the hearts of your faithful a perpetual dwelling for yourself, so that the one whose building sustains it may become illustrious through his habitation. Through.

## Prayer after the Altar Has Been Veiled

May your Holy Spirit descend, we beseech you, Lord our God, upon this altar, and may he sanctify the gifts of your people and graciously cleanse the hearts of those who receive them. Through.

## For the Masses

The God who invisibly contains all things, etc., as in the Roman Missal.

[Col. 1016B] Another:

O God, who are the author of the gifts to be consecrated to you.

Another:

O God, who [are the author] of every fitting arrangement.

### Secret

Almighty and everlasting God, [who have established] an altar dedicated to your name, etc.

### Preface

It is truly right, just, and salutary that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, through Christ our Lord. Through him we humbly beseech you to sanctify with heavenly dedication this altar prepared for holy uses, so that, just as you wonderfully received the offering of Melchizedek, the preeminent priest, so you may always deign to regard with favor the gifts placed upon this new altar; so that the people who have gathered in this holy house of your Church may, through these libations, be saved by heavenly sanctification and also obtain the perpetual salvation of their souls.

### Communion

We beseech you, O Lord, that in this place, which is dedicated to your name, etc.

[Col. 1015]

# Order of How a Church Ought to Be Dedicated

(From a ninth-century Turicensis codex, approximately.)

[Col. 1015D] First, before the bishop enters the church, twelve candles are lit around the church, and they put on the sacred vestments. When they have come to the church door, striking the ground upon the threshold with his crozier, he says the antiphon:

“Lift up your gates, O princes, and be lifted up, eternal gates.”

Psalm: “The earth is the Lord’s.”

They sing the entire psalm before the door, and, after the door has been opened, they enter and say:

“Peace to this house.”

Then the clergy begin the Litany. When they have come before the altar, the priests or Levites prostrate themselves upon the bedding until they say:

“Lamb of God, who takes away the sins of the world.”

When they have risen from prayer, the bishop does not say, “The Lord be with you,” but only, “Let us pray”; and the deacon says, “Let us bend our knees.” After they have prayed, he says, “Rise,” and the prayer follows:

“Be magnified, O Lord our God, in your saints, and appear in this temple of your building, so that you who work all things in the children of adoption may yourself always be praised in your inheritance.” Through.

Then the bishop begins at the left-hand eastern corner, writing upon the pavement with his crozier:

“A, B, C, D,”

as far as the right-hand eastern corner. [Note: [Col. 1015D] That is, the alphabet, as in Martène (*On the Ancient Rites of the Church*, vol. II, book II, ch. 13, p. 726), where it is reproduced in full, written in ancient Greek letters, each bearing above it its numerical value—I, II, III, and so forth. Compare the Roman Pontifical, *On the Dedication of a Church*, where both the Greek and Latin alphabets are prescribed to be written in the form of a cross.] Beginning again in the same way from the right-hand eastern corner, he writes “A, B, C, D” as far as the left-hand western corner of the basilica.

Then, coming before the altar, he says:

“O God, come to my assistance,”

with the Gloria but without the Alleluia.

Then he blesses salt and water mixed with ashes, and says this prayer:

“O God, who for the salvation of the human race have established the greatest Sacraments in the substance of water,” etc.

When it has been completed, he begins the antiphon:

“I will go in to the altar of God, to God who gives joy to my youth.”

Psalm: “Judge me, O God.”

While singing it with the psalm, he goes before the altar and pours at the base of the altar whatever remains of the water; the altar is wiped with linen. Afterwards he offers incense and pours oil upon the altar, making a cross in the middle and upon the four corners of the altar, singing the antiphon:

“Jacob set up the stone as a title, pouring oil over it.”

Psalm: “How lovely.”

The entire psalm is sung. He anoints it with his own hand, while another priest continually offers incense around the altar.

After the psalm has been completed, he again applies oil in the same way, singing the antiphon:

“The Lord sanctified his tabernacle and established it upon a firm rock.”

Psalm: “Our God.”

When that psalm has been completed, he applies chrism in the same way, singing the antiphon:

“Behold, the scent of my son is like the scent of a full field which the Lord God has blessed.”

Psalm: “Its foundations.”

Then, around the church, from the right to the left, he makes a cross with his thumb from that chrism upon the walls. Afterwards he makes a cross of incense over the altar. Then he says:

“Let us pray.”

The deacon, as above, says this prayer over the altar:

“Let us beseech the mercy of almighty God the Father, beloved brothers, so that by the present blessing he may sanctify this altar, which is to be consecrated for spiritual sacrifices, through the ministry of our voice, by which he is entreated; so that he may always deign to bless and sanctify upon it the offerings of his servants, placed there with the zeal of their devotion, and, appeased by spiritual incense, may stand ready as a prompt hearer of his household.” Through.

Again he says:

“Let us pray.”

The deacon, as above …

## The Blessing Follows

[Note: [Col. 1017D] In the Roman Pontifical the beginning varies; the following Preface also reads “lintean.”]

Almighty God, in whose honor we consecrate this altar under the invocation of your name, mercifully and favorably hear the prayers of our humility, and grant that the libations upon this table may be acceptable, pleasing, and rich to you, so that they may always be drenched with the dew of your Holy Spirit; and that at all times in this place you may relieve the anxieties of your household, which supplicates you, heal illnesses, hear prayers, receive vows, strengthen desires, and grant petitions. Through the Lord.

[Note: [Col. 1017D] Marten, in the cited work: “under the invocation of your name, we, though unworthy, consecrate.”]

Then he says the antiphon:

“Confirm, O God, what you have worked in us, from your holy temple which is in Jerusalem,”

with the Gloria.

Then the subdeacons or acolytes hold the linens, or all the ornaments of the church, or whatever sacred vessels ought to belong to the church for the worship of God; and the bishop blesses them in these words.

## Preface: Blessing of the Linens

[Note: [Col. 1018D] Marten, in the cited work, has “Blessing.”]

Lord God almighty, just as from the beginning you created useful and necessary things for human beings, and taught your servant Moses for forty days how to make what was suitable as pontifical and priestly garments, Levitical ornaments, and linens; and likewise, whatever Mary wove and made for the use of the ministry of the tabernacle of the covenant, so may you deign to sanctify and consecrate these linens for the use of your altar, to cover and wrap the body and blood of your Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, who lives and reigns, God, forever and ever. Amen.

[Notes: [Col. 1018D] “As the pontifical, priestly, and Levitical vestments, ornaments, etc.”; “Thus to sanctify, bless,” etc.]

## Other Blessings for Everything Used in the Basilica

[Col. 1018B]

Deign, O almighty God, King of kings and Lord of lords, Priest of all and Pontiff of the universe, through whom, together with the Father and the Holy Spirit, all things were made—Christ Jesus—deign to bless, consecrate, and sanctify these vessels with this altar, the linens, and the other vessels. Just as you once sanctified the offices of the tabernacle of testimony, together with the ark, the oracles of the Cherubim, curtains described as *alosis* (that is, winged), columns, candlesticks, the altar with silver bases, gilded boards, holocausts, sacrifices, the bronze altar with bronze vessels, tents, ropes, the oil of anointing, and all the other things which, as figures of our own things, you sanctified through the hands of holy priests; so now, abiding forever as the supreme Priest of priests according to the order of Melchizedek, as we have said, we pray from the heart that you bless, purify, consecrate, and perfect this paten, this chalice, and all the instruments of this altar of the church or basilica, which are held in our hands, and through which we believe that union between us and eternal unity is maintained without end in the highest passage. Through.

Then they go to the place where the relics had been during the preceding night with vigils. They raise them with the bier, singing hymns and praises with honor, accompanied by crosses, thuribles, and many lights. They come before the altar with a veil extended between them and the people. The bishop himself places the relics with his own hand in the altar, while they sing:

“The saints shall exult in glory; they shall rejoice upon their couches,”

with the psalm:

“Sing to the Lord; praise …”

The bishop then returns to the sacristy with the sacred orders, and they put on other solemn vestments. Meanwhile the altar or church is clothed, and the lights are kindled.

After all this, they begin the entrance antiphon:

“This place is awesome; this is the house of God and the gate of heaven, and it shall be called the hall of God,”

with the psalm and Gloria.

Meanwhile the bishop proceeds from the sacristy with his orders, as is customary.

## Prayer for the Mass

[Col. 1019A]

O God, who are the author of the gifts to be consecrated to you, pour out your blessing upon this house of prayer, so that all who call upon your name may experience the help of your protection. Through the Lord.

The reading follows.

Gradual: “This place was made by God.”

Verse: “I will worship toward your holy temple.”

The Gospel follows according to …

Offertory: “Lord God, in simplicity …”

### Prayer over the Offering

Almighty and everlasting God, pour out your grace upon this place, and show the gift of your help to all who call upon you, so that the power of these Sacraments may strengthen the hearts of all the faithful.

### Preface

It is truly right … Through Christ our Lord, through whom we humbly beseech you to sanctify with heavenly dedication this altar prepared for holy uses, and just as you wonderfully received the offering of Melchizedek, the preeminent priest, so may you deign to regard with favor the gifts placed upon this new altar; so that your people, gathering in this holy house of your Church, may be saved through these pure libations by heavenly sanctification and also obtain the perpetual salvation of their souls. Through him.

## Within the Canon

Therefore, O Lord, graciously attend to this offering of your servant or handmaid N., which they offer to you to be sacrificed at the sanctification of this temple. May the countenance of your charity illumine the hall which could not equal the merits of your blessed martyr N.; may it, by your favor, become worthy of your sacred and holy mysteries. May it be a temporary dwelling of eternal light. May no worldly filth or darkness possess this place, so that your people, coming here, may obtain the effect of their prayer and recognize this place as worthy of your Majesty, since they will have received what they asked for beforehand. May it be a remission of sins for those who build it, when it is received by you not according to the magnitude of their work but according to the devotion of those offering it.

And our days …

## At the Conclusion

May the Christian people obtain abundant benefits, we beseech you, O Lord, so that those who devoutly come to the thresholds consecrated to you in honor of the saints may receive both the supports of the present life and find the grace of eternal redemption. Through.

## Announcement When the Relics of the Holy Martyrs Are to Be Placed

[Col. 1019D]

Beloved brothers! Among the other solemn observances of virtues that pertain to the glory of Christ our Lord, he also granted this to his Martyrs, who, having accepted death in confession of his name, merited heavenly rewards: that, when their illustrious relics have been placed in accordance with the vows of the faithful, the integrity of the holy body should be believed to be present. Therefore we inform your Charity that on such-and-such a day, in such-and-such a place, the relics of that holy martyr are to be placed. We ask that you not refuse us your presence when we make this announcement.

# The Order Begins

[Col. 1020A]

## How Relics Are Placed in the Holy Roman Church

First the bishop goes into the church where the relics have been placed, performs the Litany, and gives this prayer:

“Take away our iniquities from us, O Lord, so that we may deserve to enter the Holy of Holies with pure minds.” Through.
