Afterwards he places the relics upon a paten and hands them to the presbyter in his arms, upon a shroud tied around his neck. He covers them, and they go out singing the antiphon:

“You shall go out with joy.”

The bishop proceeds to the new church where the relics are to be enclosed. Two or three ministers enter the church with him. He closes the church door, makes exorcised water, and says this prayer:

[Col. 1020B]

Let us pray.

O God, who for the salvation of the human race have established the greatest Sacraments in the substance of water, etc.

He puts chrism into it, mixes mortar from that water and lime, and makes the mortar with which the relics are to be enclosed. He baptizes the altar with that water, using a sponge once. Then the schola begins the Litany. When it has been completed, the bishop goes out and gives the prayer before the door:

“O God, who stand present as the Dedicator in every place of your dominion, hear us, we beseech you, so that this consecration may remain inviolable, and so that the whole assembly which supplicates may deserve the benefits of your gift.” Through.

[Note: [Col. 1019] The following prayers are also read in the Roman Pontifical.]

When this has been completed, he receives the relics from the presbyter and carries them with the Litany to the altar inside the church. He places them upon the new altar. Before they are enclosed, he puts chrism inside the confession, at the four corners in the form of a cross, saying:

“In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, peace to you.”

Response: “And with your spirit.”

Then he places three portions of the Lord’s body inside the confession, and three portions of incense. The relics are enclosed inside the confession. While they are being enclosed, they sing the antiphon:

“Under the altar of the Lord you have received seats; intercede for us, through him through whom you merited them.”

He places the tablet and gives this prayer:

Let us pray.

O God, who from the harmonious joining of all the saints establish for yourself an eternal dwelling, grant heavenly growth to your building, so that we who embrace the relics of those whose merits we venerate here with devoted love may always be helped by them. Through.

[Col. 1020D] Then he smears it with the lime that had previously been prepared. After it has been smeared, he makes a cross upon it with chrism, saying as above, and similarly makes a cross with chrism upon the four corners of the altar, saying as above. Then he veils the altar and gives this prayer:

Let us pray.

May your Holy Spirit descend, we beseech you, Lord our God, upon this altar, and may he sanctify the gifts of your people and cleanse the hearts of those who receive them. Through.

Then he sprinkles water with hyssop throughout the church. The tablet which he places over the relics must first have been secured with chrism, making a cross and saying as above.

When this has been done, the schola sings the entrance antiphon. After “Kyrie eleison,” “Glory to God in the highest” is said, and the Mass is completed in its proper order. Afterwards a public Mass is celebrated in that church for a week, until eight days have been completed.

## For Consecrating a Paten

We consecrate and sanctify this paten for making upon it the Body of our Lord Jesus Christ, making the sign of the cross for the salvation of us all; he lives and reigns with the Father and the Holy Spirit, God, forever and ever. Amen.

Then you make the sign of the cross with oil upon the paten:

May you deign, O Lord, to consecrate and sanctify this paten through this anointing and our blessing, in Christ Jesus our Lord, who lives and reigns forever and ever. Amen.

## For Blessing a Chalice

Let us pray, beloved brothers, that the Lord our God may sanctify his chalice, to be consecrated for ministry, through the inspiration of heavenly grace, so that he may adapt the fullness of divine favor to human blessing. Through.

Another:

Deign, O Lord, to pour upon this chalice, fashioned for the use of your mystery by the devout service of your servant, that sanctification with which you poured out the sacrament of the chalice of your servant Melchizedek; and what cannot be made by craftsmanship or metal may, through your blessing, become precious and worthy of your altars.

[Note: [Col. 1021C] Marten, in the cited work: “for the use of your ministry.”]

[Note: [Col. 1021C] P. R.: “the consecrated chalice.”]

[Note: [Col. 1021C–D] The use of glass chalices is otherwise shown by Aringhus and Bosius, *Roma subterranea*, book IV, chapter 28; Bonarotius, in his observations on glass vessels, p. 57; and the anonymous author of *On the Antiquity and Form of the Monogram of the Holy Name of Jesus*, Rome, 1747, preface, p. 12.]

## Chrismal Preface

[Note: [Col. 1021D] In Order III, in Marten, cited work, p. 703: “Blessing of the Eucharistic vessel. Let us pray, beloved and dearest brothers, that almighty God may deign to fill this bearer of the mystery of the body of his Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, with the blessing of sanctification, the protection of defense, and the gift of salvation, while we pray.” Through.]

[Col. 1021C]

Let us pray, beloved brothers, that almighty God may deign to fill this vessel bearing the ministry of the Body of your Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, with blessing, sanctification, protection, defense, and gift, while we pray. Through.

Another:

Almighty and everlasting God, inseparable Trinity, pour the help of your blessing into our hands, so that through our blessing this vessel may be sanctified and become, by the grace of the Holy Spirit, a new tomb of Christ’s body. Through.

## For Blessing Tablets

That singular propitiatory, which offered itself to us upon the altar of the cross to be sacrificed for our redemption; whose prefiguration the patriarch Jacob raised as a stone for a title, so that a sacrifice might be made and the oracle of heaven might be opened above—before you, O Lord, we humbly pour forth prayers, so that this material, polished from metals and to be imbued with heavenly sacrifices, may be ordered by him to be endowed with the abundance of his sanctification, who once wrote the law upon stone tablets. Through the Lord.

[Note: [Col. 1021D–1022C] In Order IX, Marten, cited work, p. 754: “Who, prefiguring it, …” But the reading in Order II, p. 694, is better: “By whose prefiguration … and the gate of heaven might be opened above,” etc.]

[Note: [Col. 1021D–1022C] Order IX: “so that he may receive, with the abundance of his sanctification, this polished material of metal to be imbued with heavenly sacrifices, who once wrote the law upon stone tablets. Through.” In Order II: “so that you may command this exposed material of metal, to be imbued with heavenly sacrifices, to be endowed with the abundance of your sanctification, you who once wrote the law upon stone tablets.”]

Another:

Almighty God, rational craftsman of all things, you fashioned among creatures the form of stone and metal for the service of your sacrifice, so that an altar might be prepared for your lawgiver. Graciously assent, founder of this mystery, so that whatever sacred thing is offered here may rise up for your name, advance in religion, and be founded upon hope and honored in faith. Through.

[Note: [Col. 1022D] The cited work: “Craftsman, who among creatures fashioned the form of stone and metal for the service of your sacrifice, so that your altar might be prepared for the lawgiver,” etc. Compare the Roman Pontifical, where the wording is clearer.]

[Note: [Col. 1022D] The cited work: “whatever is offered here.”]

[Note: [Col. 1022D] Or: “whatever sacred or consecrated thing may be offered,” as found in several orders in Marten.]

[Note: [Col. 1022D] The Roman Pontifical: “May it rest upon hope and be an honor to faith.”]

Another:

Holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, mercifully and favorably hear the prayers of our humility, and look upon this holocaust of your altar, which is proved not so much by fire, but may it kindle the grace infused by your Holy Spirit in honor of your sweetness, so that it may remain legitimate for us who receive and partake of it, may lift up the Eucharist in our inward parts, and grant eternal life.

[Note: [Col. 1022D] Order I, Marten: “which is tested not so much by fire.”]

[Note: [Col. 1022D] Or: “but the grace infused,” etc., “may kindle,” etc.]

[Note: [Col. 1022D] Or: “may adhere,” in the cited passage.]

## Preface

It is truly right. Holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, after the fall caused by the first man’s offense, you established for yourself the outlines of propitiatory offerings, so that the guilt which had preceded might be expiated in future times by the gift with which altars would be adorned and the temple honored. The temple which the first Noah prepared for you by his service, Abraham again furnished when he was about to sacrifice his son; afterwards the chosen Jacob raised and anointed it as a title.

May the piety of the world’s Redeemer be present, and may you deign to consecrate the mystery of these stones that have been purified, he who is the penetrable [or inner] one and the cornerstone. May you deign to consecrate them by the descent of your blessing, and may your Majesty, pleased, abide in these bronze objects with eternal regard. Whatever is sacrificed upon this in sacred rite, as the offering of Melchizedek, may this holocaust please you; and through it may whatever the vow has brought forth for sacrifice receive its reward.

You and, through our hands, pour forth the help of your blessing—you who yourself willed to be called the cornerstone and the stone cut out without hands. Bless and sanctify these stones prepared for divine worship, and appear as the sanctifier of this sacred mystery just as you are its founder. Through the Lord.

[Notes: [Col. 1022D–1023D] In Order I: “May the requested piety …”]

[Note: [Col. 1022D] Or: “You who are the inner stone …”]

[Note: [Col. 1022D] Or: “By the descent.”]

[Note: [Col. 1022D] Or: “And may you abide, pleased, with the regard of eternal Majesty.” Perhaps it should be read: “with the pleased regard of eternal Majesty.”]

[Note: [Col. 1023D] Or: “through our hands.”]

## Blessing of a Cross

Sanctify, O Lord, this sign of your Passion, so that it may be an obstacle to your enemies and become a standard for those who believe in you. Through.

We ask you, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, that you deign to bless this wood of your cross, so that it may be a saving remedy for the human race, the firmness of faith, the advancement (*profectuum*; P. R. *profectus*) of good works, the redemption of souls, and protection and defense against the savage darts of enemies. Through.

Almighty and eternal God, whose holy and terrible name, among other visible creatures, even fruit-bearing trees do not cease to praise and bless; who, as a figure of your only-begotten Wisdom, adorned the paradise of delight from the beginning with the tree of life, so that through its fruit you might instruct the first-created parent of our race, by a most sacred mystery, to avert death and preserve everlasting life; who, when through touching the forbidden tree we had incurred death instead of life, deigned mercifully through the innocent death of that same Wisdom coeternal with you—God and our Lord Jesus Christ—to call us back from death to life: we humbly beseech you to deign here to sanctify by your heavenly blessing this singular sign, which, in imitation of that first most sacred banner, your devout servant [name omitted] has raised in triumph through the precious blood of your Son [Col. 1023C], so that to all who here kneel and supplicate your Majesty there may be granted fuller compunction of heart and forgiveness of sins committed; and that, through the intercession of that most victorious Passion of your Son, they may both ask what is pleasing to you and more swiftly obtain what they ask. Grant, we beseech you, most merciful Father, in whom we live, move, and are, that as often as we behold with our eyes, or recall in mind, the triumph of divine humility which cast down the pride of our enemy, we may obtain confidence of strength against that enemy himself and a greater grace of humility devoted to you; so that, when at the dreadful judgment of your Majesty, with the elements trembling and the powers of heaven shaken [Col. 1023D], that glorious sign of our redemption appears in heaven, we ourselves may deserve to pass from death to life and behold the everlasting joys of the blessed resurrection. Through.

## For the Blessing of Episcopal Vestments

*(From the Rhenau manuscript, eleventh century.)*

### For the boots

Almighty God, author of all goodness: for restraining the snares of the ancient enemy, command that these boots be sanctified through the mystery of our humility, so that the truth of the Gospel may shine forth in their wearing and integrity of faith may be exercised in the mind. Through Christ our Lord.

### For the sandals

Bless, Lord Jesus Christ, these shoes of righteousness, which John saw the one clothed in the *poderes* wearing, so that whoever is clothed in these may be able to offer others a good example and serve you at all times with fear. You who live.

### For the gloves

We humbly beseech your immense clemency, almighty and most merciful God: just as the hands of your servants are outwardly covered with these gloves, so may they inwardly be sprinkled with the dew of your blessing, so that whatever is to be blessed or consecrated through them may be bless+ed and conse+crated by you. Through the same Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, etc.

### Blessing of the ring

God, beginning and end of every creature, in whom all things are enclosed, deign to bless+ and sancti+fy this ring, so that, as through it you grant your servant the insignia of honor, you may also grant him virtue and rewards, by which he may always retain the character of discernment and shine forth with the splendor of true faith. Armed also with the protection of the Holy Trinity, may he, as a soldier, steadfastly overcome the devil’s impregnable battle line. Through Christ our Lord.

### For the staff

Almighty and merciful Lord, who in your ineffable goodness assist the petitions of those who plead, and who, from the abundance of your compassion, grant the desire to ask: pour abundantly upon this staff, which we dedicate in your name as the sign of pastoral office, the power of your blessing. Let the shepherd marked by it guard with such care that he never permits anyone to stray from the unity of the Church, but restores what is broken, strengthens what is shattered, and preserves himself together with his flock whole and undefiled for you, so that he may never be separated from you as one unworthy. Through Christ our Lord.

### Blessing of the miter

Almighty and eternal God, who are the truth and fulfillment of the ancient figures, bless this symbolic insignia of the ancients, by whose horns Moses, your servant, figuratively declared both Testaments. Through Christ our Lord.

## For the Blessing of Priestly Vestments

### For the chasuble, dalmatic, and tunic

Almighty and eternal God, who through Moses, your servant, [commanded the making of] the episcopal vestments, etc.

### Blessing of the cloths

Lord God almighty, who from the beginning, etc.

### For albs, stoles, maniples, girdles, and amices

God, unconquerable author of power and creator of all things, etc.

### Elsewhere for the same purpose

Lord God, almighty Father, King and magnificent conqueror, who through our holy fathers, who pleased you in the priestly order, commanded vestments and ornaments of various kinds to be made for priests, and commanded priests serving you to be adorned in them: graciously hear our prayer, and deign with your holy right hand to bless+, conse+crate, sancti+fy, and puri+fy this alb, this chasuble, stole, planeta or *poderes*, girdle, and stoles, so that these garments may benefit your ministers, deacons, and priests for adorning and fulfilling divine worship. While serving at your holy altars cleanly and adorned in this sacred clothing, may they appear blameless in conduct and life, inwardly and outwardly; and may they be able to please you alone, the one God, with pure heart and clean body, serving blamelessly all the days of their life while following the examples of the holy fathers. When these sacred ministries have been completed according to your will, whenever it pleases you, may they deserve to receive the glory of the heavenly kingdom together with all those entrusted to them. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, etc.

### For the chasuble

God, fountain of mercy and justice, who ordained that the ministers of your work be clothed to the end in the garment of the chasuble, by whose protection all things are covered: grant our petitions, so that all who are clothed in this planeta, having within them the adornments of all the virtues, may possess above all the bond of peaceful charity, by which, with you granting it, they may accomplish what they desire. Through Christ our Lord.

### For corporals

Most merciful Lord, whose ineffable power is celebrated through wondrous hidden mysteries: grant, we beseech you, that these linens may be sancti+fied by the blessing of your favor, for consecrating upon them the Body of the Lord Jesus Christ, who lives and reigns with you, etc.

### Another blessing for the same purpose

Almighty and eternal God, bless these linens for covering and wrapping the body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ, who lives with you, etc.

## Blessing of the Paten, Chalice, and Other Ecclesiastical Vessels

*[Note: The following texts vary in P. R.]*

We conse+crate and sancti+fy this paten for breaking upon it the body of our Lord Jesus Christ, who suffered the cross for the salvation of us all, and who lives with the Father and the Holy Spirit, etc.

### Another for the same purpose

Almighty and eternal God, author of the legally prescribed sacrifices, who commanded that among them a mixture of fine flour be carried in golden and silver patens to your altar: deign to bless+ and sancti+fy this paten for the administration of the Eucharist of Jesus Christ, your Son, our Lord, who chose to be sacrificed for our salvation and that of us all to you, God the Father, upon the gallows of the cross; who lives and reigns with you, etc.

Here he makes the sign of the cross with chrism over the paten, drawing his thumb from the opposite side lengthwise and breadthwise, and says:

Deign, Lord, to consecrate and sanctify this paten through this anointing and through our blessing, in Christ Jesus our Lord, who lives with you.

### For the chalice

Peace be with you.

And with your spirit.

Let us pray, most beloved brothers, that God and our Lord Jesus Christ may sancti+fy this chalice, which is to be consecrated for the use of his ministry, through the inspiration of heavenly grace, and may grant it the fullness of divine favor in accordance with human blessing. He who lives.

*[Note: In Ordo VIII, Martène, p. 745: “And that which is human …”]*

### Another blessing

Deign, Lord, to bless+ this chalice, fashioned through the devout service of your servant for use in your ministry, and pour upon it that sanctifi+cation with which you poured upon your servant Melchizedek the sacred chalice. May what has been fashioned by art or through the work of metal become worthy of your altars, sanctified by your blessing, through Christ our Lord.

*[Note: Read “to pour upon it.”]*

*[Note: In Ordo IV, p. 715: “And what cannot be made worthy of your altars by art or metal, let it become worthy and sanctified through your blessing. Through …”]*

Here he makes the sign of the cross with chrism inside the hollow, drawing his thumb from the opposite side lengthwise and breadthwise, and says:

Deign, Lord, to conse+crate and sancti+fy this chalice through this anointing and our blessing, in Christ Jesus our Lord, who lives with you.

### Blessing over an already consecrated chalice

Almighty and eternal God, pour, we beseech you, the assistance of your blessing into our hands, so that through our blessing this vessel may be sanctified and, by the grace of the Holy Spirit, may be made a new tomb of the body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ. Through Christ our Lord.

Then he sprinkles the paten and chalice with blessed water and says:

In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, may this be blessed.

### For the Eucharistic vessel

Let us pray, most beloved brothers, that almighty God may deign to fill this vessel, bearer of the body of his Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, with the protection of his blessing, through the gift of his Son, our Lord, and through the power of the Holy Spirit, through Christ our Lord.

After this prayer has been said, the vessel is sprinkled with blessed water, and it is said:

In the name of the Father and of the Son, as above.

## Blessing of Banners and Images

Almighty and eternal God, who are the blessing of all and the strength of those who triumph, graciously look upon the prayers of our humility, and sancti+fy with heavenly blessing this banner, which has been prepared for military use, so that it may be strong against hostile and rebellious nations and be surrounded by your protection. May it be terrifying to the enemies of the Christian people, a support to those who trust in you, and a sure confidence of victory. For you are God who crushes wars and always add secure and desired heavenly protection to those who hope in you. Through our Lord.

### Blessing of images

We beseech you, almighty God, by your unfailing clemency, that, gracious and favorable, you may deign to bless+ this honored instrument of your saints by extending the right hand of your Majesty, so that whoever, whether awaiting their patronage nearby or recalling them from afar, invokes your mercy with faithful devotion in any necessity may enjoy the consolation and assistance desired. Through our Lord.

## Blessing of Linens, Vestments, and Sacred Vessels

*(From Codex Vindobonensis theol. 359.)*

Then the subdeacons or acolytes hold the linens, or all the ornaments of the church and sacred vessels—whatever appears to belong to the worship of God and the Church—and the pontiff blesses them according to this rite.

### Blessing of a corporal

Let us pray. Almighty and eternal God, bless this linen for covering and wrapping the body and blood of your Son, our Lord Jesus Christ. Who with you …

*[Note: From theological manuscripts, no. 277, alone.]*

### Another

Lord God, who have now deigned to sanctify this kind of material, when you deigned to be wrapped in it—the body of our Lord Jesus Christ, your Only-begotten, in his blessed Passion—grant, we beseech you, through the same Lord, to us, although unworthy servants, that this present linen may become holy through heavenly blessing and suitable for the Lord’s tomb, namely, your altar, so that the body and blood of the same Lord Jesus Christ, who is the life of all who faithfully receive him, may be placed upon it in a manner pleasing to you. He lives and reigns through all ages of ages. Amen.

### Another

Most merciful Lord, whose ineffable power and whose mysteries are celebrated through wondrous hidden things: grant, we beseech you, that this linen may be sanctified by the blessing of your propitiation, for consecrating upon it the body and blood of God and our Lord Jesus Christ. Who with you.

### Blessing of linens

Lord God almighty, who from the beginning created useful and necessary things for human beings, and taught your servant Moses for forty days to make episcopal vestments and ornaments and linens for your priests and Levites, or even those things which Mary wove and made for the use of your altar, for covering and wrapping the body and blood of your Son, our Lord Jesus Christ. Who lives and reigns with you.

### Another blessing of a linen

*[Note: From Codex theol. 27. Another prayer.]*

God, who desire the service of those who worthily serve you, graciously look upon the service of our humility, and sanctify and consecrate by the blessing of heavenly power these linens prepared for the uses of your service, so that your Holy Spirit may descend upon them, bless the offering of your people, and graciously refresh the hearts and bodies of those who receive it. Through.

Hear our prayers, Lord, and deign to bless and sanctify this linen prepared for the use of the sacred ministry. Through.

### Another blessing for linens and for all vessels and instruments used by the Church

Almighty and eternal God, King of kings and Lord of lords, priest of all and pontiff of the universe, through whom, together with the Father and the Holy Spirit, all things were made: Christ Jesus, deign to bless, consecrate, and sanctify these vessels together with these altar linens and all the rest.

Just as you once sanctified, through the hands of holy priests, the services of the tabernacle of testimony with the ark of the oracle, namely the cherubim enclosed by veils, the columns, the lampstands, the golden altar, the silver bases, the gilded boards, the burnt offerings, the victims, the bronze altar with its bronze bases, the tents, ropes, anointing oil, and the other things that prefigured our own time: so now, remaining forever as the high priest of priests according to the order of Melchizedek, may you bless, purify, consecrate, and perfect these vessels and all the instruments of this church’s altar, which are held between our palms, and through which we believe that there is established between us and eternal unity, in the supreme passage, without end.

Through you, Jesus Christ, who with the Father, in the unity of the same Holy Spirit, are God …

*[Note: Blessing of all ornaments intended for the use of the church or altar. From manuscript theol. 277 alone.]*

Almighty and eternal God, who from the beginning created useful and necessary things for human beings, and willed that temples made by human hands be dedicated to your holy name and called places of your dwelling; who through your servant Moses decreed that episcopal, priestly, and Levitical vestments, as well as ornaments of every other kind, be made for the worship and beauty of your tabernacle and altar: graciously hear our prayers, and through the service of our humility deign to purify, sanctify, bless, and consecrate all these ornaments of various materials, prepared for the use of this basilica or altar in honor and glory of you, so that they may be suitable for divine worship and sacred ministries, and that in them, in the making of the body and blood of Jesus Christ, your Son, our Lord, they may offer you worthy service. Who lives with you.

### Blessing of priestly or Levitical vestments and of those serving in the following order

Almighty God, who through your servant Moses decreed that episcopal and Levitical vestments be made for carrying out their ministry in your sight and for the adornment and praise of your name: graciously attend to our invocations, and deign, through the service of our humility, to purify, bless, and consecrate these priestly garments of your servant and priest, while your grace waters them from above with its immense blessing, so that they may be suitable and blessed for divine worship and sacred ministries.

May those of your priests or Levites who are clothed in these sacred garments deserve to be defended from every assault or temptation of evil spirits. Grant that they may serve and adhere to your ministries fittingly and worthily, and persevere in them peacefully and devoutly. Through.

### Blessing of albs, planetas, stoles, and girdles

Lord God, almighty Father, King and magnificent conqueror, who through our holy fathers, who pleased you in the priestly order, commanded vestments and ornaments of various kinds to be made for priests and commanded priests serving you to be adorned in them: graciously hear our prayer, and deign with your holy right hand to bless and sanctify this planeta of your servant N., or *poderes*, together with the girdle and stole, and to purify them, so that these garments may benefit your ministers, Levites, and priests for adorning and fulfilling divine worship.

While serving at your holy altars cleanly and adorned in these sacred garments, may they appear blameless in conduct and life, inwardly and outwardly; and may they be able to serve you alone, God, with pure heart and clean body, blamelessly all the days of their life, following the examples of the holy fathers. When these sacred ministries have been completed according to your will, whenever it pleases you, may they deserve to receive the glory of the heavenly kingdom together with all those entrusted to them. Through.

### Blessing of stoles

Lord God almighty, who from the beginning created useful and necessary things for human beings, and commanded your servant Moses to make episcopal vestments and other ornaments and linens for priests and Levites for the use of the tabernacle of the covenant, and filled him with the Spirit of wisdom to accomplish this: deign to sanctify, bless, and consecrate this ornament for use in your ministry, and graciously fill the ministers of your altar who wear it with the sevenfold Holy Spirit. Make them blessed with the stole of chastity and the garment of eternal joy, and clothe them with immortality, together with the fruit of good works suited to their ministry. Through.

## Eucharistic Preface, That Is, of the Vessel in Which the Eucharist Is Stored

Let us pray, most beloved brothers, that almighty God may deign to fill this vessel, bearer of the body of his Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, with the protection of his blessing, with the gift of his Son, our Lord, and with the power of the Holy Spirit.

### The blessing follows

Let us pray. Almighty God, inseparable Trinity, pour the assistance of your blessing into our hands, so that through our blessing this vessel may be sanctified and, by the grace of the Holy Spirit, may become a new tomb of the body of Christ. Through.

## Preface for Consecrating a Paten

Let us pray, beloved brothers, that the blessing of divine grace may consecrate and sanctify this paten for making upon it the body of our Lord Jesus Christ, who suffered the cross for the salvation of us all. Who with the Father …

### Another

We consecrate and sanctify this paten for making upon it the body of our Lord Jesus Christ, who suffered the cross for the salvation of us all. Who with the Father …

Then he makes the sign of the cross with holy chrism over the paten and says:

Deign, Lord, to consecrate and sanctify this paten through this holy blessing, in Christ Jesus our Lord. He lives and reigns.

## Preface of the Chalice

Let us pray, most beloved brothers, that God and our Lord may sanctify this chalice, which is to be consecrated for use in his ministry, through the inspiration of heavenly grace, and grant it the fullness of divine favor in accordance with human blessing.

### The blessing follows

Deign, Lord, to pour upon this chalice, fashioned through the devout service of your servant for use in your ministry, that sanctification with which you poured upon your servant Melchizedek the sacred chalice. May what cannot be worthy of your altars through art or the work of metal become precious and sanctified through your blessing. Through.

And he makes the sign of the cross with chrism over the chalice.

*[Note: “Titulus,” the name for a title, derives from the very ancient practice of making the sign of the cross in sacred places or churches; hence the churches themselves were called “titles.”]*

*(From both sources.)*

First let salt and water be blessed. Then let the blessing of the cross follow.

Bless, Lord, etc.

Another: We beseech you, etc.

Forever and ever.

The Lord be with you.

And with your spirit.

V. D. Eternal God, whose holy …

### Another

*(From manuscript Th. 277.)*

We humbly invoke you, Lord, and beseech you that this sign of the holy Cross may be salvation to those who believe in you through the Passion of your cross; and that through the sign of your holiness it may be the sign of the living God, the sign of salvation, the sign of the blessed Trinity, the sign of heavenly glory, and the sign of the Savior Jesus Christ our Lord.

This is the cross of Christ the Savior, the cross of the patriarchs, the cross of the prophets, the cross of the holy apostles, the cross of Christ’s martyrs, the cross of the Church of God, and the cross of all who believe in the holy and perfect Trinity. Through.

### Another

*[Note: Another. God, who, while prescribing on Mount Horeb to Moses, your servant, commandments to be observed by your people, instructed him how to build your holy temple, and taught him to make sacred vessels to be brought to your altar after the likeness of heavenly vessels: we pray that you may sanctify by the outpouring of your Holy Spirit and by heavenly blessing this chalice, in which we shall celebrate the most sacred mysteries; that you may hold it pleasing and acceptable and bless it, so that it may be worthily joined to your vessels, render service acceptable to you, and be worthily consecrated for your mysteries. Through our Lord, in the unity of the same [Spirit].]*

Lord, we beseech you, who grant salvation to souls through the sign of your cross: in the places and houses where this cross is fixed, may demons, unclean spirits, and the pestilential enemy be driven away; may they be free from diseases and impurities; and may all hostile powers, through knowledge of you, be driven far away.

### Blessing of a metal cross

God of the glory of the exalted Sabaoth, etc.

*[Note: The same prayer is found both in the old Roman order and in the new Roman Pontifical. See, following P. Joseph Catalanus, the commentary on the Roman Pontifical, vol. II, pp. 274 ff. II, against those who place crosses and other sacred images on altars without a prior blessing, not without detriment to ecclesiastical discipline. ## Blessing of the Thurible

Lord God, who, when a harsh fire was devastating the children of Israel because of their rebellious obstinacy, deigned to hear your priest Aaron, who stood praying between the living and the dead and offering incense to you, and freed the people from the fire: bless, we beseech you, this thurible, and grant that whenever we offer incense to you in it, you may make us, through Christ himself, an acceptable temple of good fragrance. Who with God.

### Another

*(From Codex Vindobonensis theol. 277, twelfth or thirteenth century.)*

Holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, when in the desert you punished the murmuring of the profane multitude with flame, and your priest Aaron, having filled the thurible with fire from the altar, humbly pleaded with your Majesty for the people’s deliverance, you were appeased by the incense and graciously granted his prayers. Bless, we beseech you, this thurible by your Majesty, and grant that the incense offered to you in it may be the flight of demons, the repulsion of phantoms, and the departure of unclean thoughts; and may our prayer, through its fragrance, always be acceptable to you. Through.

*(From Codex bibliothecae Caesareae theol. 359.)*

Through.

*[Note: Another from Codex theol. 277. Through the same …]*

### Another prayer

God, who through the Holy Spirit deigned to reveal to your servant Moses what you had ordained as necessary for the worship of the sanctuary, among which you commanded that fragrant incense should continually remain for the service of your Church on account of religion, so that, mystically, its fragrant sweetness might reveal to us the meaning of spiritual virtues: we beseech you, almighty God of immense Majesty, deign with your right hand to bless this creation, fashioned from a mixture of various substances, so that through the power of your holy name it may wonderfully drive away every phantom-like assault of unclean spirits and expel every disease by restoring health wherever the smoke of its aromatics has breathed forth, and may it continually give off to you, the Lord, a most fragrant sweetness.
