## Preface for the Consecration of Reliquary Chests

Let us pray, most beloved, etc.

Consecration in the form of a preface: Inestimable God, etc.

Another: Lord God almighty, who …, etc.

### Another prayer

Holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, who through your Only-begotten Son willed that the blessed apostle Paul be called a chosen vessel, and who, through his preaching and declaration, granted the same hope to all the members of our Lord Jesus Christ who are faithful: “You are the temple of the living God, and the Spirit of God dwells in you.”

We humbly implore you to pour the dew of divine sanctification upon this chest, skillfully joined and adorned to receive the members, remains, or pledges of your saints. Grant not only that you may hear those who come into their presence and humbly pray there, but also that those who carry away something from their memorials as a blessing, or faithfully receive it, may graciously be consoled, refreshed, protected, and rewarded by the grace of your boundless mercy. Through.

### Another, mentioned above in passing

We beseech you, almighty God, by your unfailing clemency, that, gracious and favorable, you may deign to bless this honored instrument for the relics of your saints by extending the right hand of your Majesty, so that whoever, whether awaiting their patronage nearby or recalling them from afar, invokes your mercy with faithful devotion in any necessity may quickly enjoy the consolation and assistance desired. Through.

## Preface of the Ciborium, That Is, the Canopy of the Altar

Let us pray, most beloved brothers, to God, ruler and governor of all ages, that, mindful of all the sins and crimes of my youth and ignorance, or of my transgression, he may graciously and mercifully deign to bless and sanctify this instrument, fashioned for the honor of your name, by the illumination of his countenance.

### Consecration

Almighty and eternal God, who commanded your servant Moses to place two cherubim over the ark of the covenant, which they were to protect with wings extended toward one another, their faces turned toward the mercy seat: we beseech your ineffable clemency that you may pour your holy blessing upon this covering of your venerable altar, on which your Only-begotten Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, who is the propitiation for our sins, is sacrificed by the hands of the faithful; and beneath which the bodies of your saints—who truly were receptacles of your ark, namely of the Holy Spirit—are placed.

Through the same Son consubstantial with you, who has been made for us by you sanctification and redemption, may every falsehood of the ancient enemy and his followers be driven away by the power of the same Spirit of truth. Together with all the ornaments belonging to this canopy, hanging from it or placed beneath it, deign to bless and consecrate them, and preserve them for a long time for the protection of the pledges of the saints and for strengthening or multiplying the vows of your faithful, with the same Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, granting this. He lives and reigns with you, God, in the unity of the same Holy Spirit, forever and ever.

### Consecration of a smaller traveling ciborium

*[Note: Here “ciborium” is called “repositorium” shortly afterward. The word differs little, and, as I think, has the same meaning as the “conditorium” in the ancient Roman order apud Mabillon: a place or small vessel in which the Eucharist was customarily stored, as Mabillon noted. It is therefore rightly distinguished from the ciborium—that is, the canopy of the altar—whose consecration is given above. The latter was spread over the altar for the sake of ceremonial display and ornament, as we have shown elsewhere, Part I, Dissertation III, chapter I, no. 9. From these larger ciboria hung what are called ciboria in modern usage, in which the Eucharist itself, or its vessel or pyx, is kept. In former times these were called *peristeria*, as we recalled in the same place from the testament of Perpetuus, bishop of Tours, who among other bequests left to the presbyter Amalarius “one common silk chest, also a *peristerium*, and a silver dove for the *repositorium*.” The reference is to the Eucharist, or even to relics, as we showed in the same place; and this is the general statement in the consecratory prayer of the smaller traveling ciborium, when this *repositorium* is called prepared for sacred uses.]*

*(From Codex theol. 277.)*

Let us ask the indulgence of almighty God, so that, setting aside the offenses of human weakness, through the gift of your customary mercy he may deign, through the Only-begotten Word—namely, his power and wisdom in the Spirit of sanctification—to consecrate this *repositorium*, prepared for sacred uses. Through the same, in unity with him.

## Consecration of a Cemetery

*(From Codex Vindobonensis theol. 277, twelfth or thirteenth century.)*

Let seven psalms be sung, and let four candles be lit.

*[Note: Nothing is said here about the holy water that is to precede the rite, although the Pontifical of Egbert of York prescribes it, as it prescribes many other things: first, with blessed water, the bishop and his clergy are to go around the entire cemetery while Psalm 50, “Have mercy on me, O God,” is sung together with the antiphon “Sprinkle me,” etc.

Thus Pope Callistus II writes to the bishops of Mâcon and Chalon concerning the consecration of the altars and cemetery of the monastery of Trenor: “We consecrated the altars, blessed the cemetery, and, pouring blessed water there, ordered boundaries to be set all around.”

In the thirteenth-century Pontifical of Christian, archbishop of Mainz, the blessing of salt and water, ashes, and wine is prescribed, as in the consecration of a church.

Joseph Catalanus gives an extremely brief form in the Roman Pontifical, vol. II, p. 222, from a manuscript Pontifical of the Church of Bari preserved at Rome in the Angelica Library of the Order of the Hermits. It is called the blessing of the *polyandrium*, or cemetery, as it is also entitled shortly afterward by the same author in the same place, Ordo II, from the manuscript Pontifical of William Durandus, preserved in the Vatican Library, no. 4744. It begins as follows:

“Although many assert that the blessing of a cemetery is not necessary, saying that for this purpose circuits outside the church and the sprinklings of the cemetery performed when the church is dedicated are sufficient”—an assertion that conflicts with ancient liturgical monuments and with both more recent and ancient practice. We read that this practice was already so longstanding and religiously observed in the sixth century that it caused anxiety and perplexity for the abbess when the body of Saint Radegund, queen of the Franks, was involved:

“What shall we do,” she asks Saint Gregory of Tours, as he himself records in *On the Glory of the Confessors*, chapter 106, “if the bishop of the city does not arrive? For the place in which she ought to be buried has not been consecrated by priestly blessing.”]*
God, who are the creator of the whole world, etc.

Another. Almighty and everlasting God, threefold majesty and one Godhead, Father and Son and also Holy Spirit, author of justice, giver of forgiveness, bestower of good things, source of holiness, distributor of spiritual gifts, and gracious receiver of all who come: mercifully grant that we may bless and sanctify this cemetery, established in honor of your name. You blessed the land which your servant, the blessed patriarch Abraham, purchased from the sons of Hebron for the purpose of burial [Col. 1033C–1034A]; and you granted the Israelite people a land of promise enduring through the ages. Kindly bestow upon the bodies of your male and female servants entering this cemetery a resting place and protection from every assault of evil spirits, so that after the resurrection and reunion of souls and bodies, by your gift and grant, they may deserve to receive everlasting blessedness. Another. Lord God, eternal shepherd, etc.

## Blessing of a Grave and Burial Place

We ask you, holy Lord, almighty and everlasting God, that you graciously bless and sanctify this grave and the burial place established in it, so that it may be a saving remedy for the one resting there, the redemption of his soul, and protection and defense against the savage darts of the enemy. Through [Col. 1034B].

Another. May this dwelling, Lord God, be sanctified through our supplication, and may the unclean spirit be driven from it through the power of our Lord Jesus Christ. May the resting of the bodies that will afterward rest here be peaceful, while your majesty, Jesus Christ, protects and preserves them. Who with [the Father and the Holy Spirit lives and reigns].

Another. Be present, Lord, to our supplications, and in your ineffable compassion come to our aid, though we presume upon nothing in our conscience, so that what the confidence of our merits does not possess may be supplied by the unconquerable abundance of your gifts. Through.

## Blessing of a Portable Altar Table

[Note: [Col. 1034D] The Venerable Bede calls this “an altar table dedicated in place of an altar” in *Ecclesiastical History of the English People*, book V, chapter 11. He is speaking of the two Ewalds, who, while traveling, offered sacrifice to God daily as the victim of the Savior.]

(From both theological manuscripts 359 and 277.)

We ask you, almighty God, for unfailing mercy [Col. 1034C], etc.

[Note: [Col. 1034D] In the same codex this prayer is placed after others and is entitled “Preface of the portable altar table”; the rest corresponds.]

Another. Let us pray with rejoicing vows to almighty God, dearly beloved brothers: he who spreads faith throughout the whole world and gathered the Church; he who is the stone cut from the mountain without hands and solidified the angular structure [Col. 1035A]—may he illuminate this stone in serenity and, watered with eternal light, enrich it with manifold and diverse spiritual gifts, so that upon it he may bless and receive the consecrated sacrifice of his body. Who with [the Father and the Holy Spirit lives and reigns].

## Consecration

Hear us, our God, and willingly receive the vows of our prayers. Sprinkle this altar, prepared for the celebration of the divine mysteries, with the fragrance of heavenly ointment; pour upon it the spices of divine sanctification. As you dedicated the stone erected by the patriarch Jacob by pouring ointment upon it, and, by the ladder in angelic visions, foreshadowed the stages of the Church, so also send upon this stone, which is to be fitted to the altar, the grace of heavenly blessing. Thus, while the mysteries of the sacred body and blood of your Only-Begotten Son are consecrated upon it for you, may sins be erased from those who ask, and everlasting grace flow upon those who deserve it. Through.

Then, taking the altar table, let him sprinkle it with blessed water, adding the fragrance of incense, and confirm it with chrism, saying:

“In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.”  
“Peace be with you.”  
“And with your spirit.”

## ORDER FOR THE DEDICATION OF A BAPTISTERY

[Note: [Col. 1035D] First let blessed water be made with a litany. Then let the prayer “O holy God, fountain…” be said. Another follows, which is later entitled “Consecration of the Font: O holy God, this baptistery…”; then another beginning “Multiply…”; then another beginning “Be propitious…”.]

(From Codex Vindobonensis theolog. 277.)

Almighty and everlasting God, fountain, etc.

### Consecration of the Font

Almighty and everlasting God, sanctify this baptistery, dedicated by heavenly visitation, through the illumination of the Holy Spirit, so that all whom this font will wash may, by your gift, obtain pardon for all sins through a threefold washing [Col. 1035C]. Through.

Another. Multiply your blessing, Lord, and strengthen our faith through the gift of your Spirit, so that those who descend into these waters may deserve to be enrolled in the book of life, to be handed over to you, God the Father, in the resurrection. Through.

## ORDER FOR THE DEDICATION OF A BAPTISTERY

(From the manuscript Codex Vindobonensis, Imperial Library, theological collection, tenth or eleventh century, no. 359, formerly 351.)

First let blessed water be made with a litany; then let the prayer be said.

Almighty and everlasting God, fountain of all virtues and fullness of graces, deign to consecrate this vessel prepared for holy baptism by the presence of your Majesty, so that, although you are wholly present everywhere, we may also here perceive you present in response to our prayers. Through.

Another. Be propitious, Lord, to your household, and graciously sanctify the vows of our humility. Preserve all who are to be reborn in this font through universal adoption. Through.

Then let him sprinkle the baptistery itself with blessed water, adding the fragrance of incense. Afterward let the pontiff return to the church door, where litanies or praises are celebrated around the bier, and before the doors let him say this prayer, signifying the door and the Church:

God, who are the author of the gifts to be consecrated to you, pour your blessing upon this house of prayer, so that all who invoke your name here may experience the help of your protection. Through.

Then, carrying the bier with great honor, together with the relics, crosses, and lights, let them go around the church, while the clergy follow singing these antiphons or responsories, and let the people, together with the women and children, sing “Kyrie eleison.”

A. Rise, saints, from your dwellings; sanctify these places, bless the people, and keep us sinful human beings in peace. *Aevia.*

A. Walk, saints of God, to the appointed place which [Col. 1036B] was prepared for you from the beginning of the world.

A. The streets of Jerusalem will rejoice, and all its lanes will sing a song of joy.

A. Your saints, Lord, have accomplished a wondrous journey, serving your commandments, so that they might be found unharmed in mighty waters. The earth appeared dry, and in the Red Sea a way was opened without hindrance.

V. For he struck the rock, and the waters flowed, and the torrents overflowed.

R. They handed over their bodies to punishments for God’s sake and deserved to receive everlasting crowns.

V. These are they who came from the great tribulation and washed their robes in the blood of the Lamb.

And they deserved it.

R. My saints, you who endured the contest in this world [Col. 1036C], I will repay you for the labors.

V. Come, blessed of my Father; receive the kingdom.

The reward.

R. The saints will rejoice in glory; they will exult in their resting places.

V. Let the righteous feast and exult in the sight of God, and delight in gladness.

R. The righteous will shine like the lily and like the roses of Jericho before the Lord.

V. But the righteous will live forever, and their reward is with the Lord.

And likewise.

When all this has been performed in due order and he has returned again to the church door, the pontiff, after silence has been made, is to address the people concerning ecclesiastical honor and concerning the tithes or offerings of the churches, and concerning the annual anniversary of the dedication of this church [Col. 1036D]. The lord and founder of the church himself is also to be admonished concerning its endowment and concerning what honor or care he ought to show to the church and to the presbyter. When he has professed that he wishes to act in every respect in this manner, the pontiff, asking the Lord to confirm these things, is to say this prayer before entering the church:

[Note: [Col. 1035D] A testimony to the very ancient practice of consecrating baptisteries is found in Sidonius Apollinaris, book IV, letter 15, to Elaphius: “For,” he writes, “you write that the baptistery which you were formerly building can now be consecrated.” That altars were once joined to baptisteries, when the newly baptized immediately also received communion of the Lord’s body and blood, we learn from Saint Paulinus’s poem *Natales* X, where he describes a baptistery:

“While the bishop carries there the twofold gifts of Christ,  
in the two entrances he consecrates the venerable rite,  
joining the holy sacraments to the cleansing bath.”

Of this kind is the Pisan baptistery, which Mabillon describes in his *Italian Journey*. To the same category belong the oratories which Anastasius the Librarian says certain pontiffs established in baptisteries.]

[Col. 1037A] Enter mercifully, we ask, Lord, into your house, and build for yourself an everlasting dwelling in the hearts of your faithful. Grant that this house, which stands solemn through your dedication, may become exalted through your dwelling. Through.

Then let the pontiff take the bier with the presbyters and enter while the schola sings the antiphon:

Enter, blessed of God. A dwelling for your seat has been prepared for you by the Lord. The faithful people also follow our procession with joy, so that you may pray for us to the majesty of the Lord.

With the responsory: “The saint of God gave you…”

A. The glory of the Lord is blessed from his place. *Aevia.*

With the verse: Sing to the Lord a new song; his praise is in the assembly of the saints.

When they have entered, with a veil stretched between the people and the altar, the pontiff is to place the relics in the altar, and the presbyters who are with him are to sing the antiphon:

A. The saints will exult in glory; they will rejoice in their resting places.

With the psalm: Sing to the Lord a new song; his praise is in the assembly of the saints.

Before the relics are enclosed, let him say this prayer:

God, who stand as the merciful and gracious dedicator in every place of your dominion, hear us, we ask, and grant that the consecration of this place may remain inviolable, and that the whole of holy Church, which entreats you, may deserve the benefits of your gift. Through.

When this has been completed, let him place chrism in the *confessio* at the four corners in the form of a cross, saying:

“In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.”  
“Peace be with you.”  
“And with your spirit.”

Then let him place three portions of the Lord’s body [Col. 1037C] in the *confessio*, and three portions of incense. Then let the relics be enclosed in the *confessio*. As they are enclosed, let them sing the antiphon:

You have received seats beneath the altar of the Lord; intercede for us with the Lord who chose you.

With the psalm:

The saints will exult in glory; they will rejoice in their resting places.

[Note: [Col. 1037D] It is frequently read in ritual books that three portions of Christ’s body are to be placed in an altar being dedicated. Durandus, in *Rationale of the Divine Offices*, chapter 7, no. 23, says that this is to be done with the Lord’s body when no relics are available; the Pontifical of Durandus likewise states: “When relics are lacking, let him place the body of Christ.”]

## Prayer for Dedicating the Altar after the Relics Have Been Placed

God, who sanctify altars to be dedicated to your name, grant, we ask, that, through the intercession of blessed N., the fullness of your Spirit may descend here—though our frailty does not merit it—sanctifying our gifts and obtaining for us the forgiveness of your mercy. Through.

Then, taking the altar table, let him confirm it underneath with chrism in the form of a cross, saying:

“In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.”  
“Peace be with you.”  
“And with your spirit.”

Then let him place the table over the relics and say this prayer:

God, who from the whole joining together of the saints establish an everlasting dwelling for your Majesty, give heavenly growth to your building, and grant that we who embrace the relics of those whose remains are here with pious love may always be aided by their merits. Through.

Then let him coat it with the lime that had previously been prepared. After it has been coated, let him make a cross above it with chrism, saying:

“In the name…”

Let him place chrism on the four horns of the altar, as written above, making the cross and singing:

A. The bodies of the saints have been buried in peace, and their names will live forever.

Add: Glory to the Father.

Then let the deacons clothe the altar, and let the schola sing the antiphon:

A. Surround Zion, Levites; clothe the altar of the Lord in white garments. And you, singing a new hymn, say: Blessed be God.

V. God is wondrous in his saints.

And: Glory to the Father.

Another A. Your saints will cry out in the veil, Lord. *Aevia, aevia, aevia.*

Afterward let him offer incense, and let the verse be said:

Let every land adore you, God, and sing psalms to you.

Prayers:

The house of the Lord has been founded upon the summit of the mountains. It has been well founded above all the hills.

The Lord is in his holy temple.

The Lord’s seat is in heaven.

“My house,” says the Lord, “will be called a house of prayer.”

The saints will exult in glory.

They will rejoice in their resting places.

Let the righteous exult in the sight of God.

And let them delight in gladness.

Precious in the sight of the Lord

is the death of his saints.

[Col. 1038C] Arise, Lord; help us.

And deliver us for the sake of your name.

Lord, hear my prayer.

And let my cry [come to you].

The Lord be with you.

And with your spirit.

Then let the pontiff say this prayer:

May the Holy Spirit, we ask, descend upon this altar, sanctifying the gifts of your people and purifying the hearts of those who receive them. Through.

Another. Almighty and everlasting God, sanctify this altar dedicated to your name with the blessing of heavenly power, and show the gift of your aid to all who hope in you, so that here the power of the sacraments and the fulfillment of vows may be obtained. Through.

Then let the pontiff return to the sacristy until the church has been decorated and the lights have been lit. Let the cantor begin the antiphon for the Introit: “This place is awesome.” Let the pontiff proceed with his ministers, as is customary on feast days, and let Mass be celebrated solemnly as prescribed in the sacramentary, with “Glory to God in the highest.” Afterward, throughout the entire week, public Masses are to be celebrated in the church until eight full days have passed.

[Note: [Col. 1038D] This rubric is frequently read in the Gregorian Sacramentary and in orders for the dedication of a church. It reflects a very ancient rite, which Eusebius testifies was observed at the dedication of the basilica of Jerusalem in book IV of *The Life of Constantine*. Sidonius Apollinaris likewise mentions the weekly festivities at the dedication of the church of Lyon in book IX, letter 3, to Bishop Faustus.]

## ORDER FOR BLESSING A CHURCH BELL

(From the manuscript Codex Vindobonensis, Imperial Library, tenth or eleventh century, no. 359, formerly 351.)

[Col. 1039A]

First the litany is said, then the six penitential psalms:

“Have mercy on me, God”;  
“God, in your name”;  
“Have mercy on me, God, have mercy on me”;  
“May God have mercy on us”;  
“O God, come to my aid”;  
“Incline your ear, Lord.”

## Reconciliation of a Violated Church

(From Codex Vindobonensis theolog. 277, twelfth or thirteenth century.)

First let the bishop come before the church itself with the clergy and people, and let him say this prayer:

Almighty and merciful God, who [to priests], etc.

Another. Take away from us, etc.

Then let the pontiff enter the church with the clergy and litanies. When these things have been completed, he says: Let us pray.

And the deacon: Let us bend our knees.

After a short while: Rise.

Prayer: God, who [the ancient sin], etc.

Then let him bless water and salt mixed with wine and ashes, and let him go around the interior of the church three times, sprinkling it and singing the antiphon:

Sprinkle me, Lord.

Psalm: Have mercy on me, God.

While washing and purifying the contaminated places, let him say this Preface:

God, forgiver of crimes, etc.

Consecration: God, whose goodness, etc.

The antiphon follows:

Strengthen this, O God.

Psalm: Let God arise and let his enemies be scattered.

Before the relics are enclosed, the pontiff says:

Let us pray.

And the deacon:

Let us bend our knees.

Rise.

The following prayer is then said:

God, who stand as merciful and gracious dedicator in every place, etc.

Then let the relics be restored to their place. See the rest under the dedication of a church.

And let them sing:

Antiphon: Strengthen this, O God [Col. 1039C],

with the verse: I will proclaim the name.

And: Glory to the Father.

The following is:

God, who [your Church], etc.

## Blessing of a New Church

(From Codex Vindobonensis theolog. 277.)

God, who promised that the gates of hell would never prevail against your principal Church, built upon the mystical rock of apostolic dignity [Col. 1040A], graciously remove from it every error, so that what the presumption of falsehood raises up against it may be overcome by the Spirit of truth. Guide it, we ask, by heavenly governance, so that, having always been prepared in your presence before the beginning of the world, it may remain under your direction until the promised fullness and glory. Build for yourself an everlasting dwelling in the hearts of your faithful, so that this people, with faces cast down to the earth, asking for your blessing, may receive from you an eternal reward. Grant, we ask, Lord, that this basilica, whose dedication rites we now proclaim [reading uncertain: *incenia*], which stands solemn through your dedication, may always become splendid through your dwelling. Through.

## Blessing upon a Gift Offered by Someone to the Church in Its Honor

[Note: [Col. 1039D] This title is written incorrectly in the Gallican Sacramentary edited by Mabillon, volume I of *Museum Italicum*, part II, page 389, from the Bobbio monastic codex. There it reads: “Blessing of everything offered in the church.” From the same source.]

[Col. 1040B]

God, by whose word and power all things were made, and by whose gift we have received whatever we possess for the remedy of life, we humbly and earnestly beseech you: from the seat of your majesty come as sanctifier of this offering of the faithful. Receive from the hand of your servants the gift offered, and, blessed by your clemency, let it remain consecrated for the use of this sanctuary.

May these things be willingly accepted in your sight, just as the gifts once offered by Abel, your fosterling, or by Melchizedek pleased you. Since they strive to adorn your church with the highest acts of service in honor of your love, repay them, Lord, with great things for small ones. As you accept their devotion, fill them with faith, cherish them with forgiveness, protect them with mercy, destroy adversity, and grant prosperity. Let them possess in this world the example of good action, zeal for charity, and the effect of holy love; and in the future, with the holy angels, may they obtain the everlasting kingdom. Amen.

[Col. 1039]

## Blessing of Salt and Water

### Exorcism of Salt Follows

[Col. 1039C]

I exorcise you, creature of salt, by the living God, by the holy God, by the Lord of all creation, who spoke with the divine voice of his mouth to his disciples, saying: “You are the salt of the earth”; and who through his apostle Paul graciously said: “Let your speech be seasoned with the salt of wisdom.” May you therefore become exorcised salt, for emptying and driving out from this sign of the Church the enemy and all the power of his corruption. May all who take from you be sanctified in soul and body; and wherever you have been sprinkled, may you grant everyone forgiveness of sins, health of mind, and protection of salvation. In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, who is to come.

## Blessing of Salt

[Col. 1040C]

We implore the strength of your power, holy Lord, almighty and everlasting Father. Among all the necessities which you commanded to be created through Jesus Christ our Lord, you graciously granted no small grace to salt, so that by it all the things which you created for human food through the same Son, our Lord, may be seasoned.

We humbly beseech you to look upon this salt, so that through the power of your Majesty it may receive strength against all unclean spirits. May it drive from this sign of the Church, and from every place where it has been sprinkled at your invocation, whatever may be pestilential; may it display the full effect of salvation; may it repel every deception [Col. 1041A] or portent of the enemy; and may it cause every kind of monster to flee far away.

May it restrain every heaviness and fantasy, and through the sign of the cross of your Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, provide the most faithful protection to those who desire it. Through the same [Lord].

### Exorcism of Water

Depart, unclean spirit, from all the sacraments through which our faith makes use of the religious ministry. Do not allege the guilt of crime, since you acknowledge the Savior’s power. It is not confidence in merit but in command, although the power of the mystery itself [the text is incomplete].

Therefore I address you, creature of water, through the one Lord, so that, understanding the preservation of sensible motion, you may not refuse to submit to the service by which we strive to appease God. Cleanse yourself from every communion with demons, from every fellowship of iniquity; destroy every stain of fantasy, capable of receiving the Lord’s protection. Having obtained the grace of sanctification, serve equally your Creator and ours, cast out from this Church all wickedness of evil spirits, and wherever you are sprinkled, bring an abundance of holy blessing.

Through our Lord and Redeemer Jesus Christ himself, who with the Father and the Holy Spirit lives and reigns forever and ever. Amen.

## Blessing of Water

Bless, Lord, this water with heavenly blessing, and let there stand over it, etc., as in the Pontifical under the blessing of a bell.

Here let salt be placed in the water.

[Col. 1041C] Let this mixture and consecration of salt and water be made in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.

### Prayer after the Mixture

Almighty and everlasting God, you distinguished for us the creature of living water which you established, so that you might provide simple liquid for washing and salty solidity for seasoning: thus filthy things might be washed, insipid things seasoned, harmful things removed, and original error corrected toward the way of salvation.

Although unworthy, we beseech you in the exercise of our ministry: may this mixture of salt and water, made in your name, be sanctified by the gift of your mercy for purifying this sign of the Church. Since you provide it ministerially as useful for baptism, hostile to guilt, suited to wisdom, and opposed to error, make it sanctified through the sanctification of your Holy Spirit. Let no contamination render unclean what we believe has been made blessed by your majesty.

Rather, through you, may it display so full an effect of sanctification that, wherever it has been cast by hand after your name has been invoked, or taken up in any manner, all ambushes of the opposing power being driven out and dispersed, not only may the devil’s devices be driven from that place and come to nothing, but the guardianship of the holy angels may also remain and abide there always [Col. 1042A]. Through you, almighty God, who reign with your Son and the Holy Spirit forever and ever. Amen.

After this, these psalms are sung:

“Praise the Lord, my soul”;  
“Praise the Lord, for he is good”;  
“Praise the Lord, Jerusalem”;  
“Praise the Lord from the heavens”;  
“Sing to the Lord a song”;  
“Praise the Lord in his saints.”

While they are being sung, let the pontiff wash the bell with blessed water and blessed salt, making crosses on it with holy oil, and let him say this prayer:

God, who through blessed Moses the lawgiver commanded silver trumpets to be made, etc., as in the Pontifical up to the words: “Before the banner of the holy cross depicted upon it.” There the prayer ends, omitting what is added in the Pontifical: “to whom every knee is bent,” etc.

[Col. 1042B] Then let him wipe it with a clean cloth, and let the antiphon be sung:

The voice of the Lord is over the waters; the God of majesty has thundered. The Lord is over many waters.

Psalm: The voice of the Lord in power, to the end of the psalm, with the Gloria.

After this let him touch it with chrism seven times on the outside and four times within, and let him say this prayer:

Almighty and everlasting God, who before the ark of the covenant, etc., as in the Pontifical.

Then let fire, incense, and myrrh be placed in the thurible, and let the bell be raised over the thurible so that it gathers all the smoke. Let the antiphon be said:

O God, your way is in holiness; what god is as great as our God? The waters saw you, O God.

To the end of the psalm, with the Gloria.

Almighty Ruler Christ, when, according to the assumption of the flesh, you were sleeping in the boat and, when a storm arose, the seas were thrown into confusion, you were immediately awakened and, at your command, they were stilled. In your kindness come to the aid of the needs of your people. Pour upon this bell the dew of the Holy Spirit, so that at its sound the enemy may always flee; the Christian people may be invited to faith; the hostile army may be terrified; and the people called together through it may be strengthened in the Lord.

And just as the Holy Spirit, delighted by David’s harp, descended from above, and as, when the long-haired Samuel sacrificed a lamb in his burnt offering, the king of eternal rule scattered the opposing crowd by the sound of the winds, so, while the sound of this little vessel passes through the clouds, may the assembly of your Church be consoled; may the crops be preserved by angelic hands; and may the minds and bodies of believers be saved by everlasting protection [Col. 1042D]. Through you, Savior of the world.

## Major Blessing of Water and Salt

[Note: [Col. 1041D] Among the Greeks, the blessing of baptismal water, formerly celebrated on the vigil and now on the very day of the Epiphany of the Lord, is called the “great sanctification.” See volume II, *Disquisitions*, V, chapter 1, no. 18, where the ancient custom of solemn baptism among us, also on the feast of the Epiphany of the Lord, and the present blessing of water are discussed; the latter agrees with this in several respects.

There, on page 439, we cited a passage from Saint Chrysostom concerning the marvelous power of this water kept in the houses of unbelievers. The same author, volume VIII of the works, page 433, mentions the common custom of washing the hands before entering the church. For this purpose, according to the same testimony and others in volume III, page 289, fountains were placed in the atria of churches—such a fountain can still be seen in the neighboring principal church of Freiburg—just as vessels filled with blessed water are now used at least for sprinkling.

The custom of washing the hands during the actual assembly has continued from the beginnings of the Church in both Churches. Concerning Greek, Maronite, Armenian, and other Eastern presbyters, this may be seen in Renaudot. Concerning the faithful approaching holy communion, Saint Chrysostom says in his homily *On Anger and Discord*: “You do not dare touch the sacred host with unwashed hands, even if you are oppressed by a thousand necessities; therefore do not approach with an unwashed soul.”

Saint Caesarius of Arles likewise says in sermon 229: “All men, whenever they desire to receive communion, wash their hands.” Men evidently received the holy host with the bare hand, whereas women received it on cloths or napkins, as Mabillon noted from the *Life of Saint Wiborada*, fifth century, Benedictine volume, page 51. A very clear testimony to this distinction is found in Saint Cyril of Jerusalem, *Mystagogical Catechesis* III; and at the beginning of *Catechesis* V there is testimony concerning the common practice of the faithful washing their hands before prayer.

Concerning this, Tertullian says in chapter 11 of *On Prayer*: “Besides, what reason is there for undertaking prayer with washed hands while the spirit is unclean?” That this was a common custom we learn from homily XLIII of Saint Chrysostom on the First Letter to the Corinthians, volume X, page 405. The same author testifies in his writings on John, volume VIII, pages 313 and 433, that the hands were also washed before the sacred reading.]

(From the manuscript Codex Vindobonensis, Imperial Library, theological collection, tenth or eleventh century, no. 359, formerly 351.)

God, come to my aid, with the Gloria.

A. This is the generation.

Psalm: The earth is the Lord’s.

Bring offerings to the Lord.

The same.

A. According to your great mercy.

Psalm: Have mercy on me, God, according to [your mercy].

Then the litany:

Lord, have mercy.

Christ, have mercy.

Christ, hear us.

Holy Mary, pray for us.

Then:

The Lord be with you.

And with your spirit.

### Prayer

God, whose ancient miracles we perceive shining forth in every age: what you bestowed upon one people through the power of your right hand for deliverance from Egyptian persecution, you now accomplish for the salvation of the nations through the regeneration of water. Grant that the fullness of the whole world may pass into the sons of Abraham and into the dignity of Israel. Through the Lord.

### Reading from the Letter of Blessed Paul the Apostle to the Corinthians

Brothers, we do not want you to be unaware that all our fathers were under the cloud, and all passed through the sea, and all were baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea, and all ate the same spiritual food, and all drank the same spiritual drink. For they drank from the spiritual rock that followed them; and the rock was Christ.

Prayer: A helper in time of need.

V. For not forever.

### According to Matthew

At that time Jesus said to his disciples:

“You are the salt of the earth. But if the salt loses its savor, what will it be good for thereafter except to be thrown outside and trampled by people? You are the light of this world. A city set on a mountain cannot be hidden. Nor do they light a lamp and put it under a bushel, but on a lampstand, so that it may shine for all who are in the house. Let your good light shine before people, so that they may see your good works and glorify your Father who is in the heavens.”

## Blessing of Water

The Lord be with you.

Let us pray.

I exorcise you, creature of water, by the living God, by the holy God, by the God of all creation, so that you may show yourself clean against every illness and every ambush of the enemy. Wherever you are sprinkled, may that house, with God propitious, be defended, just as the houses of the Hebrews were defended by the sign of the blood of the lamb.

Thus, Lord, may the houses of your male and female servants be defended through the sprinkling of this water. In the name of him who commanded fountains to flow by his word, I exorcise you, water. In his name I exorcise you, who led the children of Israel through the midst of the sea. In his name I exorcise you, who walked upon you with his feet. [Col. 1043D] In the name of him whom John baptized in you, I exorcise you, so that every spirit of error and all demonic phantasms may be driven away and separated through your sprinkling. Through the power of our Lord Jesus Christ, who is to come to judge.

Another. I exorcise you, creature of water, in the name of God the almighty Father and in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that every unclean spirit and assault of Satan may be separated from this creature of water. Therefore, become exorcised water, for driving away every phantom of the enemy and for uprooting and eradicating the enemy himself. In the name of God the almighty Father and in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, who is to come.

Another. But I adjure you, creature of water, by the living God, by the holy God; by him I adjure you who in the beginning separated you from the dry land. I adjure you by the living God, who commanded the fountains of paradise to flow, ordered them to issue into four rivers, and commanded them to water the whole earth. I adjure you by him who cleansed Naaman the Syrian of his leprosy in you, and who sweetened you by the laying on of the hands of the prophet Elisha.

Therefore become holy water, blessed water, water that washes away filth and cleanses sins. I adjure you by the living God to show yourself clean and to retain no fantasy within you. Rather, become exorcised water, so that wherever you are sprinkled—whether in a house, in the corners of rooms, in a field, upon people, upon cattle or beasts of burden, or if anyone tastes you—you may become for that person a defense of life and a remedy of health.

May the devil himself also be driven far away and put to flight, as heaven has been placed far from earth, light from darkness, the just from the unjust, and the sweet from the bitter. Thus may that unclean spirit be separated from every dwelling of God’s male and female servants, and from those places where this water has been sprinkled, through the word and power of our Lord Jesus Christ, who is to come.

## Blessing of Water

I exorcise you, creature of water, in the name of God the almighty Father and in the name of his Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, so that you may become exorcised water for driving away every power of the enemy. May you be able to uproot and eradicate the enemy himself together with his apostate angels. Through the power of our Lord Jesus Christ, who is to come.

Another. God, who for the salvation of the human race [the greatest sacraments], etc.

## Blessing of Salt

I exorcise you, creature of salt, by the living God, by the true God, etc.

## Blessing of Salt

[Col. 1044D]

I exorcise you, creature of salt, by the living God, by the holy God, by the God of all creation, who commanded you to be thrown into the water by the prophet Elisha so that the sterility of the water might be healed; who spoke with the divine voice of his mouth to his disciples, saying: “You are the salt of the earth”; who through his apostle Paul graciously said: “Let your speech be seasoned with the salt of wisdom.”

Therefore become exorcised salt, for emptying and driving out the enemy and all the power of his corruption. In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, who is to come to judge the living and the dead.

Another. Bless, almighty God, this creature of salt with your heavenly blessing, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ and in the power of your Holy Spirit, for driving away the enemy. May you, Lord, sanctify it by sanctifying it and bless it by blessing it. May it become for all who receive it a perfect medicine, remaining in the entrails of those who consume it. In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, who is to come.

[Col. 1045B] Another. Invisible God, immeasurable God, who are diffused throughout all things, we humbly beseech your piety and mercy through the holy and awesome name of your Son: pour your blessing upon this creature of salt through the power of invisible operation. When the animals which you have graciously granted for human needs receive or taste it, may this blessing and sanctification of yours preserve them unharmed and, while you protect them, guard them from every assault of the tempter. P.

Another.

We humbly implore your immense clemency, almighty and everlasting God, that in your goodness you may bless and sanctify this creature of salt, which you have granted for the use of the human race, so that it may be health of soul and body for all who take it; and so that whatever is touched or sprinkled with it may be free from every impurity and every attack of spiritual wickedness. Through.

## Blessing of Both Together

Here he blows three times and mixes them.

[Col. 1045D] God, seated upon the sublime throne above the Cherubim and Seraphim, to whom every depth of the abyss and every breadth are manifest; God, by whose eternal laws all nature is contained; God, before whose will whatever resists is weak, and whatever the hostile and unclean spirit rages [against] has been overcome by your holy words; God, who destroy the strength of the wicked and extinguish, through your servants, the enemy’s assaults that oppose us: we humbly implore you, Lord, to look favorably upon our defense, and to sanctify this creation of salt and water with the blessing of your grace. Make them effective for the necessary purifications, so that whatever is sprinkled with their liquid may become empty and free from every uncleanness of unclean spirits. Let no pestilential disease be present there, let nothing troubled by any terror remain there; let your prayer of invocation drive out from that place every demon and every hostile power through the sprinkling of this creation of your salt and water. Do not permit any snares of the devil or of his servants to harm or injure those places where reliance is placed upon your help and the power of your name is invoked. Through [Christ our Lord].

Another. We ask you, Lord, grant your saving remedy over this creation of salt and water, so that wherever it is applied it may contribute to the health of soul and body. Through [the Lord].

Another. Eternal Lord, almighty God, we, unworthy though we are, beseech you in the performance of our office: may this mixture of salt and water, sanctified in the name of your clemency, when it has been dispensed by our hands or taken in any manner, cause all the devices of demons to be driven away and expelled from that place, and may the protection of the holy angels remain there perpetually. Through the Lord.

The Lord be with you. And with your spirit. Lift up your hearts. We have them with the Lord. Let us give thanks to the Lord our God. It is right and just.

## Preface

[Col. 1046B] Lord God of heaven and earth, to whose power all things are subject, by whose word all things have been brought forth: send your Holy Spirit upon this creation of water, so that it may become sanctified water in the name of God the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Water itself has recognized you, the highest salvation and your overseer. Therefore we humbly beseech you to hear and have mercy upon our prayers, so that wherever this water has been sprinkled at your command for aspersion and purification, that house may possess joy, hope, and perpetual honor; so that every envy of the malicious may be driven out and separated, through the power of our Lord Jesus Christ, whom the angels praise and do not cease to cry out, saying: Holy, Holy, Holy, Lord God of hosts.

Let us pray.

[Col. 1046C] Instructed by saving commandments and formed by divine teaching, we dare to say: Our Father. Deliver us, we ask you, Lord, from every evil, past, present, and future, and guard us in every good work, through our deliverer, the Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you. I believe in God.

## BLESSING OF BOTH TOGETHER

God, author of unconquered power and King of unsurpassable dominion, etc.

## MINOR BLESSING OF SALT AND WATER

I exorcise you, creation of salt, by the living God, by the true God, by the holy God, by the Lord who commanded you through Elisha, etc.

## BLESSING OF SALT AND WATER  
*(From manuscript Vind. theol. 277, twelfth or thirteenth century.)*

[Col. 1046D]

Incline to my aid, O God. O Lord, hasten to help me. With “Glory be to the Father.” Lord, have mercy. Christ, have mercy. Lord, have mercy. Our Father. I believe in God. And the litany follows, if you wish.

### Blessing of Salt

I exorcise you, creation of salt, in the name of God the almighty Father, and in the charity of our Lord Jesus Christ, and in the power of the Holy Spirit. I exorcise you by the living God, by the true God, who created you for the protection of the human race and commanded you to be consecrated by his servants for the people coming to faith. Therefore we ask you, Lord our God, that this creation of salt may, in the name of the Trinity, become a saving sacrament for driving away the enemy; may you, Lord, sanctify it by sanctifying it and bless it by blessing it, so that it may become for all who receive it a perfect medicine, remaining in their inward parts, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, who is to come.

### Reading from the Book of Kings

In those days the men of the city said to Elisha: “Behold, the situation of this city is excellent, as you yourself see, but the water is extremely bitter and the land is barren.” He replied: “Bring me a new vessel and put salt in it.” When they had brought it, he went out to the spring of the waters, cast salt into it, and said: “Thus says the Lord: I have healed these waters, and there shall no longer be death or barrenness in them.” Thus the waters were healed to this day, according to the word of Elisha, which he spoke.

According to John.

[Note: [Col. 1047D] The present blessing of water at Epiphany does indeed have the Gospel concerning the baptism of John, but according to Luke; the three prayers that follow agree with the present rite, from which the purpose of the blessing in the homes of the faithful may be inferred.]

At that time John saw Jesus coming toward him and said: “Behold the Lamb of God; behold him who takes away the sins of the world. This is he of whom I said: ‘After me comes a man who has been made before me, because he was before me, and I did not know him.’ But so that he might be manifested in Israel, for this reason I came baptizing in water.” And John bore witness, saying: “I saw the Spirit descending like a dove from heaven, and it remained upon him. But the one who sent me to baptize in water said to me: ‘Upon whomever you see the Spirit descending and remaining upon him, he is the one who baptizes in the Holy Spirit.’ And I saw and bore witness that this is the Son of God.”

## BLESSING OF WATER

I exorcise you, creation of water, by the living God, by the holy God, by the Creator of the whole age, so that you may show yourself clean against every disease and the enemy’s snares; so that wherever you are sprinkled, that house may be protected by God’s favor, just as the houses of the Hebrews were protected by the sign of Christ’s blood. Thus, Lord, may the house of your male and female servants be protected. In the name of him I exorcise you who led the children of Israel through the midst of the sea. In the name of him I exorcise you who walked upon you with his feet. In the name of him I exorcise you whom John baptized in you, so that every spirit of error and all fantasies of demons may be driven out and separated through this water of sprinkling, through Christ our Lord, who is to come to judge.

Another. Grant, Lord, your saving remedy over this creation of salt and water, so that wherever it is applied it may contribute to the health of soul and body. Through our Lord. [Col. 1047D] Here blow three times in the form of a cross, mix the salt and water, and say these words:

I exorcise you, creation of salt, by the living God, who commanded you through the prophet Elisha to be cast into water, who spoke with divine voice through his own mouth to his disciples, saying: “You are the salt of the earth.” He said through the apostle Paul: “Let your heart be seasoned with salt.” Therefore, make the salt exorcised for overcoming the enemy and every assault of the demon, through the power and name of our Lord Jesus Christ, who is to come to judge the world—and you, enemy, by fire.

The Lord be with you. [Col. 1048A] And with your spirit. Lift up your hearts. We have them with the Lord. Let us give thanks to the Lord our God. It is right and just.

### Preface

It is truly right and just, fitting and saving, always and everywhere to give you thanks, Lord God of heaven and earth, to whose power all things are subject, by whose word all things were created. Send forth, send forth your Holy Spirit upon this creation of water, so that it may become sanctified water in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. May it recognize you as the highest salvation and perpetual overseer. To you we humbly pray and ask that you hear and have mercy upon our prayers, so that wherever this water has been sprinkled at your command for aspersion and purification, that house may possess joy, hope, and perpetual honor, and so that all malicious and envious persons may be driven out and separated.

Again I address you, water, which bear the likeness of light. You are beneath the sky; you are above the sky. You are beneath the earth; you are above the earth. Over you I invoke the holy and wondrous name of God, who by his power suspended you above the heavens, gathered you on the earth, and mingled you in the sea; who commanded you to rain through secret, clear, swift winds; who gave you for human use as a washing of the flesh and supplied drink through you to the thirsty; and over whom the Spirit of the Lord was borne and is still borne.

I adjure you by the voice of flashing thunder and by the power of the dread heavenly King. I adjure you by the wood of the mystery, through which water, when struck, immediately became sweet. I adjure you by him who created all things: do not despise the voice of my humility, but drive out every shadow, every Satan, and all the devilish machinations of unclean spirits, whether of the dead by violence [Note: [Col. 1048D] In printed editions: “of the condemned.”], or of wanderers, or arising from the invocation of magical art, or the devices of enchanters, or of dragons, birds, and vipers. For the Lord Jesus Christ, Son of the living God, commands you that, as soon as you have been sprinkled in the name of God almighty Sabaoth, whether in a house, vineyards, among cattle, in sown fields, in any creature, or given as a drink to a person afflicted with illness and struck by the infestation of the wicked, you immediately drive out and exclude every evil, so that the person may more quickly be saved through the power and name of our Lord Jesus Christ, who can neither be spoken, written, nor counted, whose name is God.

You are he who, through your angel, Lord, showed the spring to Hagar and gave thirsty Ishmael drink from it; who heard in Mesopotamia the prayers of Abraham when he was a boy and fulfilled all the desires of his heart; who commanded your servant Moses in the desert to strike the rock, bring water from it, and water the people; who sweetened bitter water by the insertion of wood. Thus may you deign to bless this water in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, so that wherever it has been sprinkled in your name, you may drive out all the savage assaults of the enemy.

We also ask that, just as you deigned to send the angel Raphael to the house of Raguel and bound the demon Asmodeus, so by a similar kindness you may protect this house, so that as soon as it has been sprinkled, that demon may never have any power there, either over the soul or over those dwelling in the same house, but may depart confused and restrained. Through Christ our Lord, through whom [is your majesty].

## BLESSING OF SALT

Holy Lord, Creator of all creatures and craftsman of all nature, the one master of all that brings forth, origin of peoples and usefulness of virtues: by whose providence you solidified, through heavenly fire, the flowing waters in this creation also, so that, mixed with other things for human use, it might season them and preserve them uncorrupted for longer use—grant it, Lord, as we implore you, a substance from your blessing, so that, into whose inward parts it penetrates, it may drive out and expel from them whatever the deceptions of error, confusion, wickedness, and devilish temptation have poured in; once every assault of our enemy has been driven away, may only that which was made by you remain in the human being.

Another. Holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, we humbly beseech you to bless this creation of salt, which you have granted for the use of the human race, so that those who taste it may not die forever, but may taste you, be strengthened in you, and through your grace be found worthy to come to eternal gifts, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, who is to come.

## BLESSING OF SALT FOR CATTLE

[Col. 1049C] Invisible and ineffable God, who are diffused through all things, we humbly beseech your piety and mercy through the holy and awesome name of your Son: pour into this creation of salt your blessing and the power of invisible operation, so that when the animals whom you have deigned to grant for human needs receive or taste it, your blessing and sanctification may restore them unharmed and, while you protect them, guard them from every assault of the tempter. Through.

Another. Through this creation of salt, deign, Lord, to defend our cattle from ravenous wolves, robbers, disease, deaths, the snares of the devil, every sickness, temptation, malice, hatred, envy, evil people, evil utterances (that is, incantations and curses), [Col. 1049D] evil eyes, poisons, and every temptation; deign to consecrate and save our cattle and all four-footed animals afflicted by disease and sickness, through this creation of salt, in your name, Father, and of your Son Jesus Christ, and of the Holy Spirit, who exist in perfect Trinity.

## BLESSING OF SALT AND WATER FOR SPRINKLING IN A HOUSE

Holy Lord, almighty Father, renewer and creator of all the elements, who through Christ our Lord, your Son, commanded this creation of salt to exist among other things: we beseech you, Lord, to bless this creation of salt and water, so that wherever it has been sprinkled, every unclean spirit may flee and no longer have power to remain in that place. Through.

Another prayer. Through this creation for sprinkling—or through the sprinkling of this creation—grant, Lord, health of mind, soundness of body, protection of salvation, security of hope, and strengthening of faith, here and throughout the eternal ages.

## BLESSING OF WATER FOR SPRINKLING

God who [acts] for the salvation of the human race, etc.

Also another. I exorcise you, creation of salt and water, in the name of God the almighty Father, and in the name of Jesus Christ, his Son, and of the Holy Spirit. May every power of the adversary, every assault of the devil, and every power of the enemy be rooted out and driven away from this creation of water by the true God, by the living God, by the holy God, [Col. 1050B] and by our Lord Jesus Christ, so that you may become blessed water; so that wherever you are poured or sprinkled, whether in a house or in a field, you may drive away every phantom and every power of the enemy. May the Holy Spirit dwell in this house. Through our Lord, who is to come.

## Prayer after the Sprinkling of Water
