VERSES OF FLAVIUS FOR THE MANDATUM

[Note: [Col. 1077B]

The Mandatum is called the washing of the feet, from the opening words of Christ: “I give you a new commandment.” These words are still sung during the washing of the feet, which alone now remains as an example of Christ at the Supper.

Formerly, however, it was common in monastic communities and, according to the Rule of Saint Benedict, was performed both for arriving guests and among the brothers themselves. It continued to be customary in the monastery of Saint Blasius until the sixteenth century, every Saturday throughout the year.

The feet of the poor, moreover, were washed daily according to the praised order of the Work of God, with sacred ceremonial, singing, and prayers, from the beginning of Lent until the feast of Saints Simon and Jude. On the Lord’s Supper, however, it was done according to the following rite, in the morning after Terce and after the meal.

After Terce has been said, they go to the chapter house.

Whenever it pleases the lord abbot, he gives the cantor a sign to go out and see whether the poor have been arranged for the Mandatum. If they have been arranged in due order, he immediately reports to the lord abbot, who signals the prior to strike the board in the chapter house. When it has been struck and “Bless” has been said [Col. 1077D], the lord abbot begins Psalm “Have mercy on me, O God,” and so forth.

As they go into the cloister to visit the poor, the lord abbot leads with his chaplain carrying his book; afterward comes the community, first the elders, then the boys with their master. When the psalm has ended, the cantor begins the antiphon “The Lord Jesus,” and so forth. Everyone bends the knee, and one poor person is assigned to each brother. If any brother has died during the year, one poor person is assigned to him as well.

Twelve poor persons are assigned to the lord abbot, and thirteen to Lord Regenbercht, the benefactor.

After the washing of the feet and hands, the prior strikes the board with the abbot’s permission; when it has been struck, alms are given to the poor.

When the Mandatum has been completed, the lord abbot begins the seven penitential psalms, and they go into the choir as they came out of the chapter house, reading those psalms prostrate on the ground; the lord abbot remains before the altar on a seat prepared for him. When the psalms have ended, the lord abbot says the confession with the prayers pertaining to it [Col. 1078C]. Then they come into the cloister to converse.

On the Lord’s Supper, after Sext, the prior, cellarer, cantor, or chamberlain arranges twenty-four poor persons, who sit in the ambulatory immediately after the meal.

After the meal, the lord abbot comes to the ambulatory beside the cloister door, together with the prior and some of the brothers. There the cantor ensures that the twenty-four poor persons are present in the ambulatory and that no more are seated there.

The servant of the washing house has hot water, towels, and dishes prepared for washing and drying the feet or hands. The chamberlain ensures that two pitchers of wine are present there.

Then the cantor begins the antiphon “The Lord Jesus, after he had supped,” and so forth. Immediately everyone genuflects, and meanwhile the feet of the poor are washed.

After the antiphon has been said, “May God have mercy,” the prior strikes the board and says, “Bless.” They respond, “Amen.”

Then the lord abbot says:

“May the Lord deign to bless the drink of his servants.”

Immediately the cantor begins the responsory:

“He approached the feet of Jesus.”

Then drink is given to the poor.

After the responsory, the cantor begins the verse:

“She has been forgiven.”

The cellarer gives money to the poor, fifteen customary denarii to each; there are thirty solidi.

When the verse has ended, the responsory is repeated, and drink is again served to the poor.

When this has been done, the cantor says:

“We have received your mercy, O God.”

Kyrie eleison.

“Our Father.”

Verse: “Show us, O Lord, your mercy.”

Verse: “You commanded.”

“The Lord be with you.”

“Let us pray.”

“Be present, O Lord, to the offices of our service, which you yourself deign to accomplish.”

Immediately everyone genuflects, and the lord abbot begins Psalm “Have mercy on me.” They go into the choir and do as prescribed.]

## Prayers on Good Friday for Venerating the Cross

[Note: [Col. 1079D] This salutary adoration of the cross is believed to have been propagated throughout the Church from the Jerusalem church on Mount Golgotha, in which Constantine the Great exposed for worship the true cross on which Christ hung; its veneration is already mentioned by that church’s contemporary, Saint Cyril of Jerusalem, in *Catechetical Lecture* IV. As Saint Paulinus of Nola writes in *Letter* 31 to Severus, when the Lord’s Passover is celebrated each year, the bishop of that city himself presents it for the people to adore, as chief among those venerating it. Nor, apart from this day on which the mystery of the cross itself is celebrated, is it brought forth as a kind of solemn emblem, since it is the cause of the sacraments. [Col. 1080D] Jonas of Orléans, as we indicate in volume 1 of these monuments, letter A1, p. 382 n. 3, testifies in his book *On the Worship of Images against Claudius of Turin* that, in remembrance of the saving Passion of the Lord, the cross of Christ is annually adored on the most holy day of Good Friday according to ecclesiastical tradition. The Council of Paris, held in the ninth century on the same matter, likewise states: “On the holy day on which the Lord’s Passion is specially celebrated throughout the whole world, let the entire priestly order and all the Christian people adore with complete devotion.”]

Lord Jesus Christ, true God from true God, who, for the redemption of the human race deceived by the serpent’s persuasion and entangled in the errors of the world, willed to undergo the gallows of the cross so that you might conquer wood by wood and overcome with the most powerful death the hereditary death of sin: hear me, wretched and unworthy, prostrate before the eyes of your most gracious Majesty, adoring you and blessing your holy and terrible name. Grant me to know you with a pure heart, to praise you, to proclaim you; and through this banner of the holy cross, which I have come today to adore in your name, sanctify my mind and body. Cover me with the shield of your faith, place upon me the helmet of salvation, gird me with the spiritual sword, so that, as I prepare to fight against the most wicked enemy, I may be fortified by the aid of your mercy and by the banner of the saving cross; and so that all marked with your holy name may, through you, Jesus Christ, be secure from the assault of the treacherous enemy.

### Another

O God, who commanded your servant Moses, on the road through the desolate wilderness, to raise up a bronze serpent in the midst of the gathered people in order to free the souls afflicted by deadly venom, so that whoever had been struck with a mortal wound might look upon it, escape the destructive poison, and obtain the life of the desired salvation: signifying that you yourself, after the future course of events, would be lifted up on the gallows of the cross for the salvation of your creature, so that those whom the devil had taken captive with the weapons of envy might be recalled to their homeland by your desirable Passion. Grant both to me, wretched and sinful, and to all purchased by your blood, who today suppliantly venerate your holy Passion and adore the tree of life, that with your help we may conquer the devil’s snares and be deemed worthy to share in eternal life. You who live with the Father.

### Another

Lord Jesus Christ, who on this day freed us from diabolical slavery through the Passion of the cross, so that on the same day on which you created humanity you might also restore it: hear me, wretched and sinful, confessing my crimes before this sign of the cross and entreating that, protected by the guardianship of this venerable and life-giving sign, I may be able to repel the fiery darts of the most wicked enemy, be cleansed of the wounds inflicted, and reach eternal life. You who live and reign as God with the Father and the Holy Spirit. Through.

## Blessing of the New Fire

*(From codex theol. bibl. Vind. no. 685, tenth century.)*

Lord our God, almighty Father, hear us. You are the unfailing light, O Lord, creator of all lights. Bless (Latin *bene+dic*), I ask, this light, which is sanctified and blessed (Latin *bene+dicitur*) through you. You have enlightened the whole world, O Lord. Grant, we ask, that we may be kindled and illumined by the fire of your brightness; and just as you illumined Moses’ fire, so deign to illumine our hearts and senses, that we may be deemed worthy to attain eternal life. Through.

## On the Day of the Lord’s Resurrection

[Col. 1081B]

**Antiphon:** When Christ, the King of glory, entered hell to wage war against it, and the angelic choir before his face commanded the gates of the princes to be lifted up, the holy people who were held captive in death cried out in a tearful voice: “You have come, O Desired One, whom we awaited in darkness, so that you might lead the bound out of their prison this night. Our sighs were calling for you; our abundant laments were seeking you, when you became hope for the despairing and great consolation amid torments.” Alleluia.

**Antiphon:** The angel sits at the Lord’s sepulchre, clothed in a garment of brightness. When the women saw him, they stood at a distance, terrified with immense fear. Then the angel spoke and said to them:

**Verse:** Praise the One crucified in the flesh, [Col. 1081C] and glorify the One buried for us; adore the One rising from the dead. Do not be afraid, I tell you, for he whom you seek as dead already lives, and the life of humanity has risen with him. Alleluia.

**Antiphon:** Christ, rising from the dead, no longer dies; death shall no longer rule over him. For in that he lives, he lives to God. Alleluia, alleluia.

## Metrical Litany

[Note: [Col. 1081D] These litanies are assigned within the order of the divine office throughout the year, which we shall publish in the third part, on the second day of the Rogation Days. They are here supplied with musical notation.]

Lofty hope of the world, establisher of the glorious heaven,  
Christ, graciously hear us, your servants. Lofty.

Radiant Virgin Mother of God, eternal in honor,  
Holy Mary, pray for your servants. Lofty hope.

Highest angel of God, Michael, have mercy on us,  
And Gabriel and kindly Raphael assist us. Lofty.

And you, Peter with Paul, guide us with eloquent teaching. Lofty.

Prophetic choir of patriarchs as well. Lofty.

Let us now seek Stephen the foremost in song,  
That he, gracious with the martyrs, may himself help us. Lofty.

Illustrious Laurence, who overcame the flames,  
Victorious from the heavenly choir, have mercy on us. Lofty.

Dear martyr of God, the manly glory of this fatherland,

Holy Othmar, gladden your people. Lofty.

Illustrious Magnus, now mercifully look upon your people,

Bearing the virginal flowers, Agnes and Agatha,

[Col. 1082B]

Let us resound in praise for the innocent boys who have fulfilled their course,

O all you saints, come to the aid of our life,

From your wrath, merciful Christ, rescue us. All.

We sinners ask you: hear us, O Christ. All.

We ask you, O Christ: grant us peace. All.

We ask you, Christ: release your people from every crime. All.

We ask you, Christ: grant a temperate atmosphere. All.

We ask you, Christ: grant the fruits of the earth. All.

Christ, hear us; O Lord, have mercy. All.

## The Litanies Begin

[Note: [Col. 1082D] These litanies are assigned within the order of the divine office throughout the year on the second day of the Rogation Days. Musical notation is written above them everywhere in our codex.] *(From codex 685, under Otto.)*

With humble prayer and sincere devotion,  
As we cry to you, always hear us. Humble.

Highest and almighty Father, who created all things,  
Eternal Christ, Son and God,

And sanctifying Lord, gracious Spirit,  
One Majesty and only triune God. To you we cry.

She herself, the glorious Mother of God, restorer of the world,  
Who, conceiving the Lord in a chaste body,

Ever radiant with perpetual virginity,  
Virgin Mary, your unworthy servants. Humble.

[Col. 1082D]

All the angelic princes and armies of heaven,  
Ever conspicuous in eternal light,

In a threefold host through the stars of the heavenly kingdom  
Eternally celebrate the Lord with praises. To you.

Peter with Paul, Thomas with Bartholomew,  
And the holy Jameses, may they raise us up by their prayers;

Andrew, Matthew, Barnabas, and John,  
Matthias, Luke, Mark, and the high-voiced one. Humble.

The apostolic assembly, adorned with twelve stars,  
Protect us all, your servants, favorably,

[Col. 1083A]

And, absolving those whom manifold plagues tear apart through crimes,  
Make us follow all good things. To you.

Now Stephen, Linus, Clement, Anacletus the gracious,  
Sixtus, Alexander, Cornelius, and Pius,

Hippolytus, Vitus, Laurence, and Modestus,  
And pious Gregory, by showing mercy, may they help us. Humble.

Theodole, strongest soldier of Christ the Most High,  
Help us, your servants, now.

Nothing so clear could be conveyed by a resounding voice  
As is fitting in such service of the Father now. To you.

Here, in perpetual hymns, these halls resound for you,  
And honor is always given to the sacred bones,

While the joyful servants here kindly celebrate the feasts,  
Persisting in praises of you night and day. Humble.

[Col. 1083B]

Guide our hearts, gracious one, and guide our times,  
And grant your servants to lead joyful days,

So that they may always be able to sing to you in peace  
And behold you also in the heavenly light of heaven. To you.

O beloved of God, radiant, shining with brilliant virtue,  
Holy Alban, father, continually offer prayers in common;

Graciously intercede, seeking pardon for the wretched,  
And now receive our pleasing songs. Humble.

O you adorned with mystery in the name of Christ,  
Conspicuous purple-robed princes and witnesses,

Invincible in battle, you overcame the fury of the demon;  
With united hands you conquered the threats of death. To you.

Sylvester, Damasus, Gregory, and Ambrose,  
Hilary, Zeno, Maximus, and Leo,

Martin, Proculus, Caesarius, and Eusebius,  
Pray for our various crimes. Humble.

[Col. 1083C]

Sacred order of the foremost confessors,  
Make your own safe on every side through your help,

And, dismissing our guilt through your prayer,  
Deliver us, very frail as we are, from every kind of calamity. To you.

Paul and Antony, Macarius and Arsenius,  
Pachomius, Bede, Atala, Paphnutius,

Bertoltus, Libertinus, Basil, and  
Jerome the teacher, have mercy on us, I pray. Humble.

Highest worshiper of God, ruler and abbot of monks,  
O holy and kindly father Benedict,

Sanctifying this monastery and the assembly serving you,  
Watch over all that belongs to us together. To you.

Felicity, Felix, worthy Eulalia, Verena,  
And Petronilla with perpetual Perpetua,

[Col. 1083D]

Agnes and Agatha, Christina, Euprepia, Thecla,  
Euphemia, Regula, Eugenia, and the good one. Humble.

Choir of virgins, shining with virginity,  
Crowd of maidens remaining in integrity,

Who rejoice, adorned with beautiful twin crowns,  
With the praise both of chastity and of mystery. To you.

All you saints, now come to the aid of us who have fallen,  
And bring pardon to all, helping us in heaven.

Whatever those who ask now seek through your prayers,  
The gracious Lord grants it and denies nothing. Humble.

We ask for perpetual peace; look upon us, Christ,  
So that the long joys of a sound life may endure,

[Col. 1084A]

Granting temperate weather and the fertility of the earth,  
So that abundance of fruits may overflow for all with rich joy. To you.

Lamb of God the Father, who takes away the sins of the world,  
Give your people the gifts of the desired peace.

Lord Almighty, have mercy; save all.  
[The following Greek is corrupt or uncertain: “Sub basileos ymon”]; Christ, have mercy on us.

## Another Metrical Litany

Hail, venerable day throughout every age,  
On which God conquered hell and holds the stars.

Behold, the grace of the world’s renewal bears witness  
That the gifts of humankind (*homilium*) have returned to their Lord.

For after the triumphant Christ emerged from gloomy Tartarus,  
The woodland everywhere favors him with leaf, grass, and flower.

When the laws of hell had been crushed and he ascended above the stars,  
Light, heaven, fields, and sea duly praise God.

[Col. 1084B]

Behold, the God who was crucified reigns everywhere,  
And all created things offer prayer to their Creator.

The nobility of the year, the glory of the months,  
The weapons of the days, the splendor of the hours, cherishing minutes and moments—

Christ, salvation of all things, good Creator and Redeemer,  
Only-begotten offspring from the Father’s Godhead.

You endure the funeral rites, author of life and of the world,  
Entering the path of death while giving the aid of salvation.

But, gracious Power, restore the promised pledge, I pray:  
The third day has returned; arise, my buried one.

Release the chained shadows of hell’s prison,  
And call upward whatever has fallen to the depths.

Restore your face, that the ages may behold the light;  
Restore the day that did not exist when you died.

You rescue a people into their number from the prison of death,

[Col. 1084C]

And the free person follows where his author goes.

Then, revisiting the tomb after Tartarus and having resumed the flesh,  
As a warrior you bear great trophies to heaven.

## Litany

Gracious King and Savior, receive the little offerings of our prayers.

Be present to pardon us, your servants burdened with wickedness.

O holy Mary, mother and virgin, pray for us.

Highest archangel Michael, power of God, pray for us.

Worthy Gabriel, strength of God, pray for us.

O companion Raphael, medicine of God, pray for us.

O holy excellence of the patriarchs, pray for us.

O lot fulfilled by God, prophetic power, pray for us.

O principality of the apostles, pray for us.

O holy martyrs, plead for pardon for our sins.

[Col. 1084D]

Holy confessors, ask for us by your constant prayers.

O radiant choirs of holy virgins, ask for us.

May the favorable prayers of the holy widows now benefit us.

Innocent little boys, flowerbed of martyrs, ask for us.

O all you saints, innumerable powers, ask for us.

That God may defend us here and forever from the wicked enemy.

[Col. 1085A]

That God may defend us here and forever from the pagan people.

That God may defend us here and forever from every danger.

That God may defend us here and forever from every terror.

That God may defend us here and forever from every danger.

That the Savior may grant us good and fruitful weather.

That the Savior may grant us favorable air and dew.

That the Savior may grant us fruitful rain, causing good things to sprout.

That the Savior may grant us a tranquil life, peace, and permanence.

[Col. 1085B]

That the Savior may grant us forgiveness of our sins.

That the Lord may preserve the supreme apostolic shepherd.

That the Lord may preserve N., the worthy bishop and lord.

That the Lord may preserve King Otto and his army.

That the Lord may preserve the holy Church throughout the whole world.

### Prayers before the Altar: First Day

Let us all cry with one voice: Lord, have mercy.

Mother of God, you are our life: Lord, have mercy.

We ask you, Most High: grant faith: Lord, have mercy.

We bow down; we are oppressed by sins and evils: Lord, have mercy.

[Col. 1085C]

Erase our offenses; grant peace: Lord, have mercy.

Most High, look upon us graciously; forgive: Lord, have mercy.

Remove the scourges; grant pardon: Lord, have mercy.

Hear us, gracious Father: Lord, have mercy.

Now and forever save the world: Lord, have mercy.

Let us sing a hymn to you, Christ: Lord, have mercy.

Glory to you, eternal Father: Lord, have mercy. Let us cry out.

### Second Day

To you praise, to you glory, to you thanksgiving through everlasting ages. O blessed Trinity.

We invoke you, we adore you, we praise you. O blessed Trinity.

Hear us, hear us, hear us, O blessed Trinity.

Free us, save us, justify us. O blessed Trinity.

[Col. 1085D]

Increase faith in us, increase hope, increase charity.

O blessed Trinity.

### Third Day

Take away our iniquities, that we may deserve to enter the Holy of Holies with pure minds.

Hear us, hear us, hear us; holy Mary, pray for us.

Have mercy, have mercy, have mercy on your people whom you redeemed.

Christ, by your blood, do not be angry with us forever.

## Litany

Let us all say: Lord, have mercy.

[Col. 1086A]

With our whole heart and our whole mind we pray to you, Lord.

For the holy Catholic Church, which is spread throughout the whole world, we beseech you, Lord.

For our shepherd N. and all his clergy, we implore you, Lord.

For our abbot N. and the flock entrusted to him, we beseech you, Lord.

For temperate weather and the fruitfulness of the earth, we pray to you, Lord.

For those who are sick and held by various ailments, we entreat you, Lord.

For the remission of sins and the amendment of conduct, we ask you, Lord.

Hear us, God, in all our prayer, because you are gracious, Lord.

## Litany

With suppliant vows let us raise our voices above the stars,  
That the triune and simple Almighty may govern us.

Holy Lady of the world, Mary, star of the sea,  
Pray for us to your Son, Christ the Lord.

Minister of the highest throne, Michael, “Who is like God?”  
Help us with your prayers, together with the heavenly citizens.

[Col. 1088D]

John, herald of Christ, presenter of the Lamb of God and Redeemer,  
Reconcile us to God.

Holy Peter, with Paul and all the apostles,  
Implore for us the Lord of majesty.

Christ’s martyr Theodole, and Alban our patron likewise,  
Joined in merits, release us from our crimes.

Stephen the protomartyr, and all you martyrs,  
Pray for all Catholic peoples.

O Bodard the confessor, and Martin likewise,  
Help us with your prayers together with the confessors.

O holy martyr Felicity, and choir of virgins,  
By your constant prayers ask for us.

All holy angels and human beings of the Lord,  
Commend the Catholic peoples to the Lord.

[Col. 1089A]

Obtain that forgiveness of sins, temperate weather,  
And fertility of the earth be granted to us.

Obtain that peaceful tranquility and health of body  
Be given to us by Christ through your merits.

We ask you, Christ, hear us: grant that you may preserve  
N., the bishop, his clergy, and the whole people.

We ask you, Christ, hear us: grant that our king Otto,  
His army, and his forces on every side may be preserved.

We ask you, Christ, hear us: grant that the raging sword  
And the pagan people may be driven away from us.

Christ, Christ, hear us. We sing, “Lord, have mercy”;  
We chant, “Christ, have mercy”; gracious Christ, hear us.

A certain man was very rich, dressed in purple and fine linen, feasting splendidly. By loving this transitory life, he lost the everlasting one.

A certain beggar named Lazarus, covered with sores, lay at the rich man’s gate, longing with great anguish to be filled with the crumbs from the rich man’s table. A man.

He begged; no one gave; no one had pity. Only dogs came, consoling the poor man. They licked his sores; his wounds were cared for.

A man. The rich man died and was taken into hell. He had not shown mercy and did not obtain it. For the crumbs of bread that he had denied, he was taken into hell.

A man. He calls Abraham “Father,” asking that Lazarus be admitted. He asks for a drop of water from the tip of his finger, so that his tongue may be cooled amid the burning flames.

A man. “My son, remember that from your youth you received very many good things in your life, while Lazarus, by contrast, received evil things; now he shall be consoled.”

A certain man.

**Psalm:** Save me, O God.

**Psalm:** O God, we have heard with our ears.

**Psalm:** O God, the nations have entered your inheritance.

[Col. 1089]

# Various Blessings, Consecrations, and Ordinations

## Blessings of Various Things

[Col. 1089C]

### Blessing of Apples

*(From the Vindobonese theological codex 685, tenth century.)*

We beseech you, almighty God, that you bless this new fruit of apples, etc.

### Blessing of Bread

Bless, Lord, this creature of bread, just as you blessed the five loaves in the desert, so that it may be abundant nourishment throughout the year, and those who taste it may receive health both of body and of soul.

### Blessing of Grapes or Beans

Bless, Lord, these new fruits, whether grapes or beans, etc.

### Blessing of Nuts

[Col. 1089D]

Bless, Lord, the fruit and the nuts, their kernels, and all the fruits of the earth, both of trees and of herbs, which arise at your command. Through.

## Blessing of a Lamb at Easter

[Note: [Col. 1089D] The words “through whom all these things,” added here and shortly before to the blessing of grapes or beans, show that these blessings were made with reference to those words of the canon, as we have also shown in our investigations, volume I, p. 371, concerning the blessing of other things. For example, the blessing of apples given here is the same as that found in the Gelasian Sacramentary, as is also the blessing of grapes or beans, new fruits, whose blessing was performed at the solemn Mass of the Lord’s Ascension, as Cardinal Bona noted, *On Liturgical Matters*, book II, chapter 14, from an ancient sacramentary. It is also found in Edmond Martène, *On the Ancient Discipline of the Church in the Celebration of the Various Offices*, chapter 28. Later, in chapter 33, for the eighth day before the Kalends of August, a blessing of apples is found in a very ancient ritual for the use of the diocese of Rheims, on the feast day of Saints James and Christopher, though after the Mass of that day. In the *Apostolic Constitutions*, book VIII, chapter 46, there is a formula for the blessing of firstfruits or new fruits. A prayer for the tasting of grapes on the sixth day of August also exists in the Euchologion. On that same day, even in more recent missals, the blessing of grapes is included—the same one from the commonly circulated Gelasian Sacramentary that we have just mentioned in our *Monuments*. I say nothing of the rite of that day—deservedly obsolete—of liquefying new wine pressed from fresh grapes in the chalice, concerning which see Durandus, *Rationale of the Divine Offices*, book VII, chapter 22.]

God, creator of all flesh, etc.

## The Blessing of a House Begins

*(From codex Vind. theol. 685, tenth century.)*

Let us pray for this house and for the masters of this dwelling, that the Lord may make them rejoice in good things; may the Lord deign to grant them the dew from heaven above and, from the earth’s fertility below, an abundant provision for life, and mingle the fulfillment of their desires with his mercy; and may he deign to bless our entrance, so that an angel of blessing may dwell within these walls. Through.

## Prayer over a New House

[Col. 1090D]

May this house be sanctified, and may the unclean [Col. 1091A] spirit be driven from it through the power of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that health, brightness, and joy may be granted to all who dwell there, while your Majesty, Lord, protects and preserves them. Through.

## Blessing of Water over Crops

Bless, Lord, this creature of water, so that worms and birds may flee from our crops through the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, which has been invoked over this harvest-creature, so that it may be wholesome for all who use it.

## Prayer over Crops

Holy Father, almighty, eternal God, permit your Holy Spirit, with the archangel Panchiel [Note: [Col. 1091D] A foreign angelic name of the sort invented by Adelbert the heretic, condemned in the Roman council of 745 and in Burchard, book III, chapter 198, from the canon of the Third Council of Orléans. Nevertheless, some such names are found in the Carolingian litany in Mabillon, *Analecta*, p. 170.] to defend our crops from worms, birds, and evil demons, so that your name may be magnified in every place. Through.

## Blessing of Salt for Human Eyes

[Col. 1091B]

Heal the eyes of this person, Lord, as we bless this creature of salt in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, just as you opened the eyes of the two blind men who cried out to you in the Gospel, saying, “Have mercy on us, Son of David,” and you revealed yourself to them, and their eyes were opened; and just as the one who was healed with spittle and washed in the pool of Siloam was given back his sight, so may this person’s eyes be opened through you, Jesus Christ, who live with the Father. Through.

## Blessing of the Eyes

Heal this person’s eyes, Lord, just as you healed the eyes of Tobit and of the two blind men whom the Gospel mentions. Purify the eyes; drive out the speck and the film/web (*aream*, perhaps an OCR corruption of *araneam*), and everything that harms the eyes, and may your glory appear in every place. Through.

## Prayer for the Pain of Childbirth

O God, who in the beginning made humanity and gave it a helper like itself, so that they might increase and multiply upon the earth, grant your mercy to this servant of yours, N., so that she may give birth successfully and without pain. Through.

## Prayer over a Spring Where Some Pollution Has Occurred

Holy Father, almighty, eternal God, who by the power of your invisibility made these waters, created from nothing, present a visible form like a sea, and from hidden and unsearchable hollows, through the vastness of the abyss of your generosity, caused streams to flow from springs for human use: we suppliantly beseech you [Col. 1091D] that your Holy Spirit’s grace may restore and purify these waters, which negligence has polluted, for cleanliness; that the crafty spirit of the enemy may depart; and that thereafter you may grant them, sanctified and drinkable, to your family, so that they may cleanse the bodies of those who drink and sanctify their hearts. Through.

## Blessing of a New Well

Let us pray. Bless, we ask, almighty God, this cistern of water, into which you commanded the flowing liquid, issuing from the interior of the earth through its openings, to pour forth, so that, every diabolical scheme having been driven away, whoever drinks from it may render immense thanks to you. Through.

## Prayer over Vessels Found in Ancient Places
Almighty eternal God, enter into our offices, and deign by the power of your majesty so to repair these vessels fashioned by the art of the gentiles that, once every impurity has been driven away, they may be used by your faithful in a time of peace and tranquility. Through.

## Blessing for Anything You Wish

Bless, Lord, this creature, etc.

## Blessing over a New Garment

May the seal of God be upon this new garment with which people are clothed, so that the Holy Spirit may reign in the person who clothes himself with it, and may he remain with him in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit forever and ever.

## Blessing of a Widow Who Has Professsed Chastity

[Col. 1092B]

Console, Lord, this handmaid of yours, bound by the hardships of widowhood, just as you deigned to console the widow of Sarepta through the prophet Elisha. Grant her the fruit of modesty, so that she may not remember former pleasures. Let her not know the incitements of desire, so that she may submit her own neck to you alone, whereby she may receive, for such great labors, the delightful reward of holiness in the sixtieth degree. Through.

## Blessing of the Garments of Virgins or Widows

O God, most faithful promiser of eternal goods, bless graciously these garments, signifying humility of heart and contempt of the world, which are visibly to mark your household’s holy purpose; and may she preserve, under your protection, the habit of blessed chastity which she has received with your inspiration. May you make her whom you temporarily clothe in garments of venerable promise blessedly clothed with immortality. Through.

## Prayer for Making an Abbot or Abbess

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, and accompany with the gift of your grace your servant or handmaid whom we have chosen for the governance of souls, so that, by your bounty, we may please you together with this person whom we have elected. Through.

## Order for Making a Cleric

*(From the Rhenau manuscript, approximately eleventh century.)*

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, to this servant of yours, etc.

## Also for Making a Cleric or Monk

[Col. 1092D]

Be present, Lord, to our supplications, and deign to bless this servant of yours, upon whom we impose the habit of sacred religion in your holy name, so that, by your bounty, he may deserve both to persevere devoutly in the Church and to receive eternal life. Through.

While he is being tonsured, let these antiphons be sung: “You are, Lord,” etc. And let him say the prayer: “Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, to this servant of yours,” etc.

### Prayer for the Tonsure

Almighty everlasting God, look upon this [Col. 1093A] servant (these servants) of yours, whom (you have) deigned to call to the new grace of tonsure, granting him (them) remission of all sins and access to fellowship with heavenly gifts. Through.

### For the Beard

O God, by whose Spirit every creature rejoices as it grows to maturity, hear our prayers for this servant of yours, N., rejoicing in the beauty of youthful age and cutting off the flower of his first growth. Hear, Lord, so that, fortified in all things by the help of your protection, he may receive heavenly blessing, rejoice in the safeguards of the present life, and in those of the eternal life. Through.

After the Gospel of the principal Mass, the profession of the monks is to be made in this way:

[Col. 1093B]

“I, Brother N., promise stability, conversion of my conduct, and obedience according to the Rule of Saint Benedict, before God and his saints, in this monastery of Rhenau, which has been built in honor of Saint Mary, Mother of God; in the presence of Lord N., Abbot.”

After each of them has read this, they ask pardon three times over the hands and knees, saying this verse:

**V.** Receive me, Lord, according to your word, etc.

When the community responds, adding “Glory,” etc., the novices, making a circuit on bent knees, then prostrate themselves for prayer. The Lord Abbot, standing, imposes the following:

“Lord, have mercy,” etc. “Christ, have mercy,” etc. “Lord, have mercy,” etc. “Our Father,” etc. “Have mercy on me, O God,” etc.

Save your servant (servants).

**R.** Send him (them), Lord, help from the sanctuary.

May the enemy accomplish nothing against him (them).

[Col. 1093C]

Be for him (them), Lord, a tower of strength.

The Lord be with you.

Let us pray:

O God, Father of forgiveness, who, tempering the severity of your strict judgment, granted pardon so that the son would not bear the iniquity of the father; and who, in a wondrous dispensation, frequently accomplishes the work of your gracious favor even through the wicked, using them for good: we beseech your clemency, that the fact that this servant of yours receives from us, so unworthy of such a thing, the habit of religion may not stand against him, but that the ministry outwardly performed by us may be carried out inwardly by you through the gifts of the Holy Spirit. Through.

[Col. 1093D]

O God, who created all things through your coeternal Son, and who deigned, through the mystery of his incarnation, to renew the world grown old in sins: we humbly beseech you that the grace of that same Lord of ours may graciously look upon this servant of yours, professing renunciation of the world; so that, renewed in the spirit of his mind, he may put off the old man with his deeds and deserve to put on the new, who is according to God. Through.

Lord Jesus Christ, who are the way without which no one comes to the Father, we beseech your most kindly mercy: lead this servant of yours, drawn away from carnal desires, along the path of regular discipline. You who deigned to call sinners, saying, “Come to me, all you who labor and are burdened, and I will refresh you,” grant that this word of your invitation may grow so strong in him that, laying down the burdens of sins and tasting how sweet you are, he may deserve to be sustained by your [Col. 1094A] refreshment. And just as you deigned to attest concerning your sheep, recognize him among your sheep, and let him recognize you, so that he may not follow a stranger, but you, nor hear the voice of strangers, but yours, by which you say: “Whoever serves me, let him follow me.” You who live, etc.

Holy Spirit, who have deigned to reveal yourself as God and Lord to mortals, we ask for the immense grace of your goodness: just as you breathe where you will, so grant this servant of yours an affection for devotion. Since he was created by your wisdom, may he also be governed by your providence; may your anointing teach him concerning all things according to your customary grace. Through the intercession of the most blessed Benedict, whom you gave as the foremost lawgiver of this holy institution, and of the other saints whose names he invokes in his [Col. 1094B] petition, truly convert him from the vanity of the world. Since you are the remission of all sins, dissolve in him the bonds of oppressive wickedness, and make him burn eagerly for the observance of this holy purpose amid tribulations and distress, so that he may breathe again through your unfailing consolation. Founded justly and devoutly in brotherly love through true humility and obedience, may he complete with happy perseverance what, by your gift, he promises. May you deign to grant this, you who live and are glorified with God the Father and his holy only-begotten Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, God, forever and ever. Amen.

Here the novices rise for prayer, so that the Lord Abbot may sprinkle them with blessed water.

### The Cowls Are Blessed in This Manner

[Col. 1094C]

Lord Jesus Christ, who deigned to put on the covering of our mortality, we beseech the immense abundance of your generosity: deign so to bless this kind of garment, which the holy Fathers decreed should be worn by those renouncing the world as a mark of innocence and humility, that this servant of yours who uses it may deserve to put you on. You who live with the Father.

Likewise, while removing the frock, this is said to each one:

May the Lord strip you of the old man with his deeds.

While putting on the cowl, this is said to each one:

May the Lord clothe you with the new man, who was created according to God in righteousness and the holiness of truth.

Then, after kissing the Abbot, they go into the [Col. 1094D] choir and kiss the entire community.

# Consecration of a Sacred Virgin

## Celebrated on Epiphany, or on the Second Day of Easter, or on the Feasts of the Apostles

*(From Codex Vindobonensis theol. 359, tenth century.)*

All who are to be promoted to sacred orders must be consecrated by the bishop before the proclamation of the Gospel, because the preaching of the holy Gospel is to be spread throughout the whole world by them. Virgins and widows, however, are to be veiled after the Gospel has been read, because it is fitting that the Gospel also be preached to them. The virgin’s parents offer her to the bishop with an offering, and he is to receive her hand, wrapped in a cloth, upon the altar pallium, saying with those standing by the antiphon:

[Col. 1095A]

“I am betrothed to him whom the angels serve, whose beauty the sun and moon admire.”

When a religious woman is offered to her bishop for consecration, she is to be presented in such garments as she will always use, suitable for her profession and religious life. First, however, those garments are to be offered before the altar to the bishop for blessing.

### Blessing of the Garments of Virgins

O God, most faithful promiser and most certain fulfiller of eternal goods, etc.

### Another

Lord God, giver of good virtues and generous pourer out of every blessing, we beseech you with earnest prayers: deign to bless and sanctify these garments which your handmaid N. wishes to put on as a sign by which her religious life may be recognized, so that she may be known as dedicated among other women. Through.

[Col. 1095B]

### Another

Hear, Lord, our prayers, and pour out upon this garment, which your handmaid N. asks to use as a sign, the abundant rain of your blessing, just as you poured it upon the hem of Aaron’s garments, with the blessing of ointment flowing from the head down to the beard. And just as you blessed the garments of all religious persons who please you in every way, so deign also to bless this one. And grant, most merciful Father, that for your aforesaid handmaid N. this garment may be a saving protection, a recognition of religious life, a beginning of holiness, and a strong defense against all the weapons of the enemy. If she is continent, may she receive the gift of the sixtieth fruit; if she is a virgin, may she be enriched by the abundance of the hundredfold reward, while continence perseveres on both sides. Through.

### Also, Blessing of the Sacred Veil

[Col. 1095C]

God, head of all the faithful and Savior of the whole body, sanctify with your right hand this covering of the veil which your handmaid is about to place upon her head for love of you and of your most blessed Mother, the ever-virgin Mary. May what is mystically signified through it always be preserved by your protection, undefiled in body and likewise in spirit; so that, when she comes to the everlasting recompense of the saints, she may deserve, with you leading her, to enter the marriage feast of perpetual happiness, herself prepared with the prudent virgins. Through.

Here she who is to be consecrated is to prostrate herself humbly before the altar and say this verse three times:

“Receive me, Lord, according to your word, and I shall live; and do not put me to shame in my hope.”

[Col. 1095D]

After this the bishop shall say:

“Sister, receive this garment in the name of the Lord.”

And she shall answer:

“I receive it in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.”

Then the bishop gives her the garments of virginity, retaining only the veil with him. The virgin herself goes to the sacristy and puts on these blessed garments. Taking two burning candles in her hands, she comes before the altar, and the clergy begin the Introit of the Mass. After the Gospel and the prayers have been said, while she is prostrate and the Litany has been sung, the bishop blesses her with bowed head before the altar, saying this prayer:

Look, Lord, graciously upon this handmaid of yours, N., so that she may preserve, with you governing her, the purpose of holy virginity which she has undertaken under your inspiration. Through.

### Consecration in the Form of a Preface

[Col. 1096A]

O God, gracious inhabitant of chaste bodies and lover of incorrupt souls; O God, who repair the human substance, corrupted in the first human beings by the devil’s deceit, through your Word by whom all things were made, so that you not only restore it to the innocence of its first origin but also lead it to experience certain goods that are to be possessed in the new age, and advance those still bound by the condition of mortality toward the likeness of angels: look upon this handmaid of yours, who, placing the purpose of her continence in your hand, offers her devotion to you, from whom she herself has also received this vow.

For when would a mind surrounded by mortal flesh overcome the law of nature, the freedom of license, the force of custom, and the impulses of age, unless you mercifully kindled this love of virginity through free choice? You graciously nourished this desire in her heart; you supplied strength.

[Col. 1096B]

For your grace, poured out upon all nations, adopted heirs of the New Testament from every nation under heaven in an innumerable number like the stars. Among the other virtues which you have implanted in your children, begotten not from bloods nor from the will of the flesh but from your Spirit, this gift also has now flowed from the fountain of your generosity into certain minds. Although no prohibition had diminished the honor of marriage, and the original blessing remained upon holy marriage, there nevertheless arose souls of a higher kind who disdained the union of man and woman, desired the sacrament, and did not imitate what is done in marriage but loved what marriage prefigures.

[Col. 1096C]

Blessed virginity recognized its author and, rivaling the integrity of the angels, devoted itself to the bridal chamber and bedchamber of him who is the bridegroom of perpetual virginity in the same way that he is the son of perpetual virginity.

Therefore, to her who implores your help and desires to be strengthened by the consecration of your blessing, grant the protection of your defense and guidance, lest the ancient enemy, who assails higher endeavors with subtler snares, creep in through some negligence of the mind to obscure the palm of perfect continence and snatch from the purpose of virgins what is also fitting to be present in the conduct of marriage.

[Col. 1096D]

Let there be in her, Lord, through the gift of the Holy Spirit, prudent modesty, wise kindness, serious gentleness, and chaste freedom. Let her burn with love and love nothing outside you. Let her live commendably and not desire to be praised. Let her glorify you in holiness of body and in purity of soul; let her fear you through love and serve you through love.

May you be her honor, her joy, her will, her consolation in sorrow, her counsel in uncertainty, her defense in injury, her patience in tribulation, her abundance in poverty, her food in fasting, and her medicine in sickness. May she have everything in you, whom she desires to love above all things. May she preserve what she has professed, pleasing the searcher of hearts not in body but in mind.

May she enter the number of wise maidens, so that, with lamps lit and supplied with oil of preparation, she may await the heavenly Bridegroom. May she not be troubled by the unexpected arrival of the king but, secure with her lamp and joined to the choir of the virgins who went before, may she meet him. May she not be shut out with the foolish, but may she enter freely through the royal gate with the wise virgins and remain forever in the company of your Lamb, abiding in a chastity worthy of approval. Through the same.

[Col. 1097A]

When the blessing has been completed, the bishop places the veil upon the virgin’s head:

“Receive the sacred veil, maiden, which you are to carry without stain before the tribunal of our Lord Jesus Christ, before whom every knee of those in heaven, on earth, and under the earth is bent, forever and ever. Amen.”

Then those standing by sing the antiphon for each [virgin]:

“The Lord has clothed me in a ciclade woven with gold and adorned me with immense necklaces.”

### Prayer after the Veil Has Been Received

[Col. 1097B]

May your merciful protection, Lord, strengthen your handmaid, so that she may preserve unharmed, under your protection, the purpose of holy continence which she undertook with your inspiration.

The antiphon follows:

“I am betrothed to him whom,” etc.

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that this handmaid of yours, who desires to be consecrated to you, Lord, in hope of eternal reward, may remain with full faith and a devoted mind in her holy purpose. May you, almighty Father, deign to sanctify, bless, and preserve her forever. Grant her humility, chastity, obedience, charity, and abundance in every good work. Give her, Lord, glory for her works, reverence for her modesty, and holiness for her chastity, so that she may attain the reward of glory. Through.

[Col. 1097C]

Then those standing by sing the antiphon:

“He placed a sign upon my face, so that I might admit no lover except him.”

And the bishop says over her the blessing of the Apostle Matthew.

Prayer:

O God, creator of bodies and breather of souls, who despise no age, reject no sex, and deem no condition unworthy of your grace, but are the equal creator and redeemer of all: surround with the shield of your protection this handmaid of yours, whom you have deigned to choose from the whole number of the flock, to preserve the crown of perpetual virginity and purity of soul. Prepare her, under the instruction of wisdom, for every work of virtue and glory, so that, innocent and rejecting the allurements of the flesh and what is lawful in marriage, she may deserve the unbreakable union with your Son, our Lord Jesus Christ.

[Col. 1097D]

For this we ask, Lord, that you supply weapons not of the flesh but powerful through the strength of the Spirit, so that, with you protecting her, sin may not rule her senses and members in body or soul, and so that, while she desires to live under your grace, no defender of evil or enemy of good may prevail to claim anything from this vessel already consecrated to your name.

May the rain of your heavenly grace also extinguish every natural heat, while kindling the light of perpetual chastity. May her chaste face not be open to scandals, nor may negligence carelessly provide an occasion for sinning.

[Col. 1098A]

May chaste virginity be in her, adorned and likewise armed, with unbroken faith, certain hope, and sincere charity, so that, with a prepared mind, such strength may be granted for continence as will overcome all the devil’s fabrications, and so that, by despising present things, she may pursue those that are future.

May she prefer fasts to bodily feasts, and sacred readings and prayers to banquets and drinking, so that, nourished by prayers and filled with instruction, illuminated by vigils, she may perform the work of virginal grace.

Strengthening this handmaid of yours inwardly and outwardly with these weapons of virtue, grant that she may complete the course of virginity without stumbling. Through.

### For Giving the Ring

Receive the ring of faith, the seal of the Holy Spirit, so that you may be called the bride of God if you serve him faithfully.

[Col. 1098B]

Receive the sign of Christ upon your head, so that you may become his wife; and if you remain in him, may you be crowned forever.

Meanwhile let the antiphon be sung:

“My Lord Jesus Christ has betrothed me with his ring and adorned me like a bride with a crown.”

The blessing follows:

May God the Father almighty, creator of heaven and earth, bless you. He has deigned to choose you for fellowship with holy Mary, Mother of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that you may preserve the whole and unstained virginity which you have professed before the Lord and his angels, hold fast your purpose, love chastity, preserve patience, and deserve to receive the crown of virginity. Through.

After this, leaving the candles, the maiden offers the offering. Taking the candles again, she stands inclined until she communicates, and [Col. 1098C] the Mass is completed in its proper order. After she communicates, she is to reserve some of that communion until the eighth day, so that she may communicate from it.

[Note: [Col. 1097D] The rite of giving the sacred host, from which the virgin was to communicate for eight days, as was formerly practiced in priestly ordination, is prescribed in the ancient Order R. and in various pontifical books cited by Martène, book II, *On the Ancient Rites of the Church*, chapter 6, no. 15. [Col. 1098D] This rite was changed to communion over three days, as Joseph Catalanus reports from a Vatican manuscript, around the year 400, volume I, *Commentary on the Pontifical R.*, p. 362.]

And if there is someone who also gives testimony, the bishop sends her into his hands, saying:

“See that you present this woman consecrated to God unstained before the tribunal of our Lord Jesus Christ.”

## Likewise, the Mass of Virgins

“My heart has said to you.” Psalm: “The Lord is my light.” Grant, we beseech you, Lord, to your handmaid whom virginity... Gradual: “Have mercy on me, O God.” Verse: “He sent from heaven.” Alleluia: “Praise the Lord, my soul.” Offertory: “Let them hope in you.” Secret: “With the offerings presented, Lord.” Within the Canon: “This offering, therefore.”

Blessing:

“Eternal Lord God, who mercifully redeemed both sexes from the destruction of perpetual death through Jesus [Col. 1098D] Christ your Son, born of the Virgin Mary, deign to bless this handmaid of yours, who serves you with devoted mind, with every spiritual blessing.”

Amen.

“That she may have unbroken faith, always persevere in the commandments of your law, despise earthly and transitory things, and love eternal and invisible things with profound meditation.”

Amen.

“That, remaining among the number of holy virgins, she may confidently meet the heavenly Bridegroom with the lamps of good works, and may deserve this through you, who grant it.”

[Col. 1099A]

Amen.

“May he himself deign to grant it.”

Communion: “You have made known to me.” “Look, Lord, upon your handmaid.” Sermon on the Nativity of Virgins.

## For Virgins, Handmaids of God, Who Are to Be Veiled and Whose Garments Are Changed upon Their Conversion

When a virgin, handmaid of God, is offered to her bishop for consecration, she is to be presented in such garments as she will always use, suitable for her profession and religious life. Then let him say this preface:

“Let us pray, dearest brothers, for the mercy of the Lord, that he may grant this maiden, who has vowed a vow to God, to bear a white garment with the integrity of the crown in the resurrection of eternal life, which is to come to us. Through.”

### Another

May your merciful protection, Lord, strengthen your household, so that the purpose of holy virginity which it undertook with your inspiration may, under your protection, be preserved unharmed. Through.

[Col. 1099B]

### Another

We invoke you, Lord, Father almighty, eternal God, over this handmaid of yours, who has vowed to serve you with pure mind and clean heart. Deign to join her among those 144,000 who remained virgins and did not defile themselves with women, in whose mouth no deceit was found. Make this handmaid of yours remain unstained until the end, through the undefiled Jesus Christ, our Lord, with whom you live and reign, God, in the unity of the Holy Spirit. Through.

When the blessing has been completed, the bishop places the veil upon the virgin’s head, saying:

“Receive the sacred veil, maiden, which you are to carry without stain before the tribunal of our Lord Jesus Christ, before whom every knee of those in heaven, on earth, and under the earth is bent, forever and ever. Amen.”

[Col. 1099C]

Blessing:

“May God the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit bless you with every spiritual blessing, so that you may remain without stain under the garment of holy Mary, Mother of our Lord Jesus Christ.”

He who lives and reigns.

# Consecration of a Widow

## Who Has Professed Chastity

Widows are to be veiled after the Gospel has been read, because it is fitting that the Gospel be preached to them. Since a widow is released from the law of her husband, she likewise ought to give herself to God and be veiled by a presbyter, or even receive from the bishop a consecrated veil for herself, but the bishop ought not to impose it. Presbyters are permitted to veil widows; only bishops may veil virgins.

### Blessing of the Garments of a Widow

[Col. 1099D]

God, creator of visible and invisible things, be graciously present, and, with your grace watering from above, deign to bless and sanctify these garments displaying the image of holiness. Through.

### Another

Open, we beseech you, Lord, the eyes of your majesty to bless this garment of widowhood, so that she who pleased her husband in ornate garments may deserve to preserve, in sacred garments, the vestments of your blessing. Through.

Then let the Litany be sung. After the Litany this preface follows:

[Col. 1100A]

“Let us humbly beseech the incorrupt God of eternity and Lord of inviolable nature, dearest brothers, asking on behalf of our sister N., who has vowed to serve the Lord in perfect continence and modesty of body and mind, that he himself, who is the judge of widows, may grant the petitioner perfect continence.”

### Proper Blessing of a Widow

Console, Lord, this handmaid of yours, bound by the hardships of widowhood, just as you deigned to console the widow of Sarepta through the prophet Elijah. Grant her the fruit of modesty, so that she may not remember former pleasures. Let her also not know, etc.

### Another

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that this handmaid of yours, who desires to be consecrated to you, Lord, in hope of eternal reward, etc.

Let her place the veil upon her head.

### Prayer after Receiving the Garment and Veil

[Col. 1100B]

May your merciful protection, Lord, strengthen your handmaid, etc.

### Another

Lord Jesus Christ, God of all, who, among the other teachings of virtue for our salvation, restored the vigor of chastity and modesty, we humbly beseech you to guard and defend this widow, our sister, who has turned to the grace of your mercy from her heart, safe from all the temptations of enemies. Grant that this covering of her head may persevere as a protection for the inner person. Through.

### Another

Lord God, eternal ruler of the heavenly powers, we pour out our prayers before you, asking that you deign to consecrate this handmaid of yours, N., whom you stripped from her former way of life to renew her life, making her put off the old person and put on the new. Just as Anna the prophetess, clothed in the garment of widowhood for many years, faithfully [Col. 1100C] served in the temple of your glory with fasts and prayers, so may this handmaid of yours serve you alone, God, in your Church with devoted mind. Through.

O God, lover of chastity. And the rest.

# Ordination of an Abbess

[Note: [Col. 1099D] By this term Saint Gregory the Great already refers to the matter in book VI of the *Registries*, letter 22, writing to Respecta, abbess of Marseille, in these words: “Let her be appointed not an outsider, but one whom the community chooses from among its own; nevertheless, if she is judged worthy of this monastery, let the bishop of that place appoint her.”]

## Who Professes the Canonical Rule

At the ordination of an abbess, the bishop ought to sing Mass and bless her in this manner. After the Introit antiphon, the prayer has been said, and the rest of the office of the Mass up to the Gospel, the elect is to prostrate herself before the altar with two or three of her sisters, and the Litanies are to be sung there. When these have been completed, the bishop blesses her with bowed head, saying:

The Lord be with you.

And with your spirit.

The prayer follows.

Let us pray:

Hear, Lord, our prayers, and send upon this handmaid of yours the Spirit of your blessing, so that, dedicated by a heavenly gift, she may obtain the grace of your majesty and offer others an example of good living. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, who lives and reigns with you, God, in the unity of that same Holy Spirit.

### Another

We humbly implore your almighty power, Lord, that you graciously pour out upon this handmaid of yours, whom you have deigned to assume into sacred office, the gift of your blessing, and grant her the grace of sanctification, so that what she receives through your gift she may preserve unharmed under your protection. Through.

And he continues this prayer in the form of a preface:

[Col. 1101A]

Holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, be present to our prayers, be present to our vows, be present to our service, be present to our consecrations. You wondrously administer all things through the word of your power and provide what is to be administered. You who always adorn your Church with different flowers, illuminating her both with the examples of men and with the institutions of illustrious women. You who have also deigned to attach this handmaid of yours, from the weaker sex, to the service of your service.

Pour out, we beseech you, Lord, upon this handmaid of yours, whom we faithfully dedicate to divine office, the grace of the Holy Spirit, so that she may graciously complete her service to you at all times. Deign to bless, sanctify, or consecrate her with the right hand of your power for a work worthy of your ministry, so that she may carry out the act of the ministry entrusted to her faithfully [lacuna], and be strengthened by the power of the sevenfold grace of that same Holy Spirit.

[Col. 1101B]

Therefore, Lord, may the Spirit of wisdom and piety rest upon her, and fill her with the Spirit of your fear. Grant her also seriousness in conduct and discipline in living, so that she may meditate on your law day and night. May she keep your commandments, obey your words, devote herself to sacred readings, despise earthly and transitory things, and serve good works at all times.

May she overcome every lust for perverse pleasure and hold fast the love of honorable chastity, so that she may be able to meet you, her Bridegroom, when you come, with her unextinguished lamps; may she be joined to the choir of the virgins who went before; and, lest she be shut out with the foolish, may she enter freely through the royal gate with the wise.

[Col. 1101C]

May every form of virtue abound in her: modest authority, constant modesty, purity of innocence, and spiritual observance of discipline. May your commandments shine in her conduct, so that by the example of your chastity she may offer all subject to her a pure pattern for imitation. Showing a good testimony of conscience, may she remain firm and steadfast in Christ Jesus, and, with your help, carry out the ministry she has received in such a way that, by your gift, she may deserve to attain eternal reward. Through the same Lord of ours.

Then he gives her the Rule, saying:

“Receive the Rule of holy conduct together with the grace of divine blessing. May you be able, through it, to be presented undefiled before the Lord on the day of strict judgment together with the flock entrusted to you. May he deign to help you, who lives with God the Father.”

[Col. 1101D]

The prayer follows:

Lord God almighty, who caused Miriam, the sister of Moses, with the other women leading the way, to come joyfully to the seashore amid the surging waters, with timbrels and dances, we humbly beseech you on behalf of your faithful handmaid, who today is appointed abbess as a mother in the chair over all those subject to her. May she govern all your handmaids according to the canonical rule, so that, with your help, she may joyfully enter eternal glory with all of them; and there, rejoicing with the angels and singing new songs, may she follow the Lamb wherever he goes, Christ our Lord.

May your grace always bless your handmaid, Lord, and lead her blameless to eternal life. Through.

If the ordination has taken place in her own house, “We praise you, O God” is to be sung, with the people acclaiming, “Lord, have mercy.” Afterwards this prayer is said for the dignity she has received:

O Lord, fountain of all good things and giver of the progress of the just, grant, we beseech you, that your handmaid may govern well the dignity she has obtained and demonstrate through good works what has been granted to her by you. Through.

Likewise, if she has been consecrated elsewhere, when she returns to the monastery the entire choir of virgins is to go honorably to meet her with crosses, blessed water, incense, and the Gospel. At that very entrance they are to begin “We praise you, O God,” with the crowd acclaiming, “Lord, have mercy,” and the presbyter continuing the prayer as above: “O Lord, fountain of all good things.”

# Ordination of an Abbess

## Who Professes the Monastic Rule

A chapter from the canon of Theodore, archbishop of the English.

*(From Codex monasticus Murensis, formerly of the monastery at Niedermünster, Regensburg, eleventh century.)*

[Col. 1102B]

At the ordination of an abbess, the bishop ought to celebrate Mass and bless her in this manner.

After the Introit antiphon, the prayer has been said, and the rest of the office of the Mass up to the Gospel, the elect is to prostrate herself before the altar behind the bishop. The Litanies are to be sung there, followed by the Lord’s Prayer with these petitions:

Save your handmaid, Lord, my God.

May the Lord preserve her and give her life.

**R.** And make her blessed upon the earth.

[Col. 1102C]

May the Lord guard your coming in and your going out.

**R.** From this time forth.

May the Lord guard you from every evil.

**R.** May the Lord guard your soul.

May he send you help from the sanctuary.

**R.** And from Zion.

Be for her a tower of strength.

**R.** From the face of the enemy.

Rise, Lord, help us.

**R.** And deliver us.

Lord, hear my prayer.

**R.** And let my cry come to you.

When these petitions have been completed, the bishop blesses her with bowed head, saying:

The Lord be with you.

**R.** And with your spirit.

The following prayer is said:

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that our desire may receive the effect of your mercy, and accompany with the gift of your grace your handmaid whom we have chosen for the governance of souls, so that, by your bounty, we may please you together with her through our devotion. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

### Another

O God, author of all good things, who through your servant Moses established leaders to govern the Churches, we pour out our prayers before you and beseech you with devoted minds: deign to fortify with the grace of your protection this handmaid of yours, N., whom the restraint and election of your handmaids has today established as abbess over your handmaids.

Grant that she may govern her subjects and the sheep entrusted to her in such a way that, having attained the kingdom of heaven with them all, and continually supported, with the Lord’s help, by apostolic teachings, she may joyfully enter the gates of [Col. 1103A] paradise with a hundredfold fruit, and, while you praise her, Lord, may she deserve to hear:

“Well done, good and faithful servant. Because you have been faithful over a little, I will set you over much. Enter into the joy of your Lord.”

May you yourself grant this.

Then he lays his hand upon her head.

[Note: [Col. 1103D] We noted in *Disquisitions*, part II, chapter 4, no. 11, a passage from the pontifical of Christian, archbishop of Mainz, where, after this imposition of the hand is mentioned in the consecration of an abbot, the following is added: “But this does not take place in his blessing.” Hence we were readily led to believe that here he distinguished the consecration of episcopal order, which was in some places conferred upon abbots, from the simple blessing of abbots and abbesses, which is the matter [Col. 1104D] treated here and afterward, where the same rite is prescribed in the consecration when an abbot or abbess is ordained in a monastery.]

Saying this prayer in the form of a preface.

Almighty and eternal God, graciously pour forth the Spirit of your blessing upon N., being propitiated by our prayers, so that she who today is constituted abbess by the imposition of hands may remain, through your sanctification, worthy of your election, and may never afterward be separated, as one unworthy, from your grace. May she receive, by your generosity, Lord, perseverance in good works, steadfastness in adversity, endurance in tribulation, desire for fasting, mercy amid impiety, authority in humility, hatred of pride, love in faith, vigilance in teaching, self-restraint in chastity, abstinence in luxury, moderation amid variety, and instruction in conduct. By your gift, Lord, may she be such in this ministry as Saint Stephen, the Levite chosen by the apostles, deserved to persevere. From today onward, by your abundant blessing, may she despise and reject every diabolical way of life; may she scorn present things, love heavenly things, and desire eternal rewards. May she be an example and pattern of righteousness for faithfully governing and directing the Church, so that she may always prove an able watchwoman among her fellow sisters; may she be rich in counsel, diligence, discipline, judgment, effectiveness, and correction. Thus, by your gift, Lord, may she serve you with a pure heart in all your commandments without reproach, so that, with interest multiplied a hundredfold, she may attain the prize of the heavenly calling, the crown of righteousness, and your gifts among the treasures of heaven. Through [Christ our Lord].

Then he gives her the rule, saying:

Receive the rule handed down to us by the holy Fathers, for governing and guarding the flock entrusted to you by the Lord, insofar as God himself strengthens you and human frailty permits.

Lord God almighty, who caused the sister of Moses, Miriam, to go before the other women and to come joyfully to the seashore amid the waves, with timbrels and dances, we humbly beseech you on behalf of your faithful servant N., who today is constituted abbess in the maternal chair over all her subjects: may she guard all your servants according to canonical discipline, so that, with your help, she may joyfully enter eternal glory with them all, and there, exulting with the angels and singing a new song, may follow the Lamb wherever he goes. Through [Christ our Lord].

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that your servant the abbess, by showing and practicing what is right, may instruct the souls of her subjects by the example of good works and receive from you, most loving God, the reward of eternal recompense. Through [Christ our Lord].

Lord, fountain of all good things and rewarder of righteous advancement, grant your servant to exercise well the dignity she has attained and to prove by good works the dignity bestowed upon her by you. Through our Lord.

If the appointment of the abbess has taken place inside the monastery, let the *Te Deum laudamus* be sung, with the people acclaiming, “Kyrie eleison.” Afterward let this prayer be said following the attainment of the dignity:

God, whom every power and dignity serves, grant your servant N. a prosperous exercise of her dignity, in which may she always fear you and continually strive to please you. Through [Christ our Lord].

If the abbess has been consecrated elsewhere, when she returns to the monastery let the entire choir of nuns honorably go before her with crosses, holy water, incense, and the Gospel. At the very entrance of the church let the *Te Deum laudamus* be sung, with the crowd crying, “Kyrie eleison,” and the priest continuing with the prayers given above: “God, whom every power and dignity serves,” and so forth.

# Consecration of a Sacred Virgin

Celebrated on Epiphany, or on Easter Monday, and on the birthdays of the apostles.

All who are to be promoted to holy orders must be consecrated before the proclamation of the Gospel. Virgins are to be veiled after the Gospel has been read. After the Gospel and after the litany has been said, with her prostrate and her head bowed before the altar, let the bishop bless her, saying:

Look, Lord, upon this servant of yours, N., so that the purpose of virginity which she has undertaken at your inspiration she may preserve under your governance. Through [Christ our Lord].

## Consecration in the manner of a preface

God, gracious inhabitant of chaste bodies and lover of incorrupt hearts; God, who repair in your Word—through whom all things were made—the human substance corrupted in the first human beings by the devil’s deceit, so that you not only restore it to the innocence of its first origin but also lead it to the experience of certain blessings that are to be possessed in the new age; and who raise those bound by mortal condition to the likeness of angels: look upon this servant of yours, who, placing the vow and purpose of her continence in your hand, offers her devotion to you, from whom she also received this same vow.

For when the soul enclosed in mortal flesh would have to overcome the law of nature, the freedom of license, the force of custom, and the impulses of youth, unless you mercifully kindled this love through free will, mercifully nourished this desire in her heart, and supplied strength—your grace poured out upon all nations, adopting as heirs of the New Testament people from every nation under heaven, beyond number like the stars—among the other virtues that you have implanted in your children, begotten not from bloods, nor from the will of the flesh, but from your Spirit, this gift also flowed from the fountain of your generosity into certain minds.

Although no prohibition had diminished the honor of marriage and the original blessing remained upon holy wedlock, there nevertheless arose souls of greater sublimity who rejected the union of man and woman, desired the sacrament, and did not imitate what is enacted in marriage but loved what marriage signifies beforehand. Blessed virginity, rivaling angelic integrity, recognized its author and devoted itself to his bridal chamber and his bedchamber—he who is the bridegroom of perpetual virginity in the same way as he is the son of perpetual virginity.

To her who implores your help, Lord, and desires to be strengthened by the consecration of your blessing, grant the protection and guidance of your defense. May the ancient enemy, who assails higher aspirations with more subtle snares, not creep through some negligence of mind and cut off the palm of perfect continence, nor seize from the purpose of virgins what ought by conduct to belong to married women.

Let there be in her, Lord, through the gift of your Spirit, prudent modesty, wise kindness, solemn gentleness, and chaste freedom. Let her burn with charity and love nothing outside you. Let her live laudably and not desire to be praised. Let her glorify you in the holiness of her body and in the devotion of her soul; let her fear you through love, love you through love, and serve you through love.

May you be her honor, her joy, her delight; in sorrow, her consolation; in uncertainty, her counsel; in injury, her defense; in tribulation, her patience; in poverty, her abundance; in fasting, her food; in weakness, her medicine. In you may she possess everything whom she desires to love above all things. May she preserve what she has professed, pleasing the searcher of hearts not by her body but by her mind.

Let her enter the number of the wise young women, so that she may await the heavenly Bridegroom with lamps lit and oil prepared. May she not, troubled by the unexpected arrival of the king, but secure with her light and joyfully accompanied by the choir of the virgins who went before, meet him; may she not be shut out with the foolish, but freely enter the royal gate with the wise virgins; and may she remain in the eternal company of your Lamb, abiding in approved chastity.

When the blessing has been completed, let the bishop place the veil over the virgin’s head, saying:

Receive the sacred veil of the maiden, which you are to bear without stain before the tribunal of Christ, before whom every knee of those in heaven, on earth, and under the earth is bent, forever and ever.

Then let those standing around sing an antiphon for each action:

The Lord has clothed you in a gold-woven robe (*cyclas*) and adorned you with immense necklaces.

## Prayer after taking the veil

May your mercy, Lord, guard and strengthen your servant, so that the purpose of holy continence which she has undertaken at your inspiration she may preserve unharmed under your protection. Through [Christ our Lord].

The antiphon follows: “To him be betrothed,” and so forth.

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that this servant of yours, N., who desires to be consecrated to you, Lord, in hope of eternal reward, may remain with full faith and a steadfast spirit in her holy purpose. You, almighty Father, graciously sanctify, bless, and preserve her forever; grant her humility, chastity, obedience, charity, and an abundance of every good work. Grant her, Lord, glory in exchange for her works and holiness in exchange for her modesty, so that she may attain the reward of glory. Through [Christ our Lord].

Then let those standing around sing: “He placed a sign upon your face,” and so forth.

God, creator of bodies and breather of souls, who despise no age and reject no sex, who deem no condition unworthy of your grace, but are equally creator and redeemer: you have deigned to choose this servant of yours from the entire number of the flock, as a good shepherd, to preserve the crown of perpetual virginity and the chastity of her soul. Prepare her with the shield of your protection and with wisdom as her guide for every work of virtue and glory, so that, overcoming the allurements of the flesh and refusing lawful marriages, she may deserve the indissoluble union with your Son, our Lord Jesus Christ.

For her we ask, Lord, that you supply weapons not of the flesh but powerful through the virtue of the Spirit, so that, while you defend her, her senses and members may be preserved from every sin, and, while she desires to live under your grace, no enemy of goodness may prevail in claiming anything for itself from this vessel consecrated to your name.

May heavenly grace extinguish every natural heat; may it kindle the light of perpetual chastity; may her modest face not be open to scandals, lest negligence unwisely give occasion for wrongdoing. May chaste virginity be in her, adorned with unimpaired faith, certain hope, and sincere charity, so that, with her mind prepared for continence, she may be granted such virtue as overcomes every fabrication of the devil.

By scorning present things, may she pursue future things; may she prefer fasts to bodily feasts; may she place sacred readings and prayers before banquets and drinking, so that, nourished by prayers and illumined by vigils, she may perform the work of virginal grace. Fortifying this servant of yours inwardly and outwardly with these weapons of virtue, grant that she may complete the course of virginity without stumbling. Through our Lord.

## For giving the ring

Receive the ring of faith, the seal of the Holy Spirit, so that you may be called the bride of God if you serve him faithfully. Through [Christ our Lord].

## For the necklace

Receive the sign of Christ upon your head, so that you may become his wife and, if you remain in him, may be crowned forever. Through our Lord.

Meanwhile let the antiphon be said: “With his ring he betrothed her.” The blessing follows:

May God the Father almighty, creator of heaven and earth, bless you—he who has deigned to choose you for fellowship with holy Mary, the mother of our Lord Jesus Christ—so that you may preserve before the Lord and his angels the whole and unstained virginity you have professed, hold fast your purpose, love chastity, preserve patience, and deserve to receive the crown of virginity. Through [Christ our Lord].

After this the maiden sets down the candles and offers the offering; then, taking up the candles again, she stands until Communion and the Mass have ended. Let her receive Communion through the eighth day. If there is someone who has testified for her, let the bishop place her in his hands, saying:
