Lord almighty God, who commanded the substance of the waters to be beneath your hidden things, and who, with the cooperation of the Holy Spirit, granted us through it the remission of all sins, grant through the works of your justice that this water, although flowing, may nevertheless be sanctified by the power of the Holy Trinity. May it drive away the inventions of all phantoms, and give security to the just and innocent concerning the stated cause for which they are to be examined; and to the guilty, the manifestation of their faults [Col. 1132A], so that in this proof each may praise your holy name: one through the integrity of justice, the other through the correction of obstinacy, in that glory in which you remain through ages of ages. Amen.

Lord almighty God, who commanded baptism to be performed in water and deigned through the bath of regeneration to grant the human race the remission of all sins, sanctify, we beseech you, this flowing water, and discern a just judgment in it—you alone are judge and strong—so that if this man is innocent of the stated cause, the water which received him in baptism may now receive him within itself, and he may be drawn out clean and innocent from the depths of this water. Through …

After the water has been conjured and blessed [Col. 1132B], let him strip them of their garments and have each of them kiss the Gospel and the cross of Christ. After this, having adjured him with these words, let him sprinkle each one with that blessed water:

“I adjure you, N., by the invocation of our Lord Jesus Christ and by the judgment of cold water; I adjure you by the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, and by the inseparable Trinity, and by our Lord Jesus Christ, and by all the angels and archangels, and by all the saints of God, and by the fearful day of God’s judgment, and by the twenty-four elders who praise God daily, and by the four evangelists, and by the twelve apostles, and by the twelve prophets, by martyrs, confessors, and virgins, and by principalities and powers, dominions and virtues, thrones, cherubim, and seraphim, and by all heavenly secrets [Col. 1132C], I adjure you; and by the three young men who daily praise God—Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego—and by the CIX. IIII. thousand [the number is uncertain as printed] who suffered for Christ, and by holy Mary, the mother of our Lord Jesus Christ, and by the entire people of God, and by that baptism with which the priest regenerated you over the water, I adjure you: if you know about this theft, or saw it, or carried it, or received it into your house, or were consenting or party to it; or if you have a bloated or hardened heart; or if you are guilty in this matter, let your heart vanish, and let the water not receive you, nor may any magic prevail against this.

“Do this, Lord Jesus Christ, for the praise and glory of your name, so that all may acknowledge that you are the blessed God who lives and reigns forever.”

[Col. 1132D]

After the blessing of the water, let him say these verses:

“Let God arise, and let his enemies be scattered, and let those who hate him flee from his face. As smoke vanishes, so may they vanish. As wax melts before the fire, so may they perish before the face of God.”

Three times, with the Gloria. Then [Note: [Col. 1131D] In Eccard, vol. II of *Frankish Affairs*, the title *Judgment of Hot Water and Red-Hot Iron* is prefixed; what is lacking here is supplied there. Then the judgment of bread and cheese is also added.] he shall immediately throw them into the water. All these things must be done fasting; those who put them into the water must not eat beforehand either.

When someone is questioned about theft, fornication, adultery, or any other matter, and refuses to confess to his master, elder, or others, the procedure shall be as follows. The priest, going to the church, shall put on the sacred vestments, except the chasuble, carrying in his left hand the holy Gospel with the chrismatory [Col. 1133A] and the relics of the saints, as well as the chalice. With “the crime involved” [*crimine implicito*, a corrupt or uncertain reading], in the church atrium, he shall say to the people standing at the church door:

“See, brothers, the office of the Christian religion. Behold the law in which hope and the remission of sins are found; here is the anointing of chrism; here is the consecration of the body and blood of the Lord. Take care lest you deprive yourselves of so great an inheritance of blessedness and fellowship by involving yourselves in another’s crime, for it is written: ‘Not only those who do these things, but also those who consent to those who do them, are worthy of death.’”

## ORDER OF TESTING BY WATER, GLOWING PLOUGHSHARES, BREAD AND CHEESE, ETC.

[Note: [Col. 1133D] This codex is defective at its beginning and end and also contains some lacunae in the middle, which could scarcely be supplied from elsewhere. Accordingly, we have restored from Martene, in smaller type, only those passages in our codex that have been worn away or rubbed out by age. It is readily apparent that the entire Mass was placed here; for performing the judgment of the proof in cold water, the same Martene presents it from a manuscript of Saint-Victor in Paris, vol. II, *On the Ancient Rites of the Church*, p. 942. The material found here at the beginning is the ending of the Gospel, incorrectly cited there as being from John, whereas it is from Mark XI. Thus the codex begins.]

(From the Rhenaugiensis Codex, eleventh or twelfth century.)

… your sins. But if you do not forgive, neither will your Father who is in heaven forgive your sins [Col. 1133B] … Offertory. “From the depths I have cried to you, O Lord.”

### Secret

May the holy things we handle, O Lord, absolve us from every guilt, and may these same things protect us from every assault of wickedness and diabolical illusion. Through …

### Communion

“Amen, I say to you, whatever …”

### Prayer after Communion

Strike down by the power of your right hand those who conspire against the firm support of your fullness, so that iniquity may not rule over justice, but falsehood may be subjected to truth.

Another. Show us your mercy, O Lord, for examining the right judgment, so that through the coming of the Holy Spirit every falsehood of diabolical art may be driven far away. Through …

### Conjuration

“I adjure you, men, by the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, and by the Holy Trinity, and by the invocation of the only-begotten Son, and by the Christianity which you have received (or ‘your Christianity’), and by the holy Gospel, and by these relics which are in this church, that you [plural variant: *mas*] presume in no way to receive Communion or approach the altar if you (singular: *tu*) have done this (*ti*), consented to it (*ti*), or know (*scisti*) who did it.”

Here begin the seven penitential psalms. And the following Litany.

“Kyrie eleison. Christe eleison. Christ, hear us. Savior of the world, help us. Holy Mary, pray. Saint Michael, pray. Saint Gabriel, pray. Saint Raphael, pray. All holy angels and archangels, pray for us. Saint John, pray. Saint Peter, pray. Saint Paul, pray. Saint Andrew, pray. Saint James, pray. Saint Philip, pray. Saint Bartholomew, pray. Saint Matthew, pray. Saint Thomas, pray. Saint Thaddeus, pray. Saint Simon, pray. Saint Matthias, pray. Saint Barnabas, pray. Saint Mark, pray. Saint Luke, pray. All holy apostles, pray. Saint Stephen, pray. Saint Lawrence, pray. Saint Cletus, pray. Saint Clement, pray. Saint Sixtus, pray. Saint Cornelius, pray. Saint Cyprian, pray. Saint Alexander, pray. Saint Felix, pray. Saint Agapitus, pray. Saint Callistus, pray. Saint Marcellus, pray. All holy martyrs, pray for us. [Lacuna.]

“Saint Ambrose, pray. Saint Severinus, pray. Saint Augustine, pray. Saint Jerome, pray. Saint Servatius, pray. Saint Sylvester, pray. Saint Damasus, pray. Saint Leo, pray. Saint Eusebius, pray. Saint Gregory, pray. All holy confessors, pray for us. Saint Felicity, pray. Saint Perpetua, pray. Saint Petronilla, pray. Saint Agnes, pray. Saint Agatha, pray. Saint Cecilia, pray. Saint Juliana, pray. Saint Lucy, pray. Saint Thecla, pray. Saint Afra, pray. Saint Columba, pray. Saint Anastasia, pray. Saint Susanna, pray. Saint Eugenia, pray. Saint Euphemia, pray. All holy virgins and widows, pray for us. All holy infants and innocents, pray. All holy penitents, pray for us. All holy monks and hermits, pray. All holy ones, pray for us.

“Be favorable: spare us, O Lord. Be favorable: deliver us, O Lord. From every evil, deliver us, O Lord. From evil disease, deliver us, O Lord. From the danger of death, deliver us, O Lord. From every iniquity, deliver us, O Lord. Through your cross and Passion, save us.

“We sinners, we ask you: hear us. That you grant us peace, we ask you. That you grant us health, we ask you. That you grant us the remission of sins, we ask you. That you grant us good weather, we ask you. That you grant us the fruits of the earth, we ask you. That you deign to preserve the apostolic lord in holy religion, we ask you. That you preserve our king and the army of Christians in perpetual prosperity; that you deign to grant them life, health, and victory [Col. 1134D], we ask you. For the nature of this matter, we ask you: hear us. That iniquity may not rule over justice, but falsehood may be subjected to truth, we ask you. That you deign to discern a just judgment, we ask you. Son of God, we ask you: hear us.

“Lamb of God, who take away the sins of the world, have mercy on us. Lamb of God, who take away the sins of the world, spare us. Christ, hear us.”

[Col. 1135A]

“Kyrie eleison. Christe eleison. Kyrie eleison. Our Father. You are just, O Lord, and your judgment is right. Show us your mercy, O Lord, and grant us your salvation. Let your mercy, O Lord, be upon us, as we have hoped in you. Convert us, O God, and turn your anger away from us. Have mercy on us, O Lord; have mercy on us. Not to us, O Lord, not to us, but give glory to your name. O Lord, hear my prayer. Psalm: May God have mercy on us. O Lord, God of hosts, convert us and show … The Lord be with you. And with your spirit.”

## BLESSING OF THE JUDICIAL IRON: PRAYER

Bless, O Lord, by the power of your might, this kind of metal, so that in it, with every deception of demons driven far away and every enchantment and deception of unbelievers removed, the truth of your most true judgment may be revealed to your faithful [Col. 1135B], so that your praiseworthy and glorious name may always be glorified in your holy Church. Through …

### Prayer to be made before the judgment

God, creator of human beings and author of every goodness, look upon us, your servants, crying to you with our whole heart. Mercifully grant, through the intercession of your only-begotten Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, that in this judgment of examination no darts of the enemy’s falsehood may prevail, but that through you the truth may be manifested and the rectitude of justice declared. Through the same Christ.

## BLESSING OF THE BURNING IRON FOR THE JUDGMENT OF GOD

Almighty God, God of Abraham, God of Isaac, God of Jacob, God of all who live well, God, origin and manifestation of all justice, who alone are [Col. 1135C] the just judge, strong and patient, deign to hear us, your servants, praying to you for the blessing of this iron. Therefore we ask you, Lord, judge of all, to deign to send your holy and true blessing upon this iron, so that it may be refreshment to those who carry it and possess justice and believe in your justice and strength; and that it may be burning fire for the wicked, for those who do wicked things, and for those who believe in their own injustice and in the unjust pomp of the devil.

Turn, O Lord, the unbelief of the unjust through your power and blessing and through the invocation of the Holy Trinity, the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. Send into this iron the force of your power and truth, so that in it your truest justice, known to you alone, may always, through your mercy and truth, be most clearly declared to your faithful for the correction of the wicked, whatever question may have been brought forward for judgment. Let the devil’s power have no ability either to conceal or to distort your truth. Rather, let it be for your servants a defense of faith, leading them to belief in your divine majesty and to assurance of your most manifest mercy and truest truth. Through …

Another. God, just judge, author of peace, and judge of equity, we humbly ask you to deign to bless and sanctify this iron, appointed for the just examination of any doubt [Col. 1136A], so that if an innocent person in the aforementioned matter, concerning which purgation is sought, takes (*acceperit*; plural *acceperint*) this heated iron in his hands or places (*immiserit*; plural *immiserint*) his feet upon it, he may appear (*appareat*; plural *appareant*) unharmed (*illaesus*; plural *illaesi*); but if he is guilty (*culpabilis*; variants *culpabiles*) or liable (*reus*; variants *rei*), may your power most justly declare this in it with truth, so that iniquity may not rule over justice, but falsehood may be subjected to truth. Through … [Note: [Col. 1135D] The last part is absent in Martene.]

May the blessing of God the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit descend upon this iron, for discerning the true judgment of God.

### Prayer for boiling water, for carrying out the judgment of God

God, just, strong, and patient judge, author of peace and judge of equity, judge what is just, O Lord, for your judgment is right. You look upon the earth and make it tremble. You, almighty God [Col. 1136B], who through the coming of your Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, saved the world and through his most holy Passion redeemed the human race, sanctify this water boiling with fire.

You who saved the three young men, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, when King Nebuchadnezzar commanded them to be placed in a furnace blazing with fire, preserving them unharmed and leading them out through your angel, merciful ruler, grant that if an innocent person, concerning this theft or this sexual offense, puts his hand into this water boiling with fire, just as you delivered the three young men mentioned above from the furnace of fire and freed Susanna from a false accusation, so you may bring him safely and unharmed out of this water boiling with fire.

But if a guilty person, with his heart hardened under the devil’s pressure, presumes to put his hand into this water boiling with fire, may your most just truth [Col. 1136C] reveal it, and manifest your truth in his body, so that his soul may be saved through repentance. And if, being guilty, he wishes to cover his sins by any magic or herbs, may your right hand deign to undo this. Through your only Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, who with you …

Another. I bless you, creature of water made boiling by fire, in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, from whom all things proceed. I adjure you by him who commanded you to water the whole earth from four rivers, who brought you forth from the rock, and who changed you into wine, so that neither the devil’s snares nor human malice may be able to separate you from the truth of judgment. Rather, punish the guilty (*noxium*; variant forms *os, am, as*) and keep the unharmed and innocent pure.

Through him from whom no hidden things are concealed, who sent you through the flood over the whole world to destroy sinners, and who is still to come to judge the living and the dead and the age by fire.

Another. Almighty God, we humbly beseech you concerning the examination of this matter which we are now debating here among ourselves: let iniquity not rule over justice, but let falsehood be subjected to truth. And if anyone should wish to conceal or obstruct this present examination through any magic or through herbs of the earth, may you, the holy and most just judge, deign to undo it with your right hand.

Alia. Let us pray. Almighty and eternal God, who in your unchangeable ordering justly discern all your judgments as judge everywhere, mercifully declare in this judgment, at the invocation of your holy name—which the intention of the faithful implores from you—the result of your most just examination. Through [Christ our Lord]. Afterwards let it be scented with the smoke of myrrh, and let a cauldron be taken, beneath and around which [the rite is performed]; thus every theft will be proved.

## Blessing of Cold Water for the Judgment of God

Almighty and eternal God, attend to our invocations, and pour the power of your blessing upon this water prepared for the purification of this person [or these persons], so that the health sought through the invocation of your name may be defended from every assault of the ancient enemy. Through [Christ our Lord].

### Adjuratio

I adjure you, man [or men], by the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, by the day of the dreadful judgment, and by the four Evangelists, and by the twenty-four elders who praise the Lord with tireless voice and never cease. I adjure you by the twelve Apostles and by the 144,000 innocents who suffered for Christ, by the victory of the martyrs, and by the invocation of your sacred baptism: if you are guilty in this matter, whether in deed or in any way, and if, with a hardened heart through the devil’s suggestion, you approach this judgment presumptuously, may the water not receive you, and may this sign of the cross of Christ reveal your wickedness, while the power of almighty God is manifested. Through the same [Lord].

## Blessing of the Same Water

Lord God almighty, who commanded that baptism be performed in water and graciously willed, through the bath of regeneration, to grant remission of sins to the human race, sanctify, we ask, this water, and [establish] in it a just judgment for discerning [the guilty], since you alone are the just and mighty judge. If this man is guilty of the matter previously named, may the water that received him in baptism not receive him now. But if he is blameless and innocent in this matter, may the water that received him in baptism now receive him into itself; and if he is clean and innocent in this matter, may he be drawn out sound from the depths of this water. Through [Christ our Lord].

### Adjuratio

I adjure you, water, in the name of the almighty Father, who created you in the beginning and commanded you to minister to human needs, who commanded you to be separated from the waters above. I also adjure you by the ineffable name of Jesus Christ, the Son of almighty God, beneath whose feet, as he walked upon the sea, you offered yourself to be trodden, and who also willed to be baptized in you. I also adjure you by the Holy Spirit, who descended upon the Lord when he was baptized. I adjure you by the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, by whose will the element of water was divided, and the people of Israel passed through it with dry feet; at whose invocation Elijah made the iron that had fallen from its handle float upon the water: in no way receive this man N., if he is guilty in any respect of what is charged against him. Through [Christ our Lord].

### Third Adjuratio

If that man for whom this person is to be sent for testing is guilty in any respect—whether through actions, consent, knowledge, or any device—make him float upon you, and let no cause of any kind, nor any trickery, be able to prevent that matter from being revealed. I adjure you by the name of Christ and command you to obey us through the name of him whom every creature serves, whom the Cherubim and Seraphim praise together, saying: “Holy, holy, holy is the Lord, God of hosts,” who also reigns and rules through endless ages of ages. Amen.

### Fourth Adjuratio

God, who established the greatest sacraments in the substance of water, graciously attend to our invocations, and pour the power of your blessing upon this element prepared through manifold purifications, so that this creature, serving your mysteries, may receive from divine grace the power to expose diabolical and human deceptions, to dissolve their arguments and fabrications, and to destroy their many-formed arts.

Let every ambush of the concealed enemy depart from here, so that the truth concerning those things which, unknown to divine perception and to the minds of others, are sought from us may, having been demanded by your judgment and disclosed through the invocation of your holy name, shine forth clearly. Let the innocent not be unjustly condemned because of what we seek, nor let the guilty, before you who are the true light, for whom darkness is not obscure and who enlighten our darkness, deceive those seeking the truth without penalty.

With you revealing what is hidden, and through your power, since you are the knower of hidden things, let true knowledge be made manifest here to us who believe in you. Through [Christ our Lord].

### Fifth Adjuratio

I adjure you, man N., by the invocation of our Lord Jesus Christ, for the judgment of cold water. I adjure you by the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, by the inseparable Trinity, and by all. Two leaves are missing here in the manuscript.

“The Word became flesh and dwelt among us, and we saw his glory, glory as of the Only-Begotten from the Father, full of grace and truth.”

## Judgment by Ploughshares

Lord God almighty, who created heaven and earth, the sea and all that is in them; who formed humanity in your image; who sent your only-begotten Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, with the cooperation of the Holy Spirit, into the womb of the undefiled Virgin; who willed that he take human flesh from her—we invoke you through the name of that most beloved Son of yours, our Lord Jesus Christ, and through the merits of holy Mary, Mother of God, and we humbly beseech your majesty: in this judgment of examination command all the tricks of diabolical fraud and cunning to vanish, whether the enchantments of men or women, and likewise the powers of herbs, so that it may appear to all standing here that you are just and love justice, and that no one can resist your majesty.

Therefore, Lord, ruler of heaven and earth, creator of the waters, king of all your creation, in your holy name and power we bless these ploughshares for discerning a true judgment. If this man is innocent in the matter under investigation and dispute among us, and walks barefoot upon them, may you, almighty God, just as you delivered the three boys from the furnace of blazing fire, Susanna from a false accusation, and Daniel from the lions’ den, preserve his innocent feet safe and unharmed by your powerful might.

But if this man is guilty of the matter previously named, and, persuaded by the devil, dares to test your power and walks upon them, then you who are just and judge, make a burn visibly appear upon his feet: to your honor, praise, and glory; to us, your servants, for steadfastness and confidence in your name; and to the faithless and blinded, for the confusion and repentance of their sins, so that unwillingly they may recognize what they refused willingly to acknowledge: that you are the judge of the living and the dead, living and reigning through ages of ages. Amen.

After a space of two lines, whose letters appear to have been erased deliberately, the manuscript continues:

Attend, Lord, to our supplications, so that what must be performed through the ministry of our humility may, through the intercession of all your saints, be fulfilled by the effect of your power. Through [Christ our Lord].

May your mercy, Lord, come before us, we ask, and may the clemency of your propitiation anticipate our voices. Through [Christ our Lord].

I exorcise you, creature of salt, by the living God, by the true God, by the holy God, who commanded you through the prophet Elisha to be cast into water so that the sterility of the water might be healed. Become exorcised salt for the salvation of believers, and be health of soul and body to all who receive you. Let every apparition, wickedness, or cunning of diabolical fraud, and every adjured unclean spirit, flee and depart from the place where you have been sprinkled, through him who is to come to judge the living.

I exorcise you, creature of salt, in the name of God the almighty Father, in the charity of our Lord Jesus Christ, and in the power of the Holy Spirit. I exorcise you by the living God, by the true God, by the holy God, who created you for the protection of the human race and commanded you to be consecrated through his servants for the people coming to faith, so that in the name of the holy Trinity you may become a saving sacrament for putting the enemy to flight.

Therefore we ask you, Lord our God, that by sanctifying this creature of salt you sanctify it, and by blessing it you bless it, so that it may become a perfect medicine for all who receive it, remaining in their inward parts, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, who [—].

I exorcise you, creature of salt, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, by his glory and kingdom, by his omnipotence and power. I exorcise you through that redeemer and savior of the world, who [—].

## Various Blessings

### Annual Blessing of a Well

We implore, Lord, the mercy of your loving-kindness: sanctify the water of this well with heavenly blessing, grant it as wholesome for common life, and deign so to drive from it every attack of diabolical temptation that whoever draws or drinks from it, or uses the water drawn from it for any necessary purpose, may enjoy the sweetness of complete health and strength, and may deserve always to give thanks to you, Lord and sanctifier and savior of all. Through [Christ our Lord].

### Over Vessels Found in Ancient Places

Almighty and eternal God, enter into our service, and deign by the power of your majesty so to cleanse these vessels made by the art of the pagans that, every impurity having been driven away, they may be used by your faithful in a time of peace [or: for tranquility]. Through [Christ our Lord].

Alia. God, who at the coming of your Son, our Lord, commanded all your faithful [—], graciously attend to our invocations, and cleanse by the abundance of your grace these vessels which, after the passage of time, your merciful indulgence has drawn from the abyss of the earth and restored to human use. Through [Christ our Lord].

### Blessing for New Crops

Let us pray for your mercy, almighty God, that you may drench with the rain of your blessing these first fruits of your creation, which you have graciously nourished through the moderation of air and rain, and [bring] the fruits of your earth unto matu[—]. The page ends, and the following words, written by another but contemporary hand, continue: “salutary to the human race, and through invocation … so that whoever takes … may receive bodily health and protection of soul.”

### Blessing for Anything You Wish

Bless, Lord, this creation of trees, which your generosity has graciously given us to enjoy, and grant, most merciful Father, that while we eat the fruit of these trees in the name of the holy Trinity, we may share in your everlasting blessing. Through [Christ our Lord].

Alia. Creator and preserver of the human race, giver of spiritual grace, bestower of eternal salvation, Lord, send your Holy Spirit upon this creature of yours, H., so that, armed with the power of heavenly protection, it may profit those who taste it for eternal salvation. Through [Christ our Lord], in the unity of the same Holy Spirit.

### Blessing of a War Banner

Almighty and eternal God, who are the blessing of all things, the strength of those who triumph, and who grant aid from heavenly protection to those who hope in you. [Editorial note, col. 1141D: The following is found above, col. 1121.] Through [Christ our Lord].

### Blessing of a New Sword

Hear, we ask, Lord, our prayers, and this sword, etc.

Alia. Your servant, etc.

Alia. Bless, holy Father, almighty [and eternal] God, etc. Then these antiphons are sung: “Beautiful in form,” etc.

Likewise, a prayer:

Almighty and eternal God, who [have blessed] your servant N., etc.

### Blessing of a New Well

Lord God almighty, who in the height of this well commanded an abundance of water to flow through the channel of its pipes, grant that, by your command and blessing, through the performance of our office, this well may always remain purified and cleansed, with the spectral tricks and diabolical ambushes driven away from it. Through [Christ our Lord].

### Prayer Where Negligence Has Occurred

Lord, holy Father, almighty and eternal God, who through the power of invisibility have provided these visible waters, we, your servants, humbly beseech you: may the grace of the Holy Spirit restore and purify these waters, which negligence has polluted, to cleanliness; may the spirit of the crafty enemy depart; and thereafter grant these sanctified waters as drinkable to your household, so that they may cleanse bodies and sanctify hearts. Through [Christ our Lord].

## Prayer for the Judgment of Bread and Cheese

“Holy, holy, holy” [Greek: *hagios, hagios, hagios*], holy Father, invisible and eternal God, creator of all things, who see the secrets and know all things, God who searches hearts and kidneys. God who delivered Moses and Aaron from the land of Egypt; David from King Saul; Jonah from the belly of the sea-monster; Peter from the waves; Paul from his bonds; Thecla from the beasts; Susanna from a false accusation; the three boys from the furnace of blazing fire; Daniel from the lions’ den; the paralytic from his bed; Lazarus from the tomb: show us your mercy now, so that those who committed these thefts, which are written below, may be unable to make this bread or cheese pass through their jaws or throats. Through [Christ our Lord].

### Exorcism of the Same

I exorcise you, accursed and most unclean dragon and harmful serpent, by the word of truth, by the almighty Lord, and by Jesus Christ the Nazarene, the spotless Lamb sent from the heights, conceived by the Holy Spirit and born from the Virgin Mary, whose coming the angel Gabriel announced, and whom, when John saw him, he proclaimed with a loud voice, saying: “This is the Son of the living God.” In no way allow those who committed these thefts, which we have marked in writing, to partake of this bread or cheese; but let those who are unaware of this crime eat, while those who appear to be aware of it immediately vomit it forth trembling. Through [Christ our Lord].

Alia. I appeal to you, almighty and eternal Father, God, who founded heaven and earth, set the sea within boundaries, fashioned heaven itself, and commanded the great lights—the sun and moon—to shine upon the just and unjust. Lord, make such a sign that every world and all the earth may understand that you are God, who alone performs great wonders. Lord Jesus Christ, Son of the living God, let those who [committed] the matters just mentioned, which are written below, and those who appear to be accomplices and knowledgeable concerning them, have their gullets, tongues, or throats so constricted and bound that they cannot eat this cheese. Through [Christ our Lord].

## Adjuratio of the Men

Here the bread and cheese are divided, half an ounce for each person receiving it.

I admonish you, brothers, in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ the Nazarene: if any one of you has stolen these things, or has been polluted in any way, let him come forward, confess before the holy altar, and make satisfaction. But if he refuses and enters the judgment arrogantly and fearfully [or, according to the correction, “swollen with arrogance”], let him realize that the great judge Jesus [that is, Joshua] is over him, who once killed the covetous man after he had taken spoil; let the prophet Elisha, who detected the theft of his servant, constrict his throat; let the sword of the apostle Peter stand ready to strike the soul of Ananias and Sapphira. Therefore I admonish you: give glory to God and confess to him, lest you enter into temptation.

### Adjuratio

I adjure you, most savage dragon, ancient serpent, by the word of truth and the sign of the brightness of our Lord Jesus Christ, the spotless Lamb begotten from the heights, so that no art of yours may impede it, but that the right judgment of God may stand. Let whoever has consented to this theft reveal God’s judgment with foaming mouth and constricted throat—[the phrase “who loves equity” is omitted]—who is blessed through ages of ages. Amen.

When it is placed in the mouth of the recipient, let this be said:

I adjure you, O man, by the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, by the dreadful day of judgment, by the four Evangelists, by the twelve Apostles, by the sixteen prophets, and by the twenty-four elders who daily worship God with praises; by that Redeemer who deigned to die for our sins upon the holy cross: if you are guilty of or implicated in this theft, concerning which the matter is being handled [or, according to the correction, “from which the account proceeds”], whether you committed it, knew of it, carried it away, or consented to it, let this be ordained for you by the hand of God: may you be unable to eat this bread or cheese except with puffed mouth, foam, groaning, pain, and tears, with your throat constricted and bound. Through the same [Lord].

### First [—] This Conjuration

God of angels and archangels, God of prophets and patriarchs, God of apostles and martyrs, God of confessors and virgins, God the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who at the beginning of the world formed humanity in your likeness by your own will and gave it the command not to touch the forbidden fruit, which [lacuna] paid for its transgression through many years, and which your immense and propitious divinity, in the assumed human being, bore, freed [the servant] from bondage, and restored the human race to the kingdom through perpetual mercy: incline to the prayer of our humility and show us your mercy.

Let those who do not fear committing theft against your commandment and against legal, evangelical, and apostolic institutions feel your power come upon them + through this creature of bread and cheese. If anyone among those whose names are inserted here, or concerning those things recorded in this little document, has stolen anything, consented to it, been involved in it in any way, or refused at present either to restore it or to confess before everyone, may he be unable to swallow the portion of this bread or cheese given to him. Rather, may he appear bound, with foaming mouth, spittle mixed with blood, and constricted throat.

But let the innocent and unharmed person receive it with thanksgiving and depart joyfully, because you, Lord, are a just and true judge, searching kidneys and hearts, and you alone know human thoughts. Do not destroy the just with the wicked, but show them the equity of your mercy, so that just as in the water of blessing and cursing you once decreed in the ancient Law a test of chastity and a type [of judgment], so also in our times work wonders through this creature of yours, so that all the ends of the earth may fear your judgments, because you are the blessed God through ages of ages. Amen.

### Likewise, an Exorcism

I exorcise you, creature of bread and cheese, by almighty God, and by Jesus Christ his Son, our Lord, and by the Holy Spirit proceeding from the Father and the Son, one God in Trinity, judge of the living and the dead. I adjure you by his holy angels and by the entire army of heaven: if anyone among these wishes to receive you—[the manuscript ends here: “you, who from those things which are in this little document …”].

[Editorial note, col. 1143C: Here the codex ends. In addition to these many varied texts, which we have reported from Alemannic liturgical manuscripts, there are others of the same kind noted by the aforementioned Brunius. He deals especially at length with the “divining rod,” as Cicero calls it in Book I of *On Duties*. Alas, various kinds of superstition have been introduced into Christianity and even wrapped around Christian rites, sacred objects, and formulas:

“Those very people” (I use the words of St Augustine, *Tractate VII on John*, chapter 1, p. 344) “who deceive through ligatures, enchantments, and the devices of the enemy, mix the name of Christ into their incantations; since they can no longer deceive Christians into accepting poison, they add something of honey, so that through what is sweet what is bitter may remain hidden, and it may be drunk to destruction.”

Thus we know that even the most sacred body of the Lord has been abused by wicked people, together with consecratory words and other sacred formulas, and sacred things such as baptismal water, blessed candles, blessed fragments of bell metal, priestly ornaments, and so forth.

Nothing is used more frequently than the beginning of the Gospel of St John, as Brunius notes, in the use of sympathetic powder and the divining rod to reveal hidden metals, waters, and so on. They also cut into rods figures such as a cross, and the names Gaspar, Melchior, and Balthasar; Brunius testifies that examples of these are preserved at Paris and are sufficiently ancient. Those who hold the rod also recite the psalm *De profundis*, and “I believe I shall see the goodness of the Lord in the land of the living,” as Brunius observed from Wier’s *On the Tricks of Demons*, Book IV, chapter 9, and Bodin’s *Demonology*, Book II, chapter 8. In Book VII, chapter 2, after a long investigation, Brunius establishes three points concerning it, p. 338:

1. That the little rod moves without artifice or fraud in the hands of some people.
2. That it does not always incline, and that deception or illusion sometimes intervenes.
3. That sometimes it bends where there is neither water nor metal.

Brunius advised girls accustomed to use this rod to pray to God through prayers, sacred retreat, and holy communion. He himself did this through the sacrifice of the Mass, and prayed that, if any work of the devil intervened in its use, God would prevent its effect; and this happened, so that when the rod inclined nothing was discovered, as may be read in the historical encomium of Brunius prefixed to the new edition of his work, 1750, volume I, p. XXVIII.

Later, on p. XIV and following, there is discussion of the same rod’s especially superstitious use for detecting criminals, displaced boundaries, and so forth. In this connection, since James Aymar is particularly famous for fraud, Brunius gives various judgments by various authors concerning him and others, volume III, p. 177. He also presents the letters of the celebrated abbot of La Trappe to Malebranche, that most acute philosopher, and the various dissertations and letters of Malebranche and others, with replies on both sides, explaining in different ways how the matter may occur naturally, at least in the detection of metals or waters, or superstitiously and through human or diabolical illusion—or with the cooperation of some intelligent cause that adapts itself to the will of the questioner and bends only over what is being sought.

For us, the guiding principle is the decrees of the councils, various examples of which may be read in volume XV of the councils, in the sixteenth century, when this superstition became especially widespread.]

## Prayers against the Demoniac

### Imposition of Hands upon Demoniac Catechumens

(From the most ancient Sacramentary of Rheinau.)

Almighty and eternal God, before whose face the heavens drip, the mountains melt like wax, the earth trembles, the abysses lie open, and hell is afraid; before whom every movement of anger is humbled when it looks upon you: I, your suppliant, beseech you, Lord and ruler, that through the invocation of your name the enemy may depart in confusion from the affliction of this servant of yours, and that, his soul freed from possession, he may return to the author of his salvation. May we follow our liberator after the devil’s stench has been driven away and the most fragrant odor of the Holy Spirit received. Through [Christ our Lord]. [The manuscript adds: “through …”]

### Likewise, Another for a Demoniac

Holy Father, almighty and eternal God, I implore your power with all my groans for this child oppressed by the devil. You have granted protection even to the unworthy amid their afflictions. Rise up for this defeated child, and do not delay to exact vengeance. Let the sins of the parents not come before your sight, since you did not promise to judge the father for the son, nor the son for the father. We ask you to help this person tormented by the enemy’s hidden [or, according to the correction, “furious”] violence. Do not allow his soul to be possessed by the devil without baptism; rather, free his tender age from the oppressions of the evil one, so that it may render eternal thanks to you. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who is to come to judge [—].

### Likewise, Another for a Baptized Demoniac, over a Person Troubled by a Demon

God of angels, God of archangels, God of prophets, God of apostles, God of martyrs, God of virgins, God the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ: I invoke your holy name and the splendor of your majesty [editorial supplement: “I humbly beseech your clemency”], that you may deign to grant me assistance against this most wicked spirit. Wherever he is hiding, let him hear your name, depart swiftly, and withdraw. He himself commands you, who ordered you to go back; hear, therefore, and depart, Satan, defeated and overthrown.

In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, you, therefore, most wicked Satan, enemy of the faith of the human race, robber of death [the printed edition reads “bringer of death, robber of life”], deserter from justice, root of evils, fuel of vices, deceiver of human beings, destroyer of nations, inciter of envy, origin of greed, cause of discord, arouser of sorrows, master of demons: why do you stand and resist, when you know that he destroys your powers? Fear him who was sacrificed in Isaac, sold in Joseph, slain in the lamb, crucified in the man, and afterward triumphant. Depart in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, who lives and reigns with the Father and the Holy Spirit through all ages of ages. Amen.

God, creator and defender of the human race, who formed humanity in your image and likeness with your hands and by the proper word of your divinity: look upon this servant of yours, who is attacked by the serpent’s deceit, whom the ancient adversary and victim [the printed edition reads: “the ancient enemy of the earth, etc.”] flies around with the terror of fearful dread, evades by stupefying the human mind [read: “fixes it”], disturbs with terror, and drives on with trembling fear.

Repel, Lord, the devil’s power and his deceitful ambushes. Let the impious tempter flee far away. By the sign of your name let your servant be wholly protected in soul and body. Guard the inward parts of this breast; govern the viscera; shape the heart. In the soul let the temptations of the hostile power vanish. At the invocation of your name grant grace, so that he who has terrified this person until now may himself be terrified and depart defeated [or, according to the variant, “depart”], and so that this little servant of yours may offer you the service he owes with a strengthened heart and sincere mind. Through [Christ our Lord].

Holy Father, almighty and eternal God. Hosanna in the highest. Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who assigned that exiled tyrant to Gehenna, who sent your Only-Begotten into this world so that he might crush that roaring lion [read: “crush him”]: attend swiftly; hasten to rescue the human being formed by your hands from ruin and from the noonday demon.

Lord, place your terror upon the beast that has devastated your vineyard. Give your servants confidence to stand firmly against the most wicked dragon. Let him not despise those who hope in you, and let him not say, as he has already said in Pharaoh, “I do not know God, and I will not release Israel.” Press him with your powerful right hand, Lord, to depart from your servants, lest he presume to hold captive any longer the human being whom you graciously formed in your image.

Therefore I adjure you, ancient serpent, by the judge of the living and the dead, by the maker of the world, who has power to cast you into Gehenna, to depart from this servant of God [the printed editions supply: “who returns to the bosom of the Church; depart swiftly from him with fear and the exercise of your fury; for the longer you delay to come out, the more …”], from whom your punishment increases, since you despise not a human being but him who is ruler of the living and the dead and who is to come to judge the world by fire.

(From codex Vienna, Imperial Library, Theol. 685, tenth century.)

When someone troubled by a demon comes, the priest signs him with three collects [prayers]. Afterwards he orders him to leave the church and to remove his clothing in a private place. Meanwhile, let him sing the litany. Let him bless salt and water. Then let him clothe the man in new garments sprinkled with blessed water. Then let him go before the altar and fast until None; let the priest sing Mass for him, administer the sacrament to him for seven days, and let him remain with the priest for fifteen days, eating nothing except bread and salt and, if the priest permits it, fish and legumes, with the blessing of salt and water.

If he is still unable to overcome the enemy, let him continue until God deigns to show mercy upon him, because the Lord said: “This kind cannot go out by anything except prayer and fasting.” You shall neither eat nor drink anything unless you have first taken some blessed water. Let him not eat goat’s meat, nor cheese, nor butter, nor anything produced by them, nor the head of that animal, nor fish. Until the fifteenth day let him abstain from his wife, and she likewise from her husband.

For a full year he shall not eat on Sunday bread made on that day, nor meat killed on that same day, nor warm beer made on Sunday. He shall eat and drink nothing warm for as long as he lives. This is by Liezan [the author seems to be some otherwise unknown person from whom the scribe took this superstition-laden prescription concerning the selection of foods, rather than matters pertaining to fasting or abstinence. The relevant discussion is found in Joseph Catalan, volume II, p. 323, commentary on the Roman Ritual, where it says that no medicine should be given or recommended to the sick or possessed as though some natural power to drive out demons were inherently present in certain things].

## Here Begin Prayers against the Demoniac

(From the same codex [editorial note: “Therefore the matter against demons must be handled through prayers and exorcisms, far from curious questioning and conversations with the possessed. On this point the Roman Ritual, §15, carefully warns: ‘Let the exorcist not wander into lengthy speech or superfluous or curious questions, especially concerning future and hidden matters that do not belong to his office, but let him command the unclean spirit to be silent and to answer only what is asked.’ Joseph Catalan notes how damaging and how easy to violate this is, even mortally, in his commentary on this passage, volume II, p. 316, drawing on Barrufaldi; he also appeals to Cardinal Cajetan, *Summa* II-II, question 90, article 1.

“What he next reports from Cardio is worth noting. According to his opinion, ‘first of all, one must hold that he commits mortal sin who has long and useless conversations with the possessing demon, because this would already mean entering into friendship with him, since we behave so familiarly only with friends. Secondly, he sins mortally who wishes to learn this or that matter from the demon by questioning him, for this is to expect some benefit from him, which is certainly superstitious. Thirdly, if there is a danger that the demon may disclose hidden dangers, because we are gravely bound to avoid the defamation of our neighbor. Fourthly, if someone questions him not coercively but supplicatively, because this would mean becoming his disciple and humbly subjecting oneself to him, which is unlawful. It must further be held that if someone questions the demon coercively and imperatively about some vain and useless matter, he commits only a venial sin of curiosity.’ Etc.

“Moreover, after the first prayer, the words ‘Write it on a tablet, erase it, and give it to drink’ have perhaps wrongly been added here by the same author whom we have just mentioned. Against demons one must proceed through prayers and exorcisms, and especially according to the rites and formulas prescribed by the Church, since one is confronting a very crafty enemy.”])

Separate yourself from that servant of God, accursed and most condemned unclean spirit, Satan! Just as almighty God separated heaven from earth, light from darkness, justice from iniquity, and falsehood from truth. Behold, the sign of my God is imposed upon you, which you, in your wickedness, cannot impose. Untie the knots; release the chains; loosen the bonds.

I adjure you, accursed Satan: flee with your heat from this world into the land of Egypt. Crack apart more swiftly, as the dragon cracked apart in Babylon before the feet of Daniel, servant of God. Seven chief angels, radiant and white, and burning lamps will come to burn you, seed of Cain, children of darkness, fabricated hiding places, adversary of chastity; seducer of souls, sprinkler of heretics, wearier of peoples, leader of evils.

Recognize your own art, accursed Satan. Behold, the angel Gabriel with a golden censer full of incense from the prayers of the saints. I invoke your majestic name, Father, with your Son Christ, who made wine from water at Cana of Galilee and again blessed the five senses of human beings. Let this unclean spirit remain hidden nowhere, from the nails of the fingers to the crown of the head.

Help your servant N. Lord, as you helped Sarah, daughter of Raguel; as you enlightened Tobiah’s eyes; as you delivered Lot from Sodom; as you delivered David [supplement: “from the hand of”] King Saul; as you delivered Thecla from three torments, so that he may believe in the Almighty and in the wisdom and understanding of God. Through [Christ our Lord].

I adjure and beseech you, Lord, by the bloody sign of the cross and by the appearance of Golgotha, the red rock, made red by the blood of this great King of the Jews, Jesus Christ, our Lord, the highest and almighty Lord, the only-begotten Son of the Father. May the most wondrous sign of the power of the cross of Christ, the Most High, help this man troubled by an evil power. Through our Lord [Jesus Christ].

Another. I beseech you, Lord, day and night: the sig+num [sign] of divine majesty; the sig+num [sign] of God’s supreme and ineffable goodness; the sig+num [sign] of great mercy and sublime power; the sig+num [sign] of heavenly and wondrous glory; the sig+num [sign] of eternal salvation and perpetual life; the sig+num [sign] of the palm and victory of the martyrs; the sig+num [sign] of the everlasting light of the saints, who enjoy rest without end in the kingdom [Col. 1148A] with Christ in glory; the sig+num [sign] of the high and profound mystery of baptism; the sig+num [sign] of the healing and great remedy of the soul; the sig+num [sign] consecrated beforehand by the mouth of Christ and implored, which he had foretold to the apostles would suffer the cross at the hands of the Jews for the salvation of the world. For through you hearing is given to the deaf, lepers are cleansed, illnesses are healed of their pain, and vices are removed. The sig+num [sign] of the Lord’s day and of Christ’s resurrection; the sig+num [sign] of the coming of the Holy Spirit, descending upon the holy apostles, and of the fire upon each of the believing peoples of Christ, first and in the Church of the Saints. The sig+num [sign] of Christ proclaimed throughout the circle of the earth by churches singing with one accord and inward devotion. Jesus Christ, who with the Father lives and reigns in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, throughout all ages of ages.

[Col. 1148B] Another. Holy Lord, almighty eternal God, Hosanna in the highest, Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who consigned that fugitive tyrant to the place of Gehenna, who sent your Only-Begotten into this world so that he might swiftly crush that roaring lion: attend, hasten, and deliver from ruin and from the noonday demon the human being formed by your hands. Give, Lord, your terror against the beast that will destroy your vineyard. Give your servants confidence to stand firmly against the most wicked dragon. Let him not despise one who hopes in you and say, as he already said against Pharaoh, “I do not know the Lord, nor will I let Israel go.” May your powerful right hand drive him away, so that he may depart from your servant N. May he no longer presume to hold captive the human being whom you deigned to make in your image.

I ad+jure you, ancient serpent, [Col. 1148C] by the judge of the living and the dead, by the maker of the world, by him who has power to cast into Gehenna, that you depart swiftly, with fear and all the force of your fury, from this servant of God N., who has run to the manger of God’s Church. I ad+jure you not by my weakness but by the power of the Holy Spirit, that you depart from him, N., whom almighty God made in his own image. Yield, yield—not to me but to the mysteries of Christ. For the power of him who, fastening himself to his cross, subjected you, will drive you away. Tremble at the arm of him who brought to the light the souls condemned to the groans of hell. Let the human body be terror to you; let the image of God be fear to you. Do not resist. Do not delay departing from this human being, N., [Col. 1149A] since it has pleased Christ to dwell in him.

And do not think me utterly weak because you know me to be exceedingly sinful. The Lord commands you. The majesty of Christ commands you. God the Father commands you. The Son and the Holy Spirit command you. The faith of the apostles—of Saints Peter and Paul and of the other apostles—commands you. The forgiveness of confessors commands you. The blood of martyrs commands you. The sacrament of the cross commands you. The power of the mysteries commands you.

Come out, transgressor; come out, seducer full of every deceit and fraud, enemy of truth, persecutor of innocence. Give way, most hard-hearted one; give way, most impious one. Give way to Christ, in whom you found nothing of your works, who stripped you, destroyed your kingdom, bound you after conquering you, and shattered your vessels (or: plundered them), [Col. 1149B] who cast you into the outer darkness, where destruction has been prepared for you with your ministers.

But what are you now turning over in confusion? What are you rashly reconsidering, guilty before almighty God, whose transgressor you are; guilty before Jesus Christ his Son, whom you dared to tempt and presumed to crucify; guilty before the human race, upon which death came through your persuasion? I therefore adjure you, most wicked dragon, in the name of the immaculate Lamb, who walks upon the asp and the basilisk and tramples upon the lion and the dragon, to depart from this human being, N., and from the Church of God.

Tremble and flee when the name of the Lord has been invoked—of him whom the beings below tremble, to whom Powers and Dominions are subject, whom Cherubim and Seraphim proclaim with tireless voices. The Word made flesh commands you. He who was born of the Virgin commands you. [Col. 1149C] Jesus the Nazarene commands you, who, when you were despising his disciples, commanded you to leave the human being crushed and prostrate [Note: [Col. 1149] The printed edition reads: “when you were despising his disciples,” etc.]. When he was present and had separated you from the human being, you did not even dare to touch the herd of swine. Now, adjured in his name, withdraw from the human being whom he himself formed.

It is hard for you to kick against the goad. It is hard for you to wish to remain, because the longer you delay coming out, the more your punishment increases: for you do not despise a human being, but him who is Lord of the living, who is to come to judge the world by fire, who with the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit lives and reigns as God, throughout all ages of ages. Amen.

Another. God, who [is] for the salvation of the human race, etc.

Another. God of the heavenly powers, etc.

[Col. 1149D] Another. In the name of God the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. I conjure you and charge you, devil, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, by his command, and by the power of the Holy Trinity and his omnipotence, to come out, Satan, and every diabolical power, from this human being N., without injury to his soul or body.

Come out entirely; do not presume to remain, roam about, hide, or serve in this person’s body, spirit, soul, or clothing, but depart as a fugitive. Leave no trace or pain in this person’s soul, flesh, or bones.

Come out, unclean spirits, whoever you are, whether one or many, [Col. 1150A] whatever your name may be. Come out swiftly: from his head and his hair; from this human being; from his crown, forehead, eyebrows, eyes, temples, ears, nostrils, ducts, mutilagine [reading uncertain], cheeks, tongue, area beneath the tongue, teeth, mouth, throat, gullet, the other side of the throat, uvula, palate, air, and breath; from his chest, thoughts, lips, jaws, gums, both sides of the neck, fingernails, shoulders, shoulder blades, armpits, the space between the shoulder blades, back, nape, spine, and marrow. Fly out; come forth, constrained by the power of the Holy Trinity and the name of almighty God.

Flee, melted away, from the belly, entrails, thighs, knees [printed genitibus; read genibus], popliteal regions and calves, legs, [Col. 1150B] four ankles, feet, soles, heels, joints, spaces between the joints, all nails, every marrow, veins, all bones, nerves, arteries, all flesh, all his blood, all his bodily fluid, all five of his senses, the genital organs, semen, nails, pubic region, bladder, rectum, mina [perhaps urine; reading uncertain], sweat, and all his excrement.

May you be expelled in the name of Jesus Christ crucified, who rose again. Come out from the gall, liver, all the joints, intestines, stomach and belly, and spleen; come forth entirely, never to return there. Come out from the fat, caul, kidneys, heart, region beneath the heart, lungs, and all the body’s heart, lungs, and flesh. Come out from the kidneys, [Col. 1150C] loins, teribus [reading uncertain], ribs, hiliis [perhaps flanks], necks, vertebrae, buttocks, internatibus [reading uncertain], all vital fibers, soul, navel, breasts, intervivio [reading uncertain], mula [perhaps “vulva”], large intestine, hair, and all his skin; from his entire body, all his food, all his bread, all his drink, and all his nourishment—depart.

Do not presume to approach him, bring harmful air or fetid odors, or inflict any snares upon him. Instead, expelled beyond this world by the power and sign of the holy cross of our redeemer Jesus Christ—which is the weapon of Christians and the triumph of the Lord Jesus our Savior—depart. By him you have been conquered and bound; like a sparrow in an empty wilderness, swiftly seek the deserted places, constrained and bound.

By the invocation and power of the name of almighty God, come out at this hour and at this moment, unclean spirit who invaded this human being N. Fly out. Vanish. Leave this human being healthy, whole, and sound in body, soul, and spirit, forever in the service of the Lord Jesus.

Come out, accursed one. Do not remain or hide in any joint of this person’s limbs, or in his breath, or in any corner of his houses; do not presume to conceal yourself there by any device or cunning. Do not touch or besiege anything that belongs to him. Do not presume in any way to invade his clothing, men, women, cattle, or beasts of burden that are his. Rather, chained [Col. 1151A] and bridled by the command, power, and kingdom of our Lord Jesus Christ, creator of the world, flee as an exile and seek those regions where you may presume to harm some creature of God.

Give at once honor to almighty God, whose command rules over all things and whom the unceasing elements obey. May his power expel you and compel you to depart with your entire throng—the one who drove seven demons from Mary Magdalene, who destroyed the kingdoms of death discovered through you, and who snatched his chosen ones from your power. He is the Lord of powers; he is the King of glory, who came forth from the Father’s mouth before the morning star.

And we beseech you and invoke you, God, almighty Holy Trinity, to command that this human being, seeking your mercy, be cleansed from every ambush of demons and from the infliction of their pain. In the name of [Col. 1151B] Jesus and the Holy Spirit we ask you, God the Father, that your power be brought to this sick human being and that you deign to strengthen him for eternal life.

We read and believe, Lord, in your holy Gospel, that with complete authority the Lord Jesus your Son cast out unclean spirits and powerfully healed the sufferings inflicted by them, so that what was spoken by the Lord through the prophet Isaiah might be fulfilled: “He himself bore our infirmities and our diseases, and by his bruise he healed our wounds.”

You, Lord and Savior of the world, gave your holy apostles and all who believe in you the power to cast out unclean spirits from everyone, to heal all who are sick, and to cure every illness through invocation of your holy name. You said, “Everyone who calls upon the name of the Lord will be saved.” And, “Whatever you ask the Father in my name, he will give you.” You, Lord, said, “If you, though evil, know how to give good things to your children, how much more will your Father from heaven give the good Spirit to those who ask him.” You, Lord, said, “If you have faith and say to this mountain, ‘Move,’ it will move.”

We believe that you are the omnipotent Lord and that everything is possible for you. And we invoke you, Holy Trinity: hear us, Lord Jesus our Savior. Through your holy name we ask the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit to command that your servant, named N., be cleansed from every attack of demons and that every illness which it has inflicted, whether upon his soul or body, be healed by your medicine.

You, Lord, said that the healthy do not need a physician but the sick, and you deigned to say: “I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners.” You are the true God, and you alone are good with the Father and the Holy Spirit; mediator between God and human beings, and expiation for our sins, Jesus Christ, Son of the living God.

Begotten from the Almighty before the ages, you are eternally the maker of the first age with the Holy Spirit. Send all the holy angels and archangels. Send the holy Archangel Michael, the holy Gabriel, and the holy Raphael, so that they may be present, defend, and protect your human being N., whom you formed, to whom you gave a soul, and for whom you deigned to pour out your blood.

Let them protect him and enlighten him, whether awake or asleep, from every diabolical attack, and render him so quiet and secure that thereafter no portion in which the wicked power has authority may enter or presume to enter. Let no evil spirit presume to injure, weary, terrify, or trouble his soul or body with temptations. Through the Lord.

## Also: Holy Blessing over the Sick Person

May God the Father, who created you, heal you; may the Son of God, who suffered for you, heal you; may the Holy Spirit, who was poured out upon you, heal you; may your faith, which freed you from every iniquity, heal you.

May God the Father bless you, may the Son of God guard you, and may the Holy Spirit enlighten you, so that you may have eternal life throughout the ages of ages. Amen.

May almighty God the Father from heaven bless you, who in the beginning created all things by his word. May the Son of God bless you, who deigned to come from the paternal throne to redeem us. May the Holy Spirit [Col. 1152B] bless you, who in the form of a dove rested upon Christ the Lord in the channel of the river Jordan. May the Holy Trinity and inseparable Unity bless you and guard your soul throughout everlasting ages. Amen.

## Also: Holy Blessing

May the blessing of God the Father with his angels be upon you. May the blessing of Christ with his apostles be upon you. May the blessing of the Holy Spirit with his seven gifts be upon you.

May the blessing, sanctification, and salvation of words and deeds, and the power of God’s mysteries and of the holy Gospel, in the name of the Most High God, be upon you unto eternal life.

May the blessing of the Lord’s incarnation and the blessing of the blessed passion, resurrection, and ascension of Christ be upon you. May the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, guard your understanding, your heart, [Col. 1152C] and your body, in Christ Jesus our Lord. Amen.

May the blessing of the Catholic Church with her chosen children be upon you. May the blessing of the patriarchs, the intercessions of the apostles, the victory of the martyrs, the faith of confessors, the chastity of virgins, the continence of widows, and the intercessions of all your saints, Lord, be upon you.

May their merits and prayers be with you in your thoughts, words, works, days, and nights. I commend you at all times to the power of the Holy Trinity, that it may guard you unto eternal life. Amen.

## Over a Possessed Person

Holy Lord, almighty eternal God, drive the devil from this human being N.—from his head, hair, crown, brain, forehead, eyes, [Col. 1152D] mouth, ears, nostrils, tongue, beneath the tongue, throat, gullet, neck, your body, all your limbs, the joints of your limbs, within and without, bones, veins, nerves, all evil works, power, and manner of life—and in the future may the power of Christ, who lives, work in you.

Another. Almighty eternal God, before whose face the heavens drip, the mountains melt like wax, the earth trembles, the abysses lie open, hell is afraid, and everyone who sees you angered is immediately humbled: I suppliantly beseech you, Lord and ruler, that at the invocation of your name the enemy may depart in confusion from the affliction of this servant of yours, and that, once freed from this possession, his soul may return to the author of its salvation and follow its liberator, after the diabolical stench has been driven away and the sweetest fragrance of the Holy Spirit received. Through the Lord.

Another. Holy Lord, almighty and everlasting Father, I entreat your power with all my groans for this servant of yours, oppressed by the devil from childhood, for you grant protection even to the unworthy amid their pressures. Rise up for this child who has been overthrown, and do not long withhold vengeance. Do not let the sins of the parents come before your sight, since you have promised to judge neither the father for the son nor the son for the father. We ask you to help one afflicted by the enemy’s fury. Do not allow his soul to be possessed by the devil without baptism; rather, once freed from wicked oppressions, may his tender age render everlasting thanks to you. Through.

[Col. 1153B] Also another. God of angels, God of archangels, God of prophets, God of apostles, God of martyrs, God of confessors, God of virgins, God the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ: I invoke your holy name and suppliantly ask the clemency of your splendid majesty that you deign to grant me help against this most wicked spirit, so that wherever he is hiding, when he hears your name, he may swiftly come out or depart.

He commands you, devil, who commanded the winds, the sea, and the storms. He commands you who ordered you to be plunged from the heights of the heavens into the lower regions of the earth. He commands you who ordered you to turn back. Hear, therefore, and fear, Satan; defeated and prostrate, depart in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ.

You, therefore, most wicked Satan, enemy of the human race’s faith, snatcher of life, evader of justice, root of evils, fuel of vices, seducer of human beings, destroyer of nations, instigator of envy, source of greed, cause of discord, arouser of sorrows, master of demons: why do you stand and resist, when you know that he destroys your powers?

Fear him who was sacrificed in Isaac, sold in Joseph, slain in the lamb, crucified in the human being, and thereafter triumphant. Depart in the name of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, and give way to the Holy Spirit, through this sign of the cross of Christ our Lord, who lives and reigns with the Father and the Holy Spirit.

Another. God, creator and defender of the human race, who formed the human being in your image and likeness: look upon this servant of yours, N., who is assailed by the deceits of the envious serpent, whom the old adversary and ancient enemy circles with the horror of dark dread, fixing the human mind’s understanding in stupor, disturbing it with terror, and driving it with trembling fear.

Repel, Lord, the devil’s power, and remove his deceitful snares. Let the impious tempter flee far away. By the sig+num [sign] of your name, may your servant be safe in mind and body [Note: [Col. 1153D] In the Roman Ritual, where this same prayer is found, after making the cross at the word “sign” on the forehead, three crosses are here prescribed to be made on the breast, §27. Above, in §17, whenever the exorcist sees the possessed woman moved or pricked in some part of the body, or a swelling appear anywhere, he is instructed to make the sign of the cross there. Here Joseph Catalanus aptly adds, in the fourth provincial council of Milan of Saint Charles Borromeo, Part II of the Constitutions, chapter 1, this caution: “While exorcising, let him not touch the head or body of a possessed woman except with great propriety and caution … nor do anything else that might give offense.” Likewise, in the fourth diocesan synod of Milan, decree 18: “While exorcising, let him beware of touching the head, shoulders, or hand of a possessed woman,” etc.

Saint Gregory of Langres is praised by the words of his namesake Gregory of Tours, *Lives of the Fathers*, chapter 7: without making any contact, he merely commanded the demons to depart by displaying the sign of the cross opposite them. As soon as they heard this, they released the bodies which they had tormented by their wickedness. According to the same witness, when Saint Nicetius of Trier similarly made the sign of the cross opposite three possessed persons, they, pressed by sleep, awoke, raised their voices on high, and, with an impulse toward vomiting, were cleansed.].

Guard the inward parts of this breast. Govern the entrails. Strengthen the heart. May the evil temptations of the hostile power vanish. At this invocation of your name, grant grace so that the one who has hitherto terrified may himself be terrified and depart defeated. May this servant of yours, with a steadfast heart and sincere mind, be able to offer you the service that is owed. Through.

Another. Almighty and merciful God, Father of our Lord Jesus Christ: we suppliantly beseech you to command the devil who holds this servant of yours, N., to depart from him, and free him so that he may believe in the true liberator, our Lord Jesus Christ. Once cleansed from every stain of iniquity, may he serve your majesty with a pure mind, having received the grace of the Holy Spirit, who lives with the Father.

Another. I do not command you on account of my sins, most unclean spirit; rather, the immaculate Lamb, Jesus Christ our Lord, God, Son of God, commands you. Angels press you; archangels press you; prophets press you; apostles press you; martyrs press you; confessors press you; virgins press you.

Therefore let the devil’s arts fail—by day, by night, in the month, in the hour, in the moment. Restore strength to the limbs. Restore health to the soul. Do not tempt it. Do not hand it over to death. Do not appear in food or drink, in the eyes, or in public places. Do not come upon it when awake or asleep. Do not disturb the mind or hinder it while it seeks eternal life.

[Col. 1154C] Depart, therefore, from the head, hair, tongue, beneath the tongue, arms, nostrils, chest, eyes, veins, large and small intestine. Separate yourself, devil, from this servant of God N., as almighty God separated heaven from earth, light from darkness, truth from falsehood, good from evil, and sweet from bitter. Thus shall you be separated, most unclean spirit, because the power of Christ has conquered you, whom you cannot conquer. Rather, may our Lord Jesus Christ, who condemned you eternally, prevail against you, and may the grace of your mercy descend upon us, Lord.

Sig+na [mark] his head, Lord, as the almighty Lord marked the sick at Cana of Galilee. Sig+na [mark] his eyes, so that from them the devil who injures all flesh may be expelled. May the Lord bless you as he blessed the eyes of the blind who are recorded in the Gospel. [Col. 1154D] Sig+na [mark] all his limbs, so that from them the devil who injures all flesh may be expelled. May the Lord bless you as he blessed the house of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. May the Lord’s health be upon you, as the Lord healed the woman from the flow of blood. May angels [Col. 1155A] and archangels guard you. May the God of Israel protect you and add health and his blessing to you, both here and in the age to come. Amen.

Another. Almighty everlasting God, we humbly ask your divine clemency that you mercifully rescue this servant of yours, N., whom we see to be gravely tempted by the ancient enemy and whose senses are in some way disturbed and afflicted by Satan’s envy, from his assault, so that no diabolical adversity may overthrow those who, placed in your Church and joined through the sacrament of baptism, confess your holy name. Through.

## Imposition of Hands over a Possessed Catechumen

Almighty everlasting God, before whose face the heavens drip, the mountains melt like wax, the earth trembles, the abysses lie open, hell is afraid, and everyone who sees you in the movement of anger is humbled. As above.

Another, for a small possessed person. Prayer. [Note: [Col. 1155C] Here the imposition of hands over a possessed catechumen precedes, but it is equally uncertain whether the following prayer for a small possessed person should be understood of a catechumen or of a baptized person. This question perplexed Saint Jerome, who wrote to Paula concerning the death of Blesilla, afflicted by a demon until death: “What is the reason that children two or three years old, and those still nursing at their mothers’ breasts, are often seized by a demon? For the judgments of the Lord are a great abyss. [Col. 1155D] And, O depth of the riches of the wisdom and knowledge of God, how inscrutable are his judgments and unsearchable his ways!”

This is relevant to the response of Innocent I to Decentius, chapter 6: “Your affection has asked concerning those baptized persons who are afterward seized by a demon, whether they can or ought to be signed by a presbyter or deacon. This cannot be prescribed except by bishops. For hands must absolutely not be laid upon such a person unless the bishop has given authority for it to be done. But for it to be done, it belongs to the bishop to order that hands be laid upon him by a presbyter or by other clerics. For how could it be accomplished without great difficulty that a possessed person situated far away should be brought to the bishop, when, if such a case occurred to him on the journey, he could neither easily be carried to the bishop nor returned home?”

Saint Augustine, *City of God* XXII.22, considering the miserable condition of fallen humanity, turns also to these afflictions of baptized infants: “Against the thousand-shaped attacks of demons, who trusts in his innocence? Indeed, lest anyone trust in it, they sometimes so torment even baptized children, than whom certainly nothing is more innocent, that in them above all, God permitting, the grievous misery of this life and the happiness of the other life to be desired may be displayed.”].

Holy Lord, almighty eternal Father, power. Another. God of angels. Another. God the creator. Another. Holy Lord, almighty Father God, Hosanna.

## Anointing the Possessed Person with Oil

I anoint you with sanctified oil in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, so that through the Holy Trinity you may be saved throughout the ages of ages. Amen.

### Another Prayer

May the Lord bless you and may Christ guard you from all the snares of the devil, in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit.

[Col. 1155C] Another. May the Lord bless you and guard you; may the Lord show his face to you and have mercy on you. May the Lord turn his face toward you and give you peace, and may the Lord fill you with the Holy Spirit. Amen.

May the God of peace himself sanctify you completely, so that your spirit, soul, and body may be preserved blameless and whole at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.

[Col. 1156A] Another anointing with oil.

May this anointing for you, through the sign of the cross, through sanctified oil, and through the gift of the Holy Spirit, be for your health. Through.

### Prayer after the Anointing with Oil

Look upon your servant, Lord, in his sickness, etc.

Another. Look graciously, Lord, upon this servant of yours, and deign to bring him help upon his bed of pain. Place your hand in my hand, lest the illness reject my hand, the hand of a sinner; rather, at the invocation of your name may it flee, so that this servant of yours, once the devil has been driven away and health restored, may rise and be presented to your Church to give thanks to your holy name. Through.

## Blessing of Water [Note: [Col. 1156C] Water blessed with the sign of the cross and invocation of the name of Jesus Christ, used to drive away demons and illnesses, is mentioned in Joseph the Jew in Epiphanius, *Against Heresies* 30; and, according to John Chrysostom, by George of Alexandria in his Life, cited by Photius, *Bibliotheca* codex 96. Palladius, *Lausiac History*, chapter 19, reports that Macarius, when asked by a nobleman to drive out a demon infesting his house, exorcised salt, mixed it with water according to ecclesiastical custom, and drove the demon into flight. Nor is the account dissimilar in which Saint Gregory orders temples in England to be purified with blessed water, in his letter to Mellitus, *Register* IX.71. From this, the use of blessed water in the dedications of churches, and the washing of walls, may be traced back to its beginnings; concerning the latter, see Optatus of Milevis, Book VI against the Donatists. The prescription that water be blessed by a bishop for driving away demons and routing every ambush is found in Book VIII, chapter 29.] With a Piece of the Holy Cross

[Col. 1156B] First the litany, then the Kyrie. The Lord’s Prayer. I believe in God. (From the same manuscript.)

I said, Lord. Grant us salvation, O God. Save your servant. Send him help, Lord. The enemy will accomplish nothing. Chastising, you have chastised. In my tribulation. Lord, do not remember. Help us, God our Savior. The Lord guards you. The Lord is for, etc.
