These things, however, are promised only to those who hope, because without hope they are powerless. Just as the body walks by means of its feet, so the minds of good people advance toward heavenly things by hope [Col. 1183C].

“With your holy Apostles and Martyrs: with John, Stephen, Matthias, Barnabas, Ignatius, Alexander, Marcellinus, Peter, Felicity, Perpetua, Agatha, Lucy, Agnes, Cecilia, Anastasia, and with all your saints. Admit us into their fellowship, we beseech you, not as one who assesses merit but as the giver of forgiveness, through Christ our Lord.”

The priest presumes to ask God that we may be granted a share with the saints because nothing resists God’s will. We are not called to the kingdom of the saints by merits, but solely by God’s goodness, through Christ our Lord, who became the mediator and whom we have as an advocate with the Father. Through his mercy and blessed Passion we have been reconciled to the Father [Col. 1183D].

“Through whom, Lord, you always create all these good things.” The Father creates and establishes through the Son, so that in the mystery of divine grace his body and blood may be given to us.

“You sanctify,” so that we too may be sanctified through the holy sacrifice.

“You give life.” The holy offering of bread and wine is given life, so that, having received the divine mysteries, eternal life may be granted to the faithful.

The good things of the Lord’s creation that are bestowed upon us have been sanctified because they sanctify us. They have been given life because through them blessed life is provided. They have been blessed because through them the blessing of the body and blood is given to us.

“Through him, and with him, and in him, to you, God the almighty Father, in the unity of the Holy Spirit, is all honor and glory.” Honor and glory belong to the Father, but with the Son, through whom he created all things, with whom he began to make everything, and in whom all things are perfected [Col. 1184A].

Honor and glory belong to the Father and the Son, but with the Holy Spirit, through whom those things known to have been made from the Father and through the Son are given life and sanctified.

“Throughout all ages of ages.” Ages of ages are spoken of in the same way as “holy of holies”; that is, through eternal ages. Through him the Father lives and reigns; the Son lives and reigns; the Holy Spirit lives and reigns.

“Amen”—that is, the voice of the faithful and of those who believe in the Trinity and the unity. *Amen* is Hebrew. Some interpreters translate it as “truly” or “faithfully”; others as “truly, let it be done.”

“Let us pray, instructed by saving commands.” We have been instructed by saving commands—that is, by those of the Lord and Savior, who saved us without our merits—he himself bearing witness to his disciples: “Thus you shall pray” [Col. 1184B]. Formed by divine instruction, we dare to say:

“Our Father, who are in heaven.” This is the voice of freedom. We invoke the Father who created us, because we were all created by the one God.

“May your name be sanctified.” Do we mean that the Lord’s name has not always been sanctified, when we pray that his name may be sanctified in us?

“May your kingdom come.” God’s kingdom has always existed. We pray that the devil and vices may not reign in us, but that God’s kingdom may be in us.

“May your will be done, as in heaven and on earth.” May God’s will be brought to completion in us; may we be perfected in the fear of the angels, so that we earthly beings may be joined to the fellowship of the citizens above.

“Give us today our daily bread” [Col. 1184C]—that is, the supersubstantial bread, concerning which the Lord said: “I am the living bread that descended from heaven.” May we be refreshed from the holy altar by the Body of Christ.

“And forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors.” Behold, we speak of forgiveness, concerning which the Lord says in the Gospel: “If you do not forgive the sins of human beings, neither will your heavenly Father forgive your sins.”

“And do not lead us into temptation.” Do not allow us to fall into the devil’s temptation.

“But deliver us from evil”—from the devil and from evil people.

“Deliver us, we beseech you, Lord, from all evils, past, present, and future.” This too must be requested, and almighty God must be entreated by humble prayer: that he may rescue us from present evils, that is, from those now pressing upon us; that according to his abundant mercy he may free us from past evils, so that we may not be brought back to them; and that, with his help, he may separate us from future evils—for he knows present, past, and future things [Col. 1184D].

“And through the intercession for us of blessed and glorious Mary, ever-virgin, Mother of God, and of your holy apostles Peter, Paul, and Andrew. Mercifully grant peace in our days.” May we, aided by the power of your mercy, always be free from sin and secure from every disturbance.

The blessed Mother of God, who was worthy to be a virgin in childbirth and a virgin after childbirth, must first be implored with the deepest humility to intercede for us with the Father and the Son, who was born from her according to the flesh. After her, the apostles of God, Peter, Paul, and Andrew, the first teachers of the Church, must be earnestly invoked [Col. 1185A], so that through their intercession, with Christ’s favor, peace may be granted to us in our days. Surrounded by the aid of his mercy, may we deserve to be free from these evils and, secure from every harmful disturbance, receive the Body and Blood of Christ, because we do not hope to be delivered from them by our own strength; rather, we believe that we are saved through their intercession.

“Through Christ our Lord. And so forth.” This redemption and deliverance too must be through Christ our Lord, who lives and reigns with the Father throughout the ages of ages, because through him, with him, and in him all things were made. Without him nothing was made; in him we live, move, and exist.

Then the priest announces that the people are to have peace [Col. 1185B], saying: “The peace of the Lord be always with you.” The clergy and the people respond in the same concord, adding: “And with your spirit.”

It is fitting that, after the sacraments of so great a mystery have been celebrated, and after the Body and Blood of our Lord Jesus Christ have been consecrated, peace should be announced beforehand to those who are about to receive them, because the one whom we receive is himself our peace, who made both into one. He himself bears witness to his disciples: “I leave you peace; my peace I give you.” And again: “Have peace among yourselves.”

After peace has been enacted among all the faithful in the Church of God, his body and blood are rightly received by those who are worthy. He is the true peace, and in him there can be no deception. For the Body and Blood of our Lord Jesus Christ can be worthily received only by those who are peaceful and remain in concord, as Scripture testifies: “Whoever eats the Lord’s Flesh and drinks his Blood unjustly eats and drinks judgment upon himself.”

While the Body and Blood of Christ are being received, the clergy chant the “Lamb of God,” because he is the true, spotless Lamb, as John says: “who takes away the sins of the world” [Col. 1186A]. While he himself is received by the faithful, it is fitting that the communion of the sacrament should, through the gentleness of its melody, soothe the ears of those receiving it, so that, attentive to this voice, they may be less able to recall idle things and may delight in it, and so that their hearts may be stirred to compunction by love for what they receive.

Then the priest offers the prayers of holy communion, and a blessing is given over the people, so that, having worthily received these things, we may remain steadfast in faith and pure in heart, and may believe that we possess salvation of souls and bodies.

Through our Lord Jesus Christ, who lives and reigns with the Father, God together with the Holy Spirit, throughout the ages of ages. Amen.

Then the deacon announces to the people, saying: “Go, the dismissal has taken place.” It is called “Mass” because, at the time of the sacrifice, the catechumens are sent outside [Col. 1186B]. Afterwards the clergy respond: “Thanks be to God.”

For, according to Augustine, in the celebration of this Mass, “supplications are first made, then prayers and intercessions, and also thanksgivings.” We understand “supplications” to mean prayers, which we make in the celebration of the sacrifices before what is on the Lord’s table begins to be blessed; nearly the whole Church concludes this petition with the Lord’s Prayer.

Prayers are offered while the holy offering is blessed and prepared for distribution. Intercessions—or, as some manuscripts read, petitions—are made when the people are blessed. At that time the bishops, as advocates, offer those entrusted to them to the most merciful power through the laying on of hands [Col. 1186C]. When these things have been completed, and so great a sacrament has been shared, thanksgiving concludes everything; the Apostle also commended it finally in these words.

# FLEURY CALENDAR

*(In Martène, Expanded Collection, vol. VI, p. 649.)*

## JANUARY

[Col. 1185D]

Kalends of January. **Circumcision of the Lord.**  
Eighth day before the Ides. **Epiphany of our Lord Jesus Christ.**  
Fourth day before the Ides. **Birthday of blessed Paul, the first hermit.**  
Ides of January. **Burial of Hilary of Poitiers.**  
Nineteenth day before the Kalends of February. **Birthday of Saint Felix.**  
Seventeenth day before the Kalends. **Birthday of Saint Marcellus.**  
Sixteenth day before the Kalends. **Burial of Saint Antony.**  
Fifteenth day before the Kalends. **Birthday of Saint Prisca.**  
Thirteenth day before the Kalends [Col. 1186D]. **Birthday of Saint Sebastian.**  
Twelfth day before the Kalends. **Birthday of Saint Agnes, from her Passion.**  
Eleventh day before the Kalends. **Birthday of Saint Vincent.**  
Fifth day before the Kalends. **Birthday of Saint Agnes, from her nativity.**

## FEBRUARY

Fourth day before the Nones. **Purification of Blessed Mary.**  
Second day before the Nones. **At Auxerre, burial of the body of Saint Alexander, pope.**  
Fidicula.  
Nones of February. **Birthday of Saint Agatha** [Col. 1187A].  
Sixteenth day before the Kalends of March. **Birthday of Saint Valentine.**  
Fourteenth day before the Kalends. **Birthday of Saint Juliana.**  
Sixth day before the Kalends. **Birthday of Saint Matthias [read: Mathias], apostle.**

## MARCH

Seventh day before the Ides. **Birthday of the Forty Holy Martyrs.**  
Fourth day before the Ides. **Birthday of Saint Gregory, pope.**  
Thirteenth day before the Kalends. **Burial of the Lord Cudbercht, bishop.**  
Twelfth day before the Kalends. **Burial of Saint Benedict.**  
Eighth day before the Kalends. **Annunciation of the archangel to Saint Mary.**  
Sixth day before the Kalends. **Resurrection of our Lord Jesus Christ.**

## APRIL

Fifth day before the Ides. **The Seven Virgins who were worthy to receive crowns together.**  
Eighteenth day before the Kalends of May. **Birthday of Saints Tiburtius, Valerian [Col. 1187B], and Maximus.**  
Ninth day before the Kalends. **Birthday of Saint George, martyr.**  
Seventh day before the Kalends. **The Greater Litany at Saint Peter’s, and of Saint Mark the Evangelist.**  
Fourth day before the Kalends. **Birthday of Saint Vitalis, martyr.**

## MAY

Kalends of May. **Birthday of Saint Philip, apostle. At Auxerre, of Amator, bishop.**  
Nones of May. **Finding of the Holy Cross, and the Passion of Saint Alexander, pope, with his companions.**  
Eighth day before the Ides. **Birthday of Saint Victor, martyr.**  
Sixth day before the Ides. **Birthday of Saint Gordianus, martyr.**  
Fourth day before the Ides. **Birthday of Saint Pancratius, martyr.**  
Second day before the Ides. **Birthday of Saint Isidore.**  
Sixteenth day before the Kalends of June. **At Auxerre, Passion of Saint Peregrinus [Col. 1187C], bishop and first martyr of that city.**  
Fourteenth day before the Kalends. **Birthday of Saint Pudentiana. At Auxerre, dedication of the church of Saint Stephen the Elder.**  
Thirteenth day before the Kalends. **Birthday of Saint Bassilla.**  
Eighth day before the Kalends. **Birthday of Saint Urban, pope.**  
Seventh day before the Kalends. **Burial of Bede, priest.**  
Third day before the Kalends. **Birthday of Saint Felix, pope.**  
Second day before the Kalends. **Birthday of Saint Petronilla.**

## JUNE

Sixth day before the Ides of June. **Birthday of Saint Medard.**  
Fifth day before the Ides. **Birthday of Saints Primus and Felician.**  
Fourth day before the Ides. **Birthday of Saint Barnabas.**  
Sixteenth day before the Kalends of July. **Birthday of Saint Vitus.**  
Fifteenth day before the Kalends. **Birthday of Saints Diogenes and Blastus.**  
Fourteenth day before the Kalends. **Birthday of Saints Marcellinus and Mark.**  
Thirteenth day before the Kalends [Col. 1187D]. **Birthday of Saints Gervasius and Protasius.**  
Tenth day before the Kalends. **Birthday of Saint James, apostle.**  
Eighth day before the Kalends. **Birthday of Saint John the Baptist.**  
Sixth day before the Kalends. **Birthday of Saints John and Paul.**  
Fourth day before the Kalends. **Birthday of Saint Leo, pope.**  
Third day before the Kalends. **Birthday of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul.**

## JULY

Sixth day before the Nones. **Birthday of Saints Processus and Martinian.**  
Second day before the Nones. **Octave of the apostles.**  
Sixth day before the Ides. **Birthday of the Seven Brothers.**  
Fifth day before the Ides. **Arrival of the most blessed Benedict, abbot.**  
Ides. **Birthday of Saint Cyricus.**  
Eighth day before the Ides. **Birthday of James, apostle, brother of John** [Col. 1188A].  
Fourth day before the Ides. **Birthday of Saints Felix, Simplicius, Faustinus, and Beatrice.**  
Third day before the Ides. **Birthday of Saints Abdon and Sennen.**  
Second day before the Ides. **Birthday of Saint Germanus, bishop and confessor.**

## AUGUST

Kalends of August. **Birthday of the Four Maccabees.**  
Fourth day before the Nones. **Birthday of Saint Stephen, pontiff.**  
Eighth day before the Ides. **Birthday of Saint Sixtus, pope, and Saints Felicissimus and Agapitus.**  
Fourth day before the Ides. **Birthday of Saint Lawrence.**  
Third day before the Ides. **Birthday of Saint Tiburtius.**  
Eighteenth day before the Kalends of September. **Assumption of Saint Mary.**  
Fifteenth day before the Kalends. **Birthday of Saint Agapitus.**  
Eleventh day before the Kalends. **Birthday of Saint Timothy.**  
Eighth day before the Kalends. **Birthday of Saint Bartholomew, apostle** [Col. 1188B].  
Fifth day before the Kalends. **Saint Augustine, bishop. At Auxerre, translation of the body of Saint Germanus, bishop.**  
Fourth day before the Kalends. **Passion of Saint John the Baptist.**

## SEPTEMBER

Sixth day before the Ides of September. **Birthday of Saint Mary.**  
Third day before the Ides. **Birthday of Saints Protus and Hyacinth.**  
Eighteenth day before the Kalends of October. **Birthday of Saints Cornelius and Cyprian, and Exaltation of the Holy Cross.**  
Eleventh day before the Kalends. **Birthday of Saint Matthew, apostle.**  
Tenth day before the Kalends. **Passion of Maurice and 6,660 [uncertain reading]. At Auxerre, reception of the body of Saint Germanus from Italy.**  
Eighth day before the Kalends. **Conception of John the Baptist.**  
Fifth day before the Kalends. **Birthday of Saints Cosmas and Damian.**  
Third day before the Kalends. **Dedication of the basilica of the archangel Michael.**  
Second day before the Kalends. **Birthday of Saint Jerome, priest.**

## OCTOBER

[Col. 1188C]

Kalends of October. **Birthday of Saint Remigius.**  
Fifth day before the Nones. **Passion of the two Heuveddi.**  
Seventh day before the Ides. **Birthday of Saints Marcellinus and Genuius.**  
Sixth day before the Ides. **Burial of the Lord Paulinus, bishop of Ebroicensis [read: Eboracensis].**  
Fifteenth day before the Kalends. **Saint Luke the Evangelist.**  
Fifth day before the Kalends. **Birthday of the apostles Simon and Judas.**

## NOVEMBER

Sixth day before the Ides of November. **Birthday of the Four Holy Crowned Martyrs.**  
Third day before the Ides. **Birthday of Saint Martin, bishop.**  
Ides. **At Auxerre, reception of the bodies of Saints Alexander, pope, and Chrysanthus.**  
Tenth day before the Kalends of December. **Birthday of Saint Cecilia** [Col. 1188D].  
Ninth day before the Kalends. **Birthday of Saint Clement.**  
Eighth day before the Kalends. **Birthday of Saint Chrysogonus.**  
Third day before the Kalends. **Birthday of Saint Saturninus and Saint Chrysanthus.**  
Second day before the Kalends. **Birthday of Saint Andrew, apostle.**

## DECEMBER

Second day before the Nones of December. **Saint Benedict, abbot.**  
Third day before the Ides. **Birthday of Saint Damasus, pope.**  
Sixteenth day before the Kalends of January. **Birthday of Saint Ignatius, martyr.**  
Twelfth day before the Kalends. **Birthday of Thomas, apostle.**  
Tenth day before the Kalends. **Birthday of Saint Eugenia.**  
Eighth day before the Kalends. **Birthday of our Lord Jesus Christ.**  
Seventh day before the Kalends. **Birthday of Saint Stephen, martyr.**  
Sixth day before the Kalends. **Birthday of Saint John the Evangelist.**  
Fifth day before the Kalends. **Birthday of the Holy Innocents.**  
Second day before the Kalends. **Birthday of Saint Silvester, pope.**

# VERY ANCIENT CALENDAR

*(In Bandini, Catalogue of the Laurentian Library, Supplement.)*

## [NOTE]

… This codex—namely, that of the Laurentian Library—belongs to the beginning of the ninth century and is written in almost square characters. Besides two books on ecclesiastical computation and other astronomical monuments, it has a fragment of a calendar prefixed at its beginning. Since this was unknown to the distinguished Leonardo Ximenes, S.J., priest, in his historical introduction to the Florentine Gnomon, printed at Florence by the royal press in 1767, and provides an exact record of more recent material, it seemed worthwhile to present it in full. Although—something greatly to be regretted—it is mutilated through nearly half its extent, what remains may nevertheless be of considerable use for astronomical observations.

The calendar fragment begins with the sixth day of the month of June in the following manner:

# The Stavelot Calendar

## January

[Col. 1193B]

On the Kalends of January: Circumcision and the octave of the Lord. At Rome, Saint Concordius, martyr. Thiatmar, bishop.

On the fourth day before the Nones: At Rome, Saint Telesphorus, pope and martyr; the eighth.

On the third day before the Nones: At Paris, the burial of Saint Genevieve, virgin. At Rome, Antherus, pope and martyr; the eighteenth.

On the second day before the Nones: In Antioch, Saint Simeon the monk; and in Jerusalem, Saint Simeon the prophet.

On the Nones: Nativity of Saint Severinus, confessor. Hepo, dean, died.

On the eighth day before the Ides: Epiphany of the Lord.

On the seventh day before the Ides: In Thrace, Saint Isidore, bishop, and the holy martyrs Fausta and Evilasius; Saint Valentine, bishop.

On the sixth day before the Ides: In Gaul, in the city of Beauvais, the nativity of the holy martyrs Lucian, Maximian, and Julian.

On the fifth day before the Ides: Sicco died.

On the fourth day before the Ides: In the Thebaid, the burial of Saint Paul, the first hermit.

On the third day before the Ides: The Lord’s departure from Egypt. Havuini, priest, died.

On the Ides: Octave of the Epiphany. Saint Hilary, bishop, and the holy Julian and Basilissa. In Campania, in the city of Nola, the passion of Felix, Agapitus, and Pontianus, martyrs.

On the nineteenth day before the Kalends of February: Burial of Saint Remigius, confessor.

On the eighteenth day before the Kalends: At Rome, Saint Marcellus, pope XXX, and at Perrona, Saint Furseus, abbot, and Honoratus, martyr.

On the seventeenth day before the Kalends: Saint Sulpitius, martyr, and Saint Antoninus.

On the sixteenth day before the Kalends: At Rome, Saint Prisca, virgin, and the Chair of Saint Peter.

[Col. 1193D] On the thirteenth day before the Kalends: At Rome, Fabian, pope XX, martyr; Sebastian, martyr; and the martyrs Mari, Martha, Audifax, and Abacuc. Saint Pontianus, martyr.

On the twelfth day before the Kalends: Saint Agnes, virgin.

On the eleventh day before the Kalends: The passion of Saint Vincent, deacon, and Anastasius, martyr.

[Col. 1194B] On the tenth day before the Kalends: The passion of the holy Emerentiana, Macnarius, and Eugenius.

On the ninth day before the Kalends: In Antioch, Bishop Babylas with three boys. Death of Emperor Otto III.

On the eighth day before the Kalends: In Damascus, the conversion of Paul; and at Clermont, Praejectus, martyr.

On the seventh day before the Kalends: Queen Aedit died.

On the sixth day before the Kalends: Archbishop Gisilharius died.

On the fifth day before the Kalends: At Rome, Saint Agnes, virgin.

On the fourth day before the Kalends: Saint Valerius, bishop; Papias and Maurus, martyrs. Saint Constantine, martyr.

On the third day before the Kalends: At the monastery of Malmedy, Saint Aldegund, virgin.

On the second day before the Kalends: Saint Julius, confessor. Roaolt, subdeacon, died.

## February

[Col. 1194C]

On the Kalends of February: Saint Brigid, virgin, and Saint Polycarp, bishop.

On the fourth day before the Nones: Purification of the Holy Mother of God. On the same day, in the year 1014, the ordination of Tagen, third archbishop of the holy Magdeburg church.

On the third day before the Nones: Saint Blaise, bishop and martyr.

On the Nones: In Sicily, the passion of Saint Agatha, virgin.

On the eighth day before the Ides: Amandus, bishop; Saint Vedast, bishop; and Saint Dorothy, virgin.

On the seventh day before the Ides: Saint Helena.

On the third day before the Ides: Saint Soteris and Scholastica, virgin; Zoticius, Hereneus, and Jacintus. Adricus, priest, died.

On the second day before the Ides: Saint Castrensis, martyr. Hilderadus, priest, died.

[Col. 1194D] On the sixteenth day before the Kalends of March: At Terni, Valentine, bishop. At Rome, Valentine, priest; Vitalis, Felicula, and Tenon.

On the fifteenth day before the Kalends: Burial of Saint Silvinus, bishop; Faustinus and Jovita, martyrs.

On the fourteenth day before the Kalends: At Combas, the passion of Saint Juliana, virgin, and Onclimus, confessor.

[Col. 1195A] On the twelfth day before the Kalends: Our sister Vestburg died.

On the eleventh day before the Kalends: Godila, deacon, died.

On the tenth day before the Kalends: Saint Eucharius, bishop and confessor.

On the ninth day before the Kalends: Saint Felix, confessor.

On the eighth day before the Kalends: In Antioch, the Chair of Saint Peter; Thecla and Concordia. In the year 1008, on Sunday, the crypt of our basilica was dedicated.

On the seventh day before the Kalends: Husenuardus, priest, and Bodo, our fellow brother, died.

On the sixth day before the Kalends: Saint Matthias, apostle.

On the fifth day before the Kalends: The arrival of Walburga, virgin; Saint Maurice, martyr.

On the fourth day before the Kalends: In Alexandria, Saint Fortunatus, confessor. Amuco, priest, died.

On the third day before the Kalends: Hazacho, priest, died.

## March

[Col. 1195B]

On the Kalends of March: Burial of Saint Alban, Donatus the martyr, and Leo.

On the sixth day before the Nones: At Rome, Saint Simplicius, pope XLVIII. Archbishop William died.

On the fifth day before the Nones: Lady Chunigunda, empress and august woman, died, worthy of honorable and pious remembrance.

On the fourth day before the Nones: Saint Adrian, martyr, with his companions; Lucius, pope and martyr. Abbot Ende died.

On the third day before the Nones: The passion of Saint Phocas, bishop.

On the second day before the Nones: Saint Quiriacus, priest. Count Thiederic died.

On the Nones: The passion of the holy Perpetua and Felicity. Death of Alferus, priest.

On the seventh day before the Ides: In Sebaste of Lesser Armenia, the Forty Martyrs.

[Col. 1195C] Archbishop Bruno died.

On the fourth day before the Ides: At Rome, Saint Gregory, pope. Amuired, a laywoman, died.

On the Ides: Count Sigifrius died.

On the seventeenth day before the Kalends of April: Saint Cyriacus, martyr, and Saint Eusebia, virgin. Reinwardus, priest, died. Fritherun, a nun, died.

On the sixteenth day before the Kalends: In Scotland, Saint Pancratius; and at Nivelles, Saint Gertrude, virgin.

On the fifteenth day before the Kalends: At Rome, Saint Pimen, martyr.

On the fourteenth day before the Kalends: In Bethlehem, Saint Joseph, nourisher of the Lord. Fritheric, priest, died.

On the thirteenth day before the Kalends: At Fontenelle, the burial of Bishop Wilfrid; Cuthbert, apostle and bishop. Bernhard, deacon, died.

[Col. 1195D] On the twelfth day before the Kalends: Burial of Saint Benedict, abbot.

On the ninth day before the Kalends: Bishop Wihbert, our brother, died.

On the eighth day before the Kalends: Annunciation, conception, and passion of the Lord. Passion of James, the Lord’s brother.

On the seventh day before the Kalends: Saint Castulus, priest, and Acacius. Liudger, bishop and confessor. Thiedric, dean. Badegoz, priest, died.

On the sixth day before the Kalends: Resurrection of the Lord.

On the fifth day before the Kalends: Liudulf, a layman, died.

On the third day before the Kalends: In Thessalonica, Saint Victor, martyr.

On the second day before the Kalends: At Senlis, Saint Regulus, bishop and confessor.

## April

On the Kalends of April: In Thessalonica, Saints Quintianus, Agapus, and Chionia.

[Col. 1196A] On the third day before the Nones: The passion of Saint Theodosia, virgin.

On the second day before the Nones: At Milan, the burial of Saint Ambrose, bishop and confessor.

On the eighth day before the Ides: At Rome, Saint Celestine, pope XLIV.

On the seventh day before the Ides: Liudulf, archbishop.

On the fifth day before the Ides: Saint Antoninus, confessor; and in Sirmium, the Eight Virgins.

On the fourth day before the Ides: Saint Antonius, martyr.

On the third day before the Ides: At Rome, Saint Leo, pope XLVI, and Saint Zeno, martyr. Also at Rome, Saint Julius, pope XXXV.

On the Ides: In the city of Chalcedon, the passion of Saint Euphemia, virgin. Wilping, deacon, died.

On the eighteenth day before the Kalends of May: At Rome, the holy martyrs Tiburtius, Valerian, Maximus, and Fronto. Kristin, subdeacon.

[Col. 1196B] On the seventeenth day before the Kalends: Nativity of Saint Helena, mother of Constantine.

On the sixteenth day before the Kalends: Erp, a layman, died; Merquuard, priest, died.

On the fourteenth day before the Kalends: Eleutherius, bishop and martyr, and Antia, his mother.

On the twelfth day before the Kalends: Saint Victor, bishop; Felix and Alexander. At Pavia, Senesius, martyr. Thiezuca, a nun, died.

On the eleventh day before the Kalends: Saint Maximus, martyr. Thoncuuard, priest, died.

On the tenth day before the Kalends: At Rome, Saint Soter, pope XII.

On the ninth day before the Kalends: Saint George, martyr. Saint Adalbert, bishop and martyr. Taba, our sister.

On the seventh day before the Kalends: In Alexandria, Saint Mark the Evangelist.

On the fifth day before the Kalends: At Rome, Saint Anastasius, pope and confessor XL.

[Col. 1196C] On the fourth day before the Kalends: The holy martyrs Vitalis, Torpetes, and Pamphilus, bishop and confessor. Atheldagus, archbishop.

On the third day before the Kalends: At Rome, Saint Cletus, pope and martyr II, and the translation of Saint Richarius, priest.

On the second day before the Kalends: At Rome, Quirinus, bishop and martyr.

## May

On the Kalends of May: Nativity of the Apostles Philip and James. Passion of Saint Cyriacus, bishop; Sigismund, king; and Walburga, virgin.

On the sixth day before the Nones of May: Saint Anastasius, bishop and confessor.

On the fifth day before the Nones: At Rome, Saint Alexander, pope VI; the holy Eventius and Theodulus; and the Finding of the Holy Cross. Biso and Egico, our brothers.

On the fourth day before the Nones: Saint Florian, martyr, with forty companions. Abbot Herding died.

[Col. 1196D] On the Nones: Death of Otto the Great, emperor. Sztodorusinus, priest, died.

On the eighth day before the Ides: At Milan, Saint Victor, martyr, and Corona, virgin.

On the seventh day before the Ides: Saint Beatus, priest and confessor, and Gerontius, martyr.

On the sixth day before the Ides: At Rome, the nativity of the holy martyrs Gordian and Epimachus. Commemoration of Saint Remaclus, bishop.

On the fifth day before the Ides: At Vienne, the burial of Saint Mamertus, bishop.

On the fourth day before the Ides: At Rome, the holy martyrs Nereus, Achilleus, and Pancratius.

On the third day before the Ides: At Maastricht, Saint Servatius, bishop; Aracus, Probus, and Andronicus.

[Col. 1197A] On the second day before the Ides: At Rome, Saint Theodore, pope LXXXIII. Abbot Richarius died.

On the fourteenth day before the Kalends of June: At Rome, Saint Potentiana, virgin.

On the thirteenth day before the Kalends: Saint Conon and Saint Basilla, virgin.

On the twelfth day before the Kalends: At the monastery of Augia, Saint Vitalis, martyr.

On the eleventh day before the Kalends: Saint Faustinus, confessor, and Saint Helena, virgin.

On the tenth day before the Kalends: The holy martyrs Desiderius, bishop, Sulpitius, and Servilianus.

On the ninth day before the Kalends: In the city of Nantes, the passion of the holy Donatian and Rogatian.

On the eighth day before the Kalends: At Rome, Saint Urban, pope and martyr XVI, and Saint Desiderius, martyr. Gunther, deacon and our brother, died.

On the seventh day before the Kalends: In Britain, Saint Augustine, first bishop of the English, and Bishop Symmetrius. Thiatsvith, our sister, died.

[Col. 1197B] On the fifth day before the Kalends: At Paris, the burial of Saint Germanus, bishop.

On the fourth day before the Kalends: At Trier, the burial of Saint Maximinus, bishop.

On the third day before the Kalends: At Rome, Saint Felix, pope and martyr XXVI.

On the second day before the Kalends: At Rome, Saint Petronilla, virgin, and the holy martyrs Cantius, Cantianus, and Cantianilla.

## June

On the Kalends of June: Saint Pamphilus, martyr; the holy Faustinus, bishop and martyr, and his companions Abundius, Gratianus, and Secundus, martyrs; Juvinus, confessor. Adelger, deacon, died. Hecil. Commemoration of Hiva, abbess.

On the fourth day before the Nones: At Rome, the nativity of the holy martyrs Marcellinus and Peter, and Saint Martina with forty-seven others. Prebor, our brother, died.

On the third day before the Nones: Pergentinus and Laurentinus, martyrs.

On the second day before the Nones: Saint Quirinus, bishop and martyr.

On the Nones: At the monastery of Fulda, the nativity and passion of Saint Boniface the martyr are celebrated. Also the dedication at Stavelot.

On the eighth day before the Ides: The holy martyrs Vincent and Benignus. Radulf, a layman and our fellow brother.

On the seventh day before the Ides: Ordination of Henry II, king.

On the sixth day before the Ides: Nativity of Saints Medardus and Gildardus.

On the fifth day before the Ides: At Rome, Saints Primus and Felician.

On the fourth day before the Ides: Saint Getulius, martyr.

On the third day before the Ides: Saint Barnabas, Paul’s assistant. Sicco, subdeacon, died. Alfker and Ricolf, monks, died.

On the second day before the Ides: Saints Basilides, Cyrinus, Nabor, Nazarius, Tripodis, and Mandalis.

On the Ides: Saint Felicula, virgin.

On the eighteenth day before the Kalends of July: The passion of Saints Valerius and Rufinus.

On the seventeenth day before the Kalends: The passion of Saints Vitus, Modestus, and Crescentia.

On the sixteenth day before the Kalends: Saints Ferriolus, Ferrutio, Aureus, and Justinus.

On the fifteenth day before the Kalends: Burial of Saint Avitus, priest, and Diogenes, martyr.

On the fourteenth day before the Kalends: At Rome, the holy martyrs Marcus and Marcellianus.

On the thirteenth day before the Kalends: At Milan, the passion of Saints Gervasius and Protasius.

On the twelfth day before the Kalends: Aedelberht, first archbishop of the Magdeburg church.

[Col. 1198A] On the eleventh day before the Kalends: In Alamannia, the passion of Saint Albinus, martyr; Saint Eusebius the historiographer.

On the tenth day before the Kalends: In the city of Nola, the burial of Saint Paulinus, bishop.

On the eighth day before the Kalends: Nativity of Saint John the Baptist.

On the seventh day before the Kalends: Translation of Saint Remaclus.

On the sixth day before the Kalends: At Rome, the holy martyrs John and Paul, brothers; and at Valencia, Saint Salvius, martyr.

On the fifth day before the Kalends: In Ephesus, the revelation of the Seven Holy Sleepers.

On the fourth day before the Kalends: At Rome, Saint Leo, pope, and the vigil of the Apostles.

On the third day before the Kalends: The holy Apostles Peter and Paul. Fortunatus, bishop and confessor. Gero, archbishop of Cologne.

On the second day before the Kalends: The solemnity of Saint Paul; Saint Marcellianus, bishop and confessor.

## July

[Col. 1198B] On the Kalends of July: At Rome, Saint Caius, bishop, and the holy Faith, Hope, and Charity with their mother Sophia.

On the sixth day before the Nones: At Rome, Saints Processus and Martinianus, and Saint Monegundis. Death of the soldiers of Saint Maurice who were killed at Arnaburg.

On the fifth day before the Nones: Translation of Saint Thomas the Apostle.

On the fourth day before the Nones: Feast of Saint Odalricus, bishop. Pope Benedict died.

On the second day before the Nones: Octave of the Apostles, and Saint Goar, confessor.

On the Nones: Gerlacus, monk.

On the eighth day before the Ides: In Germany, Saint Kilian and his companions.

On the seventh day before the Ides: In Egypt, the passion of Cyril, bishop, Procopius, and Saint Ephrem the monk, and Briccius, confessor.

[Col. 1198C] On the sixth day before the Ides: At Rome, the passion of the Seven Brothers, sons of Felicity: Philip, Vitalis, Martial, Alexander, Silvanus, Januarius, and Felix.

On the fifth day before the Ides: Translation of Saint Benedict, abbot.

On the fourth day before the Ides: The holy martyrs Felix and Primitivus.

On the third day before the Ides: Saint Margaret, virgin.

On the second day before the Ides: Frideric, deacon. Adiel, priest, died.

On the Ides: Ekkihard, deacon, died.

On the seventeenth day before the Kalends of August: Hilary, martyr. Adelmann, priest, died.

On the sixteenth day before the Kalends: In Carthage, the nativity of the holy Speratus, bishop; Martial, Januarius, and Cythius.

On the fifteenth day before the Kalends: Vestarius, Felix, Aquilinus, Jactantius, Generosus, Vesta, Donata, and Secunda, martyrs. Arnulf, bishop.

[Col. 1198D] On the fourteenth day before the Kalends: Saint Arsenius, monk.

On the thirteenth day before the Kalends: At Gemmeticum in Gaul, Saint Philibert, abbot.

On the twelfth day before the Kalends: Saint Praxedes, virgin; the passion of Saint Symphorosa with her seven sons. Gisla, daughter of King Conrad, died.

On the eleventh day before the Kalends: The holy martyrs Sisinnius and Florentius; Mary Magdalene. Burchard, priest, died.

On the tenth day before the Kalends: At Ravenna, Saint Apollinaris, martyr.

On the ninth day before the Kalends: Saint Christina, virgin, and Saint Simplicius.

On the eighth day before the Kalends: Saint James, the Lord’s brother; Saint John the Evangelist; and the holy martyrs George, Aurelius, Natalia, and Christopher. Bishop Liudulf died.

On the seventh day before the Kalends: At Rome, Saint Eutychian, pope XXVII. The holy martyrs Rusticus and Florentius. On the same day, Saint Fronymus, bishop.

[Col. 1199A] On the sixth day before the Kalends: In Syria, Simeon the monk; at Rome, Aconius and Emeritus, martyrs.

On the fifth day before the Kalends: At Rome, Innocent, pope XLI. Azo, priest and provost.

On the fourth day before the Kalends: In Africa, Felix, Simplicius, Faustinus, and Beatrix; Lubi, confessor. Rich, priest and layman, died.

On the third day before the Kalends: At Rome, Abdon and Sennen, and Saint Ursus, bishop.

On the second day before the Kalends: At Auxerre, the burial of Saint Germanus, bishop and confessor.

## August

On the Kalends of August: At Rome, Saint Peter in Chains; the passion of the Seven Maccabean Brothers with their mother.

On the fourth day before the Nones: At Rome, Saint Stephen, pope XXIII.

On the third day before the Nones: At Jerusalem, the finding of the body of Stephen, the protomartyr.

[Col. 1199B] Thiatmar died.

On the second day before the Nones: At Rome, Saint Justus, priest, who collected the bodies of the saints.

On the Nones: Cassianus, bishop; Memmius, bishop; and Holwald, king.

On the eighth day before the Ides: The holy martyrs Sixtus, bishop; Felicissimus and Agapitus; Magnus, Januarius, Justus, and Pastor.

On the seventh day before the Ides: The passion of Saints Donatus, bishop, Elarinus, monk, and Afra.

On the sixth day before the Ides: Saint Cyriacus, deacon and martyr, with twenty others. Hadamar, priest, died.

On the fifth day before the Ides: At Rome, Saint Romanus, Firmus, and Rusticus, martyrs.

On the fourth day before the Ides: The passion of Saint Lawrence, martyr and Levite. Thiadric, priest, died.

[Col. 1199C] On the third day before the Ides: The holy martyrs Tiburtius and Susanna; Saint Gaugericus, bishop and confessor; and Radegund. Gero and Waldo.

On the second day before the Ides: In the city of Catania, the passion of Saint Euplus, deacon. Saint Cassianus, martyr. Bishop Walthard died.

On the Ides: At Rome, the holy martyrs Hippolytus and Cassianus; Wigbert, confessor.

On the nineteenth day before the Kalends of September: Saint Eusebius, priest.

On the eighteenth day before the Kalends: Assumption of the Holy Mother of God.

On the seventeenth day before the Kalends: Saint Arnulf, bishop and confessor.

On the sixteenth day before the Kalends: Octave of Saint Lawrence, and Saint Mammes, monk and martyr.

On the fifteenth day before the Kalends: The passion of Saint Agapitus, martyr.

On the fourteenth day before the Kalends: In Alexandria, Saint Magnus, martyr; Felix [Col. 1199D] and Fortunatus. Liudulf, deacon.

On the thirteenth day before the Kalends: Saint Maximus, confessor.

On the twelfth day before the Kalends: Saint Privatus, martyr.

On the eleventh day before the Kalends: Saints Timothy and Symphorianus, martyrs.

On the tenth day before the Kalends: In the city of Aegea, Saints Timothy, Apollinaris, Claudius, Austerius, and Neon.

On the eighth day before the Kalends: In India, the passion of Bartholomew the Apostle; Genesius, martyr; Saint Audoin, bishop. At Arles, the passion of Saint Genesius, martyr. Count Landolt died.

On the seventh day before the Kalends: At Rome, Saints Irenaeus and Abundius. Liutharius, priest, died.

On the sixth day before the Kalends: In Capua, Saint Rufus, martyr.

[Col. 1200A] On the fifth day before the Kalends: At Rome, Saint Hermes; Saint Augustine; Saint Julian, martyr. Conrad, priest, died.

On the fourth day before the Kalends: At Rome, Saint Sabina, martyr, and the beheading of Saint John the Baptist.

On the third day before the Kalends: In Apulia, the passion of Saints Felix and Audactus.

On the second day before the Kalends: At Trier, the burial of Saint Paulinus, bishop and confessor, and of Justus and Clement.

## September

On the Kalends of September: At Capua-Aquaria, the holy martyrs Priscus, Peter, Felix, Donatus, and Victor; Sennis, Lubi, Sixtus, and Sinnicius, bishops.

On the fourth day before the Nones: The holy martyrs Anicetus and Phonitus, and Saint Justus, bishop of Lyon. Helmric, dean, died.

On the third day before the Nones: Saint Antoninus, martyr. Burial of Saint Remaclus [Col. 1200B] bishop and confessor.

On the second day before the Nones: The holy martyrs Marcellus and Justus. Eggihard, priest and philosopher, died.

On the Nones: At Vienne, Saint Ferriolus, bishop; Ferrutius, Quintinus, Ingenuus, Taurinus, Acensus, Herculanus. Saint Victorinus, martyr and bishop.

On the seventh day before the Ides of September: Evurtius, bishop; Clodoald, king; and Regina, virgin. Saint Madalbertha, virgin.

On the sixth day before the Ides: Nativity of the Mother of God; Saint Adrian, martyr; and Corbilianus, confessor.

On the fifth day before the Ides: Saint Gorgonius, martyr, and Saint Audomar, bishop.

On the fourth day before the Ides: Saint Salvius, martyr.

On the third day before the Ides: At Rome, the holy martyrs Protus and Hyacinth; Felix and Regula. Adiel, priest, died. Waldo, [Col. 1200C] bishop, died.

On the second day before the Ides: Heinrich, subdeacon, died.

On the Ides: Burial of Saint Lidorus, bishop.

On the eighteenth day before the Kalends of October: Exaltation of the Holy Cross, and the holy martyrs Cornelius and Cyprian.

On the seventeenth day before the Kalends: Saint Nicomedes.

On the sixteenth day before the Kalends: The passion of Saint Euphemia, and of Saints Lucia and Geminianus.

On the fifteenth day before the Kalends: The passion of Lambert, bishop.

On the thirteenth day before the Kalends: In Campania, the passion of Saint Januarius; Theodore, bishop; the holy martyrs Fausta and Evilasius; and Saint Eustochia. Saint Florentius, bishop and martyr.

On the twelfth day before the Kalends: Vigil of Saint Matthew the Apostle and Evangelist.

[Col. 1200D] On the eleventh day before the Kalends: Nativity of Saint Matthew the Apostle and Evangelist. Eggihard, priest, died.

On the tenth day before the Kalends: The passion of the holy martyrs Maurice, Exuperius, Candidus, Victor, Innocent, Vitalis, and 6,656 companions. On the same day, at Regensburg, Saint Emmeram, martyr, and Luitdrudis, virgin. Wulfhard, bishop, died.

On the ninth day before the Kalends: At Rome, Saint Linus, pope, first after Peter, and Saint Thecla, virgin.

On the eighth day before the Kalends: Conception of Saint John the Baptist; Saint Rupert, bishop; and Saint Eonius.

On the seventh day before the Kalends: The passion of Saint Firminus.

On the sixth day before the Kalends: The holy martyrs Cyprian and Justina.

On the fifth day before the Kalends: The passion of Cosmas and Damian, and of Saint Timothy, Paul’s disciple; the holy martyrs Fidentius and Terentius.

[Col. 1201A] On the fourth day before the Kalends: Burial of Lioba, virgin, and Stacteus, martyr. Nativity of Saint Gunthild, virgin.

On the third day before the Kalends: On Mount Garganus, dedication of the basilica of the Archangel Michael.

On the second day before the Kalends: At Bethlehem, the burial of Saint Jerome, priest. Ositeri, an infant, died.

## October

On the Kalends of October: Piaton, martyr; Saint Nicetius, bishop; Bavo, Remigius, and Vedast.

On the sixth day before the Nones: The passion of Leodegarius, martyr.

On the fourth day before the Nones: Saint Mark, confessor.

On the second day before the Nones: Saints Caprasius and Faith, martyrs.

On the Nones: At Rome, Saint Mark, pope, and Saints Mark, Apuleius, [Col. 1201B] Sergius, and Bacchus, martyrs. Ostericus, deacon, died.

On the eighth day before the Ides of October: Saint Reparata, virgin; burial of Saint Amor, confessor. Elvier, priest, died.

On the seventh day before the Ides: At Paris, the passion of Saint Dionysius, bishop, with his companions. At Cologne, Saint Gereon with 319 martyrs.

On the sixth day before the Ides: Saint Victor, martyr, and Paulinus, confessor. On the same day, the holy martyrs Cassius and Florentius.

On the fifth day before the Ides: Remembrance of our brothers. Konco, priest, died.

On the third day before the Ides: Saint Lupentius, priest and confessor.

On the first day before the Ides: At Rome, Saint Callistus, pope XVI. He instituted the fast of the four seasons. Volcherd, a layman [Col. 1201C] and our brother.

On the Ides: The holy Moors.

On the seventeenth day before the Kalends of November: Nativity of Saint Gall, confessor.

On the fifteenth day before the Kalends: In Bithynia, Saint Luke the Evangelist.

On the fourteenth day before the Kalends: Saint Januarius with his companions. Saint Maximus, martyr.

On the twelfth day before the Kalends: Burial of Saint Hilarion. At the village of Basona, Saint Walden, confessor. Thuard, our brother, died.

On the eleventh day before the Kalends: In Francia, Saint Philip, bishop and martyr.

On the tenth day before the Kalends: At Paris, Saint Venantius, abbot.

On the ninth day before the Kalends: Saint Columbanus, monk; Eraclianus, confessor and bishop.

On the eighth day before the Kalends: In the city of Soissons, the holy martyrs Crispin [Col. 1201D] and Crispinian. Miniatus, martyr. Godescalc, our brother, died.

On the sixth day before the Kalends: Alfruin, our brother, died.

On the fifth day before the Kalends: Nativity of the Apostles Simon and Jude.

On the third day before the Kalends: Eusebius, martyr. Bishop Hilleric died. On that same night, when Archbishop Tagenus was returning after the nocturnal office with his two chaplains, Theoderic the subdeacon and Eric the priest, the opened sky became bright with an exceedingly brilliant light, as though through a door, for approximately the course of one hour.

On the second day before the Kalends: In Gaul, the passion of Saint Quintinus, martyr. Eusebius and Gavinus.

## November

On the Kalends of November: At Rome, Saint Caesarius, deacon. [Col. 1202A] The passion of Saint Eustace with his sons.

On the third day before the Nones: Saint Humbert, bishop; Valentinus, priest; and Hilary, deacon.

On the second day before the Nones: Saint Germanus, bishop; Domninus; and Amandus, bishop. Fritheric, priest, and Richard, priest.

On the Nones: Saint Felix, priest, and Eusebius, monk. Herculanus, martyr. Otto, duke, died.

On the eighth day before the Ides: Burial of Saint Willibrord, bishop.

On the sixth day before the Ides: At Rome, the Four Crowned Martyrs: Severus, Severianus, Victorinus, and Carpophorus.

On the fifth day before the Ides: Saint Theodore, martyr.

On the fourth day before the Ides: Leo, confessor.

On the second day before the Ides: At Tours, the burial of Saint Martin and Saint Menna, martyr.

On the Ides: At Tours, Saint Briccius, bishop.

On the sixteenth day before the Kalends of December: In Alamannia, Saint Magnus, confessor, and Saint Othmar, confessor. Hager, priest, died.

On the fifteenth day before the Kalends: At Orléans, the burial of Saint Anianus, bishop. Bernhard, a brother of our monastery.

On the fourteenth day before the Kalends: Saint Romanus, monk and martyr.

On the thirteenth day before the Kalends: Saint Simplicius, bishop and confessor.

On the eleventh day before the Kalends: In Istria, in the city, Saint Maurus, martyr.

On the tenth day before the Kalends: At Rome, the passion of Saint Cecilia, virgin.

On the ninth day before the Kalends: At Rome, Saints Clement and Felicity.

On the eighth day before the Kalends: At Rome, Saint Chrysogonus and the translation of Saint Felicula. On the same day, Saint Prosper, bishop and confessor, and Saint Eleutherius, martyr. On the same day, Saint Felicity, mother of seven sons. Bishop Gunthar died.

[Col. 1202C] On the seventh day before the Kalends: Saint Audentius, confessor. Bishop Hilliward died.

On the fifth day before the Kalends: Count Henry died.

On the fourth day before the Kalends: At Rome, Saint Gregory, pope LXXXVIII. Everhard, a layman, died.

On the third day before the Kalends: At Rome, Saturninus, Chrysantus, Maurus, and Darius with 70,000 others.

On the second day before the Kalends: In Achaea, the passion of Saint Andrew the Apostle.

## December

On the Kalends of December: At Noyon, Saint Eligius, confessor, and Candida, virgin, and the ordination of Boniface. The holy martyrs Sabinus, Latinus, and Superantius.

On the fourth day before the Nones: At Capua, Longinus the soldier, who pierced the Lord’s side. Emnil, a nun, died.

On the third day before the Nones: In Alamannia, the burial of Saint Sola, virgin.

[Col. 1202D] On the second day before the Nones: Saint Barbara, and the translation of Benedict’s body to Fleury. Liutherius, a layman, and Countess Mathilda died.

On the Nones: Saint Dalmatius, martyr.

On the eighth day before the Ides: Saints Nicholas, Hermogenes, and Rogatus.

On the seventh day before the Ides: Saint Sabinus, bishop. Octave of Saint Andrew. Otto, emperor Augustus, died. Biso, our brother and deacon, died. Gerdagus, bishop, died.

On the fifth day before the Ides: Tricus, deacon, died.

On the fourth day before the Ides: In the city of Barcelona in Spain, the passion of Saint Eulalia, virgin and martyr.

On the third day before the Ides: At Rome, Saint Damasus, pope XXXVIII; Victoricus, Fuscianus, and Gentianus.

On the second day before the Ides: Saint Finian, bishop.

On the Ides: At Syracuse, the passion of Saint Lucy. At Cambrai, Saint Authbert, bishop and confessor.

[Col. 1203A] On the nineteenth day before the Kalends of January: At Reims, the burial of Saint Nicasius, bishop and martyr.

On the eighteenth day before the Kalends: Count Widukind.

On the sixteenth day before the Kalends: In Antioch, the passion of Saint Ignatius, bishop and confessor. Empress Adelheid died.

On the fifteenth day before the Kalends: Our sister Bagred died.

On the thirteenth day before the Kalends: Liudric, priest and monk.

On the twelfth day before the Kalends: In India, the passion of Saint Thomas the Apostle. Brun, priest.

On the tenth day before the Kalends: At Rome, Saint Victoria, martyr, and Saint Gregory, priest.

[Col. 1204A] On the eighth day before the Kalends: Nativity of Our Lord Jesus, and the passion of the holy virgins Anastasia and Eugenia.

On the seventh day before the Kalends: In the town of Jerusalem, the passion of Saint Stephen, the protomartyr. Burhard, an infant, died. Athilger, priest, died.

On the sixth day before the Kalends: In Ephesus, the Assumption of Saint John the Apostle and Evangelist.

On the fifth day before the Kalends: At Bethlehem, the Holy Innocents. Abbot Geppe died.

On the fourth day before the Kalends: Brigid, abbess, died.

On the third day before the Kalends: Saint Perpetuus, bishop and confessor at Tours. Saints Sabinus and Exuperantius. Ewrhard, a layman, died.

On the second day before the Kalends: At Rome, Saint Sylvester, pope XXXIII.

[Col. 1203]

# The Verdun Calendar

## January

[Col. 1203B]

The first and seventh days of January are feared at the end.

January has 31 days and 30 lunar days.

On the Kalends of January: CIRCUMCISION OF OUR LORD JESUS CHRIST. Egyptian day. On the fourth day before the Nones: Octave of Saint Stephen. Isidore, bishop and martyr.

On the third day before the Nones: OCTAVE OF SAINT JOHN. Genevieve, virgin.

On the second day before the Nones: Octave of the Holy Innocents.

On the Nones of January: Saint Simeon the prophet. Vigil of the Epiphany of the Lord.

On the eighth day before the Ides: EPIPHANY OF THE LORD. Julian, martyr.

On the seventh day before the Ides: Saint Isidore, bishop and confessor.

On the sixth day before the Ides: Saint Lucian and Maximian.

On the fifth day before the Ides: Saint Vitalis and Felix.

[Col. 1203C] On the fourth day before the Ides: Saint Paul, the first hermit.

On the third day before the Ides: THE LORD’S DEPARTURE FROM EGYPT. Saint Felicity.

On the second day before the Ides: Saint Muscentius and Saturus.

On the Ides of January: OCTAVE OF THE EPIPHANY. Hilary, bishop.

On the nineteenth day before the Kalends of January: Saint Felix, priest.

On the eighteenth day before the Kalends: Chrysogonus and Zeno.

On the seventeenth day before the Kalends: Marcellus, pope and martyr; Furseus, confessor.

On the sixteenth day before the Kalends: Sulpitius, bishop; Antonius, monk.

On the fifteenth day before the Kalends: Prisca, virgin and martyr. The sun enters Aquarius.

On the fourteenth day before the Kalends: Maurus, Martha, Audifax, Abacuc.

On the thirteenth day before the Kalends: Fabian, pope; Sebastian, martyr.

On the twelfth day before the Kalends: Patroclus, martyr; Agnes, virgin and martyr.

[Col. 1203D] On the eleventh day before the Kalends: Vincent, martyr; Anastasius, monk.

On the tenth day before the Kalends: Emerentiana, virgin and martyr. Count Gerard died.

On the ninth day before the Kalends: Babylas, bishop, with three child martyrs.

On the eighth day before the Kalends: CONVERSION OF SAINT PAUL. Praejectus, martyr. Egyptian day.

On the seventh day before the Kalends: Polycarp, bishop and martyr.

On the sixth day before the Kalends: Vitellianus; John Chrysostom.

On the fifth day before the Kalends: Octave of Saint Agnes, virgin.

[Col. 1204B] On the fourth day before the Kalends: Valerius, bishop; Papias and Maurus.

On the third day before the Kalends: Aldegund, virgin.

On the second day before the Kalends: Victor and Publius.

## February

But the fourth of February is such that the third precedes the end.

February has 29 days and 29 lunar days.

On the Kalends of February: Severus, bishop; Brigid, virgin.

On the fourth day before the Nones: PURIFICATION OF SAINT MARY.

On the third day before the Nones: Blaise, bishop and martyr.

On the second day before the Nones: Castor, priest and martyr; Geminus and Gelasius. Egyptian day.

On the Nones of February: Agatha, virgin and martyr.

On the eighth day before the Ides: Vedast and Amandus, martyrs.

[Col. 1204C] On the seventh day before the Ides: Augulus, bishop.

On the sixth day before the Ides: Paul, bishop; [lacuna] pope. Bishop Thiatgrimus.

On the fifth day before the Ides: Ammon and Alexander, martyrs.

On the fourth day before the Ides: Zoticus, Irenaeus, and Hyacinth.

On the third day before the Ides: Scholastica, virgin.

On the second day before the Ides: Simplicius, bishop; Dorothy, virgin.

On the Ides of February: Stephen, bishop and confessor.

On the sixteenth day before the Kalends of March: Valentine, martyr; Vitalis, Felicola, and Zeno.

On the fifteenth day before the Kalends: Faustinus.

On the fourteenth day before the Kalends: Juliana, virgin and martyr.

On the thirteenth day before the Kalends: Polychronius, bishop.

On the twelfth day before the Kalends: Pigmenius, priest.

On the eleventh day before the Kalends: Publius and Julian.

[Col. 1204D] On the tenth day before the Kalends: Eucharius, bishop and martyr.

On the ninth day before the Kalends: Eucharius, confessor.

On the eighth day before the Kalends: CHAIR OF SAINT PETER.

On the seventh day before the Kalends: Polycarp, martyr. Vigil.

On the sixth day before the Kalends: NATIVITY OF SAINT MATTHIAS THE APOSTLE. FINDING OF THE HEAD OF SAINT JOHN THE BAPTIST. Leap year.

On the fifth day before the Kalends: Nestor and Castus.

On the fourth day before the Kalends: Fortunatus, confessor.

On the third day before the Kalends: Egyptian day. Servilianus, martyr.

On the second day before the Kalends: Claudianus, martyr.

## March

[Col. 1205A]

The first of March, whose point is thus, is the fourth.

March has 31 days and 30 lunar days.

On the Kalends of March: Suidbert, confessor; Albinus and Donatus. Egyptian day.

On the sixth day before the Nones: Simplicius, pope.

On the fifth day before the Nones: Felix and Lucian.

On the fourth day before the Nones: Lucius, pope and martyr.

On the third day before the Nones: Saturninus, martyr.

On the second day before the Nones: Quiriacus and Victor.

On the Nones of March: Perpetua and Felicity, virgins.

On the eighth day before the Ides: Cyril, bishop.

On the seventh day before the Ides: The Forty Holy Martyrs.

On the sixth day before the Ides: Ansbert, bishop.

On the fifth day before the Ides: Zosimus and Pilonus.

[Col. 1205B] On the fourth day before the Ides: SAINT GREGORY, POPE.

On the third day before the Ides: Macedonius, priest.

On the second day before the Ides: Donatus and Leo, martyrs.

On the Ides: Longinus, martyr; Matrona, martyr.

On the seventeenth day before the Kalends: Eugenia, virgin; Eusebia, virgin.

On the sixteenth day before the Kalends: Patrick, bishop; Gertrude, virgin.

On the fifteenth day before the Kalends: Pimen, martyr. The sun enters Aries.

On the fourteenth day before the Kalends: Joseph at Bethlehem.

On the thirteenth day before the Kalends: Guthbert, bishop and confessor.

On the twelfth day before the Kalends: Benedict, abbot. Equinox.

On the eleventh day before the Kalends: Saturninus.

On the tenth day before the Kalends: Theodore, priest; Fidelis and twenty others.

On the ninth day before the Kalends: Seleucus.

On the eighth day before the Kalends: ANNUNCIATION OF SAINT MARY. PASSION OF THE LORD.

[Col. 1205C] On the seventh day before the Kalends: SAINT LIUDGER, BISHOP AND CONFESSOR.

On the sixth day before the Kalends: RESURRECTION OF THE LORD.

On the fifth day before the Kalends: Rogatus, Alexander, and Successus. Egyptian day.

On the fourth day before the Kalends: Eustasius, abbot and confessor; Pastor, priest.

On the third day before the Kalends: Victor, martyr.

On the second day before the Kalends: Regulus, bishop; Balbina, virgin and martyr.

(Four following months are missing.)

## August

The first [day] of August, the scorpion, drives away the second from the end.

August has 31 days and 29 lunar days.

On the Kalends of August: Peter in Chains. The Seven Maccabean Brothers.

[Col. 1205D] Egyptian day.

On the fourth day before the Nones: Stephen, pope.

On the third day before the Nones: Finding of the body of Stephen, the protomartyr.

On the second day before the Nones: Justinus, bishop and confessor.

On the Nones: Memmius, bishop and confessor; Oswald, king and martyr.

On the eighth day before the Ides: Sixtus, pope and martyr; Felicissimus and Agapitus, martyrs.

On the seventh day before the Ides: Donatus, bishop and martyr; Afra, virgin and martyr.

On the sixth day before the Ides: Cyriacus, Largus, Smaragdus, and Crescentianus, martyrs.

On the fifth day before the Ides: Romanus, martyr. Vigil.

[Col. 1206A] On the fourth day before the Ides: SAINT LAWRENCE, MARTYR.

On the third day before the Ides: Tiburtius, martyr; Gaugericus, bishop.

On the second day before the Ides: Euplus, martyr.

On the Ides: Hippolytus, martyr, with his companions.

On the nineteenth day before the Kalends of September: Eusebius, confessor.

On the eighteenth day before the Kalends: ASSUMPTION OF SAINT MARY, MOTHER OF GOD.

On the seventeenth day before the Kalends: Arnulf, confessor.

On the sixteenth day before the Kalends: Octave of Saint Lawrence. Theoderic, priest, died.

On the fifteenth day before the Kalends: Agapitus, martyr. The sun enters Virgo.

On the fourteenth day before the Kalends: Magnus, martyr.

On the thirteenth day before the Kalends: Athanasius, bishop.

On the twelfth day before the Kalends: DEDICATION OF THE CHURCH OF SAINT MARY, OR OF “TURBIS VINCENTII” [reading uncertain].

On the eleventh day before the Kalends: The holy martyrs Timothy and Symphorianus.

[Col. 1206B] On the tenth day before the Kalends: The holy martyrs Timothy and Apollinaris. VIGIL.

On the ninth day before the Kalends: Nativity of Saint Bartholomew the Apostle.

On the eighth day before the Kalends: Genesius, martyr. Maximianus, martyr.

On the seventh day before the Kalends: The holy martyrs Irenaeus and Abundius.

On the sixth day before the Kalends: Rufus, martyr.

On the fifth day before the Kalends: Hermes, martyr, and Saint Augustine, bishop.

On the fourth day before the Kalends: Beheading of Saint John the Baptist; Sabina, virgin. Egyptian day.

On the third day before the Kalends: The holy martyrs Felix and Adauctus.

On the second day before the Kalends: Paulinus, bishop.

## September

[Col. 1206C]

The third of September strikes the fox from the foot ten times.

September has 30 days and 30 lunar days.

September 1. Saint Priscus, martyr.  
September 2. Saint Justin, bishop and confessor.  
September 3. Saint Antonius, martyr; Remaclus, confessor. Egyptian day.

September 11. Saints Protus and Hyacinthus, martyrs.

September 14. Exaltation of the Holy Cross; Saints Cornelius and Cyprian, martyrs.  
September 15. Saint Nicomedes, martyr.  
September 16. Saints Lucius and Germinianus, martyrs; Saint Euphemia, virgin.  
September 17. Saint Lambert, bishop and martyr. The sun enters Libra.

September 28. Saints Faustus, Januarius, and Martialis, martyrs; Lioba, virgin.  
September 29. Dedication of the basilica to Saint Michael the Archangel.  
September 30. Saint Jerome, presbyter.

## October

“The third of October binds the sword in the tenth place.”

October has thirty-one days and twenty-nine lunar days.

October 1. Saints Remigius, Germanus, Vedastus, Amandus, and Bavo, confessors.  
October 2. Saint Leodegarius, bishop and martyr.  
October 3. Saints Ewald and Ewald, presbyters, at Cologne. Egyptian day.

October 10. Saints Gereon, Victor, Cassius, Florentius, and four hundred thirty-two others, martyrs.  
October 11. Saints Tharacus, Probus, and Andronicus, martyrs.  
October 12. Saints Cyprian and Felix, martyrs; Nidistus, martyr.  
October 13. Saint Laurence, bishop and confessor; Lupentius, bishop and confessor.

October 18. Saint Luke, evangelist and confessor. The sun enters Scorpio.  
October 19. Saints Desiderius, Ferius, and Januarius, martyrs.  
October 20. Saint Neorus, martyr; Saints Lucius and Marcellinus, martyrs.  
October 21. Saint Hilarion, monk, and the eleven thousand holy virgins at Cologne.  
October 22. Saint Philip, bishop and martyr; Severus, bishop; Mark, bishop and confessor.  
October 23. Saint Severinus, bishop, at Cologne; Venantius, abbot. Egyptian day.  
October 24. Saint Columbanus, monk and confessor.  
October 25. Saints Crispin and Crispinian, martyrs.  
October 26. Saint Amandus, bishop and confessor; Daria, virgin.  
October 27. Saint Evaristus, pope; Florentius, martyr. Vigil.  
October 28. Saints Simon and Jude, apostles.  
October 29. Saint Quirinus, martyr; Narcissus, bishop.  
October 30. Saint Theonestus, martyr; Eusebius, martyr.  
October 31. Saints Quintinus and Gavinus, martyrs. Vigil.

## November

“The fifth of November: the needle scarcely remained third in the urn.”

November has thirty days and thirty lunar days.

November 1. Solemnity of All Saints; Caesarius, martyr.  
November 2. Saint Benignus, presbyter and martyr; Hugbert, confessor.  
November 3. Saint Germanus, bishop; Valentinus, presbyter.  
November 4. Saint Proculus, bishop and martyr.

November 18. Romanus, confessor and martyr.  
November 19. Simplicius, bishop.  
November 20. Saints Bassus and Dionysius, martyrs.

November 22. Saint Cecilia, virgin and martyr.  
November 23. Saint Clement, bishop and martyr; Saint Felicity.  
November 24. Saint Chrysogonus, martyr.  
November 25. Saint Peter, bishop and martyr; Maximus, confessor.  
November 26. Amator, bishop; Nicander and Cassianus, martyrs.  
November 27. Saint Theodulus, martyr.  
November 28. Saint Sisinnius, bishop. Egyptian day.  
November 29. Saint Saturninus, martyr. Vigil.  
November 30. Saint Andrew, apostle.

## December

“The cohort of twelve gives seven, then ten, in December.”

December has thirty-one days and twenty-nine lunar days.

December 2. Saint Longinus, soldier and martyr.  
December 3. Saint Lucius, king and confessor.  
December 4. Saint Barbara, virgin and martyr.  
December 5. Saint Talmatius, martyr.

## Martyrology of the Distinguished Church of Auxerre

## January

“The first day of January is feared at its seventh ending.”

January 1. Circumcision and octave of our Lord Jesus Christ. At Rome, Saint Almachius, martyr, and Saint Martina, virgin and martyr. At Spoleto, the passion of Saint Concordius, martyr. At Caesarea in Cappadocia, the commemoration of Saint Basil, bishop and confessor. In Africa, the commemoration of Saint Fulgentius, bishop and confessor. At Alexandria, Saint Euphrosyne, virgin. In the territory of Lyon, the commemoration of Saint Eugendus, abbot. At Ravenna, Saint Severus, bishop and martyr. Likewise at Rome, thirty martyrs.

Robert, levite and canon, died. On the same day, in the territory of Auvergne, at the monastery of Silviniacum, the burial of Lord Odilo, abbot of Cluny.

January 2. In the Thebaid, the burial of blessed Macarius, abbot. And in the Pontic city of Tomis, of the three brothers Argeus, Narcissus, and Marcellinus, a boy and martyr. In Frisia, the passion of Saint Theagenes, martyr.

January 3. At Rome, the commemoration of Saint Antherus, pope and martyr. At Paris, the burial of Saint Genevieve, virgin. In the city of Aulana, the passion of Saint Peter, who was killed by the punishment of the cross. At Vienne, Saint Florentius, bishop.

Gislebert, bishop, and Ablenus, archdeacon, died.

January 4. In Crete, the commemoration of Saint Titus, disciple of the apostles. At Rome, the holy martyrs Priscus, presbyter, Priscillianus, and Benedicta, a most religious woman, and blessed Daphrosa, martyr, together with seven other martyrs.

January 5. At Rome, the commemoration of Saint Telesphorus, pope and martyr. At Jerusalem, blessed Simeon the prophet, who received our Lord Jesus Christ into his arms. At Antioch, in the church called “Repentance,” the burial of Simeon the monk, who stood upon a column.

Ebrard, subdeacon and canon, died. Having given one hundred solidi toward the construction of the cloister, he also gave his house and vineyards to the canons, on the condition that his brothers should celebrate his anniversary from them and that the canons should provide a meal for the canons. If they refused to do this, the canons were to take the house and vineyards for themselves and celebrate the same anniversary with alms and a meal.

January 6. Epiphany of our Lord. In the city of Antioch, the commemoration of Saint Julian, martyr, and Basilissa, Celsus the boy, Marcianilla, Antonius the presbyter, and Anastasius, martyrs. In the territory of Reims, the passion of Saint Magna, virgin. At Auxerre, the translation of Saint Germanus, confessor.

Lord W., bishop of this holy church, died. On the same day, Wadricus, a soldier from Warziacum, died.

January 7. The return of Jesus from Egypt. At Antioch, the commemoration of Saint Lucian, presbyter and martyr, who was divided into four parts, bound to separate stones, and sunk in the sea.

January 8. At Naples in Campania, Saint Severus, confessor; at Beauvais, Saint Lucian, presbyter; Maximianus and Julianus, martyrs.

Anastasius, archbishop of Sens, died.

January 9. At Smyrna, the commemoration of Saints Vitalis, Revocatus, and Fortunatus; and in Caesarean Mauritania, the commemoration of Saint Martina, virgin.

January 10. In the Thebaid, the burial of Saint Paul, the first hermit, who remained alone in the desert from his sixteenth year until his one hundred thirteenth year; and blessed Antony saw his soul carried by angels into heaven among the choirs of the saints. And in Cyprus, blessed Nicanor, who was one of the seven deacons.

On the same day Leotard, priest and dean of Sens, died. Likewise Frotmund, a soldier of Saint Stephen, died.

January 11. In Africa, the commemoration of Saint Salvius, martyr. At Alexandria, the commemoration of Saints Peter, Severus, and Leuticius, confessors.

January 12. In Achaea, the commemoration of Saint Saturus, martyr. On the same day, Saint Arcadius, martyr. At Langres, Saint Gregory, bishop and confessor.

January 13. At Rome, on the Lavican Way, the crown of forty soldiers. At Poitiers, the burial of Saint Hilary, bishop and confessor. At Reims, the commemoration of Saint Remigius, bishop and confessor. Octave of the Epiphany of the Lord.

On the same day Rainald, bishop of Autun, was transferred from this world.

January 14. At Antioch, Glycerius the deacon and many others suffered numerous torments and were sunk in the sea. At Nola in Campania, the passion of Saint Felix, presbyter, buried at Pincus. And elsewhere, the burial of Saint Euphrasius, bishop and confessor.

Ordination of Gerrannus, bishop, who gave to the brothers, in the county of Laticum, Gaiacum with all its appurtenances. He also gave a vineyard in the suburb of the city called Cerseredus; whoever possessed it by charter was to give the brothers one modius of wine according to the smaller measure.

On the same day King Rotdulf died. On that day Tetard, a soldier, was killed by enemies, as was Frotmund, a priest. Likewise on that day Heldric, abbot of Saint Germanus, died.

January 15. In Egypt, blessed Macarius, abbot and disciple of Saint Antony. And elsewhere, Saint Isidore, confessor. At Angers, blessed Maurus, monk and abbot. And elsewhere, the burial of the prophets Habakkuk and Micah.

January 16. At Rome, on the Salarian Way, in the cemetery of Priscilla, the burial of Marcellus, pope and martyr. At Arles, Saint Honoratus, bishop and confessor. At Parron, in the monastery, Saint Furseus, confessor. At Clermont, the commemoration of Saint Bonitus, bishop and confessor.

Heribert, bishop and afterward a monk, died. Arnald, deacon and master, died. Likewise Gyla, a woman of good memory and consecrated to God, died. On the same day Gaufridus, canon and dean of this church, died.

January 17. In Egypt, in the Thebaid, the commemoration of blessed Antony, monk. At Bourges, the burial of Sulpicius, bishop and confessor. At Langres, the passion of the holy twins Speusippus, Eleusippus, and Meleusippus, of Leonilla, Jovilla, and Neon.

On the same day Gurard, canon of this church and provost of Saint Mary, died. Likewise Vauterius, levite and canon, died; he gave to the service of the altar of Saint Stephen priestly vestments and a book necessary for celebrating Mass, and he gave the brothers two mills at Villeneuve, a house, a garden, and wine, for the commemoration of himself.

January 18. Chair of Saint Peter the apostle, on which he first sat at Rome. On the same day, the commemoration of Saint Prisca, virgin and martyr. And in Pontus, the commemoration of Saints Moses and Ammon, martyrs. At Alexandria, Saint Maximus, bishop and confessor. In the city of Apollonia, the passion of Saints Thyrsus, Leucius, and Callinicus. At Auxerre, dedication of the blessed and glorious Virgin Mary.

Gislaudus, priest, died; together with his brother Fredebertus, deacon, and Vinbertus, a layman, he gave the brothers his holding with all its appurtenances: eight arpents of vineyards and six ancingae of land, situated in the county of Sens, in the village of Caciacum, for the canons’ meal to be celebrated.

Commemoration of Gaufridus and his wife Heldrada. For their absolution and in honor of Saint Mary, their son Ricco gave a vineyard from which, on the feast of the dedication of that Virgin, a meal was to be provided for the brothers at the proper time.

January 19. At Jerusalem, the commemoration of Martha and Mary, sisters of Lazarus. At Smyrna, the commemoration of Saint Germanicus, martyr, condemned to the beasts. At the monastery of Corbion, the commemoration of Saint Launomarus, confessor.

Airricus, levite, died. On the same day Frodo, levite and canon, died; for the salvation of his soul he made for this church a silver dove, gilded with gold […] with a crown and silver chains, hanging above the altar for preserving the body of our Lord Jesus Christ.

On the same day Willelmus, canon and levite, died; for the remedy of his soul he gave four pounds of his money toward establishing a library. Likewise Rodulfus, priest and canon, died; for the remission of his sins he gave the church a silver chalice, an excellent missal, and priestly vestments.

January 20. At Rome, the commemoration of Fabian, pope and martyr, and Saint Sebastian, martyr, buried in the footsteps of the apostles. In the cemetery of Callistus on the Appian Way, Marius and Martha with their sons Audifax and Abacuc. At Lyon in Gaul, Clement, presbyter.

January 21. At Rome, the passion of Saint Agnes, virgin. At Athens, blessed Publius, bishop, who was ordained bishop by blessed Paul the apostle. At Troyes, the commemoration of Saint Patroclus, martyr. In Spain, the commemoration of Saints Fructuosus, bishop, and Augurius and Eulogius, deacons.

On the same day John, a humble bishop, departed to the Lord; he lived in the episcopate one year, eleven months, and the same number of days.

January 22. In Spain, Saint Vincent, deacon and martyr. At Rome, at the Waters of Salvias, the commemoration of Saint Anastasius, monk and martyr from Persia. On the same day in Gaul, at the city of Embrun, Saints Vincent, Orontius, and Victorinus, martyrs. In the territory of Vienne, the passion of eighteen holy martyrs.

January 23. At Rome, the commemoration of Saint Emerentiana, virgin and martyr. In the Mauritanian city of Caesarea, the commemoration of Saint Severianus and Aquila, his wife, burned by fire. On the same day, the commemoration of Saint Parmenias, deacon, who was one of the seven deacons. At Toledo, the commemoration of Saint Hildefonsus, bishop and confessor.

January 24. At Ephesus, the commemoration of Saint Timothy, disciple of blessed Paul the apostle; his body was transferred to Constantinople in the twentieth year of the Emperor Constantine. At Antioch, the commemoration of Saint Babylas, bishop. At Troyes, Saint Sabinianus, martyr. In the city of Neocaesarea, the commemoration of the holy martyrs Mardonius, Musonius, Metellus, and Eugenius.

January 25. Conversion of Saint Paul the apostle and translation of his body. At Damascus, the burial of Ananias, who baptized Paul. On the same day, the commemoration of blessed Gregory of Nazianzus, bishop, who is called “the Theologian.” At Clermont, Saint Praeiectus, bishop and martyr, and Marinus, a man of God. At the city of Javols, Saint Severianus, bishop.

January 26. At Nicaea in Smyrna, the commemoration of Saint Polycarp, bishop and martyr, disciple of Saint John the apostle, and Theogenes with thirty-six others. At Bethlehem, the death of Saint Paula, mother of Eustochium, virgin of Christ. And in the monastery of Cala, the burial of Bathildis, queen.

January 27. At Constantinople, the burial of Saint John Chrysostom, bishop and confessor. On the same day, the commemoration of Saint Marius, abbot, at the monastery of Bobacum.

Heribald, levite, died; he gave the brothers from his estate a holding and a half in the county of Sens, in the village called Liviniacum, with slaves and all appurtenances, and five arpents of vineyard in the village of Pauliacum. Hubert, deacon, died, as did Adoyn, priest and dean.

Atto, priest and canon of this church, an outstanding succentor, died. Having given all that he possessed in alms, together with slaves, vineyards, and other property, he enriched the church with his books.

January 28. At Rome, the octave of Saint Agnes, virgin and martyr. At Alexandria, the burial of blessed Cyril, bishop. In the Reomay monastery at Tornodorum, the death of the apostolic man, the outstanding teacher and supreme confessor John.

Emperor Charles died. Gotelindis was consecrated to God.

January 29. At Rome, Saints Papias and Maurus, soldiers and martyrs. At Trier, the burial of Saint Valerius, bishop and disciple of Saint Peter the apostle. At Troyes, Saint Savina, virgin.

January 30. At Antioch, the passion of Saint Hippolytus, martyr. At Jerusalem, blessed Matthias, bishop. On the same day, Saint Alexander, martyr. At the monastery of Malbodium, the commemoration of Saint Aldegundis, virgin.

January 31. At Alexandria, the commemoration of Saint Metranus, martyr. Likewise at Alexandria, the commemoration of Saints Thyrsus, Saturninus, and Victor, martyrs. At Trent, blessed Vigilius, bishop and martyr. And elsewhere, Saints Cyrus and John, martyrs, and the holy virgins Theodota, Theotiota, and Eudoxia, together with their holy mother Athanasia.

## February

February 1. At Antioch, the commemoration of Saint Ignatius, bishop and martyr. And in Scotland, Saint Brigid, virgin. At Smyrna, the commemoration of Saint Pionius, martyr. And elsewhere, blessed Ephrem, deacon. In the city of Tricastinum, Saint Paul, bishop and confessor.

February 2. Purification of Saint Mary. At Caesarea, blessed Cornelius the centurion, bishop of that city. At Rome, the commemoration of Saint Apronianus, martyr. At Orléans, the burial of Flosculus, bishop, and Sicaria, a virgin consecrated to God.

February 3. In Africa, blessed Celerinus, deacon, and the holy martyrs Celerina, his grandmother, and Laurentinus and Ignatius. At Lyon, the burial of blessed Lupicinus, bishop.

February 4. In the Egyptian city called Thmuis, the passion of the most blessed Phileas, bishop of that city, and Philoromus, tribune, and countless martyrs. At Troyes, Saint Aventinus, bishop and confessor. At Auxerre, Saint Alexander, subdeacon and confessor.

Emmena, consecrated to God, died.

February 5. In the Sicilian city of Catania, the passion of Saint Agatha, virgin. At Vienne, blessed Avitus, bishop and confessor.

On the same day Gislebert, priest and dean, afterward made a monk, died; and Raginald, priest and canon, died.

February 6. At Caesarea in Cappadocia, the commemoration of Saint Dorothea, virgin and martyr, and Saint Theophilus, martyr and scholar. At Clermont, the commemoration of Saint Antholianus, martyr. At Arras [reading: Atrebatis], the most glorious bishops Vedastus and Amandus, confessors.

February 7. In the British city of Augusta, the commemoration of Saint Augulus, bishop and martyr. In the province of Asia, Saint Apollinaris, bishop of the city of Hierapolis.

February 8. In Lesser Armenia, the commemoration of Saints Dionysius, Aemilianus, and Sebastian. At Rome, the burial of Saint Paul, bishop. At Alexandria, the commemoration of Saint Cointha, martyr.

February 9. In Pontus, Saint Athenodorus, bishop, brother of blessed Gregory, also called Theodore. At Alexandria, the commemoration of Saint Apollonia, virgin.

February 10. At Benevento, the commemoration of Saint Scholastica, virgin, sister of Saint Benedict. In the East [Note: [Col. 1213D] This is an error, for more correctly, at Rome on the Appian Way], Saint Soter, virgin. At Rome, Saints Zoticus, Irenaeus, Hyacinthus, and Amantius, martyrs. At Saintes, Trojanus, bishop and confessor.

February 11. At Alexandria, the burial of Saint Euphrasia, virgin. At Lyon, the commemoration of blessed Desiderius, bishop and confessor. On the same day, Saint Severinus, abbot.

Aldoenus, priest, died; he gave the brothers his patrimony in the village of Valeria.

February 12. In Africa, Saints Saturninus, presbyter, Felix, Apel(ius), and his companions, martyrs, who suffered for Christ under the proconsul Anolinus. At Alexandria, Modestus and Ammonius, martyrs. In Africa, the passion of Saint Damianus, soldier.

On the same day Robert, bishop of this church, died. He established an annual benefice for a deceased canon and granted to the brothers of this church the mill acquired from Atto below the wall, and removed a double safeguard from Pulvereno […].

February 13. At Antioch, the commemoration of Saint Agabus, prophet. In the Armenian city of Melitene, the commemoration of Saint Polyeuctus, martyr, whose name in Latin means “praying much.” At Angers, Saint Licinius, bishop and confessor.
