At Lyon, the burial of Saint Stephen, bishop and confessor.

Aaron, bishop, died.

February 14. At Rome, the commemoration of Saint Valentine, presbyter and martyr. At Interamna, the commemoration of Saint Valentine, bishop. At Alexandria, Saints Bassus, Antonius, and Protol(i)cus, martyrs, who were sunk in the sea. On the same day, Saints Vitalis, Felicula, and Zeno with many others, martyrs. At Heraclea, the commemoration of Saint Felix and Januarius. And elsewhere, the passion of Saint Serenus.

February 15. At Rome, the commemoration of Saint Craton, martyr. At the city of Sebaste, the passion of Saint Blasius [reading: Blavius], bishop, and seven holy women. On the same day, the burial of Quindidius, bishop, and Saint Silvinus, bishop. At Interamna, the commemoration of Saint Agape, virgin.

February 16. The commemoration of Saint Onesimus, apostle, who was stoned at Rome; his body was carried to Ephesus, where he had been ordained bishop. And at Cumae, Saint Juliana, virgin. And in Egypt, Julianus, martyr, with five thousand others.

February 17. In Persia, the commemoration of Saint Polychronius, bishop and martyr. In Africa, the passion of Donatus, Secundianus, Romulus, and eighty-six others. In Scotland, Saint Fintan, presbyter and confessor.

February 18. At Jerusalem, blessed Simeon, bishop and martyr. At Rome, the holy martyrs Claudius and his wife Praepedigna, their sons Alexander and Cures, and Claudius’s brother, blessed Maximus. At Alexandria, blessed Dionysius, bishop and confessor.

Walter, bishop of Orléans, died.

February 19. At Rome, the commemoration of Saint Gabinus, presbyter and martyr, father of the most blessed Susanna. In Africa, Publius, Marcellus, and Julianus, martyrs.

Robert, a soldier, died.

February 20. At Tyre, many martyrs, whose number God’s knowledge alone reckons. At Rome, the burial of Gaius, bishop; and elsewhere, of Victor and Corona. In Alemannia, blessed Gallus, confessor.

On the same day Erembert, priest and provost, died; he gave the brothers an allod in the village of Antonnus, which he had bought from Regembertus.

February 21. In Sicily, seventy-nine martyrs suffered various torments under Diocletian. In the African city of Hadrumetum, the commemoration of the holy martyrs Verolus, Secundus, Servulus, and twenty others.

Goffridus, canon of Saint Stephen and dean of Saint Peter, died.

February 22. At Antioch, the Chair of Saint Peter the apostle, on which he first sat at Antioch. At Alexandria, Abilius, bishop and assistant of John the apostle and evangelist; and elsewhere, blessed Aristion, who was one of the seventy-two disciples.

February 23. At Smyrna, the commemoration of Saint Sinerus, monk and martyr, and seventy-two martyrs. In Asia, Polycarp, bishop.

On that day Otto, margrave of Burgundy, died in the year 963 of the Lord’s Incarnation. Likewise Obertus, a soldier, died.

February 24. The commemoration of Saint Matthias, apostle, and the finding of the head of John the Baptist and forerunner of the Lord. At Caesarea in Cappadocia, the commemoration of Saint Sergius, martyr.

Lord Betto, bishop, died; he gave the brothers the church of Vendosa and the village of Rontonnacum, and at Corboiacum one holding, for providing a meal and common service.

February 25. In Egypt, the commemoration of the holy martyrs Victorinus and Victor, Nicephorus, Claudianus, Dioscorus, Serapion, and Papias. In Pamphylia, the commemoration of Saint Nestor, confessor.

February 26. In the city of Perge in Pamphylia, blessed Nestor, bishop and martyr. At Alexandria, blessed Alexander, most glorious bishop and confessor.

February 27. In Spain, in the city of Seville, the commemoration of Saint Leander, bishop, to whom blessed Gregory wrote the books of the *Moralia*. And at Alexandria, Julianus, martyr.

February 28. In the territory of Lyon, in the Jura region, the burial of blessed Romanus, abbot. On the same day, Saints Macarius and Rufinus.

## March

March 1. At Rome, the commemoration of two hundred sixty holy martyrs whom Claudius first ordered condemned in Christ’s name to dig an arena, and then commanded them to be sent outside the wall of the Salarian Gate and killed by soldiers’ arrows in the amphitheater of that city. At Angers, Albinus, bishop and confessor. At Carthage, the passion of Donatus, martyr. At the city of Antinoopolis, the passion of blessed Leonidas.

Actaldus, priest, died; he gave to the hospital of his brothers in the village of Gratis a holding with an adjoining vineyard. On the same day Rotfredus, dean, entered the way of all flesh. Guadilo, subdeacon, died on the same day; he gave his brothers his allod at the place called Vallis, with vineyards, woods, and slaves. On that day Enricus, subdeacon, was killed. Likewise Waldr(ic), provost, gave his earthly body to the ground and his blessed spirit to Christ.

March 2. At Rome, the commemoration of the holy martyrs Jovinus and Basileus, and many other martyrs condemned to death under Alexander. Likewise at Rome, Simplicius, pope and martyr.

March 3. In Spain, Saints Emeterius and Chelidonius, crowned by martyrdom. At Auxerre, the commemoration of Saint Camilla, virgin. At Caesarea, the commemoration of the holy martyrs Marinus, soldier, and Aerius, senator.

March 4. The commemoration of Saint Lucius, pope and martyr. Likewise at Rome, nine hundred holy martyrs who are buried in the cemetery at Saint Cecilia. On the same day, the commemoration of Saint Gaius Palatinus, sunk in the sea. At Nicomedia, the passion of Saint Adrian with twenty-three others.

March 5. At Antioch, the passion of Saint Phocas, martyr; if any believer touches the door of his church, he is immediately healed after being bitten by a serpent. On the same day, Saint Eusebius Palatinus and nine other martyrs.

Walo, bishop of the church of Troyes, died. On the same day, the ordination of Lord Hugh, bishop, who on the day of his ordination gave the brothers the altar of the church of Billiacum.

March 6. At Nicomedia, the commemoration of Saints Victor and Victorinus, who, afflicted by many torments and shut in prison, completed the course of their lives there. In the city of Toledo, the burial of Saint Julianus, bishop.

March 7. In the Mauritanian city of Tuburbo, the passion of Saints Satyrus, Perpetua, and Felicity, martyrs, and with them Revocatus, Saturninus, and Secundolus.

March 8. At Carthage, the commemoration of Saint Pontianus, deacon, and blessed Cyprian, bishop. In the city of Antinoopolis, the commemoration of the holy martyrs Philemon, Apollonius, Arrianus, Theoticus, and three others who were sunk in the sea.

On the same day, the commemoration of the deceased monks of the monastery of Charity was solemnly celebrated; they too celebrate for our dead.

March 9. In the city of Nissa, the commemoration of Saint Gregory, bishop, brother of blessed Basil. At Barcelona, Pacianus, bishop and confessor. At Sebaste in Lesser Armenia, the commemoration of the forty glorious soldier-martyrs in the time of King Licinius; both their names and deeds are recorded. In Africa, Cyril, Felix, Philip, Marianus, Rogatus, and Concessus.

Wala, bishop, died. To preserve his memory, his brother Ansergisus, archbishop, […] distributed two holdings to the brothers with royal and episcopal consent, and in the administration of the light of the divine altar of the church of Saint Stephen, in the village of Piscasiolum, one holding.

March 10. At Apamea, the commemoration of Saints Alexander and Gaius of Eumenia, martyrs. In Persia, forty-two holy martyrs. At Antioch, Agatha, virgin. At Paris, Saint Droctoveus, abbot, disciple of blessed Germanus, bishop. At the monastery of Luxeuil, Saint Attalus, abbot.

March 11. At Alexandria, the commemoration of Saint Philo, bishop, Candidus, Valerius, and twenty others. At Sebaste in Lesser Armenia, the commemoration of the forty holy martyrs who completed their martyrdom by the breaking of their legs. At Carthage, the commemoration of Saint Heraclius. At Auxerre, Saint Vigilius, bishop and martyr.

On that day Aganus, dean of Saint Stephen, died.

March 12. The commemoration of Saints Innocent, pope, and the most blessed Pope Gregory, the chief teacher. At Nicomedia, the commemoration of blessed Peter, most excellent martyr, who in faith and name was heir of the holy apostle Peter, together with eight others.

Adalgarius, deacon, died; he gave the brothers six arpents of vineyards around Gratiacum for his memory to be celebrated. On the same day, the ordination of Lord Betto, bishop.

March 13. At Nicomedia, the commemoration of the holy martyrs Macedonius, presbyter, and Patricia, his wife, and Modesta, their daughter. In the city of Nicaea, the commemoration of the holy martyrs Theuseta, Horis, Theodora, Nymphodora, Marcia, and Arabia, all of whom were given to the fire. In the Thebaid, Saint Euphrasia, virgin. In the territory of Nevers, Saint Vincentius, presbyter.

March 14. At Rome, the commemoration of forty-seven holy martyrs who were baptized by blessed Peter while he was held in custody; all were killed by Nero’s sword. At Laodicea, the commemoration of Saint Segaris, bishop and martyr. At Nicomedia, Felicissimus, Dativus, and Frontina. At Rome, Innocentius, bishop. In Africa, Saint Peter, martyr, and Saint Euphrasius.

March 15. At Caesarea in Cappadocia, the passion of Saint Longinus, who pierced the Lord’s side with a lance, as is found in his acts. In the city of Thessalonica, the commemoration of Saint Matrona, martyr, who remained manfully in confession of Christ until death. At Rome, Zacharias, pope.

On the same day Adelhelmus, priest and cantor, died. On the same day Odo, a soldier, died; he gave his allod at the village of Crevenum to the canons.

March 16. At Aquileia, blessed Hilary, bishop, and Tacianus, deacon, who together with his son Felix, Largus, and Dionysius completed their martyrdom. At Rome, Cyriacus, martyr, and with him Smaragdus and Crescentianus and twenty other martyrs. At Clermont, Saint Patrick, bishop and confessor. At Nicomedia, Castorius, martyr.

March 17. In Scotland, the commemoration of Saint Patrick, bishop and confessor, who first preached Christ there. At Alexandria, the commemoration of Saint Ambrose, deacon. At the monastery of Nivigella, Saint Gertrude, virgin.

March 18. At Caesarea, the commemoration of Saint Alexander, bishop and martyr, who together with Narcissus assumed the governance of the Church of Jerusalem. At Rome, Cyril, bishop and confessor.

Walaharius, priest and dean, died.

March 19. At Caesarea in Cappadocia, Saint Theodore, presbyter. At the city of Penera, blessed John of great holiness. At Sorrento, Saints Quintus, Quintillus, Quartilla, and Marcus with nine others, martyrs.

March 20. In Britain, the commemoration of Saint Chudberct, bishop and confessor. On the same day, the commemoration of Saint Archippus, fellow soldier of the apostle Paul. In Syria, Saints Paul, Cyril, and Eugenius with four others. On that day, Saint Wilfrannus.

Adoardus, priest, and Aroildis, devoted to God, died; they gave the brothers at Villare Tornetrense and Marolium an excellent allod with a chapel, for their memory to be celebrated.

March 21. At the fortress of Cassinum, our holy father Benedict, abbot, who was filled with the spirit of all the righteous. At Flavigny, the arrival and reception of the body of Saint Regina, virgin and martyr. In the territory of Lyon, blessed Lupicinus, abbot. And at Alexandria, blessed Serapion, anchorite.

March 22. In Gaul, in the city of Narbonne, the commemoration of Saint Paul, bishop and confessor, disciple of the apostles. At Corinth, blessed Dionysius, bishop. In the city of Béziers, Saint Aphrodisius, bishop and confessor.

Conrad, count, and Maginfrid, knight of Saint Stephen, died. On the same day Theoderic, canon and priest, died; he gave his house and vineyards, and whatever property he appeared also to possess, to the hospital of the poor, in order to obtain forgiveness for his sins.

### 23 March

The feast of the holy martyrs Victorianus, Frumentius, another Frumentius, and two brothers, crowned by an outstanding martyrdom under King Huneric. In Africa, the blessed martyr Fidelis.

Gislar, archdeacon, died. He gave to his brothers [Col. 1219D] all his estate which he appeared to possess at Melun and in its surroundings, to have his memory commemorated. On the same day William, a layman, died; he gave to the brothers and the altar his patrimony in the Senonais, in the village called Conflans. On the same day Andrew, a knight, died.

### 24 March

In Syria, the feast of Saint Seleucus. On the same day, Saints Romulus and Secundolus, who suffered for Christ in Mauretania. At Rome, the passion of Saint Pigmenius, priest. He had nourished the apostate Julian from childhood and instructed him in the sacred writings; later, Julian had him killed in the Tiber for the faith of Christ. Afterwards his body was recovered and buried in the cemetery of Pontianus, not far from Saints Abdon and Sennen. In Syria, [Col. 1220A] Saint Seleucius; likewise, in Phrygia, Saint Agapitus.

### 25 March

At the city of Nazareth in Galilee, the Annunciation of the holy and perpetual Virgin Mary; and at Jerusalem, the crucifixion of Our Lord Jesus Christ. At Sirmium, the feast of Saint Hereneus, bishop and martyr. At Rome, the passion of Saint Cyrinus, martyr. At Nicomedia, the feast of Saint Sedula, martyr. On the island of Antros, the feast of Saint Ermeland, abbot.

Ilduinus, archdeacon of Sens and canon of this church, died.

### 26 March

At Rome, Saint Castulus, priest and martyr. In Pentapolis of Libya, Theodore, bishop; Irenaeus, deacon; Serapion and Ammonius, readers. At Sirmium, the feast of Saint Montanus, priest, [Col. 1220B] and his wife Maxima, who were drowned in the sea.

Aya, servant of Saint Mary, died. On the same day Anastasia, mother of Lord Acardus, priest, died. She gave to the canons of Saint Stephen the Protomartyr a certain excellent vineyard, on the condition that those who attended the morning services might drink its wine for as long as it lasted. The canons who were in chapter had granted this arrangement.

### 27 March

In Egypt, the blessed John, hermit, a man of admirable holiness and endowed with the spirit of prophecy. At Jerusalem, the Resurrection of Our Lord Jesus Christ. At Smyrna, the blessed Thraseas, bishop and martyr. In Pannonia, Saint Alexander, martyr.

### 28 March

At Caesarea in Palestine, the feast of the holy [Col. 1220C] martyrs Priscus, Malchus, and Alexander. At Chalon, the burial of Lord Guntram, king. At Rome, Pope Sixtus. At Tarsus in Cilicia, Castor and Dorotheus.

On the same day Ansellus, a young knight of Saint Stephen, died. Likewise, Condrada, consecrated to God, died.

### 29 March

The feast of the holy martyrs Armogastes, Archinimus, and Satyrus during the Vandal persecution. At the monastery of Luxeuil, the burial of the blessed Eustasius, abbot and disciple of Saint Columbanus.

The ordination of Lord Waldric, bishop. On the same day Dodo, knight of Saint Stephen, died.

### 30 March

At Rome, the feast of the holy martyrs Quirinus and Tribunus. At the fortress of the people of Senlis, the burial of Saint Regulus, confessor and first bishop of that city. At Thessalonica, the feast of Saints Domninus [Col. 1220D] and Victor.

### 31 March

At Rome, Saint Balbina, virgin, who lies buried beside her father, Quirinus the martyr. On the same day, the prophet Amos. In Africa, Saints Diodolus and Anesius.

On that day Belinus, levite and canon, a man of honorable life, died. He gave the canons of Saint Stephen one thousand solidi for the purchase of revenues, so that a common meal might be provided for the canons every year from them.

## APRIL

### 1 April

In Armenia, Saints Quintianus and Victor, martyrs. At Rome, the burial of the most blessed martyr Theodora. At Thessalonica, the feast of the holy virgins and martyrs [Col. 1221A] Agape and Chionia. In Sardinia, the blessed Meritor, bishop and confessor. On the same day, Saint Venantius, bishop and martyr.

Guido, canon, and Edissa’s archdeacon, died.

### 2 April

At Lyons, the blessed Nicetius, bishop and confessor. In Palestine, the burial of the blessed Mary of Egypt, who is called “the Sinner.”

### 3 April

At Caesarea in Cappadocia, the passion of Saint Theodosia, virgin. At Nicomedia, Saints Donatus and Amphianus. In Scythia, in the city of Tomis, the feast of Saints Evagrius and Benignus.

Abbo, a knight of this church, died.

### 4 April

At Milan, the blessed Ambrose, bishop and confessor, an eminent teacher. At Seville, the burial [Col. 1221B] of Saint Isidore, bishop and confessor.

On that day Leotricus, viscount and standard-bearer of this church, died.

### 5 April

At Thessalonica, the feast of Saint Irene, virgin and martyr. In Egypt, the feast of Saints Nicanor, Apollonius, and Marciana, whose acts are extant.

On the same day, the ordination of Lord Heribald, bishop. Likewise, on that day Ingeluinus, knight, died.

### 6 April

At Rome, the feast of Saint Sixtus, pope and martyr, who suffered during the reign of Hadrian. In Macedonia, Saints Timothy and Diogenes. In Upper Libya, Theodore, bishop; Hereneus, deacon; Serapion and Ammonius, readers. Elsewhere, the feast of Saints Marina and Egulina.

[Col. 1221C] Remigius and Warimbert, bishops, died. On the same day Gaufridus, archdeacon and abbot of Saint Eusebius, died.

### 7 April

In Africa, the feast of Saints Epiphanius, bishop, Donatus, and thirteen others. On the same day, Hegesippus and fourteen most holy [companions; the source is elliptical]. At Alexandria, Saint Peleusius, priest.

John, levite and abbot of Saint Eusebius, still a young man, instructed in the wisdom of letters and distinguished by goodness, died. On that day Adila, a religious woman, died.

### 8 April

At Toulouse, the feast of Saint Exuperius, bishop and confessor, whose deeds blessed Jerome memorably recorded. At Rome, Pope Callistus.

[Col. 1221D] Beraldus, priest and cantor, died.

### 9 April

At Antioch, the feast of Prochorus, martyr, who was one of the seven deacons. At Sirmium, the feast of seven virgins, who were worthy to be crowned together; God knows their names.

Suavis, subdeacon, died, greatly devoted to letters. On the same day the queen, wife of Guibertus, died; with her consent and at her request, Guibertus gave the church of Saint Stephen to the canons in the village of Acolay.

### 10 April

At Rome, the feast of the many martyrs whom Pope Alexander baptized and whom Aurelian caused to be killed in the sea; elsewhere, [Col. 1222A] the prophet Ezekiel. At Auxerre, the burial of Saint Palladius, bishop and confessor.

Waningus died. He gave to the brothers his demesne holding, with an excellent vineyard and adjoining garden, at the place called Mausiac, so that his memory might be commemorated. On the same day King Louis died.

### 11 April

At Rome, the feast of Saint Leo, pope, during whose pontificate the holy Council of Chalcedon took place. In Crete, in the city of Gortyna, the feast of Saint Philip, bishop and confessor. In Dalmatia, in the city of Salona, the feast of Saint Domnio, bishop and confessor, with eight soldiers. At Nicomedia, Saint Eustorgius.

### 12 April

At Rome, on the Via Aurelia, the burial of the blessed [Col. 1222B] Julius, bishop and confessor. On the same day, Bishop Zeno. At Wassigny, the burial of Bishop Constantine. At Auxerre, the blessed Tetricus, bishop.

On the same day William, subdeacon and canon, happily gave up his spirit. For the remission of his sins, he gave his house and vineyard to the canons.

### 13 April

At Chalcedon, the feast of Saint Euphemia, virgin and martyr. At Pergamum, a city of Asia, the feast of the holy martyrs Carpus, bishop, Papylus, deacon, and the blessed Agathonica, together with many others. In Spain, the feast of Saint Hermenegild, king and martyr.

### 14 April

At Rome, the feast of Saints Tiburtius, Valerian, and Maximus. At Terni, Saint Proculus, martyr. At Alexandria, [Col. 1222C] the blessed Honton and Saint Domna, virgin, crowned with her companions, the virgins.

On the same day, the ordination of Lord Richard, prelate. On that day Otbertus, knight of Saint Stephen, died.

### 15 April

In the city of Cordoba, the feast of the noble holy martyrs Olympias and Maxima. In Italy, the holy martyrs Maro, Euthyches, and Victorinus. At the monastery of Réomé, the blessed Sylvester, disciple of Saint John the Confessor.

### 16 April

At Caesaraugusta, the eighteen holy martyrs, whose names and passion are recorded. At Corinth, the feast of Saint Calixtus and Carisius with seven others. At Rome, Saint Anicetus, pope and [Col. 1222D] martyr; and in Mauretania, the feast of Saint Basilia.

On the same day Godolgarius, priest, and Augustus, priest, died. Augustus gave to the brothers his estate at Maisilina, with the adjoining vineyard, in the village called Loconiac, so that his memory might be commemorated.

### 17 April

In Africa, the feast of Saint Mappalicus, who was crowned with many others. At Antioch, the feast of Saints Peter, deacon, and Hermogenes.

Peter, deacon, died. He gave to the brothers in the Senonais, in the village called Rivisiac, and in the county of Auxerre, in the village called Poziac, all his property, [Col. 1223A] whatever he appeared to possess, with holdings, lands, and vineyards, so that his memory might be commemorated. On that day David, levite and provost, departed this life. Likewise, John, levite and humble abbot, departed from this world into the mercy of Christ. Richard, count, died. Victoria, countess, [died].

### 18 April

At Messina, a city of Apulia, the feast of the most glorious holy martyrs Eleutherius, bishop, and Anthia, his mother. At Rome, the passion of Saint Apollonius, senator. In Africa, Victor-Pamphilus with seven others.

### 19 April

At Corinth, the feast of Saint Timo, crucified, who was one of the seven deacons. In Armenia, in the city of Melitene, the feast of Saints Rufus, Aristonicus, and Hermogenes, with six others. At Caucoliberis [Col. 1223B] in Spain, the feast of Saint Vincent, martyr. At the monastery called Laubias, the burial of the blessed Ursmar, bishop and confessor.

Ersendis, a widow consecrated to God, died. For the absolution of the soul of Aginus, her former husband, and of her own soul, she gave to the brothers, in the Senonais, in the village of Caciacum, a vineyard enclosure of four arpents, and to Saint Priscus, among the monks and brothers, the small vineyards that she had there. Stephen, knight, died.

### 20 April

The feast of Saint Victor, pope and martyr. Likewise at Rome, Saints Sulpitius and Servilianus, martyrs. At Auxerre, the burial of Saints Mamertinus and Marianus, confessors.

### 21 April

In Persia, the feast of Saint Simeon, bishop and martyr, with many others. In Gaul, [Col. 1223C] in the city of Embrun, the feast of Saint Marcellinus, bishop and confessor. At Alexandria, the feast of Saints Fortunatus, Arator the priest, Felix, Silvius, and Vitalis, who found rest in prison.

Lord Galdricus, bishop, died. Hugh, the most noble knight of Saint Stephen, died. He gave to the brothers the village of Acolay with its appurtenances, with the consent of his lord, Bishop Goffridus, so that his memory might be commemorated.

### 22 April

At Rome, Saint Caius, pope and martyr. In Persia, the five hundred holy martyrs. At Lyons in Gaul, the feast of Saint Epipodius, martyr. Elsewhere, Saint Parmenias with his companions. At Sens, Saint Leo, bishop and confessor.

[Col. 1223D] On the same day Elya, wife of Robert, duke, breathed out her final spirit, while the world mourned and heaven rejoiced. On that day Elizabeth, wife of Josbert, knight, died. With her consent and at her request, Josbert gave the canons of Saint Stephen a certain wood and one olca not far from the village of Acolay, so that her memory might be commemorated.

### 23 April

In the Persian city of Diospolis, the passion of Saint George, martyr. In Gaul, in the city of Valence, the feast of Saints Felix, priest, Fortunatus, and Achilleus, deacons. At the monastery of Fontenelle, Saint Wulfran, bishop and confessor.

On the same day Gwilencus, knight, died.

### 24 April

At Lyons in Gaul, the feast of Saint Alexander, [Col. 1224A] martyr, with thirty-four others. In Britain, Saint Mellitus, bishop and confessor.

Ansellus, levite and distinguished canon, an eminent teacher in the divine Scriptures, died. For the salvation of his soul, he gave the canons the vineyard that he had on Mount Defensum.

### 25 April

At Alexandria, the feast of Saint Mark the Evangelist. At Lyons, the burial of the blessed Rusticus, bishop. At Rome, the greater litany at Saint Peter’s. In the Sicilian city of Syracuse, the feast of Saints Evodius, Hermogenes, and Callista.

Lord Eribaldus, bishop, died. He gave, for the purchase of clothing for the brothers, the village of Condé with its appurtenances, and the little abbey of Saint Remigius with its vineyards—namely, the courtyard (corticanum) and plantings—and, for their stipends, half of Maximiac, that is, twenty-one holdings [Col. 1224B].

### 26 April

At Rome, the feast of the holy martyrs Cletus and Marcellinus, pope. In the county of Ponthieu, at the monastery of Centula, the burial of Saint Richarius, confessor. At Auxerre, the dedication of the greater church of Saint Mary.

### 27 April

At Rome, the feast of Saint Anastasius, pope. At Nicomedia, Saint Anthimus, bishop and martyr, with an innumerable multitude of martyrs. In the city of Tarsus in Cilicia, the feast of Saint Castor.

Lambertus, canon and sacristan of this church, died. To have his memory commemorated, he gave to this church two silver basins, a silver censer, a pallium cope, two candlesticks, and two carpets. To the canons he gave one hundred solidi and the oven that he built at Crévennes, as well as all the houses and other buildings that he possessed both at Crévennes and at Acolay [Col. 1224C].

### 28 April

At Ravenna, the feast of Saint Vitalis, martyr, father of Saints Gervasius and Protasius. At Alexandria, the blessed Theodora, virgin and martyr, and Saint Didymus, martyr. In Pannonia, Saint Eusebius, bishop, and Saint Pollio, martyr.

Stephen, a layman, died. He gave to the brothers of Saint Stephen the estate that he had acquired at the village of Loconiac from George, priest, to be commemorated after the death of his wife Gelesindis.

### 29 April

At Paphos, the feast of Saint Tychicus, disciple of the apostles. In Tuscany, Saint Torpes, martyr. In Numidia, at the colony of Cirta, the feast of the holy martyrs Agapius and Secundinus, bishops [Col. 1224D]. Six others suffered with them.

On the same day Ayglulfus, priest and dean, dispenser of divine words, departed from this light. He granted to the canons of Saint Stephen three arpents of vineyard from his estate in the village of Garric.

### 30 April

The feast of the holy martyrs Marianus, priest, and James, deacon, with many others. At Saintes, the feast of Saint Eutropius, martyr. In Asia, the passion of Saint Maximus, martyr. At Rome, on the Appian Way, the burial of Quirinus, bishop and confessor.

Nivelon, knight, died. Likewise, Hugh, canon and dean of this church, died.

## MAY

[Col. 1225A]

### 1 May

The feast of the holy apostles Philip and James. At Jerusalem, the feast of Saint Cyriacus, bishop and martyr, who was also called Judas. Elsewhere, the prophet Jeremiah. At Auxerre, the burial of the most holy Amator, bishop and foremost confessor of Christ. In Gaul, in the territory of Viviers, the passion of Saint Andeolus, subdeacon. At the city of Sion, at Agaunum, the passion of Saint Sigismund, king. At Toulouse, the burial of Saint Orientius, bishop and confessor.

### 2 May

At Alexandria, the feast of our holy father Athanasius, bishop and confessor. Likewise at Alexandria, the feast of Saints Saturninus and Neapolis, who found rest in prison. At Jerusalem, the feast of the blessed Simeon, [Col. 1225B] bishop and martyr, who was related by flesh to the Savior. At Auxerre, Optatus, bishop, Memorius, priest, and Sanctinus, priest.

Remigius, monk and distinguished teacher, died. On the same day Norgaudus, bishop of Autun and canon of this church, died. Through the hand of Humbaldus, bishop of our church, he gave ten pounds’ worth from a pallium, an excellent cope, and five marks of the purest silver to adorn the altar table, together with two coverings for the altar, wonderfully and skillfully worked.

### 3 May

At Jerusalem, the finding of the holy Cross by Queen Helena on Mount Golgotha, 283 years after the Lord’s Passion, during the reign of the emperor Constantine. At Rome, on the Via Nomentana, the feast of the holy martyrs [Col. 1225C] Alexander, pope, Eventius, and Theodulus, priests. On the same day, Bishop Juvenal, confessor. At Auxerre, Eusebius, priest, and Avitus, deacon.

### 4 May

In Palestine, in the city of Gaza, the feast of Saint Silvanus, bishop, crowned with a great number of his clergy. Elsewhere, forty holy martyrs. At Nicomedia, the feast of Saint Antonia, martyr. At Auxerre, the burial and translation of Saint Corcodomus, deacon and confessor. At Lauriacum, the feast of Saint Florian, martyr.

Walter, levite, canon, and provost of Saint Mary, died. On the same day Girbertus, levite, teacher, and abbot of Saint Eusebius, gave his body to the tomb and his soul to Christ.

### 5 May

The Ascension of the Lord into heaven. At Alexandria, the feast of Saint Euthymius, deacon [Col. 1225D]. At Thessalonica, the feast of Saints Hereneus, Peregrinus, and Irene, who were burned in the fire. At Arles, the burial of Saint Hilary, bishop and confessor. At Auxerre, the passion of Saint Juvinianus, reader. At Vienne, the blessed Nicetius, bishop, a man of venerable holiness.

Frodo, archpriest and canon, well instructed in letters, died.

### 6 May

At Rome, Saint John, apostle and evangelist, when he was placed before the Latin Gate in a cauldron of boiling oil. At Antioch, the feast of Saint Evodius, bishop and martyr. On the same day, the blessed Lucius, bishop of Cyrene; elsewhere, the feast of the holy martyrs Heliodorus, Venustus, Postumius, Maximus, Nicetius, and seventy-two others. At Auxerre, the burial of Saints Valerius and Valerian, bishops and confessors.

On the same day at Milan, the ordination of Lord Humbaldus, bishop, and the death of Master Guido, canon and archchancellor of Saint Stephen. He gave to our church from his books two passionaries, an antiphoner, a gradual, a hymnal, and an excellent psalter.

### 7 May

At Terracina, a city of Campania, the feast of the blessed Domitilla, virgin and martyr, with other virgins crowned by martyrdom. On the same day, the feast of Saints Nereus and Achilleus, eunuchs. At Troyes, Saint Mastidia, virgin. On that day at Nicomedia, the passion of Saints Flavius, Augustus, and Augustinus, brothers.

On that day Ilgerius, venerable provost of this church, [Col. 1226B] a mirror and model of clerics, finally assuming the monastic habit, lost death and found life. So that a meal might be provided for the brothers on the anniversary of his uncle, Bishop Humbaldus, he gave this church the mill that he had built at Agligniac from his own property. He also adorned this church with many priestly vestments, namely clothing for deacons and subdeacons. He also gave a silver chalice, silver tubes, an excellent pallium cope, a missal, a breviary, and many other books. Among the many benefactions that he made to this church, he gave five linen altar coverings, reverently worked. He constructed the principal doors of this church, spending three hundred solidi on their workmanship. He also gave, for the annual provision of a meal for the brothers on the anniversary of his death, half the land of Albex, which he bought from Gaufridus Rufus, and the mill that he built in the village called Molins [Col. 1226C]. On the same day Hugh, bishop of Nevers and canon of this church, died.

### 8 May

At Milan, the feast of Saint Victor, martyr. At Auxerre, the burial of Saint Eladius, bishop and confessor. In the territory of Saintes, [reading: Nantes?] at the monastery of Vertou, the burial of Saint Martin, priest and confessor. At Rome, Pope Benedict. In the territory of Bourges, at the monastery of Silviniac, the burial of Saint Desideratus, confessor.

### 9 May

In Persia, the holy martyrs, three hundred and ten. At the fortress of Vendôme, the blessed Beatus, confessor, whose acts are recorded [Col. 1226D]. At Constantinople, the feast of Saint Timothy.

### 10 May

The death of the prophet Job. At Rome, on the Via Latina, in its cemetery, the feast of the holy martyrs Gordianus and Epimachus with many others. Likewise at Rome, Calepodius, bishop and martyr. Likewise at Rome, at Centumcellae, Quartus and Quintus.

### 11 May

At Rome, on the Via Salaria, the feast of the blessed Anthimus, priest and martyr, and Saint Pontius. At Vienne, the feast of Saint Mamertus. At Silviniac, the feast of Saint Maiolus, abbot. On the same day, the passion of Saint Gengulfus, martyr.

Wibertus, a layman, and Dutinus, a boy, died. They gave us a small holding with a vineyard in the valley near [Col. 1227A] Matriacum. On that day Landricus, count, died.

### 12 May

At Rome, in the cemetery of Praetextatus, the feast of the holy martyrs Nereus and Achilleus, brothers. Likewise at Rome, on the Via Aurelia, the feast of Saint Pancratius, martyr. On the same day, the blessed Dionysius, uncle of the blessed Pancratius. In Cyprus, Saint Epiphanius, bishop and confessor.

Hugh, abbot, and Wigbaldus, bishop, died. Wigbaldus gave the brothers twelve holdings at Chichiriac by royal charter. Likewise, Countess Hermengardis died.

### 13 May

At Rome, the dedication of Saint Mary at the Martyrs, instituted by Pope Boniface. At the church of Tongeren, the burial of Saint Servatius, bishop and confessor; elsewhere, the blessed Mithrius, priest and [Col. 1227B] confessor. At Auxerre, the burial of Saint Marcellianus, bishop and confessor.

### 14 May

In the city of Cimela, the feast of Saint Pontius, martyr. In Syria, the feast of Saint Victor and Saint Corona, who suffered together. On that day, the feast of Saint Pachomius, our father. On the same day, the passion of Saint Boniface, martyr, who was buried at Rome on 5 June, when his more celebrated feast is also observed.

Letardus, priest, died. He gave to the brothers whatever he appeared to possess in the Senonais, in the village called Bagnenti, and in the county of Auxerre, in the village called Molendinis, so that his memory might be commemorated.

### 15 May

The feast of the holy confessors Torquatus, Tisefons, Secundus, Indaletius, Caecilius, Hesychius, and Euphrasius, [Col. 1227C] who were ordained bishops at Rome by the holy apostles. On the island of Chios, the feast of Saint Isidore, martyr. At Lormes, the feast of Saints Peter, Paul, Andrew, and Dionysia, whose remarkable passions are read. At Autun, the feast of Saint Tetricus, bishop.

### 16 May

At Auxerre, in the village of Baugis, the passion of Saint Peregrinus, the city’s first bishop. In the county of Troyes, Saint Fidolus, bishop and confessor. Elsewhere, the feast of Saints Aquilinus and Victorianus, whose acts are recorded. In the county of Fréjus, in the village called Calidianus, the feast of Saint Maxima, virgin. In Provence, in the city of Aix, Saint Mithras, martyr.

On the same day Lord Richard, bishop, entered the way of all flesh. On the same day Fulk, [Col. 1227D] canon and priest of Saint Amator, died. For the salvation of his soul, he gave his house at Petrina to the brothers.

### 17 May

At Hierapolis, the blessed Papias, bishop. In Tuscany, the burial of the body of Torpes, martyr, who completed his martyrdom on 27 April, but whose feast is more solemnly observed on this day. At Alexandria, Victor.

Gauzelmus, bishop of the holy church of Langres, died.

### 18 May

In Egypt, Saint Dioscorus, reader and martyr. On the same day, the feast of Saint Felix, bishop and martyr. At Auxerre, the reception of the relics of Saint Eugenia, virgin and martyr.

[Col. 1228A]

### 19 May

At Rome, the feast of Saint Potentiana, virgin and martyr, and Saint Pudens, her father. Likewise at Rome, the feast of the holy martyrs Calocerus and Parthenius, eunuchs of the wife of the emperor Decius. In Africa, the feast of Saints Quintus, Primulus, Salustus, Fortunatus, and Domnio.

### 20 May

At Rome, on the Via Salaria, the feast of Saint Basilia, virgin and martyr. In Gaul, in the city of Nîmes, the feast of Saint Baudelius, martyr. At Bourges, the feast of Saint Austregisilus, bishop and confessor. At Auxerre, in the basilica of Saint Germanus, the dedication of the crypts beneath it, and on the western side of the same church, the consecration of the oratory of Saint John the Baptist.

### 21 May

In Mauretania, the feast of the holy martyrs Timothy, Polyus, and Eutychius, deacon. At Auxerre, [Col. 1228B] the feast of Saint Valerius, confessor.

Ricco, priest, died. He gave to the canons of Saint Stephen all his estate, which he possessed at Montigny, together with the plots situated within the city, in order to obtain forgiveness for his sins and so that an excellent meal might be provided for the same brothers on the day of his death.

### 22 May

In Africa, the feast of the holy martyrs Castus and Aemilius. At Auxerre, Saint Helena, virgin, whose illustrious deeds are contained in the Acts of Saint Amator. In Corsica, the passion of Saint Julia, who was crowned with the punishment of the cross. Likewise at Auxerre, the burial of Saint Romanus, monk and confessor, and disciple of Saint Benedict.

On the same day Louis, the young king, died, as did Heldradus, [Col. 1228C] knight of Saint Stephen.

### 23 May

At Langres, the passion of Saint Desiderius, bishop. At Vienne, the passion of Saint Desiderius, bishop, who suffered in the territory of Lyons.

Ablenus, levite, died. He gave to the canons of Saint Stephen, in the Senonais, in the village of Juilly, his patrimony, in order to obtain forgiveness for his sins and so that an excellent meal might be provided for the same brothers on the day of his death. On that day Walo, priest and dean of Saint Peter, died.

### 24 May

At Porto Romano, the feast of Saint Vincent, martyr. Elsewhere, the feast of Manahen and the most blessed Joanna. In Gaul, in the city of Nantes, the feast of the holy martyrs Donatian and Rogatian [Col. 1228D] brothers.

Legerius, levite and canon, died. Returning from Jerusalem, he received burial at sea.

### 25 May

At Rome, the feast of Saint Urban, pope and martyr. At Milan, the feast of Saint Dionysius, bishop and confessor. In the territory of Troyes, Saint Leo, monk and confessor. Elsewhere, four holy martyrs.

### 26 May

At Athens, the blessed Quadratus, bishop and disciple of the apostles. In Britain, the feast of Saint Augustine, bishop and confessor. Likewise, Quadratus, martyr. In the territory of Auxerre, at the place called Quotiacum, the passion of Saint Priscus, martyr, with a great multitude. At Rome, twenty-three holy martyrs.

[Col. 1229A]

### 27 May

In Moesia, in the city of Durostorum, the feast of Saint Julius, martyr. At Orange, the feast of Saint Eutropius, bishop and confessor. In the territory of Adartum, Saint Ragnulfus, martyr.

### 28 May

At Rome, the feast of Saint John, pope and martyr. At Paris, the passing of Saint Germanus, bishop and confessor. At Chartres, the passion of Saint Caraunus. In Sardinia, Saints Aemilius, Felix, Priamus, and Lucianus.

Walo, levite and canon, who later became a monk, died.

### 29 May

At Rome, on the Via Aurelia, the feast of Saint Restitutus. On the Via Tiburtina, the feast of the seven brothers. At Trier, the blessed Maximinus, bishop and confessor. At Iconium, the feast of Saint Corona, martyr. On the same day, [Col. 1229B] the feast of the holy martyrs Sisinnius, Martyrius, and Alexander.

Frotmundus, knight of Saint Stephen and later a monk of Saint Benedict, died. On that day Count Raynaldus was killed.

### 30 May

At Rome, on the Via Aurelia, the feast of Saint Felix, pope and martyr. At Torres in Sardinia, the feast of the holy martyrs Gabinus and Crispulus. At Antioch, the feast of Saints Isicius and Palatinus, who suffered many torments. On that day, the feast of Saint Hubertus, bishop of Tongeren.

### 31 May

At Rome, the burial of Saint Petronilla, virgin, who was the daughter of the blessed apostle Peter. On the same day at Aquileia, Cantius, Cantianus, and Cantianilla, brothers and sister. At Torres in Sardinia, the feast of Saint Crescentianus.

[Col. 1229C] On the same day Elizabeth, a woman, died. For her soul, Obertus, her husband and a knight, gave the church of Saint Stephen two olcae situated in the village of Crévennes, so that her memory might be commemorated.

## JUNE

### 1 June

At Rome, the dedication of Saint Nicomedes, martyr; his martyrdom is celebrated there on 15 September. At Autun, Saints Rivirianus, bishop, and Paulus, priest, with ten other martyrs. At Caesarea in Palestine, the feast of Saint Pamphilus, priest and martyr. On the same day, Saint Caprasius, abbot, at the monastery of Lérins. At Vienne, Eladius, bishop and confessor.

### 2 June

At Rome, in the cemetery between the two laurels on the Via Labicana, the feast of Marcellinus, priest, and Peter, exorcist. On the same day at Lyons, the passion of Saint Blandina, virgin, with forty-eight martyrs, who were brought into the territory of Auxerre, to the village of Bacernum, by the blessed Balbina [Col. 1229D].

### 4 June

At Arezzo, a city of Tuscany, the feast of the holy martyrs Pergentinus and Laurentinus, brothers. Likewise in Campania, the blessed Erasmus, bishop and martyr. In the territory of Orléans, at the village of Meung, the burial of Saint Lifardus, priest and confessor.

### 4 June

At Rome, in the cemetery of the Catacombs on the Appian Way, the feast of the holy martyrs Aretas and Datianus. In Illyricum, at the city of Siscia, the feast of Saint Quirinus, bishop and martyr.

Alto, canon, died. He gave to the brothers, in the county of Auxerre, in the village called Poziac, a continuous tract of vineyard measuring more or less five arpents. On the same day Stephen of Caselles died. For his soul, his son John, through the hand of Pope Innocent and Count William, relinquished to the canons of this church who serve the Lord God the portion that he appeared to possess at Caselles, and in the village of Nantes three arpents of arable land and eight denarii of rent for the soul of his father (*patris*; the source's *atris* is an evident OCR loss), near the city wall.

### 5 June

In Egypt, the feast of the holy martyrs Marcianus, Nicander, and Apollonius, whose acts are recorded. At Tarsus, the feast of Saint Boniface, martyr. Likewise, Boniface, bishop and martyr, who came from Britain and suffered in Frisia.

On that day Theobaldus, knight, died.

[Col. 1230B]

### 6 June

At Caesarea, the burial of Saint Philip, deacon, who was one of the seven deacons. At Rome, the holy martyrs Artenius, his wife Candida, and their daughter Paulina. At Antioch, Saint Asclepiades, bishop and confessor.

### 7 June

At Constantinople, the feast of Saint Paul, bishop and martyr. At Cordoba, the holy martyrs Peter, priest, Aventius, Jeremiah, and three others, whose acts are recorded.

Letericus, subdeacon, died. He gave his estate at the village of Adrebletum to the brothers.

### 8 June

In Gaul, at the city of Soissons, the feast of Saint Medardus, bishop and confessor. On the same day, the burial of Saint Godardus, bishop of Rouen and brother of the same Saint Medardus. They are said to have been born on one and the same day, ordained bishops on one and the same day, and likewise [Col. 1230C] taken from this life on one and the same day. At Durostorum, Saint Marcus, bishop.

### 9 June

At Rome, on Mount Caelius, the feast of the holy martyrs Primus and Felicianus. In Scotland, Saint Columba, priest and confessor. In Gaul, in the city of Agen, at the place called Pompeiacus, the passion of Saint Vincentius, levite and martyr.

### 10 June

At Rome, on the Via Aurelia, the feast of Saint Basilides, martyr, and twenty-two other martyrs. At Auxerre, the burial of Saint Censurius, bishop and confessor. On the same day, the blessed Gestulius, martyr.

### 11 June

In India, the feast of Saint Barnabas, apostle. At Corinth, the feast of Saint Sosthenes, disciple of Saint Paul. At Aquileia, the holy martyrs Felix and [Col. 1230D] Fortunatus. At Rome, on the old Via Salaria, the feast of Saint Basilla.

### 12 June

At Milan, the finding and translation of the bodies of the holy martyrs Nazarius and Celsus. Their finding is observed on 13 June, and their martyrdom on 28 July; nevertheless, their public and solemn commemoration is celebrated more solemnly on the feast of the holy martyrs Protasius and Gervasius. Elsewhere, the holy martyrs Basilides, Cyrinus, and Nabor; also Nazarius and Celsus, whom antiquity celebrates in its records as having suffered at the city of Embrun. At Rome, on the Via Aurelia, Tripulus, Magdalen, Sabinus, Donatella, and Secunda.

### 13 June

At Rome, the feast of Saint Felicula, virgin [Col. 1231A] and martyr. At Cordoba, the feast of Saint Fandila, priest and martyr. In Africa, Saints Lucianus, Fortunatus, Crescentianus, and Thecla.

### 14 June

At Soissons, the passion of the holy martyrs Valerius and Rufus, who were indeed born at Rome but were crowned with glorious martyrdom in Gaul. Elsewhere, the prophet Elisha. At Orléans, the translation of the body of Saint Aignan, bishop, and the liberation of that city from the Huns. In Africa, Saints Quintianus, Theodola, Festiva, and Cantianilla.

Iterius, monk and outstanding teacher, died.

### 15 June

In Sicily, the feast of the holy martyrs Vitus, Modestus, and Crescentia. On the same day, at the city of Durostorum, the feast of Saint Esitius, soldier and martyr. At Aquileia, Saints Cantianus, Protus, Marcus, and Clement.

[Col. 1231B] Umbaldus and his wife Ingelsindis died. They gave their estate in the village of Alneda to the brothers. On that day King Robert was killed in battle.

### 16 June

At Antioch, the feast of the holy martyrs Cyricus and Julitta, his mother, and four hundred and four others. At the city of Besançon, the feast of the holy martyrs Ferreolus, priest, and Ferrutio, deacon. At Nantes, Saint Similianus, bishop and confessor. At the village of Madriacum, Saint Felix, martyr.

Hugh, count, died.

### 17 June

At Rome, the feast of two hundred and fifty-two holy martyrs. At Orléans, the burial of the blessed Avitus, priest and confessor. At the monastery called Golden, the burial of Saint Wulmarus, confessor.

[Col. 1231C]

### 18 June

At Rome, on the Via Ardeatina, the feast of the holy martyrs Marcus and Marcellianus, brothers. In Spain, in the city of Málaga, the feast of the holy martyrs Cyriacus and Paula, virgin. At Alexandria, the feast of Saint Marina, virgin.

Adhelardus, priest, died. For the love of eternal life, he gave his estate at Montigny to the canons of Saint Stephen, and in the city of Auxerre the plot on which he lived.

XIII Kalends of July. At Milan, the feast of the holy martyrs Gervasius and Protasius, and the commemoration of the holy Nazarius and Celsus. At Ravenna, the feast of Saint Ursicinus the martyr.

A good woman named Aeia died.

XII Kalends of July. At Rome, the deposition of Saint Novatus, brother of Timothy the presbyter; they had been instructed by the blessed apostles. At Ravenna, Crispulus and Vitalis, martyrs. In the city of Tomis, [Col. 1231D] the saints Paul, Cyriacus, Paula, Felicia, Thomas, and Felix.

The emperor Louis died. On the same day Ingrannus and his wife Elizabeth died; for their commemoration, their son Milo gave the canons of Saint Stephen twelve coins as an annual rent.

XI Kalends of July. In Sicily, in the city of Syracuse, the feast of the holy martyrs Rufinus and Martia. At Rome, Saint Demetria the virgin. In the city of Caesarea, the feast of Saint Eusebius the historiographer.

X Kalends of July. The feast of Saint Alban the martyr with eight hundred eighty-eight others. In the city of Nola in Campania, the feast of Saint Paulinus, bishop and confessor. On the same day, blessed Niceus, bishop of the city of Romatiana.

[Col. 1232A] IX Kalends of July. The vigil of Saint John the Baptist. On the same day, Saint John the presbyter and martyr, buried on the old Salarian Way. In Britain, Saint Ediltrudis, virgin and queen.

VIII Kalends of July. The Nativity of blessed John the Baptist. At Autun, the deposition of Saint Simplicius, bishop and confessor. At Rome, in the cemetery of Gaudentius, the saints Felix and Emerita.

VII Kalends of July. The feast of Saint Sosipater, disciple of the apostle Paul. At Alexandria, Gallicanus the martyr. At Rome, on the Salarian Way [read: Salaria], the feast of Saint Lucia the virgin and martyr with twenty-two others, and of Aceia, a barbarian king. In Crete, Saint Philip, bishop of Gortyna.

VI Kalends of July. The feast of the holy martyr brothers John [Col. 1232B] and Paul, the first of whom was chief officer and the second chief secretary of Constantia, the virgin daughter of Constantine. In Africa, Gaudentius, Felix, and Emita.

Leotericus, archbishop of Sens, died.

V Kalends of July. In Galatia, blessed Crescentius, disciple of the apostle Paul. In the city of Tibur in Italy, the feast of Saint …, martyred with her seven sons. At Córdoba in Spain, the holy Zoilus and nineteen others. At Carthage, Saint Guddena, virgin and martyr. At the monastery of Oia, Saint Florentius the confessor.

John, priest and canon, died. For the celebration of Masses and for the redemption of his soul, he gave priestly vestments and a silver chalice, and to the brothers twenty-two solidi in annual rents, so that a common meal might be provided for them. Moreover, he gave his house [Col. 1232C] to the church. Galo the layman also died; for love of eternal life, he gave the brothers all the patrimony that he possessed in the district of Tornetrum, at Villari-villa, for his commemoration to be made.

IV Kalends of July. The vigil of the apostles Peter and Paul. On the same day, the feast of Saint Leo, pope and confessor. At Lyon in Gaul, Saint Irenaeus, bishop and martyr, and seven others.

III Kalends of July. At Rome, the feast of the holy apostles Peter and Paul, who suffered under the consuls Bassus and Tuscus during Nero’s reign. In the same city, on the Aurelian Way, nine hundred seventy-seven holy martyrs.

The day before the Kalends of July. The feast and second celebration of blessed Paul the apostle. Also, of the most blessed Lucina, disciple [Col. 1232D] of the apostles. At Limoges, the feast of Saint Martial, bishop and confessor. On the same day, Saints Corsicus the presbyter and Leo the subdeacon. In the territory of Viviers, Saint Hostianus, priest and confessor.

On the same day Andrew, a soldier buried at Jerusalem, died.

## JULY

Kalends of July. On Mount Hor, the deposition of Aaron, the first priest. In the territory of Lyon, the deposition of the most blessed Domitian, abbot. On the same day, at the monastery of Aninsula, the feast of Saint Carelephus, priest and confessor. At Tours, Saint Monegundis the virgin. In the city of Angoulême, the deposition of Saint Eparchius, bishop and confessor. In the territory of Reims, Saint Theodoric, priest and confessor. In the territory of Cambrai, at the port called Valentiana, the feast of Saint Salvius the martyr. At Autun, the deposition of Leontius, bishop and [Col. 1233A] confessor.

Rainardus, a soldier, died. Jonas, levite and canon, also died; he gave forty solidi toward the restoration of this church’s books.

VI Nones of July. At Rome, the feast of the holy martyrs Processus and Martinianus, who were baptized and instructed by the most blessed Peter and Paul. In the same city, the feast of Saint Euticius and Pope Melchiades.

V Nones of July. At Edessa in Mesopotamia, the passion of Saint Thomas the apostle, whose translation is celebrated on the twelfth day before the Kalends of January, when the more solemn observance takes place. At Constantinople, [Col. 1233B] the feast of Saint Eulogius. At Laodicea, Saint Anatolius, bishop and confessor. At Neocaesarea in Pontus, blessed Gregory the bishop and blessed Athenodorus, his brother and bishop. At Sens, Saint Sidronius the martyr.

IV Nones of July. Hosea and Haggai, prophets. At Tours, the translation of Saint Martin, bishop and confessor, and his ordination to the episcopate. In Africa, the feast of Saint Jocundianus the martyr. In the territory of Bourges, at the village of Vestenus, the feast of Saint Laurianus the martyr. At Sirmium, the feast of the holy Innocentius and Sabbatia with thirty others.

III Nones of July. In Syria, the feast of Saint Domitius the martyr. At Rome, the feast of Saint Zoe the martyr, wife of blessed Nicostratus. At Alexandria, Saint Arpotis.

[Col. 1233C] The day before the Nones of July. Hosea and Joel, prophets, and the octave of the apostles. At Rome, the feast of Saint Tranquillinus the martyr, father of the martyrs Mark and Marcellian, who believed in Christ through the preaching of blessed Sebastian. In the Threcarensian district, Saint Gotharus, priest and confessor. At Autun, the deposition of Leontius, bishop and confessor.

Nones of July. At Alexandria, the feast of Saint Pantaenus, an apostolic man. At Rome, the holy martyrs Nicostratus, Claudius, Castorius, Victorinus, and Symphorianus, whom blessed Sebastian taught to believe in Christ and whom the presbyter Saint Polycarp baptized.

Bishop Angilelmus died. He gave a villa called Puiverenus for the support of the canons [Col. 1233D]. He also assigned for their use the properties that had passed to him by hereditary right, both at Biliacum and at Annau, together with their servants.

VIII Ides of July. In Asia, Saints Aquila and Priscilla, concerning whom it is written in the Acts of the Apostles. In Palestine, the feast of Saint Procopius the martyr. At Heraclea, Saints John and Aprus. On the same day, Saint Caecilianus the martyr.

VII Ides of July. At Rome, at the ever-flowing spring called Gutta, the feast of Saint Zeno and ten thousand two hundred three others. On the same day, blessed Cyril, bishop and martyr. In the city of Tyre, the feast of Saint Anatolia the martyr and Saint Audax the martyr. In the city of Martula, the feast of Saint Briccius, bishop and confessor. [Col. 1234A] On the same day, the deposition of Saint Ephrem, our father, deacon. At Sens, Saint Heraclius the bishop.

Odo, a monk of Saint-Denis, died.

VI Ides of July. At Rome, the feast of the seven holy martyr brothers, sons of Saint Felicitas: Januarius, Felix, Philip, Alexander, Vitalis, Silvanus, and Martial. In Africa, the feast of the holy martyrs Januarius, Marinus, Nabor, and Felix. Likewise at Rome, the feast of the holy virgin sisters and martyrs Rufina and Secunda. At Ephesus, on Mount Coelius, the deposition of the Seven Sleepers, whose names are: Maximianus, Malchus, Martianus, Dionysius, John, Serapion, and Constantine.

V Ides of July. The translation of the body of Saint Benedict, abbot. In Nicopolis, a city of Lesser Armenia, the feast of the holy martyrs Januarius and Pelagia. In the territory of Poitiers, the feast of Saint Sabinus the confessor. He was one of the disciples of Saint Germanus, bishop of Auxerre.

IV Ides of July. At Aquileia, the feast of Saint Hermagoras, bishop and martyr, disciple of Saint Mark the Evangelist. In Cyprus, the feast of blessed Vason, an ancient disciple of Christ. At Milan, the translation of the bodies of the holy martyrs Nabor and Felix. At Rome, in the Vatican, Saint Pius the pope. (Added by a recent hand: Receipt of the relics of Saint Amator.)

III Ides of July. The feast of Saint Silas the apostle, helper of blessed Paul the apostle. In Africa, the feast of the holy confessors Eugenius, bishop of Carthage, and the entire clergy of that church, who were put to death by slaughter and starvation, nearly five hundred or more in number. [Col. 1234C] In Lesser Britain, the feast of Saint Thuriavus, bishop and confessor. At Antioch, the passion of Saint Margaret the virgin. At Alexandria, Serapion and Trophimus.

The day before the Ides of July. At Rome, the feast of Saint Anacletus the pope. In Pontus, the feast of Saint Phocas, bishop and martyr. At Alexandria, the deposition of Saint Heracleas, bishop. At Lyon in Gaul, Saint Justus, bishop and confessor.

Gualdricus, levite and canon of Saint Stephen and abbot of Saint Eusebius, died.

Ides of July. At Alexandria, Saints Philip, Zeno, Narses, and the Ten Infants. At Nisibis, the feast of Saint James, bishop and a man of great virtue. At Carthage, Saints Catulinus the deacon, Januarius, Florentius, Julia, and Justa, who are buried in the basilica of Faustus. At Jerusalem, [Col. 1234D] the division of the twelve apostles for preaching.

Jonas, priest and canon of blessed Saint Stephen, died, fulfilling the debt of the present life; he gave up his spirit joyfully.

XVII Kalends of August. In the city of Ostia, the feast of Saint Hilarinus the martyr. At Antioch in Syria, the feast of Saint Eustachius, bishop and confessor. And elsewhere, Saints Valentinus, Theonius, and Diocletis.

XVI Kalends of August. At Carthage, the feast of the twelve holy Schillitan martyrs. At Auxerre, the deposition of blessed Theodosius, bishop and confessor.

XV Kalends of August. At Rome, the passion of the seven brothers: Peter, Marcellianus, Dionysius, Januarius, Symphronius, [Col. 1235A] Clement, and Irenaeus. In the city of Metz, the feast of Saint Arnulf, bishop and confessor.

XIV Kalends of August. In the city of Colossae, the feast of blessed Epaphras, bishop and martyr. In Spain, at Seville, the feast of Saints Justa and Rufina, crowned through martyrdom. On the same day, the feast of Saint Arsenius, our father, monk and confessor, who, because of the abundance of his tears, always carried a handkerchief in his bosom. At Lyon in Gaul, Saint Rusticus, priest and confessor.

XIII Kalends of August. The feast of Saint Joseph, who was surnamed Justus. In the city of Córdoba, the feast of Saint Paul, deacon and martyr. In the Thebaid, Saint Victor. At Damascus, the holy martyrs Sabinus and Maximinus with fourteen others. At Auxerre, Saint Marinus the presbyter.

[Col. 1235B] XII Kalends of August. The death of the prophet Daniel. At Rome, the feast of Saint Praxedis the virgin. In the city of Marseille, the feast of Saint Victor the martyr. Three soldiers, Alexander, Felicianus, and Longinus, suffered martyrdom with him. At Troyes, the passion of Saint Julia the virgin.

On the same day, King Robert of France died.

XI Kalends of August. The feast of Saint Mary Magdalene, from whom, as the Gospel relates, the Lord cast out seven demons. At Ancyra in Galatia, the feast of Saint Plato the martyr. At the monastery of Fontenelle, the deposition of Saint Wandregisel, confessor and abbot.

X Kalends of August. At Ravenna, the feast of Saint Apollinaris, bishop and martyr. He was ordained at Rome by blessed Peter the apostle, sent to Ravenna, and suffered martyrdom there.

[Col. 1235C] IX Kalends of August. At Emerita, a city of Spain, the feast of Saint Victor the martyr with his two brothers. In Italy, in the city of Tyro, which is near Lake Bolsena, the feast of Saint Christina the virgin and martyr. On the same day, the feast of Saints Nicetas and Aquila, who earned the palm of martyrdom by decapitation.

VIII Kalends of August. The feast of blessed James the apostle, brother of John the Evangelist, whom Herod beheaded. In the city of Samos in Lycia, the feast of Saint Christopher the martyr. In the city of Barcelona, the passion of Saint Cucuphas. At Rome, Nemesius the deacon and martyr.

VII Kalends of August. The feast of blessed Herastus, who was ordained at Philippi by blessed Paul the apostle and, having been crowned by martyrdom there, entered into rest. At Rome, in Porto, the feast of Saint Hyacinthus the martyr. Likewise at Rome, on the Latin Way, the holy [Col. 1235D] martyrs Symphronius, Olympius, Theodulus, and Exuperia.

VI Kalends of August. At Nicomedia, the feast of Saint Hermolaus, priest and martyr, whose teaching converted blessed Pantaleon to the faith. Elsewhere, the feast of twelve saints, whose acts are preserved. In Sicily, blessed Simeon the monk. At Auxerre, blessed Hitherius, bishop and confessor.

V Kalends of August. At Nicomedia, the passion of Saint Pantaleon. In Lesser Britain, at Dol, Saint Samson, bishop and confessor. At Milan, the passion of the holy martyrs Nazarius and Celsus, whose passions were recorded on the second day before the Ides of June, when their sacred bodies were discovered.

The lord Gerannus, bishop, died. On the same day, Hacardus, [Col. 1236A] abbot of Saint Germanus, was taken from this life.

IV Kalends of August. At Rome, on the Aurelian Way, the translation of the body of blessed Felix, bishop and martyr, who was crowned through martyrdom on the fourth day before the Ides of November. On the same day, the holy martyrs Simplicius and Faustinus and Saint Beatrice, their sister and martyr. At Troyes, the deposition of Saint Lupus, bishop and confessor. Likewise at Rome, the feast of blessed Seraphia, virgin and martyr, whose more solemn day is observed on the third day before the Nones of September.

Ragenaldus, [lacuna] of this church, was killed in battle at Sens on the same day. On the same day, Philip, king of the Franks, died.

III Kalends of August. At Rome, the holy martyrs Abdon and Sennen, martyred on the fifth day before the Kalends of August and buried on the third day before the Kalends of that same month. In Africa, in the city of Lucernaria, the feast of the holy virgins and martyrs Maxima, Donatilla, and Secunda. At Auxerre, the deposition of Saint Ursus, bishop and confessor.

The day before the Kalends of August. At Ravenna in Italy, the passing of Saint Germanus, bishop of Auxerre. At Caesarea, Saint Fabius the martyr.

On the same day, Louis, king of France, died.

## AUGUST

Kalends of August. At Rome, Saint Peter in Chains. At Antioch, the passion of the seven holy Maccabee brothers with their mother, who suffered under King Antiochus. In Italy, in the city of Vercelli, the feast of Saint Eusebius, bishop and martyr. In the city of Philadelphia, seven holy [Col. 1236C] martyrs crowned on one day. In the city of Girona, the feast of Saint Felix, the pre-eminent martyr. At Rome, the holy virgins and martyrs Hope, Faith, and Charity, and their mother Sophia.

IV Nones of August. At Rome, in the cemetery of Callistus on the Appian Way, the feast of Saint Stephen, pope and martyr. In the province of Bithynia, in the city of Nicaea, the feast of Saint Theodota, martyred with her three sons. In Italy, in the city of Verona, the feast of Saint Felix. Elsewhere, the feast of Saint Nicetas.

III Nones of August. At Jerusalem, the discovery of the body of blessed Stephen, Christ’s first martyr, and of Saints Gamaliel, Nicodemus, and Abibon. At Rome, on the Appian Way, the feast of Saint Tarsicius the martyr. At Autun, the deposition of Eufronius, bishop and confessor.

[Col. 1236D] The day before the Nones of August. At Rome, at Saint Lawrence’s, the feast of Saint Justin the presbyter. On the same day, blessed Aristarchus, disciple of Saint Paul the apostle, who was bishop of the Thessalonians. At Rome, in the Arenarian crypt, blessed Tertullian the martyr.

King Henry of the Franks died. On the same day, Geoffrey, count of Chalon, a casatus of this church, became a monk and died at his castle of Donzy.

Nones of August. At Autun, the feast of Saint Cassianus, bishop. At Châlons, the feast of Saint Memmius, bishop. On the same day, the feast of Saint Oswald, king of the English and martyr.

On the same day, Hugh, provost of Saint Stephen, was committed to burial [Col. 1237A] on the Jerusalem road. On the same day, Rainaldus, son of Count William, was killed.

VIII Ides of August. The Transfiguration of the Lord on the mountain. At Rome, the feast of Saint Sixtus, bishop and martyr, with whom suffered the deacons Felicissimus and Agapitus and four others: Januarius, Magnus, Vincentius, and Stephen the subdeacon, together with blessed Quartus, as Saint Cyprian writes. Likewise at Rome, Saint Hormisdas the pope.

Bishop Maurinus died. He gave for the support of the brothers a small estate of his own property called Villare, not far from Varziacum.

VII Ides of August. In Tuscany, in the city of Arezzo, the feast of Saint Donatus, bishop and martyr. At Milan, [Col. 1237B] Saint Faustinus. At Rome, the passion of twenty-eight saints. In Crete, in the city of Augusta, the passion of Saint Afra.

Ermenfredus, provost, died. He gave the brothers his estate above the river Balea, and [properties] at Capiliacum, in the district of Sens, and at Basau, to have his commemoration celebrated.

VI Ides of August. At Rome, Saint Cyriacus and his companions. He suffered on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of April; afterward blessed Marcellus, bishop, together with the most blessed Lucina, transferred his sacred body to his estate and, with his own hand, buried it with spices together with the bodies of twenty-two of his companions on the eighth day of August, when he also established his solemn feast. At Vienne, Saint Severus the presbyter.

On the same day Heriveus, bishop of Nevers [Col. 1237C] and a canon of this church, died. Ato the soldier also died; for the sake of his soul, his brother Humbaud left to the canons of Saint Stephen the land at Loniacum that he held.

V Ides of August. At Rome, Saint Romanus the soldier, who, moved by the confession of Saint Lawrence, was baptized and martyred. On the same day, the vigil of Saint Lawrence, archdeacon and martyr.

Salomon, canon and dean of Saint Stephen, died.

IV Ides of August. At Rome, the feast of Saint Lawrence, deacon and martyr. Likewise at Rome, [the feast of] one hundred sixty-five soldiers.

III Ides of August. At Rome, on the Lavican Way between the two laurel trees, the feast of Saint Tiburtius the martyr. Likewise at Rome, [Col. 1237D] the feast of Saint Susanna, virgin and martyr. At Cambrai, the feast of Saint Gaugericus, bishop and confessor. In the city of Évreux, the feast of Saint Taurinus, bishop.

Hugh, the venerable bishop of this church, died. The holiness of his life and the integrity of his conduct adorned him, and the manner in which he lived piously and religiously was sufficiently confirmed by the end of his life. For the love of God and so that his memory might be recalled each year, he gave the church of Auzay to this church for the brothers’ refectory on the day of his anniversary. He also gave it other churches, namely the churches of Bacerna and Saint Briccius, and those of Induniacum and Veniosa, together with the tithes of Visiacum. Moreover, he himself enriched that church with many pallium capes, two carpets, many priestly vestments, [Col. 1238A] and other ornaments.

The day before the Ides of August. In Sicily, in the city of Catania, the feast of Saint Euplus, deacon and martyr. On the same day, the feast of Saint Hilaria the martyr, mother of Saint Afra, with whom suffered Digna, Eumenia, and Euprepia. In the city of Filare, the passion of Saint Gratilianus and Felicissima the virgin.

The venerable master Gislebertus, of blessed memory, died. He was an eminent glossator of the Old and New Testaments, deservedly called “the Universal”; he was a canon of this church and afterward became bishop of London. Besides the other ornaments that he had sent from England to our church, he contributed eighty-two pounds to it. The brothers then purchased properties from this sum and devoutly established that his anniversary should be celebrated each year.

[Col. 1238B] Ides of August. At Rome, on the Tiburtine Way, the feast of Saint Hippolytus the martyr. His nurse Concordia also suffered, and nineteen others from his household. At Forosilla, the feast of Saint Cassianus the martyr. At Poitiers, the deposition of Queen Saint Radegund.

Norgaudus, a soldier of Saint Stephen, died.

XIX Kalends of September. The vigil of the Assumption of Saint Mary. On the Appian Way, in the cemetery of Callistus, the deposition of Saint Eusebius, priest and confessor. At Aquileia, the passion of the holy brothers Felix and Fortunatus. In Africa, Demetrius with ten others.

XVIII Kalends of September. The Assumption of the most holy and glorious Mary, Mother of God. On the same day, the feast of Saint Tarsicius, acolyte and martyr. Elsewhere, Saint Eusebius the martyr.

[Col. 1238C] XVII Kalends of September. At Nicaea in Bithynia, the feast of Saint Ursatius the confessor. At Rome, the feast of Saint Serena, wife of Diocletian Augustus. At Auxerre, the translation of the bishops Augurius and Desiderius. In Persia, the feast of Saint Thyrsus the martyr. At Nevers, the feast of Saint Arigius, bishop and confessor.

On the same day Odo, master of Saint Stephen, ended his present life.

XVI Kalends of September. At Caesarea in Cappadocia, the feast of Saint Mammes the martyr. In Africa, the holy martyrs Liberatus the abbot, Boniface the deacon, Servus and Rusticus the subdeacons, Rogatus and Septimus the monks, and Maximus the boy. At Rome, the octave of Saint Lawrence.

XV Kalends of September. In the city of Praeneste, [Col. 1238D] the feast of Saint Agapitus the martyr. At Rome, the holy presbyters John and Crispus. At Carthage, the passion of the holy martyrs of Massa Candida: nearly three hundred men who were plunged into a fiercely burning lime-kiln for the faith of Christ. From this, that blessed company earned the name Massa Candida: “Massa” because of their number, “Candida” because of their merit. Their commemoration is observed on the ninth day before the Kalends of September. Nevertheless, it should be known that they suffered on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of that month.

Gualterius, the viscount, died.

XIV Kalends of September. The feast of Saint Magnus, or Saint Andrew, martyrs, with their companions, two thousand five hundred ninety-seven. On the mountain called Jura, Saint Donatus, priest [Col. 1239A] and confessor. At Rome, blessed Julius, senator and martyr. In the territory of Bourges, the feast of Saint Marianus the confessor, whose acts are preserved.

On the same day Ebrardus, a soldier of Saint Stephen, died.

XIII Kalends of September. The prophet Samuel. On the same day, blessed Porphyrius, the man of God. On the island of Herio, at the place called Deas, the feast of Saint Philibert, abbot.

XII Kalends of September. In the territory and city of Gévaudan, at the village of Mende, the feast of Saint Privatus, bishop and martyr. On the same day, the feast of the holy martyrs Bonosius and Maximianus, whose acts are preserved.

Adelelmus, a noble and humble soldier, died. On the same day, William, count of Nevers, died most holily while leading a religious life at Carturia.

[Col. 1239B] XI Kalends of September. At Rome, the feast of Saint Timothy the martyr, who came from Antioch to Rome and by his preaching converted many to Christ. For this he was martyred and buried beside the blessed Apostle, who had had a disciple of the same name. At Autun, the feast of Saint Symphorianus the martyr. Likewise at Rome, blessed Antonius the martyr, and the holy pilgrim martyrs Martial, Epiterius, and Saturninus with their companions.

Stephen, provost and canon of this church, died.

X Kalends of September. At Antioch, the feast of the holy martyrs Donatus, Restitutus, Valerianus, and Fructuosa with twelve others. At Alexandria, blessed Theonas, a man of God. Elsewhere, Saint Zacchaeus, bishop, and the holy martyrs Minerius, [Col. 1239C] Eleazar, and his nine sons. On the same day, the feast of Saints Timothy and Apollinaris, who, having completed their martyrdom near the city of Reims, earned the heavenly kingdom. In the city of Aegea in Lycia, Saints Claudius, Asterius, and Neon, who, after bitter tortures, were fastened to a cross. At Autun, the deposition of Saint Flavianus, bishop.

On the same day Eribertus, bishop of Auxerre, entered upon the way of all flesh.

IX Kalends of September. In India, the feast of the apostle Saint Bartholomew. At Carthage, the commemoration of the saints of Massa Candida, whose solemnity was noted above on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of September. At Rome, the feast of Saint Genesius the martyr. In the city of Rouen, the feast of Saint Audoenus, bishop and confessor. In the territory of Nevers, [Col. 1239D] the feast of the holy confessors Patrick, abbot, and Gildard, priest.

Count Hugh died.

VIII Kalends of September. At Rome, the feast of the holy martyrs Eusebius, Pontianus, Peregrinus, and Vincentius. At Arles, the feast of Saint Genesius the martyr, baptized in his own blood. In the city of Complutum, the passion of the holy brothers Justus and Pastor, who, while still boys being taught their letters, threw down their school tablets and ran of their own accord to martyrdom. Likewise at Rome, on the Nomentan Way, eighteen soldiers.

VII Kalends of September. At Rome, the holy martyrs Herena and Abundius. Likewise at Rome, the feast of Saint Zephyrinus the pope. At the fortress of Victimilium in Italy, the feast of Saint Secundus [Col. 1240A] the martyr. In the city of Bergamo, the feast of Saint Alexander the martyr. At Salona, the passion of Saint Anastasius, whose festive commemoration was noted above on the twelfth day before the Kalends of September. At Auxerre, the deposition of Saint Eleutherius, bishop.

VI Kalends of September. At Capua, Saint Rufus the martyr. At Arles, Saint Caesarius, bishop and confessor. At Autun, the deposition of Saint Siagrius, bishop and confessor. At Tomis, the feast of the holy martyrs Marcellinus the tribune, his wife Mannea, his son John, Serapion the cleric, and Peter the soldier. On the same day, the passion of the holy Georgius the deacon, Aurelius, Felix, Natalia, and Liliosa. In the city of Bourges, the translation of the body of Saint Sulpitius, bishop and confessor.

[Col. 1240B] V Kalends of September. At Rome, the passion of Saint Hermes the martyr. At Constantinople, the feast of Saint Alexander, glorious aged bishop, by whose prayer Arius, through divine judgment, burst apart in the middle, his entrails spilling out. In the city of Hippo, the feast of Saint Augustine, bishop and confessor, who, touched by the divine Spirit, wrote one thousand thirty books, treatises, and letters, not counting those that cannot be numbered. At Saintes, the feast of Saint Bibianus, bishop and confessor. On the same day, in the village of Brioude, the feast of Saint Julian the martyr.

Gimo, a soldier of Saint Stephen, died.

IV Kalends of September. At Rome, at the Arch of Faustinus, the most blessed Sabina the martyr, who was the wife of the once-famous Valentinus and daughter of Herod the Metalworker; she suffered under the emperor Hadrian, under the prefect [Col. 1240C] Helpidius. Likewise at Rome, the passion of Saint Seraphia the virgin. In the province of Palestine, in the city …, the beheading of Saint John the Baptist.

On that same day, the ordination of the lord Herefridus, who gave the brothers, for the preparation of that day’s meal, the villa of Artaldus, one mansus at Lindriacum, another mansus at Capiliacum, and a mill below the wall. At the Nativity of Saint Mary, when he first sat in the episcopal chair, he gave the brothers the church of Bacerna and Lindriacum, and Lupinum, as well as Logniacum. He gave Gimiliacum on the feast of Saint Clement. Bishop Archemboldus died.

III Kalends of September. At Rome, on the Ostian Way, one mile from the city, the most blessed martyrs Felix and Adauctus, both priests. Likewise at Rome, Gaudentia [Col. 1240D] the virgin.

Ermembertus, a priest, died; he had been killed innocently by the sword.

The day before the Kalends of September. At Trier, the feast of Saint Paulinus, bishop and confessor. At Athens, blessed Aristides, renowned for faith and wisdom. At Auxerre, the deposition of Saint Optatus, bishop and confessor. At Ancyra in Galatia, Saints Gaianus and Julianus.

## SEPTEMBER

Kalends of September. Joshua son of Nun and Gideon, prophets, and the most blessed Anna the prophetess, who is mentioned in the Gospel. At Capua, the feast of Saint Priscus the martyr. At Sens, the deposition of blessed Lupus, bishop and confessor. At Le Mans, the feast of Saint Victor, bishop and [Col. 1241A] confessor. On the same day, the passing of Saint Giles, abbot and confessor.

Count Richard died.

V Nones of September. At Lyon, the feast of Saint Justus, bishop and confessor, who departed to the Lord in the wilderness on the day before the Ides of October; his sacred body and that of blessed Viator, his servant, were brought back to Lyon and buried with due honor on the fourth day before the Nones of September. On the same day, in the aforesaid city, the deposition of blessed Helpidius, bishop. At Apamia, blessed Antoninus the martyr.

III Nones of September. The feast of Saint Phoebe, concerning whom the Apostle writes to the Romans: “I commend to you Phoebe,” and so forth. At Rome, the commemoration of blessed Seraphia, virgin and martyr, who suffered on the fourth day before the Kalends [Col. 1241B] of August and was buried on the day before the Kalends of August; but her more solemn feast is observed on the fourth day before the Nones of September, when the place of prayer was dedicated and her tomb adorned. At Capua, the feast of the holy martyrs Antoninus the boy and Aristaeus the bishop.

The day before the Nones of September. Moses the lawgiver. In the city of Chalon, the feast of Saint Marcellus the martyr. Elsewhere, the feast of the holy martyrs Rufinus, Silvanus, and Vitalica. At Rome, in the cemetery of Maximus on the Salarian Way, the feast of Saint Boniface, bishop.

Nones of September. In the suburb of Rome, blessed Victorinus the martyr. At Rome, in Porto, the feast of Saint Herculianus the martyr. On the same day, the feast of Saint Bertinus, abbot.

Lambertus, levite and outstanding teacher, died. On the same day, Elizabeth, consecrated to God, died.

[Col. 1241C] VIII Ides of September. The death of the prophet Zechariah, and the feast of Saint Onesiphorus, concerning whom the Apostle writes to Timothy: “May the Lord grant mercy to the household of Onesiphorus,” and what follows. In Africa, the most blessed bishops Donatianus, Praesidius, Mansuetus, Germanus, and Fuscus.

VII Ides of September. In Gaul, in the territory called that of the Aedui, at the place of Alesia, once a very strong city but destroyed by Julius Caesar, the feast or passion of the most holy Regina the virgin. At Nicomedia, the feast of blessed John, a man of God. At Orléans, the deposition of blessed Evurtius, bishop. At Paris, in the village of Noisy, Saint Clodoaldus, priest and confessor.

VI Ides of September. The Nativity of holy Mary, Mother of God and ever-virgin, whom the Holy Spirit [Col. 1241D] guarded and sanctified as the chosen one, so that from her womb the most high God-Man might be born. At Rome, the festival of the burial of Saint Adrian, who suffered at Nicomedia with twenty-three others on the fourth day before the Nones of March.

Eribaldus, levite and chief treasurer, died; he was unexpectedly killed by his enemies with the sword. On the same day, Dodo the priest was killed in battle. On that day Ingelbaldus, priest and dean of Saint Stephen, died.
