Almighty Lord God, great and wondrous Lord, who have granted us entry into the Holy of Holies through the incarnation of your Only-Begotten Son, our Lord, we who beseech you ask for your kindness, because we are in fear and trembling and desire to stand before your holy and glorious altar. Send upon us the gift of the grace of the Holy Spirit, and renew our souls and bodies, so that with a pure heart we may offer you a sacrifice, a fruitful gift, for the remission of our sins and those of your people, through the glory and humanity of Jesus Christ your Son, who with you, etc.

Standing before the altar with the procession, he should pronounce this confession and grant indulgence to the ministers:

May he himself, who knows all hidden things, through our Lord Jesus Christ, his Son, together with the Holy Spirit, deign graciously and reverently to receive the contrition of your spirit, the groaning of your heart, and the confession of your mouth; he who forgave all sins to the weeping sinful woman and opened the gates of Paradise to the thief upon a single confession—may he absolve you, as participants in his redemption, from every bond of sins, and restore to the body of the holy Church, by the healing medicine of his mercy, those members that have been weakened in some degree, returning them through grace, and preserve them perpetually strengthened. He lives and reigns.

After granting the indulgence, he should add these prayers. Let us pray.

Almighty and everlasting God, we humbly beseech you not to permit us to perish, because we are your creature, but grant us a span of life in which to live, so that before the day of our departure we may be worthy, through true repentance, right faith, and pure confession, to please you, almighty Lord, in this present life. Through, etc.

Another.

Grant, we beseech you, almighty and merciful God, that the confession of our guilt may be able to receive pardon for our offenses. Through, etc.

Another.

We beseech you, Lord, forgive the offenses of your servants; and although we are unable to please you by our deeds, may we be saved through the intercession of the Mother of your Son, the Lord our God, and of these and all your saints. Through the same, etc.

Then, in the same place, he should offer the kiss of peace to the presbyters leading him and to the deacons; and after receiving peace from the bishop, each of them should ascend to the side of the altar and kiss it. The presbyters should then return to lead the bishop to the altar, and as he ascends he should say this prayer:

The Lord be with you.

And with your spirit.

Let us pray.

Take away from us, we beseech you, Lord, our iniquities, so that we may be worthy to enter the Holy of Holies with pure minds.

And when he has reached the altar, he should himself impose the antiphon:

“I shall go in to the altar of God, to God who gives joy to my youth,” with the psalm, “Judge me, God, and discern my cause from the nation.”

[Col. 1311A] When this is finished, he should add these prayers:

“I made my sin known to you, and I did not hide my injustices; I acknowledge my iniquities, and my sins are always against me. Turn your face away from my sins, and blot out all my iniquities.

“Restore to me the joy of your salvation, and strengthen me with a governing spirit. Make me hear your mercy in the morning, for I have hoped in you.

“Make known to me the way in which I should walk, for I have lifted up my soul to you.

“Deliver me from my enemies, Lord; I have fled to you. Teach me to do your will, for you are my God.

“Your good Spirit will lead me into a right land; [Col. 1311B] for your name’s sake, Lord, you will revive me in your righteousness.

“You will lead my soul out of tribulation, and in your mercy you will destroy my enemies.

“And you will destroy all who trouble my soul, for I am your servant.

“Go forth, Lord, for the salvation of your people, for salvation with your Anointed.”

Then he greets the Gospel, saying:

May the peace of Christ, which he handed down to us through his Gospel, confirm and preserve our hearts and bodies unto eternal life. Amen.

Then he should kiss the altar, saying this prayer:

Almighty and everlasting God, who have willed me, a sinner, to stand at the sacred altars and to praise the power of your holy name, grant, I ask, through the mystery of this Sacrament, pardon for my sins, so that I may be worthy to minister worthily to your majesty and to love you with everlasting charity. Through, etc.

After this, he should say this confession privately:

Receive my confession, Lord my God Jesus Christ, sole hope of my salvation, for I have been ruined by gluttony, drunkenness, fornication, lust, sadness, sloth, sleepiness, negligence, anger, desire, envy, malice, hatred, detraction, perjury, falsehood, lying, vainglory, frivolity, and pride; and I have been utterly destroyed by thought, word, deed, and every evil. You who justify the ungodly and give life to the dead, justify me and raise me again, Lord my God. You who live, etc.

[Col. 1311D] Another.

I confess my sins to you, eternal Pontiff, minister of the saints, and priest of the true tabernacle, who once a year entered the holy mysteries and offered the holy, immaculate Lamb of your own body as a sacrifice for my sins. I confess to you that I am your debtor—not merely that I owe you an accounting for ten thousand talents of my sins, but that I must render an account of my entire life—because I know that throughout my whole life I have perfectly kept none of your commandments. I confess that I have sinned in speech, sight, hearing, gesture, step, deed, thought, suggestion, and consent.

But now, Lord, in confession I go before your face, and in the presence of the angels and [Col. 1312A] all the saints I confess my sins to you. I ask pardon for my offenses, and I beseech you that in this acceptable time you hear me, and in these days of salvation help me, so that in the present life I may be able perfectly to recognize my sins, confess them to the eternal Judge, and thereby merit pardon for all my offenses, so that you may bring me securely to your dreadful judgment, free from every accusation of the enemy. Through, etc.

Another.

I, a wretched sinner, who consider and know myself to be the most criminal of all Christians, confess to the Lord and to all his saints that from the beginning of my life until the present day I have continually been occupied with countless crimes and wickedness, without any regard for divine fear: especially excessive and varied fornications, perpetrated through persistent drunkenness; every kind of negligence; perjuries; lies; envy; pride; malice; gluttony; greed; robbery; theft; vainglory; arrogance; disobedience; stubbornness; hardness of mind; contradiction; grumbling; indignation; detraction; anger; hatred; cursing; whispering; sadness; empty joy; speaking; keeping silent; rebuking immoderately; forgiving rashly; empty love; laughter; joking; vulgarity; discord; sowing discord; feigned friendship; giving and receiving. I confess that I have been corrupted in all the senses of my body, and I profess that I am weighed down and filled with every plague that contributes to my death; so much so that I cannot even consider myself safe from homicide, because through my negligence many have been killed by hunger whom I could have restored to life to some extent if I had devoted more attentive care to them from what was superfluous.

Although I had always done all these things, I never cleansed them by a sincere confession or diminished them by due penance, but continually added worse things to serious ones. For all these and countless other things, which I shall be unable not only to enumerate but even to recall, I ask pardon from the most merciful Lord, because I do not know where to flee from his wrath except to him.

After the individual confession, the prayers follow.

I beseech your mercy, Lord, that you grant me pardon for my sins and preserve me in the observance of your commandments. Also deign to hear me, unworthy as I am, on behalf of all those whose confessions or alms I have received, or who have entrusted themselves to me in the confidence of charity, so that, whether they live or rest in hope of your peace, they may continually experience the help of your favor.

Save me, Lord, King of eternal glory, who can save; grant me both the will and the ability to do and complete what pleases you and benefits me. Grant help in disturbance, consolation in persecution, and strength in every temptation. Deign to grant pardon for past things, correction of present evils, and protection for what is to come. Amen.

[Col. 1313A] Another.

I beseech you, Lord Jesus, to make all the gates of my city gates of justice, so that, entering through them, I may confess your name, and that, when your majesty visits it more frequently with the heavenly ministers, no stench of a swollen corpse may confront it. Rather, let salvation occupy its walls and praise its gates.

Another.

Almighty God, have mercy on your suppliant, for I am not like the countless servants who are exalted by contempt of the world, glorious by the merit of justice, angelic in the praise of chastity, nor like many of those who, after public crimes, by repentance merited to become devoted to you. Even if I have done anything good through the generosity of your grace, I do not know with what end I do it or by what strictness it is weighed by you.

[Col. 1313B] Another.

I confess, Lord, that I am unworthy of your sacred things, for I am darkened daily by countless sins. Although I presume to ask you with flattering words, I very often offend you by wicked deeds. You pour medicine into me, who am sick, while I continually do things contrary to my health. I read your law written in the sacred pages, but, wretched, I neglect sound discipline. I approach your altar as though devoted, but depart from your commandments with a rebellious heart. I present myself as worthy in the eyes of human beings, but in your sight, which hidden things do not deceive, I am stained and polluted by various crimes.

But it is yours, Lord God, to give the sinner a contrite heart and a fountain of tears, by which I may worthily wash away [Col. 1313C] the multitude of my crimes. If you grant forgiveness of offenses, it is mine to mourn them; it is yours to erase them quickly like a cloud. And although, at the enemy’s persuasion, I have lost the palm of innocence, at least, through confession and your mercy, may I merit pardon, so that glory, praise, and honor may belong to you, who rule all things forever and ever, etc.

Another.

God, be merciful to me, a sinner, because you are immortal and without sin, you alone, Lord my God. Forgive me, your unworthy servant and sinner, because I am a sinner and unworthy to presume to approach the holy altar and invoke you. For I have sinned before you and before your angels. But through their intercession grant me pardon for my offenses, establish me in your holy Church in the faith of the Orthodox, [Col. 1313D] and teach me to do your will all the days of my life.

Another.

Lord Jesus Christ, Redeemer of the world, be merciful to me, a sinner lying in sins in every way. For you alone, Lord, are immortal and without sin. Forgive me, most wretched, as I presume to approach your holy altar and invoke you, because from my infancy until now I have sinned before you, before your angels, and before all your saints. But through their intercession grant me divine clemency and pardon for my sins, and teach me to do your will all the days of my life. Amen.

[Col. 1314A] Another.

God of mercy and truth, I earnestly beseech your kindness to grant me, wretched as I am, pardon for my countless sins by which I provoked the wrath of your power, so that, through your mercy, cleansed in this life according to your will, I may reach participation in eternal blessedness. Extend also the hand of your mercy to all living in the body or outside the body who are joined to me by spiritual or bodily connection, to those who have commended themselves to me either by confessing or by asking, to those whose money or alms I have received, and to those who have been corrupted through my negligence or malice; by your ineffable generosity grant them adopted pardon for their sins and deign to lead them to the rest [Col. 1314B] of the blessed spirits. Through, etc.

Another.

Most merciful Christ, Redeemer of the souls of the faithful, I beseech you to be favorably present and hear my unworthy prayers. Trembling, I stand to offer the sacrifice of your sacred Passion, while I recognize manifold and harmful crimes accusing me. Unworthy, I presume to offer sacrifices owed to your altars before your presence; I lie before the presence of your majesty, polluted in body, mind, and heart.

But, Christ, may you have your antidote amid these things, with which you, good Physician, know how to heal the wounds of souls. I beseech you, gracious Judge, erase the bond of sin written against me, lest the avenger be able to demand his coin from me any longer. For this reason, Lord, with unworthy mouth and mind, I ask your kindness to deign to look upon your household, awaiting the duties of your sacred name, with a serene countenance. Do not let the price of their salvation perish because of me, unworthy as I am; for them you deigned, by pouring out your holy blood, to become redemption. Preserve us always and everywhere by your protection, so that those whom you redeemed on earth with your precious blood you may cause to be numbered with your saints in eternal glory in heaven, you who, with the eternal Father, live and reign as God in the unity of the Holy Spirit forever and ever. Amen.

Meanwhile he should say these prayers until the verses at the Introit, the Kyrie eleison, and then the song of the angels are sung.

“Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace to people of good will. We praise you, we bless you, we adore you, [Col. 1314D] we glorify you. We speak a hymn to you; we give you thanks for your great glory. Lord God, heavenly King, God the almighty Father; Lord Jesus Christ, the only-begotten Son; Lord God, Lamb of God, Son of the Father; you who take away the sins of the world, have mercy on us. You who take away the sins of the world, receive our supplication. You who sit at the right hand of the Father, have mercy on us. For you alone are holy, you alone are Lord, you alone are Most High, Jesus Christ, with the Holy Spirit, in the glory of God the Father. Amen.”

The following prayer should be said by the bishop meanwhile, until the angelic hymn is finished.

Let us pray.

God, who are justly angered and mercifully forgive, who desire not the death of sinners but life, do not repel from your kindness me, a wretched and fragile sinner, filled with the filth of offenses, nor look upon my sins, which I committed by living badly, but upon your immeasurable mercies, by which you customarily assist sinners through a freely given gift. Therefore I beseech you, Lord, to be forgetful of my sins and mindful of your mercies; graciously receive my vows and prayers, and, overlooking the sins of my frailty, open my lips and, appeased, admit me to the confession of your praise.

You who, through the incarnation and humanity of our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, gave peace to human beings and the fellowship of the heavenly angels: grant that I may be filled with the abundance of your peace and rejoice in the unity of the angelic fellowship; [Col. 1315B] and so make me participate in these temporal offices that you may command me to be joined to the perpetual choirs of your elect, there to sing your mercies with them forever. Through, etc.

When the angelic praise has ended, the priest should say the missal prayer. Then the reading should be recited, and between the reading and the Gospel—that is, during the Gradual, Alleluia, and Sequence—the bishop should say these prayers:

Before your eyes, Lord God, I stand as a witness of conscience. I do not dare to ask for what I do not deserve to obtain. You know, Lord, what is done within us. We are ashamed to confess what we are not afraid to commit. We obey you only in words, we lie in our hearts, and what we say we wish, we prove by our actions that we do not wish.

But spare those who trust in you; forgive those who pray; have mercy on those who beseech you. And because my understanding is weak in your sacraments, and before you sinners have no words free from guilt, grant, Lord, that if you do not receive words from us, the unworthy and hard-hearted, you may yourself bestow pardon. You who live, etc.

Another.

Christ, spare me and have mercy on me, not according to my merits but according to your mercy. Do not despise me, a sinner. Do not reject me, but receive me according to your word, and I shall live; do not disappoint me in my expectation. Have mercy on me, Lord, for I have sinned against you. Give me a fountain of tears, fountain of life and light of light. Grant me in this present life true repentance for my sins [Col. 1315D] and perseverance in goodness. Lord, hear my prayer. You who live, etc.

Another.

We beseech your boundless kindness, God: do not condemn us for our iniquity, but direct us on the right path according to your mercy. Do not become angry with us who offend as we deserve, but assist our frailty with unconquerable goodness, and forgive all who go astray according to the greatness of your mercy.

Another.

Warned by the goads of an accusing conscience and by the remembrance of our offenses, we beseech the Lord of pardon that whatever we have done wrong in word, deed, or thought—whether through the impulse of slippery youth [Col. 1316A] or through the error of ignorance—our Lord’s mercy may deign to release and forgive. Thus, with your assent, Lord, may we be able to avoid what is evil and consequently accomplish what is good. And because you made us belong to your sacraments, may you mercifully work their gift within us. Forgive all who go astray according to the greatness of your mercy.

Another.

If we compare before your eyes, Lord, the faults we have committed and the wounds, even the most severe, that we can suffer in this life, what we suffer is less, and what we deserve is greater. We feel the punishment of sin, yet we do not avoid persistence in sinning. Under your scourges our frailty is broken, but our iniquity is not changed. A sick mind is tormented, yet a stubborn neck is not bent. Life sighs in pain, yet it does not amend itself in its conduct.

If we are spared, we are not corrected; if you punish, we do not endure it. In correction we confess what we have done; at the visitation we forget what we wept over. If you press your hand upon us, we promise to do what is required; if you suspend the sword, we do not fulfill our promises. If you strike, we cry out for you to spare us; if you spare us, we provoke you again to strike. If anguish comes, we ask for time for repentance; if mercy comes to our aid, we abuse the patience that spared us. The inflicted wound has scarcely passed, and the ungrateful mind does not even remember what it endured.

If you hear us quickly, we grow insolent because of mercy; if more slowly, we murmur because of impatience. O Lord, we want you to preserve what you have done, but we are not afraid to neglect what you have commanded. You have guilty confessors, Lord; spare us, because you are compassionate.

We vow that, unless you forgive, you may rightly punish us. But with you there is abundant mercy and exceedingly plentiful propitiation. Grant without merit what we ask, you who created those who would ask you. And now that we cry out to you, Lord, have mercy. May a faithful and tearful voice move your kindness, and may that mercy in which we place all our hope not reckon what we have offended while it regards what we ask. Although it is a great misery that we are guilty, may your clemency toward us miserable ones be greater.

Raise us up, Lord our God, and lift us by your mercy, so that, through communion in salvation and the joy of charity, while we ourselves desire to be saved by your gift, we may also rejoice in the faith and peace of all nations. Through, etc.

Another.

Before the sight of your immeasurable majesty, holy Trinity and true Unity, almighty and everlasting God, I, a very lowly petitioner, approach—not without due reverence, yet without any dignity of office—and I stand as a witness charged by conscience. I accuse myself and do not excuse myself, but before witnesses, namely, the relics of all your saints and all your saints in heaven and on earth, I confess all my injustices to you, so that through their merits and intercessions you may forgive all the wickedness of my sin. For I have sinned against heaven and before you; I am not worthy to be called your son, wrapped in the filth of sins.

But you, knower of hidden things, have mercy on me, raise me from the death of my soul, illumine my heart with the sevenfold [Col. 1317A] grace of the Holy Spirit, and teach me everywhere to do your will, because you are my God. Amen.

Another.

Have mercy, God, on all who go astray and belong to you, and show mercy to all those for whom we are obliged to pray, whether living or dead, whose alms and confessions we have received and whose names we have written down for commemoration. Mercifully forgive them all and grant them eternal life; also forgive those who persecute and slander us, according to the greatness of your mercy. Amen.

Another.

Come to my aid, my God, before I die, before torments seize me, before darkness envelops me. For I am held by fear of your judgment and dread your wrath. If even the just person will scarcely be saved, where shall I, the ungodly, be? What shall I do when the day of dreadful judgment comes? When the Judge’s examination arrives, what shall I answer? What indeed shall I say when I am presented before the tribunal of Christ? It would have been better not to have been born into the world than to endure eternal punishments in torment.

For I have often sinned in word, deed, and thought, and I have sinned cruelly. No sin is found whose filth has not stained me, wretched as I am; there is no disease of vices from which I have not contracted contagion. I have always repeated my offenses. By my depraved habits I have turned very many people toward iniquity; many have been overthrown by the examples of my life.

I beseech all the choirs of holy patriarchs, prophets, apostles, martyrs, and all the saints to pray for me, so that God may have mercy on me and erase my sins, take away my iniquity, and receive me into everlasting joy. You, merciful, kindly, and compassionate Lord, abandon no one, reject no one, and exclude no one from your mercy.

Turn my soul toward the rest of Paradise. You sought the wandering sheep and, when you found it, carried it back to the flock on your shoulders. I ask you to draw this most worthless soul to yourself with your hands and offer it to your blessed and immortal Father before the cherubim and seraphim and before the holy angels, so that, enjoying the delights of Paradise, I may be able to say with them:

“Glory to the immortal Father, glory to the immortal Son, glory to the immortal Holy Spirit, forever and ever.” Amen.

Another.

Lord Jesus Christ, who redeemed me with your blood, hear me, a sinner who sins daily and lies in excessive sins. Against you alone I have sinned; I have confessed you, Christ. I have sinned before you and before all your saints, in words and deeds and in all the thoughts I have been able to devise.

Wretched am I, a human being: my sins are countless. Have mercy on me, God, almighty God. Before you and your saints I ask pardon for all my past, present, and future sins. God, be merciful to me, a sinner, and grant me permission in this life to practice repentance, by which I may erase all my sins, for I do not know where to flee except to you, Christ, because you are the life of the living and the resurrection of the dead.

Pray for me, wretched as I am, all holy apostles, martyrs, confessors, holy virgins and widows, and all the saints and elect of God. Pray for me, so that almighty God may illumine his face upon me, wretched as I am, and have mercy on me. He who lives and reigns, etc.

Another.

Lord Jesus Christ, lover of integrity, fortify my heart against all the arrows and snares of the enemy, extinguish in me every blaze of lust, and turn my breast toward true humility and the tranquility of patience. Set it ablaze with the goads of charity, so that, hating every way of iniquity, I may please you all the days of my life. You who live, etc.

Another.

I pray for your kindness, Lord, that you grant your servant remission of all sins and bestow the gift of your mercy upon all, living or dead, for whom I am obliged to pray, so that under your governance they may reach eternal life and everywhere receive the gifts of your grace. Through, etc.

Another.

As our deeds cast us into condemnation, Lord, give water to our head and pour a fountain of tears into our eyes, so that, washing away the stains of sin, we may overcome the avenging flames of punishment with the abundance of our weeping. Since what we have done is not hidden from you, Lord, grant that within us there may be not only confession of the mouth but also confession of the heart, not an excuse for crimes but lamentation for sins.

For the sight of lust has violated the chaste eyes of our heart; our conduct is corrupt, discipline violated, pretense in our face, deceit in our words, treachery in our heart, fickleness on our tongue, foolish action, a doubtful mind, carnal desire, earthly anxiety, forgetfulness of the soul, negligence of holiness. Above all this, fear of death has increased.

Have mercy on us, Lord, have mercy on us, and grant pardon for past evils, correction for present ones, and caution for the future. You who live, etc.

Another.

The duty of ministering impels me, a sinner, to offer the saving sacrifice for the people’s offense. But conscience terrifies me because of the guilt of an unworthy priesthood: if the sacrifice is offered by me—the offscouring (peripsema) of all priests—the crime of a polluted conscience is increased. If it is not offered to such great majesty and to the Judge of all flesh, the guilt of negligence is charged against me.

Amid these things, almighty God, I implore the balance of your mercy. I dread the day of your vengeance, which an accusing conscience makes me fear. I ask you not to judge me, unworthy as I am, without mercy, since you do not exclude me from the time of repentance.

Suspend, I beg you, through the intercession of these and all the saints’ merits, the axe until the cultivator of the vineyard brings a basket of manure to the root of the unfruitful tree. Spare me, O most merciful Lord, a penitent, [Col. 1319A] who mercifully recalled David to forgiveness after his fall; O Merciful One, who regarded the tears of Peter as he wept bitterly; who enlightened the thief, guilty of so great a crime on the gallows of the cross, with divine grace. To him confession immediately obtained the Son of God’s favor, faith its reward, punishment forgiveness, and lamentation everlasting joys: while the confessor remained on the cross, he became the possessor of Paradise because of the cross. But since your words of forgiveness require your mercy, and the works of an unworthy priest do not commend them, at least receive the prayers of those standing here, so that through their prayers you may grant forgiveness to me, and through their merits may the sacrifices confer upon us the healing of our wounds. Since, however, O Almighty, you became the saving sacrifice for the sins of all, be present to us as justification for our offenses, Jesus Christ, Savior of the world. You who, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, [Col. 1319B] live and reign, etc.

### Prayer for oneself

Save me, O Lord, King of eternal glory, who are able to save; and grant me the ability both to do and to complete what pleases you and is beneficial to me. O holy Lord, almighty Father and God, grant me help in tribulation, consolation in persecution, and strength at every time of temptation.

O holy, most devout Lord and Father, grant me forgiveness for past offenses, correction in the present, and protection for the future, because I cannot abandon evil or do good unless your great mercy comes to my aid. Grant that I may deserve to know, fear, and love you with my whole heart, Lord Jesus Christ, Redeemer of all, who are the refuge of the poor and [Col. 1319C] the consoler of the afflicted. Through your great mercy, be my consolation in all my distress and tribulations, because I have hope in no one but you; for you are my refuge and strength in my tribulations, which have found me exceedingly. Therefore I cry out to you with my whole heart, that you may deign to hear me, and that by your merciful kindness I may deserve to obtain all these things for which I, unworthy as I am, pray. And whatever it is that my unhappiness does not know how, or does not dare, to ask of you, grant that thing in accordance with your mercy and majesty, because you are the consolation and protection of my life at all times, etc.

### Prayer in any tribulation

O God, who do not despise the groaning of the contrite or spurn the devotion of the deserving, attend to our prayers, [Col. 1319D] which in our tribulation we presume to pour out while imploring your mercy. Mercifully deign to receive them, and grant that whatever diabolical and human adversities contrive against us you may reduce to nothing and crush by the counsel of your mercy, so that, unharmed by any adversities but delivered from every tribulation and distress, we may joyfully give thanks to you in your holy Church through Christ. Through him, O most high God, we ask you to heed these prayers and, with propitious favor, look upon this prayer of ours, which we offer to you for deliverance and release from the pressure of our weakness.

Now, Lord, look upon us with a gracious countenance and, in your singular mercy, remove from us what the savagery of evils promises, [Col. 1320A] what the perversity of enemies inflicts, what the opposition of the wicked binds through their counsels, what threatens from judgment, what hangs upon a sentence, what conspiracy contrives, what accusation shatters, what our own iniquities deserve, what binds us through the fabrications of others, what casts us down through pressures, what weighs upon us through torments, and what constrains us through distresses. We ask, Lord, that you not exercise your justice upon our injustices, but rather manifest your mercy in our iniquities. Do not cast us down in persecution; do not destroy us through intolerance. Discipline us through tribulation, raise us up through mercy, and guide us through compassion, so that, protected by you from the arrows of our enemies and freed from our present tribulation, we may praise you, the living Lord in the Trinity, with harmonious voice. [Col. 1320B] You who live and reign with your only-begotten Son and the holy Spirit, the Paraclete, through infinite ages of ages. Amen.

### Prayer of the shepherd, to be said for himself and for those entrusted to him

Forgive, O almighty Lord God, whatever through the intemperance of a biting tongue the heedless rebuke of our mouth has wounded those entrusted to us; spare whatever we have said short of the perfection of goodness; forgive whatever we have expressed incongruously or with insufficient moderation. Let heedless presumption not punish me, but let the compassionate mercy of your pity absolve me as I acknowledge my iniquities. And because I have no confidence elsewhere except in your mercy, arm both my mouth with the proclamation of truth and sanctify my work with fuller abundance, so that you may save one who is unworthy and sanctify, in your mercy, the flock entrusted to me. [Col. 1320C]

Heal whatever in them has been corrupted, and cure whatever in me you see to be defective. If, through the fault of my lukewarmness or negligence, they have contracted any offenses, mercifully forgive them. If, whether unknowingly or knowingly, they have fallen into crime, and if they have plunged into ruin because of the stumbling block of my example, rescue them from it by the hand of your mercy, and do not repay wretched me with the vengeance due for such faults. Yet for those toward whom I seemed to apply the judgment of rebuke, may the rebuke contribute to salvation. And may this interceding prayer call those entrusted to me back from error, so that they may not suffer the infernal torments, for which we, being mortal, have imposed the laws of penance. Thus, sparing the disadvantages of both parties, grant forgiveness to their iniquities and wash away my offense, contracted through the burdens of governing. [Col. 1320D]

Give ear, O God, to our sacrifices, and inscribe me and those entrusted to me in your books, so that, together with the flock committed to my care, I may be cleansed from every crime and deserve to come to you in peace. Make peaceful, O God, the dwelling place of our hearts by expelling carnal vices. And because I strive to exercise the highest virtues among those entrusted to me, may I, with the afflictions of minds and bodies brought to peace, deserve to be crowned peacefully with the angels when you judge.

Therefore, we ask you, merciful God, make us, as we gaze upon you, burn in your presence through the gift of your grace, so that zeal for your house may consume us. And so temper us, as we govern those entrusted to us through the vigor of the Holy Spirit, that they may gain benefit from the discipline of our governance, that their hardness may be broken, and that their life may be sanctified. [Col. 1321A]

Receive, Lord, the offerings of our vows, and through them grant that whatever correction we bestow upon those entrusted to us, whether by word or by merit, may not lead to our discord, but may, to our joy, have advanced both them and us toward the joy of everlasting sweetness. Wash us, almighty God, from both another’s offense and our own, so that in both we may receive the effectiveness of spiritual grace and pray to your name with greater confidence. Through, etc.

### When incense is put into the thurible before the Gospel, the priest says

May the Lord kindle and fill our hearts with the fragrance of your heavenly inspiration, so that we may hear and fulfill the precepts of his Gospel. You who live, etc.

### Blessing of the same

In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, may this incense be blessed [Col. 1321B] and become acceptable as a fragrant odor.

Then, as the deacon bows, he gives him God’s blessing, saying:

May the blessing of God the almighty Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, descend upon you; and may Christ the Lord open your mouth to proclaim his holy Gospel worthily and fittingly. May the Lord God be in your heart and on your lips, so that you may properly announce the Gospel of peace.

The deacon, taking up or kissing the Gospel, says:

Give me, Lord, a right and well-sounding word in my mouth, so that my words may please you and all who hear them, for the sake of your holy name, unto eternal life. Amen.

[Col. 1321C] After the Gospel has been read, the deacon says:

Through these words of your holy Gospel, Lord, forgive me all my sins.

And all the others say:

Peace be with you.

Then, when the incense and the Gospel are brought forward for veneration, each says:

Through these holy words of the Gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ, may the Lord forgive us all our sins.

When the incense is offered, each says:

Let my prayer be directed like incense in your presence, O Lord.

Then the priest begins the Creed, that is:

I believe in one God, the almighty Father, maker [Col. 1321D] of heaven and earth, of all things visible and invisible. And in one Lord Jesus Christ, the only-begotten Son of God, born from the Father before all ages: God from God, light from light, true God from true God; begotten, not made, consubstantial with the Father, through whom all things were made. For us human beings and for our salvation he descended from heaven. And he was incarnate from the Holy Spirit and the Virgin Mary, and became man. He was also crucified for us under Pontius Pilate; he suffered and was buried. And he rose again on the third day according to the Scriptures, and ascended into heaven; he sits at the right hand of the Father. And he will come again with glory to judge the living and the dead, and his kingdom will have no end. And in the Holy Spirit, [Col. 1322A] the Lord and giver of life, who proceeds from the Father and the Son; who with the Father and the Son is worshiped together and glorified together; who spoke through the prophets. And in one holy, catholic, and apostolic Church. I confess one baptism for the forgiveness of sins, and I await the resurrection of the dead and the life of the age to come. Amen.

When the Apostles’ Creed has ended, the priest says:

The Lord be with you.

And with your spirit.

Then he washes his hands, saying this prayer:

Grant to our senses, almighty Father, that just as the stains of our hands are washed away outwardly here, so the pollutions of our minds may be cleansed inwardly by you, and may the increase of holy virtues grow within us. [Col. 1322B] Through, etc.

This prayer mentioned above is to be said by the priest when he washes his hands, whether before Mass, during it, or afterward.

For as long as the offertory and the verses are sung, he says these prayers:

O almighty Lord God, make me, a sinner, approach your holy altar today according to your great mercy, and grant that this sacrifice may not be for me a guilt leading to punishment, but a saving cleansing leading to forgiveness. Through, etc.

O God, who make the worthy from the unworthy, the just from sinners, and the clean from the unclean, cleanse my heart and my body from every evil thought and stain of sin, [Col. 1322C] and make me serve worthily and diligently at your holy altars. Mercifully grant that on this altar, to which I approach unworthy, I may offer acceptable sacrifices to your mercy for my sins and offenses and my countless daily transgressions; and for the flock entrusted to me, and for your male and female servants who have confessed their sins to me and given their alms; and for the people subject to me, and all those standing here, and all who are joined to me by familiarity; and for all who pursue me with detestable hatred and oppose the church entrusted to me; and for all Christian believers together.

And through him may my vow and sacrifice be acceptable to you, who offered himself to you, God the Father, as a sacrifice for us; [Col. 1322D] who is the highest priest and pontiff, and the only one without the stain of sin, Jesus Christ, your Son, our Lord, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, through all things, etc.

### Another

Most merciful God, with all my strength I humbly beseech and implore your majesty to forgive the crimes that frail flesh wickedly committed through the temptation of evil spirits. Do not permit me to return to them again, but strengthen me in your justifications, grant me perseverance in them, and make me worthy to stand before the sight of your Majesty and offer you, Lord, a sacrifice with a chaste body and a pure heart. Through, etc.

[Col. 1323A] When the altar has been adorned, before receiving the offerings, he says these prayers most humbly before the altar, accusing himself tearfully:

Before your eyes, Lord, I stand as a guilty witness of my conscience. I do not dare to ask for what I do not deserve to obtain. You know, Lord, what is done within us; we are ashamed to confess what we are not afraid to commit. With words alone we obey you, but in our hearts we lie, and by our actions we show that we do not want what we say we want. But spare those who confess, Lord; forgive sinners; have mercy on those who ask you. And because my understanding is weak regarding your sacraments, and sinners have no words before you that are free from guilt, grant, Lord, that if you do not receive words from us, unworthy and hard-hearted sinners, you may grant forgiveness through yourself. [Col. 1323B] You who live and reign, etc.

### Another

O God, who command yourself to be entreated by sinners and a sacrifice of a contrite heart to be offered to you, deign to accept this sacrifice, which I, your unworthy servant, trusting in your mercy, presume to offer to your immense majesty. And, being appeased, grant that I may deserve to be to you priest and altar and temple and sacrifice, so that through the performance of this ministry I may deserve to obtain forgiveness of my sins; and grant your most merciful favor to me and to all for whom it is offered. Through, etc.

### Another

Although trembling in conscience, Lord, we approach your altar, [Col. 1323C] we retain confidence in your mercy. Although we are always found unworthy to celebrate the sacrifices, nevertheless, if we withdraw, we fear being condemned for disobedience. Therefore, almighty God, we ask that in paternal mercy and with a gracious countenance you deign to cleanse the inner parts of our hearts; and although we are guilty, may the mysteries consecrated to you nevertheless be pleasing to you.

### Another

I stand guilty before the sight of your divine Majesty, presuming to invoke your holy name. Have mercy on me, Lord, a sinful human being; forgive an unworthy priest, through whose hands this offering appears to be offered. Spare me, Lord, polluted above all by the stain of capital crimes, and do not enter into judgment [Col. 1323D] with your servant, because no living person will be justified in your sight. I am weighed down, that is, by vices and the pleasures of the flesh. Remember, Lord, that I am flesh; in your sight even the heavens are not clean, how much less I, an unclean earthly human being, like a menstruating cloth. I am unworthy, Lord Jesus Christ, to be alive; but you, who do not desire the death of a sinner but rather that he be converted and live, grant me forgiveness while I remain in the flesh, so that through the labors of penance I may deserve to enjoy eternal life in heaven, etc. You who live, etc.

### Another

Most High God, forgive me, a sinner, because the iniquity of my whole life has overcome me. With what face shall I look upon you, [Col. 1324A] Lord, or with what words shall I excuse myself before your presence? For I cannot be hidden from you, who consider the secrets of the heart. Woe is me, a sinner, who, standing unworthy before your holy altar, have offered no adornment of mind according to your will. But you, Lord, merciful and compassionate, who created all things from nothing and also formed me, undeserving as I am, and appointed me to serve you worthily, do not repel me from your heavenly sanctuary or confound me before the sight of your awesome Majesty.

I resolved to serve you and please you, Lord, but through my negligence I did not fulfill this. Therefore I see myself abandoned and naked both on earth and in heaven, because I have not kept the commandments of your precepts. I have no hope of salvation [Col. 1324B] in my works, but my soul hangs solely upon the immensity of your mercy and trusts in the multitude of your compassion, that you may save it, Lord Jesus Christ, who do not desire the death of sinners, but that they be converted and live.

Look upon me, miserable as I am, according to your great mercy, and let the cords of my sins be broken, so that I may not perish. Look upon me, Lord, from the seat of your Majesty, and drive away the darkness of my heart with the ray of your light. Protect me, Lord, with the shield of your truth and faith, so that the flaming arrows of the devil may not pierce me. And whatever it is that my unhappiness does not know how, or does not dare, to ask of you, grant that thing, Lord, according to your power: that which may save my soul from death, stretch out your hand to me as I emerge from this mire of darkness, [Col. 1324C] show me the light, forgive what I have done, and grant that I may not do it again. Amen.

### Another

Forgive me, I beg you, Lord, whom the conscience of a stained life has made fearful and the confusion of my crimes has made captive. Since I cannot obtain forgiveness for myself, I stand here to pray for others. I bring before you, if you deign, Lord, to receive them: the groans of captives, the tribulations of peoples, the dangers of nations, the needs of travelers, the poverty of the weak, the despair of the sick, the failings of the elderly, the sighs of the young, the vows of virgins, the lamentations of widows, and the desolations of churches.

But because the same chain of sin binds me as binds the people, I therefore mourn all their sufferings. [Col. 1324D] May a prayer subjected to sins not harm your people, Lord. Through me the vow is offered; through you, Lord, may my duty be completed, because you live and reign, etc.

Then, approaching the altar and kissing it, he says:

I beseech you, O almighty God and Lord, that through the merits of your saints, whose relics are contained here, you may deign through their intercession to forgive me all my sins. You who live, etc.

Then he turns to receive the offerings of the priests and others. When someone offers an offering into the hand of a bishop or priest, he says:

To you, Lord, my creator, I offer a sacrifice for the remission [Col. 1325A] of all my sins and of all your faithful, living and dead.

### For himself and for the entire Christian people

To you, Lord, my creator, I offer a sacrifice of appeasement for my offenses and those of your people. I ask, Lord, that you grant us forgiveness for all our sins.

### For the king, our bishop, all the clergy, and the entire Christian people

To you, Lord, my creator, I offer a sacrifice of appeasement and praise for myself, for our king, for our bishop, and for all the Christian people. I ask, Lord, that you grant us eternal life.

The bishop or priest, receiving the offerings, says:

Receive, Holy Trinity, this offering, [Col. 1325B] which your servant N. offers to you, and grant that it may ascend pleasing to you into your presence, etc.

After receiving the offerings from the clergy or people, the deacon receives the offering from the hand of the subdeacon, saying:

May your sacrifice be acceptable to almighty God and to all his saints.

Then the deacon comes before the bishop and offers it, saying this offertory:

Receive, holy Father, Lord, this offering and this sacrifice of praise in honor of your name, so that it may ascend with sweetness to the ears of your mercy. Through, etc.

And the bishop, receiving the offering from the deacon, says:

May your offering be acceptable to almighty God.

[Col. 1325C] Then, with a pure heart, he offers the offering to the Lord, saying:

Receive, holy Father, almighty and eternal God, this spotless victim, which I, your unworthy servant, offer to you, my living and true God, because I humbly entreat you for the eternal salvation of your entire Church. Through, etc.

### Another

Receive, most merciful Father, the sacrifices of appeasement and praise that I, your unworthy servant, offer to you. You know my formation, for I have sinned in your sight and am unworthy to offer you a sacrifice. But you, merciful and compassionate, forgive me, and, being appeased, receive one who seeks forgiveness, most merciful Father. You who live, etc.

[Col. 1325D] These prayers are to be said when the offerings are offered at the altar; this is the first daily and general prayer:

Receive, Holy Trinity, this offering, which I offer to you in memory of the incarnation, birth, passion, resurrection, and ascension into heaven of our Lord Jesus Christ; and in honor of your saints who have pleased you from the beginning of the world, and of those whose feast is celebrated today, and whose names and relics are held here. May it benefit them for honor and us for salvation, so that all of them may deign to intercede for us in heaven, whose memory we celebrate on earth. Through, etc.

### For oneself

Receive, Holy Trinity, this offering, which [Col. 1326A] I offer to you for my countless sins and offenses, so that you may forgive me for the past and guard me from the future; for the salvation of my body and soul, so that, with your gift, I may keep your commandments here and deserve to attain eternal rewards in the future. Through.

### Another for oneself

Receive, Holy Trinity, this offering, which I offer to you for myself, a sinner and the most wretched of all human beings, and for my countless sins with which I have sinned before you in words, deeds, and thoughts; so that you may forgive me for the past and guard me from the future; for the health of my body and soul; and in thanksgiving for your blessings, which I use every day. Lord, turn your face away from my sins and blot out all my iniquities. [Col. 1326B]

Hear, Lord, the voice of my supplication, when I pray to you, when I lift up my hands toward your holy temple. Lord, hear my prayer, and let my cry come to you.

### Apology of the priest

Receive my confession, Lord, my only hope of salvation, my God, because I have sinned against your law in thoughts, words, and deeds. My sins are many, and I am negligent regarding the work of God and my order, because I have sinned through vainglory, pride, detraction, fornication, theft, false testimony, perjury, adultery, and negligence in the work of God, which I performed carelessly; through carnal desire, laughter, hearing, sight, gluttony, drunkenness, and all my evils, which I committed negligently. [Col. 1326C] For these I ask forgiveness, Lord, because I acknowledge myself guilty.

### Another

O God, who spoke through the mouth of David: “Vow and repay to the Lord your God,” I earnestly beseech you to watch over me, your servant, vigilantly, and, through the intervention of Blessed Mary ever-virgin, mercifully accept the offering that I offer to you for myself. You who live, etc.

### Another

Receive, Holy Trinity, this offering, which I, your unworthy and sinful servant, presume to offer to you for the absolution of my sins, so that, through your mercy, Lord, remission and forgiveness of sins may be granted to me. [Col. 1326D]

### For relatives, brothers, and sisters

Receive, Holy Trinity, this offering, which I offer to you for myself, a sinner, and for the salvation of our community; for all our brothers and sisters in Christ; for all the Christian people; for all who give us alms; and also for those who have commended themselves to our prayers and those who remember us in their prayers. May we receive forgiveness of sins here and deserve to attain eternal rewards in the future.

### For the king and the Christian people

Receive, Holy Trinity, this offering, which we offer to you for our king, his venerable offspring, [Col. 1327A] and the stability of his kingdom; for all the Christian people; for our almsgivers; and for those who continually remember us in their prayers. May they receive forgiveness of sins here and deserve to attain eternal rewards in the future. Through, etc.

### For the Catholic Church

Receive, Holy Trinity, this offering, which I offer to you for your holy Catholic Church, so that it may be pleasing to you and always salutary to it. Through, etc.

### For the salvation of the living

Receive, Holy Trinity, this offering, which I offer to you for the salvation of your servant N., so that, having received forgiveness of sins through your gift, [Col. 1327B] he or she may also deserve to receive the immense joys of eternal life.

### For the sick

Receive, Holy Trinity, this offering, which I offer to you for your sick servant N., so that, having recovered health of mind and body, he or she may offer praises to you in your holy Church and deserve to attain eternal rewards from your chastisement.

### For one deceased person

Receive, Holy Trinity, this offering, which I offer to you for the soul of your servant N., so that through this saving sacrifice, having been purified, he or she may deserve to be joined to the fellowship of your saints. Through, etc.

### For the dead

Receive, Holy Trinity, this offering, which I offer to you for the souls of your male and female servants. [Col. 1327C] Grant them eternal rest among your saints and elect, so that in their fellowship they may enjoy eternal life. Through, etc.

### Another

Receive, Holy Trinity, this offering, which we offer to you for all who have died in confession of your name, so that, as you extend the right hand of your help, they may have rest in everlasting life; and, separated from the punishments of the impious, may they always persevere in the joy of your praise. Through, etc.

### Universal prayer for all

Receive, Holy Trinity, this offering, which I offer to you for our elder and the entire congregation of Saint Peter; for my parents, brothers, benefactors, the faithful, friends, and relatives; [Col. 1327D] for all those standing here; for all who have commended themselves to me; for those who pray for me; and for those for whom I am bound to pray, both living and dead. May you, Lord, in your mercy, grant forgiveness and remission of sins to them and to me, and bestow eternal life. Through, etc.

Then he places the offering on the altar and says:

Sanctify, Lord, this offering, so that it may become for us the body of your only-begotten Son, our Lord Jesus Christ. You who live with you, etc.

Then the deacon receives wine from the subdeacon and mixes it with water in the chalice, saying:

O God, who wonderfully created the dignity of human substance and more wonderfully restored it, [Col. 1328A] grant us, we ask, that through the mystery of this water and wine we may become participants in the divinity of him who deigned to become a participant in our humanity, Jesus Christ.

Then the deacon offers the chalice upon the altar and says to the bishop:

Offer to the Lord a sacrifice of praise and repay your vows to the Most High. May the Lord be your helper; may he make you clean, and when you pray to him, may he hear you.

And the priest, offering the chalice, says this offertory:

We offer you, Lord, the chalice of salvation, and we beseech your mercy, that it may ascend before the sight of your divine majesty with the fragrance of sweetness.

### The following prayer

Lord Jesus Christ, who on the cross of your passion [Col. 1328B] willed blood and water to flow from your side, from which you might consecrate your Church to yourself, receive this sacrifice placed upon your altar, and most mercifully grant that, for our redemption and also for that of the whole world, it may ascend before the sight of your divine Majesty with the fragrance of sweetness. You who live, etc.

After placing the chalice on the altar, the priest says:

Sanctify, Lord, the chalice offered to you, so that it may become for us the blood of your only-begotten Son, our Lord Jesus Christ. You who live with him, etc.

Then he blesses both with raised hand and says:

In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, may this new sacrifice be marked, ordered, sanctified, and blessed.

He adds:

[Col. 1328C] Come, sanctifier, almighty and eternal God, and bless this sacrifice prepared for you. You who live, etc.

Afterward the bishop receives incense from the deacon and places it in the thurible, saying:

Through the intercession of the holy archangel Gabriel, who stands at the right hand of the altar of incense, and of all his elect, may the Lord deign to bless this incense and receive it as a fragrant odor.

This prayer is to be said while, after incense has been placed in the thurible, the thurible itself is carried around the bread and chalice.

We remember, eternal God, almighty Father, the most glorious passion of your Son, as well as his resurrection and his ascension into heaven. [Col. 1328D] Therefore we ask your Majesty that the prayers of our humility may ascend, together with this incense, into the presence of your mercy, and that the fullness of divinity may descend upon this bread and upon this chalice. May there also descend, Lord, that incomprehensible and invisible majesty of the Holy Spirit, just as once it descended upon the sacrifices of the fathers. Through the same one, of the same one, etc.

As the bishop or priest goes around the altar with incense, he says:

May this incense, blessed by you, ascend to you, Lord, and may your mercy descend upon us.

The following:

Let my prayer be directed like incense in your presence, O Lord.

[Col. 1329A] When the fragrance of the incense is offered to the priest and the brothers, each one says:

May the Lord kindle within us the fire of his love and the flame of eternal charity.

Then the priest turns most humbly toward those standing around and says:

Pray for me, brothers and sisters, a sinner, that my sacrifice and yours may be acceptable to the Lord God almighty in his presence.

Then each of them answers him:

May almighty God receive the sacrifice from your hands, and may your prayers ascend as a memorial before the Lord. May he himself hear you, who appointed you an intercessor for our sins.

May all the saints and elect of God pray for you; [Col. 1329B] may he remember all your sacrifice, and may your holocaust be made rich.

Offer to the Lord a sacrifice of praise and repay your vows to the Most High.

May the Lord hear you as you pray for the salvation of us all.

May almighty God have mercy on you and forgive you all your sins.

May the Lord be in your heart and in your mouth, and may he receive from your hands a sacrifice acceptable to you for our salvation and that of us all.

Then the priest turns to the altar and pours out this prayer for himself before the Secret:

Lord Jesus Christ, our faith and confidence, and our entire consolation in the hardship of this present life, [Col. 1329C] mercifully look upon me, unworthy and a sinner, and hear me with favor. Send your holy angel from heaven to receive this offering and present it before the sight of your mercy as a memorial of me, for the praise and glory of your name. You who live, etc.

Then he begins the Secret prayers. When they have been completed and the Preface has been said, while the others sing “Holy, holy, holy,” the priest is to say this prayer quickly:

Lord God, who desire not the death but the repentance of sinners, do not repel me, miserable and fragile sinner that I am, from your mercy. Do not look upon my sins, crimes, impurities, and shameful thoughts, by which I am tearfully separated from your will. Rather look upon your mercies and upon the faith [Col. 1329D] and devotion of those who through me, a sinner, implore your mercy. And because you have willed that I, unworthy as I am, should stand between you and your people, make me such that I may worthily be able to entreat your mercy for myself and for this same people of yours.

Lord, join our voices to the voices of your holy angels. As they praise you continually and tirelessly in eternal blessedness, so may we also, through their intervention, deserve to praise you blamelessly in this pilgrimage. Through, etc.

When this prayer has ended, before the sacraments begin, he commends himself to the Lord again, saying:

As I am about to commemorate the saving sacrifice of the whole world, [Col. 1330A] I behold its dignity and my own foulness, and my conscience is tormented by sins. Yet because you, God, are greatly merciful, I implore you to deign to give me a contrite spirit, which you have revealed as a sacrifice pleasing to you, so that, purified by it, I may approach with devout hands the life-giving sacrifice that abolishes all my sins and infuses into me thereafter the protection needed to avoid them forever. May it also bestow the benefits of salvation in this life and the life to come upon all the faithful, living and dead, for whom it is offered to you. You who live and reign, etc.

Then, with the greatest reverence, he begins the “Therefore,” and the ministers, standing on their steps, sing the psalms until the “Therefore” is finished.

May the Lord hear you.

To you, O Lord, I have lifted up my soul.

[Col. 1330B] Have mercy on me, O God, according to [the] great …

O Lord, refuge …

He who dwells in [the] help …

### Then the Prayers

Save your servant, O Lord, my God, who hopes in you.

You have granted him the desire of his heart, O Lord, and have not denied him the request of his lips.

He asked life of you, and you granted it to him, O Lord, length of days forever and ever.

The eyes of the Lord are upon the just, and his ears are toward their prayers.

Let your mercy, O Lord, be upon us, just as we have hoped in you.

Arise, O Lord; help us and redeem us for the sake of your name. [Col. 1330C]

Lord, hear my prayer, and let my cry come to you.

### Prayer for the priest

May your servant, Lord, rejoice in the benefits obtained. To him to whom you have granted confidence in hoping for your mercy, graciously grant the fulfillment of the mercy desired.

### Another common prayer

We ask, Lord, lend your merciful ears to our prayers, and, knower of hidden things, graciously hear the prayers of those who entreat you, so that, by your gift, we may attain eternal life. Through, etc.

### Within the Canon

In the first place, together with your servant our Pope N., and [Col. 1330D] for all orthodox bishops and cultivators of the Apostolic Faith, abbots, governors, and rulers of the holy Church of God, and for all the holy people of God.

Remember, Lord, your male and female servants—namely, all those joined to me by blood relationship, familiarity, or friendship; all those who confess their sins to me and refresh me with good things in your name; and all those standing here.

This offering also of my humility and devotion, which I offer to you for the chastisement and forgiveness of my sins and criminal deeds, for dissolving and illuminating the blind and stony hardness of my heart, I ask, Lord, that you receive it graciously, and spread over me the bosom of your compassion; enlighten me, open my understanding, grant me the spirit of amendment, and grant wretched me access to return to you through the laments of repentance. Through Christ our Lord, etc.

May you, O God, graciously receive this offering in all things, we ask.

Use this in the same canon when some council or deliberation is being conducted, after you have said “to the eternal, living, and true Lord.”

We humbly beseech you to receive graciously this offering, which we present to you according to the nature of this matter, debated in the proceedings of the present deliberation, so that, brought to an end or directed mercifully not by human counsel but by your holy counsel and equitable judgment, it may be concluded with the bounds of justice and truth, and in every respect arranged and completed according to your will. Through Christ our Lord.

“Communicating,” and commemorating.

For oneself.

Remember, Lord, and have mercy on me, for my illnesses are many and great; they are evil and exceedingly bad, but the multitude of your mercy is greater. Have mercy on me, Lord, and through this one remedy of the world pour some little drop of heavenly grace into my parched heart, so that I may know you.

“But to us sinners.”

For oneself and for debtors.

Remember, Lord, your male and female servants N. N. I especially beseech you for those who remember me before you in their prayers, or who have commended themselves to my unworthy prayers; also for those who have confessed their offenses to me in your sight; for those who have shown some service of charity or devotion toward me or your congregation, or have given according to their generosity; and for those who are joined to me by kinship, blood relationship, or the affection of your charity. Be gracious also to me, your most unworthy servant, and cleanse me from every offense caused by sins. Through, etc.

“But to us sinners.”

Likewise, to be said for oneself in the same canon.

Remember me also, I ask, O God, and have mercy. Although these sacrifices are offered to you, holy Father, almighty and eternal God, by my unworthy hands—and I am not worthy even to invoke your holy and venerable name—nevertheless may those sacrifices offered in honor, praise, and memory of your most glorious and beloved Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, be kindled before your divine majesty like incense, with a sweet fragrance. Through the same Christ our Lord, etc.

“But to us sinners.”

Likewise, for the salvation of the living and the dead.

Remember also, Lord, your male and female servants, and the most blessed Virgin Mary and all your saints. We humbly beseech you, almighty God, through their meritorious intercession, to protect with your abundant mercy the men and women servants whose alms we have received, or who are joined to us by familiarity, and to defend them from every attack, so that they may be saved everywhere by your protection. Grant also indulgence and remission of all sins to the souls of your male and female servants—namely, all the orthodox whose commemoration we make, whose bodies rest here and everywhere, or whose names appear to be written here in the book of life—and deign to have them in the fellowship of your elect.

Here recite the names of those whom you wish.

We beseech you to grant these and all who rest in the Catholic faith a place of peace, refreshment, and rest, and to forgive them. Through Christ, etc.

“But to us sinners.”

Remember also, Lord, your male and female servants N. N., who went before us with the sign of faith and sleep in the sleep of peace. We beseech you to grant them and all who rest in Christ a place of refreshment, light, and peace, and to forgive them. Through the Lord.

“But to us sinners.”

When the secret and the Lord’s Prayer have been completed, when he has said:

“May the peace of the Lord be always with you.”

Mix the Lord’s body with the blood, and say:

“May this most holy mingling of the body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ be salvation of mind and body for all of us who receive it, and a saving preparation for attaining eternal life. Through the same, etc.”

“May the mingling and consecration of the body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ be for eternal life to all of us who receive it.”

The bishop should not put a portion of the offering into the chalice, as presbyters customarily do, but should wait until, after the blessing has ended, the bishop is to receive Communion. Then, taking the portion which he had broken earlier and holding it over the chalice, he should put it in, saying:

“May the mingling of the sacred blood with the holy body of our Lord Jesus Christ benefit all who receive it unto eternal life.”

Prayer.

Grant, Lord Jesus Christ, that just as you have given these sacraments of your body and blood to your faithful as a remedy, so these same mysteries may not be condemnation for me, your unworthy servant, and for all who receive them through me, but may benefit us toward the forgiveness of all offenses, through you, Jesus Christ, etc.

After these words have been said, let him kiss the altar, saying:

“Lord Jesus Christ, who said to your Apostles, ‘I leave you peace; I give you my peace’: do not regard my sins, but the faith of your Church, and deign to pacify and unite it according to your will.”

Then let him turn toward those present and bring peace, saying:

“Hold fast the bond of peace and charity, so that you may be fit for the most holy Mysteries.”

And they should say to one another as they make peace:

“May the peace of Christ and of the Church abound in our hearts.”

When the priest takes the Lord’s body into his hands, let him say:

“I will receive the heavenly bread and call upon the name of the Lord.”

The following prayer:

“May the receiving of your body, Lord Jesus Christ, which I, though unworthy, presume to take, not result for me in judgment and condemnation, but by your compassion benefit me as a protection of mind and body, you who with the Father, etc.”

Another.

“May this sacrament of yours, Lord, which I, though unworthy and a sinner, presume to receive, trusting in your abundant clemency, become for me access to the depths of your mercy and to saving grace, for the healing of soul and body and the remission of all sins. May I deserve to receive it, Savior of the world, not for judgment but for a remedy, etc.”

When the body is received:

“May the body of our Lord Jesus Christ be for me an everlasting remedy unto eternal life.”

When the priest takes the chalice into his hands, let him say:

“What shall I render to the Lord for all that he has rendered to me? I will receive the cup of salvation and call upon the name of the Lord. Calling upon the Lord, I shall praise him, and I shall be saved from my enemies.”

The following prayer:

“May the Communion and confirmation of the body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ benefit me for the remission of all my sins and preserve me unto eternal life.”

Another, for both:

“Holy Father, almighty and eternal God, give me this body and blood of your Son in such a way that through it I may deserve to receive the remission of all sins and be filled with your Holy Spirit, because you are God, and besides you there is no other, whose glorious name endures forever and ever. Amen.”

When the blood is received:

“May the blood of our Lord Jesus Christ preserve me unto eternal life.”

After Communion has been received:

“Lord Jesus Christ, Son of the living God, who by the will of the Father, with the cooperation of the Holy Spirit, gave life to the world through your death: through this sacred body and blood of yours free me from all my iniquities and all my evils; make me obey your commandments, and deign never, forever, to separate me from you. You who live, etc.”

Another.

“May your body, Lord, which I have received, and the chalice which I have drunk, cling to my inward parts; and grant that no stain of sin remain there where your holy sacraments have entered. You who live, etc.”

Then, when presbyters and deacons receive the body into their hands and communicate, it is said to each individually:

“Peace be with you.”  
R\. “And with your spirit.”

Another.

“The Word became flesh and dwelt among us.”

When giving the chalice with the most holy mingling, let him say to each person:

“May this most holy mingling of the body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ benefit you unto eternal life.”

He should communicate the subdeacons and the other clergy in this manner, saying:

“May the reception of the body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ sanctify body and soul unto eternal life. Amen.”

When communicating the people, let him say:

“May the body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ benefit you for the remission of all sins and unto eternal life. Amen.”

Meanwhile, while they are receiving Communion, let him say:

“Forgive me, Lord, because while I am compelled to pray, while I take your holy name upon unclean lips and confess the secrets of unclean deeds, I have before you no words free from guilt. For you know the wounds of my conscience; you know the hidden things of my thoughts; and you alone recognize my uncleanness. Have mercy on me, Lord, have mercy. Forgive me as I handle the secrets of your mystery, and do not judge unworthy of your mercy the one whom you permit to pray for others; and although you recognize in me no testimony of a good work, at least do not refuse the duty of the stewardship entrusted to me. Savior, have mercy on me.”

After Communion has been received:

“May we grasp in mind what we have received with the mouth, and may what is temporal in the gift become for us an everlasting remedy. Through, etc.”

Prayer.

“I beseech you also, most merciful helper of all, that what I presume daily to invoke with a polluted conscience your holy name, and what I, though unworthy, dare to receive—the body and blood of Christ your Son—may not result for me in eternal damnation. Rather, cleanse me diligently through this and fortify me against the arrow of every enemy; and through him whom you sent to redeem us from every defilement of spirit and flesh, deign to dwell in me. Through that same only-begotten Son of yours, our Lord Jesus Christ, free us all from every evil and preserve us in every good. You who live with him, etc.”

Another.

“May your gifts preserve us, Lord, and grant us eternal life. Through, etc.”

Another.

“Guard within us, Lord, the gift of your grace, so that against all the evils of the present and future age we may be fortified by the strength and power of the Eucharist which we have received. You who live, etc.”

Another.

“Grant, Lord Jesus Christ, Son of the living God, that what we, unworthy, have eaten and drunk—the body and blood given for us—may become for us salvation and an everlasting remedy of redemption from all our offenses. Through, etc.”

After the Deacon has said, “Go, the Mass is ended,” let the Priest come before the altar and, kissing it, say:

“May the service of my ministry please you, Holy Trinity, and grant that the sacrifice which I have offered before the eyes of your majesty may be pleasing to you, and, by your mercy, propitiatory for me and for all on whose behalf I have offered it. You who live, etc.”

When the Mass is finished, let him approach the altar and kiss it, saying:

“Through the merits and intercession of blessed Mary ever-Virgin, and of these and all his saints, may almighty God have mercy on us, he who lives, etc.”

When everything has been completed, let the bishop, returning from the altar to the sacristy with the deacons and as many others as he wishes, sing the hymn of the Three Boys.

“Bless the Lord, all works of the Lord.”

“Praise the Lord, all nations.”

“Praise the Lord in his holy places.”

Afterward:

“Our Father, who are in heaven.”

And the versicles:

“Let all your works give thanks to you, Lord, and let your holy ones bless you.”

“The saints shall exult in glory; they shall rejoice in their dwellings.”

“Let the righteous exult in the sight of God, and let them delight in gladness.”

“Not to us, Lord, not to us, but to your name give glory.”

“Your priests, Lord, shall be clothed with righteousness, and your holy ones shall exult.”

[Col. 1336A] “Do not enter into judgment with your servants, Lord, for no living person shall be justified in your sight.”

“Lord God of hosts, restore us; show us your face, and we shall be saved.”

“May the Lord our God bless us; may God bless us, and may all the ends of the earth fear him.”

“Lord, hear my prayer, and let my cry come to you.”

Let us pray.

“O God, whom all your works bless, whom the heavens glorify, whom the multitude of angels praise together: we ask you that, just as you freed the three boys from the furnace of fire not only unharmed but also crying out in your praises, so you may snatch us, wrapped in the bonds of sins, as it were from the abyss of fire. Thus, while we praise you with equal blessing, overcoming the flames of offenses and the fires of carnal works, may we rightly and deservedly render to you the hymn that is your due. Through our Lord, etc.”

Another.

“O God, who mitigated the flames of fire for the three boys, mercifully grant, through their intercession and the merits of all your saints, that the flame of vices and torments may not consume us, your servants. Through the Lord, etc.”

Another.

“We ask, Lord, that by your inspiration you precede our actions and by your assistance accompany them, so that every prayer and all our activity may always begin from you and, begun through you, be brought to completion. Through, etc.”

[Col. 1336C] Here ends the order concerning the office of the Mass.

[Col. 1335]

## Fragment of the Mass

From the beginning up to the Gospel, interpolated with various prayers after the manner of the preceding section.

[Col. 1335C] Here begins the order according to which the Mass should be celebrated. First, the priest should say a prayer while putting on his footwear.

“Fit my feet, Lord, with the preparation of the Gospel of peace, and protect me in the shelter of your wings.”

For washing the hands.

“Grant to my senses, almighty Father, that just as the impurities of my hands are washed away outwardly, so the pollutions of my mind may be cleansed inwardly by you, and that the signs of holy virtues may increase in us. Through Christ, etc.”

For the towel.

“Give strength, Lord, to my hands to wipe away every unclean stain, so that without pollution of mind and body I may be able to serve you. Through Christ.”

For the amice.

“Cast the shadow of holy faith over my head, Lord, and drive away from me the clouds of ignorance.”

For the alb.

“Clothe me, Lord, with the garment of salvation, and surround me with the breastplate of strength.”

For the cincture.

“Gird within me, Lord, the guardianship of my mind, lest my mind be puffed up with the spirit of exaltation. Amen.”

For the stole.

“Surround my neck, Lord, with the stole of righteousness, and cleanse my mind from every corruption of sin.”

For the chasuble.

“Clothe me, Lord, with the ornament of humility, charity, and peace, so that, fortified on every side by virtues, I may be able to resist vices and the enemies of mind and body.”

For the maniple.

“Give me, Lord, sound understanding and a pure voice, so that I may fulfill your praise. Amen.”

Then, with the clergy present, let him sing these psalms, “How lovely,” that is, Psalm 83, which begins in the Italian version as follows [Note: At the place cited we stop here the words of Cardinal Bona: “This, however, must not be omitted at this point: although all the Introits are generally composed from verses of the psalms, Gregory, their author, did not follow that version of the Psalter which all Churches today use in the divine offices, but the ancient one that was in use before Saint Jerome and was called by the holy Fathers the Itala and the Vulgate. He observed the same thing most exactly in the Responsories, Tracts, Offertories, and Communions.

“Since this matter contains some obscurity, it should be briefly elucidated. For many people do not know what that version was or from what sources it arose. To explain this more clearly, its beginning must be traced somewhat farther back. It is known to everyone with even moderate learning how greatly authoritative was once, both before and after Christ’s coming, the Greek translation from the Hebrew language made by the seventy-two interpreters. The Jews used it in their synagogues, as Tertullian testifies; discussing it in chapter 18 of the Apology, he says at the end, ‘The Jews too publicly read it aloud.’ The most learned of the Hebrews, Philo and Josephus, also used it, as is clear from their books.

“The apostles and the faithful at the beginning of the nascent Church likewise read it publicly in ecclesiastical gatherings, as Cyril of Jerusalem teaches in Catechesis 4. Discussing these interpreters and their authority, he says: ‘Study diligently these alone, whom we also recite securely and safely in the Church. The apostles and those ancient bishops, the leaders of the Church, who handed these down, were far wiser than you.’ Irenaeus likewise asserts this in book 3, chapter 25, saying, after recounting the history of those interpreters: ‘The apostles agree with the aforesaid interpretation, and the interpretation agrees with the tradition of the apostles.
